author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.title: Research Summary: June 08, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by safety, alignment, and agent monitoring, alongside provocative efficiency and theory contributions.

Safety & Alignment leads with strong mechanistic and empirical work:

  • The Piggyback Hypothesis gives a concrete causal mechanism for emergent misalignment—chat-template tokens carry finetuned misbehavior onto unrelated tokens—plus an effective mitigation.
  • Think Fast measures no-CoT task-completion time horizons across 30,000+ questions in 43 benchmarks, directly probing reasoning monitorability.
  • CapCode detects and prevents reward hacking in coding agents via randomized tests with a deliberately capped non-cheating score.
  • The Geography of Algorithmic Judgment audits 7 LLMs for racial steering in housing search across 4 US cities using paired testing.

Efficiency & Architecture features bold rethinks with industry stakes:

  • FP8 is All You Need (Matsuoka) argues hardware FP64 is unnecessary for HPC, leveraging FP8 tensor throughput plus the Ozaki Scheme II.
  • Sparsely gated tiny linear experts pushes MoE sparsity to single-neuron experts with the nonlinearity removed, yielding isoflop gains and interpretability benefits.

Theory, Benchmarks & Meta-Science round out the list:

  • Flatland unifies the definition of large step sizes for gradient descent under only local Lipschitz/Hölder continuity.
  • MMBU is the largest biomedical vision-language benchmark, spanning 35 submodalities with grounded/ungrounded tasks.
  • "Don't Just Fix it in Post" (Biderman, Saphra, Barez, Mireshghallah) argues a science of AI must study training dynamics, not post-hoc patches.
  • How Language Models Fail characterizes reasoning failures via token-level uncertainty, distinguishing committed (early lock-in) from persistent failures.

Safety & Alignment leads with strong mechanistic and empirical work:

  • The Piggyback Hypothesis gives a concrete causal mechanism for emergent misalignment—chat-template tokens carry finetuned misbehavior onto unrelated tokens—plus an effective mitigation.
  • Think Fast measures no-CoT task-completion time horizons across 30,000+ questions in 43 benchmarks, directly probing reasoning monitorability.
  • CapCode detects and prevents reward hacking in coding agents via randomized tests with a deliberately capped non-cheating score.
  • The Geography of Algorithmic Judgment audits 7 LLMs for racial steering in housing search across 4 US cities using paired testing.

Efficiency & Architecture features bold rethinks with industry stakes:

  • FP8 is All You Need (Matsuoka) argues hardware FP64 is unnecessary for HPC, leveraging FP8 tensor throughput plus the Ozaki Scheme II.
  • Sparsely gated tiny linear experts pushes MoE sparsity to single-neuron experts with the nonlinearity removed, yielding isoflop gains and interpretability benefits.

Theory, Benchmarks & Meta-Science round out the list:

  • Flatland unifies the definition of large step sizes for gradient descent under only local Lipschitz/Hölder continuity.

entry.title: The Piggyback Hypothesis of Generalization: Explaining and Mitigating Emergent Misalignment

author.name: Jiachen Zhao, Zhengxuan Wu, Aryaman Arora, Yiyou Sun, David Bau, Weiyan Shi

entry.summary: This paper proposes the Piggyback Hypothesis to explain emergent misalignment, showing that chat-template tokens carry finetuned misbehavior onto unrelated queries. The authors validate it via prefix perturbations and introduce Token-Regularized Finetuning (TReFT) to mitigate misalignment.

entry.title: Think Fast: Estimating No-CoT Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models

author.name: Dewi Gould, Francis Rhys Ward, Anders Cairns Woodruff, Rauno Arike, Josh Hills, Alex Serrano, Ida Caspary, Jason Ross Brown, Jo J. Jiao, Patrick Leask, Twm Stone, Ram Potham, Ionut Gabriel Stan, Harry Mayne, Simeon Hellsten, Shubhorup Biswas, Ariana Azarbal, William L. Anderson, Elle Najt, Ryan Greenblatt, Julian Stastny

entry.summary: This study measures how well frontier models reason without chain-of-thought across 30,000+ questions in 43 benchmarks, estimating human time-horizon equivalents for tasks solved without explicit thinking tokens. It matters because CoT-based oversight breaks down if models can reason complexly internally. The strong author roster and safety-relevant framing make this notable.

entry.title: The Geography of Algorithmic Judgment: LLM Intermediaries, Place Identity, and Racial Steering in Housing Search

author.name: Hana Samad, Trung Lam, Christoph M\"ugge-Durum and Michael Akinwumi

entry.summary: This behavioral audit of seven LLMs across four US cities tests racial steering in housing recommendations under progressively detailed prompting that mirrors fair-housing paired-testing. It finds steering is an emergent property of model interpretation interacting with user identity and preferences rather than a static property.

entry.title: Flatland: The Adventures of Gradient Descent with Large Step Sizes

author.name: Leonardo Galli, Curtis Fox, Wiebke Bartolomaeus, Mark Schmidt, Holger Rauhut

entry.summary: This theoretical paper provides a unifying definition of large step sizes for gradient descent requiring only local Lipschitz or Holder gradient continuity, addressing the longstanding question of maximum convergent step size for non-smooth objectives. It designs adaptive methods that provably operate at the edge of stability from training start.

entry.title: Do Coding Agents Deceive Us? Detecting and Preventing Cheating via Capped Evaluation with Randomized Tests

author.name: Thanawat Lodkaew, Johannes Ackermann, Soichiro Nishimori, Nontawat Charoenphakdee, Masashi Sugiyama, Takashi Ishida

entry.summary: Introduces CapCode, which builds coding datasets with randomized tests whose maximum non-cheating score is deliberately capped, so scores above the cap reveal reward hacking, plus CapReward to discourage exploitation. Addresses deceptive performance in coding agent evaluation and training.

entry.title: MMBU: A Massive Multi-modal Biomedical Understanding Benchmark to Probe the Perception Capabilities of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ryan D'Cunha, Alejandro Lozano, Xiaoxiao Sun, Daniel Vela Jarquin, Min Woo Sun, Josiah Aklilu, James Burgess, Yuhui Zhang, Ryan Nayebi, Paola Avila, Robayo, Jin Ye, Ming Hu, Zhongying Deng, Junjun He, Xin Chen, Yue Yao, Robert Tibshirani, Jeffrey J. Nirschl, and Serena Yeung-Levy

entry.summary: MMBU is the largest biomedical vision-language benchmark to date, covering 35 submodalities with structured metadata and tasks spanning ungrounded/grounded classification and object detection. It probes fine-grained perception capabilities of VLMs across diverse biomedical imaging contexts.

entry.title: FP8 is All You Need (Part 1): Debunking Hardware FP64 as the HPC Holy Grail

author.name: Satoshi Matsuoka

entry.summary: Argues provocatively that native hardware FP64 is not essential for scientific computing, showing that FP8 tensor throughput plus the Ozaki Scheme II can recover full FP64 accuracy on AI-optimized GPUs like NVIDIA B300. Introduces a Tensor-Memory Equilibrium roofline model to support the claim.

entry.title: How Language Models Fail: Token-Level Signatures of Committed and Persistent Reasoning Failures

author.name: Tanvi Thoria, Kiana Jafari, Marc R. Schlichting, Mykel J. Kochenderfer

entry.summary: The authors characterize LLM reasoning failures using token-level uncertainty signals, distinguishing committed failures (early lock-in) from persistent uncertainty (accumulating doubt). The framework offers falsifiable diagnostics reproducible across 23 model-dataset configurations, useful for failure detection in reasoning systems.

entry.title: Optimal Rates for Generalization of Gradient Descent Methods with Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Junyu Zhou, Puyu Wang, Yunwen Lei, Yiming Ying, Ding-Xuan Zhou

entry.summary: This theoretical paper establishes the first minimax-optimal generalization rates for deep ReLU networks trained with gradient descent and SGD in the NTK regime, extending prior work limited to shallow architectures. It assumes polynomial width scaling with depth and training samples.

entry.title: The Effect of Training Task Diversity on In-Context Learning through the Lens of Low-Dimensional Subspaces

author.name: Soo Min Kwon, Alec S. Xu, Can Yaras, Dogyoon Song, Laura Balzano, Qing Qu

entry.summary: This paper develops an analytical model explaining how training task diversity shapes in-context learning in transformers by modeling task vectors as a mixture of low-rank Gaussians. It provides theoretical grounding for previously observed but unexplained ICL phenomena.

entry.title: Position: Don't Just "Fix it in Post": A Science of AI Must Study Training Dynamics

author.name: Stella Biderman and Mohammad Aflah Khan and Niloofar Mireshghallah and Catherine Arnett and Fazl Barez and Naomi Saphra

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that a genuine science of AI must study training dynamics rather than relying on post-hoc fixes, advocating for predicting outcomes from early signals, intervening on trajectories, and designing training to reliably produce desired properties. Frames scaling laws as just a start toward understanding emergence.

entry.title: Inside the Visual Mind: Neuroscience-Motivated Concept Circuits for Interpreting and Steering Vision Transformers

author.name: Tang Li, Yanlin Chen, Mengmeng Ma, Xi Peng

entry.summary: ViSAE is a neuroscience-motivated mechanistic interpretability toolbox for Vision Transformers, using sparse autoencoders to extract human-interpretable concept circuits with a 64K-image probing suite and 16K concept vocabulary. It enables understanding and steering of ViT internals to mitigate spurious cues.

entry.title: Autonomous heterogeneous catalyst discovery with a self-evolving multi-agent digital twin

author.name: Zhilong Song, Zongmin Zhang and Lixue Cheng

entry.summary: Presents CatDT, a self-evolving multi-agent digital-twin system that autonomously discovers heterogeneous catalysts from a bulk crystal and natural-language reaction description using eight specialized agents and 27 scientific tools. It predicts surfaces, reaction pathways, transition states, and kinetics in minutes on a single GPU.

entry.title: Attack Selection in Agentic AI Control Evaluations Meaningfully Decreases Safety

author.name: Catherine Ge-Wang, Tyler Crosse, Benjamin Hadad IV, Joachim Schaeffer, Ram Potham, Tyler Tracy

entry.summary: Studies attack selection in AI control evaluations, decomposing attacker behavior into when-to-start and when-to-abort policies across agentic environments BashArena and LinuxArena. Shows strategic timing of attacks meaningfully reduces safety, exposing a gap in current control evaluations that assume non-strategic attackers.

entry.title: Principles and Practice of Deep Representation Learning: or a Mathematical Theory of Memory

author.name: San Buchanan, Druv Pai, Peng Wang, Yi Ma

entry.summary: A book-length treatment by Yi Ma and colleagues aiming to open the black box of deep networks through the lens of representation learning, framed as a mathematical theory of memory covering principles and practice of deep representation learning. It seeks to explain the mechanisms behind deep learning's empirical power.

entry.title: What Do People Actually Want From AI? Mapping Preference Plurality

author.name: Julia Sep\'ulveda Coelho and Scott A. Hale

entry.summary: Analyzing 1,500 open-ended responses from the PRISM dataset across 75 countries, this paper maps what people actually want from AI and exposes failures of RLHF preference aggregation. It finds most values are requested by minorities and that shared words like truthfulness hide divergent meanings.

entry.title: Data-Efficient Autoregressive-to-Diffusion Language Models via On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Xingyu Su, Jacob Helwig, Shubham Parashar, Atharv Chagi, Lakshmi Jotsna, Degui Zhi, James Caverlee, Dileep Kalathil, Shuiwang Ji

entry.summary: OPDLM transforms autoregressive language models into diffusion language models via on-policy distillation, addressing two distribution shifts: objective change discarding ARLM knowledge and train-inference mismatch from random masking. The on-policy distillation aligns training with confidence-based decoding trajectories.

entry.title: Data-Constrained Language Model Pretraining: Improved Regularization and Scaling Laws

author.name: Zhiwei Xu, Shihao Wu, Hanseul Cho, Wei Hu, Yixin Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies data-constrained LLM pretraining via masked-input regularization (MIR), an auxiliary masked next-token loss, and revised scaling laws for the compute-rich multi-epoch regime. It tests whether diffusion-style masking helps autoregressive pretraining without architectural changes.

entry.title: Sparsely gated tiny linear experts

author.name: Simon Schug

entry.summary: Demonstrates that pushing MoE sparsity to the extreme—single-neuron experts selected from many, with the nonlinearity removed (sparsely gated linear neurons, sgatlin)—improves perplexity over standard FFN layers at matched FLOPs while aiding interpretability. Challenges the assumption that experts must be large and nonlinear.

entry.title: Streaming Video Generation with Streaming Force Control

author.name: Hanhui Wang, Yiming Xie, Haiwen Feng, Zhaoyang Lv, Shenlong Wang, Huaizu Jiang

entry.summary: StreamForce is a causal, unified streaming video generation framework offering physically grounded control through continuous, time-varying force inputs (local and global), with a unified force representation and distillation pipeline, running up to 16.6 FPS on one GPU at SOTA force adherence. Advances real-time physics-controllable video generation.

entry.title: A solvable high-dimensional model where nonlinear autoencoders learn structure invisible to PCA while test loss misaligns with generalization

author.name: Vicente Conde Mendes, Lorenzo Bardone, C\'edric Koller, Jorge Medina Moreira, Vittorio Erba, Emanuele Troiani, Lenka Zdeborov\'a

entry.summary: Constructs a solvable high-dimensional spiked model with two latent factors, one visible to covariance and one detectable only via higher-order moments, where nonlinear autoencoders recover structure invisible to PCA. It also rigorously shows test loss can misalign with generalization quality.

entry.title: CrowdMath: A Dataset of Crowdsourced Mathematical Research Discussions

author.name: Sherin Muckatira, Jesse Geneson, Slava Gerovitch, Pavel Etingof, Mikhail Gronas, Anna Rumshisky

entry.summary: Introduces CrowdMath, a dataset of 164 expert-annotated progress chains from collaborative open-problem mathematical research discussions spanning 2016-2025. It captures collaborative proof-building including partial arguments, error identification, and incremental synthesis, unlike final-answer benchmarks.

entry.title: What Matters When Cotraining Robot Manipulation Policies on Everyday Human Videos?

author.name: Richard Li, Aditya Prakash, Andrew Wen, Saurabh Gupta, Yilun Du, Pulkit Agrawal

entry.summary: Investigates what enables transfer from everyday Internet human videos to robot manipulation policies, using a new dataset of 532 human videos with high-quality triangulated hand labels. Finds hand-pose quality matters but the embodiment motion gap requires vision and policy networks to specialize per embodiment, yielding a 29.7% absolute success gain.

entry.title: The Identity Trap in EEG Foundation Models: A Diagnostic Audit

author.name: Jun-You Lin, Ying Choon Wu, Tzyy-Ping Jung

entry.summary: This paper identifies the Identity Trap in EEG foundation models, where high clinical accuracy may reflect subject-identity features rather than genuine biomarkers. The authors propose FMScope, a frozen-representation diagnostic protocol with five tests to detect this confound before fine-tuning.

entry.title: A Geometric Account of Activation Steering through Angle-Norm Decomposition

author.name: Georgii Aparin, Tatiana Gaintseva

entry.summary: This paper revisits the assumption that hidden-state norm carries no concept-relevant information by decomposing activation steering into angular and radial components across seven language models. It finds concepts are primarily encoded in angular structure, clarifying why steering methods differ.

entry.title: Hearing the Unspoken: Language Model Priors for Acoustic Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Jiani Xie, Andrew C. Cullen, Paul Montague, Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein

entry.summary: The Semantic Gambit attack augments adversarial attacks on real-time ASR systems with LLM-derived predictive context, breaking the causal information bottleneck of streaming transcription. It triples word error rates to 35.6%, exposing a new vulnerability from common LLM tooling.

entry.title: Stability beyond Bounded Differences: Sharp Generalization Bounds under Finite $L_p$ Moments

author.name: Qianqian Lei, Soham Bonnerjee, Yuefeng Han, Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: This work develops stability-based generalization bounds requiring only finite Lp moment conditions, extending McDiarmid-style concentration beyond bounded or sub-Gaussian assumptions. It derives sharp high-probability bounds across multiple learning paradigms.

entry.title: ThinkBooster: A Unified Framework for Seamless Test-Time Scaling of LLM Reasoning

author.name: Vladislav Smirnov (1), Chieu Nguyen (1), Sergey Senichev (7), Minh Ngoc Ta (1), Ekaterina Fadeeva (2), Artem Vazhentsev (1), Daria Galimzianova (1), Nikolai Rozanov (1 and 3), Viktor Mazanov (6), Jingwei Ni (2), Tianyi Wu (4), Igor Kiselev (5), Mrinmaya Sachan (2), Iryna Gurevych (1), Preslav Nakov (1), Timothy Baldwin (1), Artem Shelmanov (1) ((1) MBZUAI, (2) ETH Z\"urich, (3) Imperial College London, (4) NUS, (5) Accenture, (6) Innopolis University, (7) Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: ThinkBooster is a unified framework for test-time compute scaling of LLM reasoning, providing a modular library of scaling strategies and scorers, a benchmark evaluating quality-cost trade-offs, and a deployable OpenAI-compatible proxy. It standardizes fragmented and inconsistently evaluated TTC methods.

entry.title: A Geometric View for Understanding Concept Learning and Neuron Interpretation in Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Chenhao Zhang, Chris Lin, Su-In Lee

entry.summary: This paper proposes a unified geometric framework for understanding concept learning and neuron interpretation in sparse autoencoders, formalizing concepts as point sets and casting learning as set alignment. It yields three notions of learning with geometric conditions and capacity constraints.

entry.title: TRACE: Trajectory Reasoning through Adaptive Cross-Step Evidence Aggregation for LLM Agents

author.name: Vijitha Mittapalli, Shreyaa Jayant Dani, Satya Srujana Pilli, Snigdha Ansu, Mohammadreza Teymoorianfard, Franck Dernoncourt, Hongjie Chen, Yu Wang, Ryan A. Rossi, Nesreen K. Ahmed

entry.summary: TRACE is a monitoring framework for long-horizon LLM agent trajectories using a triage-inspect-judge loop to connect evidence across temporally distant actions and detect hidden malicious objectives. It is evaluated on SHADE-Arena against state-of-the-art baselines.

entry.title: AsyncPatch Diffusion: spatially-flexible image generation

author.name: Samuele Papa, Valentin De Bortoli, Guillaume Couairon, Daniel S\'ykora, Romuald Elie, and Klaus Greff

entry.summary: AsyncPatch Diffusion is a joint-diffusion framework that assigns distinct noise levels to different spatial input dimensions, enabling spatially heterogeneous denoising trajectories, and proves the first valid ELBO for this process. A single pretrained model can perform spatially adaptive generation.

entry.title: Self-evolving LLM agents with in-distribution Optimization

author.name: Yudi Zhang, Meng Fang, Zhenfang Chen, Mykola Pechenizkiy

entry.summary: Q-Evolve is a self-evolving framework for LLM agents that combines automatic process-reward labeling with policy learning under an in-distribution RL paradigm, learning a critic from mixed expert and agent trajectories to stabilize credit assignment in sparse-reward, long-horizon tasks. It addresses a core bottleneck in training reliable interactive LLM agents.

entry.title: Automatic, Debiased, and Invariant Counterfactual Generation under General Interventions

author.name: Raphael C Kim, Jingsen Zhu, Ramin Zabih, Michele Santacatterina

entry.summary: ADIGen is a counterfactual generation framework under general interventions that combines Riesz regression, causal invariance, and orthogonal learning for stable, doubly robust, distribution-shift-robust estimation, with excess-risk guarantees. Targets reliable decision support under complex high-dimensional interventions.

entry.title: Sycophantic Praise: Evaluating Excessive Praise in Language Models

author.name: Daniel Vennemeyer, Phan Anh Duong, Meryl Ye, Ruihong Huang, Tianyu Jiang

entry.summary: Argues that sycophantic praise and flattery are a distinct alignment problem from agreement-based sycophancy, introducing a parameterized framework measuring whether praise is excessive relative to contribution quality and user ability. Finds excessive praise more frequent in social/interpretive domains and that the framework beats generic LLM judges.

entry.title: Whisper Hallucination Detection and Mitigation via Hidden Representation Steering and Sparse AutoEncoders

author.name: Georgii Aparin, Vadim Popov, Tasnima Sadekova, Assel Yermekova

entry.summary: Investigates Whisper ASR hallucinations on non-speech audio using internal encoder activations and sparse autoencoder latents, showing hallucination-related information is linearly separable in deeper layers, and proposes steering strategies that cut hallucination rate from about 73% to 14%. Combines interpretability with practical mitigation.

entry.title: WorldBench: A Challenging and Visually Diverse Multimodal Reasoning Benchmark

author.name: Yida Yin, Harish Krishnakumar, Chung Peng Lee, Boya Zeng, Wenhao Chai, Shengbang Tong, Wenhu Chen, Hu Xu, Xingyu Fu, Gabriel Sarch, Aleksandra Korolova, Zhuang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces WorldBench, a challenging visually diverse multimodal reasoning benchmark built from a taxonomy of thousands of visual concepts and manually crafted questions that frontier MLLMs fail. It emphasizes visual diversity over expanding task types to better evaluate real-world reliability.

entry.title: MedSIGHT: Towards Grounded Visual Comprehension in Medical Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Aofei Chang, Le Huang, Alex James Boyd, Parminder Bhatia, Taha Kass-Hout, Fenglong Ma, Cao Xiao

entry.summary: MedSIGHT unifies vision-language comprehension and pixel-level segmentation in medical LVLMs via a Region Perceiver module producing region-centric tokens and a medical region codebook added to the LLM vocabulary. This enables grounded visual comprehension connecting visual findings to semantic interpretation.

entry.title: Interpreting Brain Responses to Language with Sparse Features from Language Models

author.name: Michael A. Lepori, Kendrick Kay, Greta Tuckute

entry.summary: This paper introduces Augmented Sparse Encoding Models that replace dense LM hidden states with hierarchical sparse autoencoder features plus surprisal to interpret brain responses to language. It uses 7T fMRI data to test whether model-brain alignment reflects primary or idiosyncratic LM variation.

entry.title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Zhennan Shen, Yanshu Li, Qingyu Yin, Chak Tou Leong, Zhilin Wang, Yanxu Chen, Rongduo Han, Sunbowen Lee, and Yi R. Fung

entry.summary: This paper characterizes the parameter-space training dynamics of on-policy distillation, finding it occupies a relaxed off-principal regime between SFT and RLVR and exhibits subspace locking into a narrow low-dimensional channel. It offers geometric understanding of an increasingly used reasoning improvement method.

entry.title: Covariance Shrinkage via Stochastic Interpolation

author.name: Mathieu Chalvidal, Florentin Coeurdoux and Eric Vanden-Eijnden

entry.summary: Recasts classical covariance shrinkage as empirical risk minimization over stochastic interpolants between source and target distributions, recovering known estimators and revealing scheduling, couplings/optimal transport, and nonlinear flow maps as risk-reduction mechanisms. Offers a unifying theoretical lens connecting shrinkage and generative interpolants.

entry.title: RealDocBench: A Benchmark for Field-Level QA and Layout Understanding on Real-World Regulated Documents

author.name: Ameya Joshi, Joon Kim, Gus Eggert, Joseph Bajor, Cindy Hao, Jing Reyhan, Kushal Byatnal, Eli Badgio

entry.summary: RealDocBench is a two-track benchmark built from real regulated documents (mortgage, finance, logistics, clinical) with 1,356 field-level QA questions and typed gold answers, evaluating parsers on what downstream agents actually need rather than markdown similarity. Highlights the gap between academic benchmarks and high-stakes document workflows.

entry.title: How AI Agents Reshape Knowledge Work: Autonomy, Efficiency, and Scope

author.name: Jeremy Yang, Kate Zyskowski, Noah Yonack, Jerry Ma

entry.summary: Using production data from Perplexity's Search and Computer products, this study measures how autonomous AI agents reshape knowledge work, finding the agentic Computer product performs 26 minutes of autonomous work per session versus 33 seconds for Search and shifts follow-up queries toward higher-complexity tasks. Provides rare empirical evidence on real-world agent adoption.

entry.title: MemDreamer: Decoupling Perception and Reasoning for Long Video Understanding via Hierarchical Graph Memory and Agentic Retrieval Mechanism

author.name: Cong Chen, Guo Gan, Kaixiang Ji, ChaoYang Zhang, Zhen Yang, Guangming Yao, Hao Chen, Jingdong Chen, Yi Yuan, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: MemDreamer decouples perception and reasoning for hours-long video understanding by building a hierarchical graph memory of spatiotemporal and causal relations and using agentic tool-augmented retrieval in an observation-reason-action loop, achieving SOTA on long-video benchmarks. Mitigates token explosion and attention dilution.

entry.title: A generalizable 3D framework and model for self-supervised learning in medical imaging

author.name: Tony Xu, Sepehr Hosseini, Chris Anderson, Anthony Rinaldi, Rahul G. Krishnan, Anne L. Martel, Maged Goubran

entry.summary: Introduces 3DINO, a self-supervised learning method adapted for 3D medical imaging, pretrained on roughly 100,000 multimodal multi-organ scans to produce a general-purpose ViT model. It reportedly generalizes across modalities and organs and beats SOTA on many segmentation and classification tasks.

entry.title: Lean4Agent: Formal Modeling and Verification for Agent Workflow and Trajectory

author.name: Ruida Wang, Jerry Huang, Pengcheng Wang, Xuanqing Liu, Luyang Kong, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Lean4Agent, claimed to be the first framework using the Lean4 dependent-type formal language to model and verify LLM agent workflows and execution trajectories. Provides an extensible FormalAgentLib for formally specifying and checking agent semantic correctness.

entry.title: Robots Need More than VLA and World Models

author.name: Elis Karcini, Faisal Mehrban, Quang Nguyen, Mac Schwager, Arash Ajoudani, Cesar Cadena, Jan Peters, Marco Hutter, Haitham Bou-Ammar

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that scaling Vision-Language-Action models and world models alone is insufficient for generalist robots, identifying the missing ability to convert abundant unstructured behavioral data (human motion, video, simulation) into grounded robot supervision. Names four missing components needed beyond VLA and world models.

entry.title: From Pixels to Newtons: Predicting In Vivo Joint Contact Forces from Monocular Video

author.name: Jessy Lauer

entry.summary: This paper presents a physics-free pipeline that predicts 3D hip and knee joint contact forces directly from uncalibrated monocular video, without markers, force plates, or musculoskeletal models. It could democratize biomechanical assessment relevant to osteoarthritis, implants, and rehabilitation that currently requires invasive instrumentation.

entry.title: Anchored, Not Graded: Vision-Language Models Fail at Slant-from-Texture Perception

author.name: Qian Zhang, Michal Golovanevsky, Fulvio Domini, and James Tompkin

entry.summary: This study shows that vision-language models fail at slant-from-texture perception, predicting slant only at a few discrete anchors with little dependence on stimulus properties, unlike graded human biases. Supervised fine-tuning only partially fixes the anchoring, revealing a gap in low-level geometric sensitivity.

entry.title: Multi-Robot Planning and Control from CCTV Camera Networks in a Real Warehouse

author.name: Luke Robinson, Benjamin Ramtoula, Anas Izaaryene, Paul Newman, Daniele De Martini

entry.summary: This paper extends off-board robot control from environment-embedded cameras to coordinated fleets in a real warehouse, driving multiple robots using only a distributed CCTV network and edge compute. It operates entirely in image space over an uncalibrated topological camera graph with a hierarchical planner preventing collisions and deadlocks.

entry.title: What Your Posts Reveal: A Benchmark and Agentic Framework for User-Level Privacy Leakage on Social Media

author.name: Zifan Peng, Yini Huang, Aiwen Lu, Qiming Ye, Peixian Zhang, Jingyi Zheng, Yule Liu, Xuechao Wang, Xinlei He, and Jiaheng Wei

entry.summary: SopriBench is a synthetic multimodal benchmark for user-level privacy leakage on social media, covering 50 profiles and 1,569 images with attributes, sensitivity, and leakage types abstracted from real accounts. It introduces an agentic framework and severity metric to capture cumulative cross-post exposure.

entry.title: GRASP: Geometry-aware Residual Alignment for Scalable Pretraining Data Attribution

author.name: Yue Min, Ruining Chen, Yujun Li

entry.summary: GRASP reframes data attribution as subset-level counterfactual utility prediction, modeling interactions via a quadratic geometric penalty rather than additive isolated scores. It uses feature sketches and confidence-bound selection for pretraining-scale efficiency.

entry.title: ActionMap: Robot Policy Learning via Voxel Action Heatmap

author.name: Pei Yang, Hai Ci, Yanzhe Chen, Qi Lv, Han Cai, and Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: ActionMap introduces a voxel heatmap action head that replaces the single-point action decoder in vision-language-action models, exploiting the geometric structure of the action space. It drops into existing VLAs in place of token-bin, regression, or flow-matching decoders.

entry.title: Tree-of-Experience: A Structured Experience-Management Solution for Self-Evolving Agents under Low-Repetition and Implicit-Reward Environments

author.name: Zihao Deng, Yining Zhu, Leiming Wang, Jingfei Lu, Junbo Wang, Chuncheng Ran, Yu Yang, Dixuan Yang, Jikun Shen

entry.summary: OpenHalDet is a unified benchmark for hallucination detection across diverse generation scenarios, standardizing the pipeline from prompt construction to detector scoring and supporting black-box and other access settings. It addresses inconsistent configurations and limited domain coverage in prior evaluations.

entry.title: $\alpha$-PFN: Fast Entropy Search via In-Context Learning

author.name: Herilalaina Rakotoarison, Steven Adriaensen, Tom Viering, Carl Hvarfner, Samuel M\"uller, Frank Hutter, Eytan Bakshy

entry.summary: Alpha-PFN uses a two-stage amortization with prior-data fitted networks to approximate entropy search acquisition functions in a single forward pass, avoiding the slow and error-prone Monte Carlo estimation of information gain. It learns to predict expected information gain via in-context learning.

entry.title: Mitosis Detection in the Wild: Multi-Tumor and Context-Aware Generalization in the MIDOG 2025 Challenge

author.name: Marc Aubreville, Jonas Ammeling, Sweta Banerjee, Viktoria Weiss, Taryn A. Donovan, Robert Klopfleisch, Jiaqi Lv, Shan E Ahmed Raza, Rapha\"el Bourgade, Thomas Walter, Yasemin Topuz, Song\"ul Varl{\i}, Charles-Antoine Collins-Fekete, Zhuoyan Shen, Navya Sri Kelam, Nitin Singhal, Christian Marzahl, Brian Napora, Tengyou Xu, Hongyan Gu, Mario Vento, Gennaro Percannella, Norbert Ropiak, Izabela Wasiak, Jie Xiao, Shaojun Liu, Seungho Choe, April Khademi, Vidushi Walia, Sujatha Kotte, Andrew Broad, Alex Wright, Guillaume Balezo, Esha Sadia Nasir, Mostafa Jahanifar, Yosuke Yamagishi, Shouhei Hanaoka, Mattia Sarno, Francesco Tortorella, Biwen Meng, Jingxin Liu, Sara Krauss, Daniel Hieber, Lavish Ramchandani, Dev Kumar Das, Mieko Ochi, Yuan Bae, Piotr Giedziun, Mateusz Maniewski, Vangala Govindakrishnan Saipradeep, Naveen Sivadasan, Leire Benito-Del-Valle, Adrian Galdran, Kaustubh Atey, Sameer Anand Jha, Adinath Dukre, Imran Razzak, Maxime W. Lafarge, Viktor H. Koelzer, Nils Porsche, Nikolas Stathonikos, Mitko Veta, Dominik Hirling, Zsanett Zs\'ofia Iv\'an, Peter Horvath, Katharina Breininger, Christof A. Bertram

entry.summary: Reports the MIDOG 2025 challenge on mitosis detection across 12 human, canine, and feline tumor types and multiple scanners, evaluating model robustness to real-world biological and contextual diversity beyond hand-selected hotspots. Important benchmark for clinically deployable computational pathology.

entry.title: A Comprehensive Anatomy of Human and DeepSeek-R1 LLM Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Yuxiang Chen and Jun Wang

entry.summary: Annotates 10,247 reasoning steps across all 30 AIME 2025 problems to compare human versus DeepSeek-R1 reasoning, finding humans alternate compactly between analysis and deduction while the model engages in redundant revisiting and shallow verification (described as topological mimicry). Offers fine-grained insight into LLM reasoning structure.

entry.title: Socratic-SWE: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Trace-Derived Agent Skills

author.name: Chuan Xiao, Zhengbo Jiao, Shaobo Wang, Wei Wang, Bing Zhao, Hu Wei, Linfeng Zhang, Lin Qu

entry.summary: Socratic-SWE is a closed-loop self-evolution framework for coding agents that distills the agent's own historical solving traces into structured skills summarizing recurring failures and repair patterns, then uses them to generate targeted training tasks aligned with the agent's weaknesses. Addresses scarcity of high-quality SWE training data.

entry.title: Accelerated Decentralized Stochastic Gradient Descent for Strongly Convex Optimization

author.name: Ming Sun, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes Multi-Gossip Accelerated DSGD combining Nesterov-type primal-dual extrapolation with multi-round fast gossip averaging to simultaneously achieve accelerated dependence on both condition number and network spectral gap for strongly convex decentralized stochastic optimization—previously unattained jointly. Closes a gap in decentralized optimization theory.

entry.title: AxisGuide: Grounding Robot Action Coordinate System in RGB Observations for Robust Visuomotor Manipulation

author.name: Jiyun Jang, Yujin Sung, Woosung Joung, Daewon Chae, Sangwon Lee, Sohwi Kim, Jinkyu Kim, Jungbeom Lee

entry.summary: AxisGuide is a lightweight guidance method that grounds the robot's base-frame action coordinate system in RGB image space to improve visuomotor manipulation robustness under distribution shifts. It uses camera parameters and end-effector poses to render axis cues, bridging semantic scene and action-coordinate understanding.

entry.title: Diagnosing Visual Ignorance in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Runyu Zhou, Qi Zhang, Qixun Wang, Yisen Wang

entry.summary: This work diagnoses why vision-language models rely on language priors over visual evidence, using counterfactual layer replacement and layer-wise MLP probing. It reveals a multi-stage bottleneck where intermediate and later layers fail to retrieve or suppress visual information.

entry.title: Constructing VAE Latent Spaces with Prescribed Topology

author.name: Jilles S. van Hulst, Jakub M. Tomczak, W.P.M.H. Heemels, Duarte J. Antunes

entry.summary: This paper presents a constructive framework for building VAE latent spaces with prescribed topology, resolving topological mismatch for manifolds admitting product covering spaces including tori, Mobius strips, and Klein bottles. It uses factorized distributions with closed-form decoupled KL divergences.

entry.title: Online Pandora's Box for Contextual LLM Cascading

author.name: Alexandre Belloni, Yan Chen, Yehua Wei

entry.summary: Formulates LLM API cascading as an online contextual Pandora's Box problem with output-mediated feedback, where querying reveals output and cost but reward is only observed for the deployed choice. Provides algorithms for adaptively querying and selecting among LLM APIs to balance cost and quality.

entry.title: Your UnEmbedding Matrix is Secretly a Feature Lens for Text Embeddings

author.name: Songhao Wu, Zhongxin Chen, Yuxuan Liu, Heng Cui, Cong Li, Rui Yan

entry.summary: Identifies that LLM-derived text embeddings over-align with frequent uninformative tokens when projected onto vocabulary space, suppressing nuanced semantics, and introduces EmbedFilter—a simple linear transformation using the unembedding matrix as a feature lens to refine embeddings. Improves LLMs as off-the-shelf text embedders.

entry.title: On the existence of consistent adversarial attacks in high-dimensional linear classification

author.name: Matteo Vilucchio, Lenka Zdeborov\'a, Bruno Loureiro

entry.summary: Theoretically investigates what distinguishes adversarial attacks from ordinary misclassification in high-dimensional linear classification, introducing a metric for vulnerability to label-preserving (consistent) perturbations. It provides exact asymptotic characterizations revealing distinct vulnerability patterns versus standard robust error measures.

entry.title: Rigorous Asymptotics for First-Order Algorithms Through the Dynamical Cavity Method

author.name: Yatin Dandi, David Gamarnik, Francisco Pernice, Lenka Zdeborov\'a

entry.summary: Formalizes the non-rigorous dynamical cavity method from statistical physics and uses it to give a new proof of Dynamical Mean Field Theory equations describing first-order optimization algorithms in high dimensions. Bridges physics intuition with mathematical rigor.

entry.title: SafeGene: Reusable Adapters for Transferable Safety Alignment

author.name: Yanghan Wang, Zhiqiang Kou, Fu Feng, Jing Wang, Xin Geng

entry.summary: Proposes SafeGene, a reusable safety-adapter module that decouples safety alignment from task-specific fine-tuning, derived from aligned-versus-degraded model discrepancies and transferable across a model family. Addresses the recurring problem of fine-tuning eroding safety alignment in open-weight LLMs.

entry.title: On the Hardness of Optimal Motion on Trees

author.name: Tzvika Geft

entry.summary: This theoretical paper settles the complexity of Multi-Agent Path Finding on trees across distance, makespan, and flowtime objectives for labeled and colored variants. It proves NP-hardness for several previously open basic cases, including the classical Pebble Motion problem.

entry.title: ShallowBench: Benchmarking Generative Drug Design Models on Shallow-Pocket Targets

author.name: Saket Reddy, Shiwei Liu

entry.summary: ShallowBench is a curated benchmark of 5,780 shallow-pocket targets from CrossDocked2020 for evaluating generative drug design models on historically undruggable targets like KRAS and MYC. Evaluation reveals state-of-the-art models produce weaker binding affinity on low-concavity interfaces.

entry.title: SCOUT: Semantic scene COverage via Uncertainty-guided Traversal

author.name: Junyu Mao, Sara Ayoubi, Vishnu D. Sharma, Ilija Had\v{z}i\'c, and Matthew Andrews

entry.summary: SCOUT is an online semantic exploration framework that couples active robot traversal with probabilistic 3D scene graph construction, maintaining posterior beliefs over open-vocabulary object labels and structural relations. Beliefs feed back to guide uncertainty-driven exploration, closing the perception-decision loop.

entry.title: When to Think Deeply: Inhibitory Deliberation for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Zhixuan He and Yue Feng

entry.summary: IDPR is a framework for response-conditioned inhibitory deliberation that first generates a concise intuitive answer, then uses an inhibition controller to decide whether to release it or invoke slow reasoning. The controller conditions on the fast answer's confidence, logit margin, parseability, and generation cost.

entry.title: Performance Variation in Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haruto Tanaka, A. Rupam Mahmood

entry.summary: This paper critiques conventional uncertainty estimates in deep RL for underreporting run-to-run performance variation, and proposes percentile-based statistics (min-max IPR and run-wise percentile highlighting) for evaluation. The tools are interpretable and rely on standard runs.

entry.title: AdMem: Advanced Memory for Task-solving Agents

author.name: Runzhe Wang, Huilin Lu, Shengjie Liu, Li Dong, Jason Zhu

entry.summary: AdMem is a unified automatic memory framework for task-solving LLM agents integrating semantic, episodic, and procedural memory in a bi-level short/long-term design. A multi-agent actor-memory-critic architecture enables automatic memory generation, reward annotation, and adaptive retrieval addressing failure cases.

entry.title: Quantifying Media Representation Dynamics Across 25 Years of News Reporting on Policing-related Deaths

author.name: Farhan Samir, Jappun Dhillon, Meghna Ravikumar, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed, Vered Shwartz

entry.summary: This paper performs the largest computational analysis of 4,000 Canadian news articles on police-involved deaths over 25 years, introducing the PerspectiveGap model grounded in media sociology. It finds state bureaucrat perspectives appear nearly three times more often than civilian perspectives, with civilian representation rising recently.

entry.title: AdaGRPO: A Capability-Aware Adaptive Enhancement for Flow-based GRPO

author.name: Jiazi Bu, Pengyang Ling, Yujie Zhou, Yibin Wang, Yuhang Zang, Tianyi Wei, Xiaohang Zhan, Jiaqi Wang, Tong Wu, Xingang Pan, Dahua Lin

entry.summary: AdaGRPO is a capability-aware adaptive enhancement to flow-based GRPO for text-to-image alignment, addressing blind spots in prompt selection and advantage estimation. It introduces adaptive data selection and global policy improvement measurement.

entry.title: Characterize Then Distill: Mechanistic Reasoning in Large Output Spaces

author.name: Debjyoti Saha Roy, Byron C. Wallace, and Javed A. Aslam

entry.summary: This work mechanistically characterizes how reasoning models handle extreme multi-label tasks as a two-phase shortlist-then-fine-grained-reasoning process. It leverages this to develop a mechanistic distillation strategy that outperforms standard distillation.

entry.title: Unified Safe In-context Image Generation in Multimodal Diffusion Transformers via Restricting Unsafe Information Flows

author.name: Xiang Yang, Feifei Li, Mi Zhang, Geng Hong, Xiaoyu You, Mi Wen, Min Yang

entry.summary: UVR is a training-free safe image generation framework for multimodal diffusion transformers that restricts unsafe information flows in multimodal attention. It targets image-to-image editing safety, which prior U-Net-based mechanisms handle poorly.

entry.title: Stream3D-VLM: Online 3D Spatial Understanding with Incremental Geometry Priors

author.name: Hanxun Yu, Xuan Qu, Lei Ke, Boqiang Zhang, Yuxin Wang, Jianke Zhu, Dong Yu

entry.summary: Stream3D-VLM enables online 3D spatial understanding from streaming video using autoregressive streaming control, incremental geometry priors, and adaptive voxel compression. It moves beyond offline 3D multimodal models that require complete scene observations.

entry.title: Uniform Stability and Generalization Error of GD and SGD on Fixed-Point Parameters

author.name: Jonghyun Shin, Sejun Park

entry.summary: This paper analyzes generalization error and uniform stability of GD and SGD over discrete parameter spaces with deterministic or stochastic rounding. It shows deterministic rounding degrades GD generalization with matching lower bounds, while SGD with deterministic rounding retains nontrivial stability.

entry.title: LIMMT: Less is More for Motion Tracking

author.name: Yu Guan, Zekun Qi, Chenghuai Lin, Xuchuan Chen, Dairu Liu, Wenyao Zhang, Jilong Wang, Xinqiang Yu, He Wang, Li Yi

entry.summary: LIMMT is a data-centric study for physics-based humanoid motion tracking that defines motion data quality via physics feasibility, diversity, and complexity. It shows that training on under 3% of AMASS yields better tracking than the full dataset.

entry.title: Deep Single-Index Fr\'echet Regression

author.name: Muqing Cui, Yidong Zhou, Su I Iao, Hans-Georg M\"uller

entry.summary: DeSI is a deep single-index Frechet regression framework for predicting metric-space-valued outputs (distributions, networks, SPD matrices) from high-dimensional inputs. It estimates an interpretable index direction with a neural network to mitigate the curse of dimensionality.

entry.title: GenPO++: Generative Policy Optimization with Jacobian-free Likelihood Ratios

author.name: Ke Hu, Shutong Ding, Panxin Tao, Jingya Wang, Ye Shi

entry.summary: GenPO++ proposes a reversible generative policy optimization framework that enables exact likelihood evaluation for flow-based policies in on-policy reinforcement learning without dummy-action augmentation. It addresses a real bottleneck in applying expressive generative policies to continuous control.

entry.title: RASFT: Rollout-Adaptive Supervised Fine-Tuning for Reasoning

author.name: Yongliang Miao, Fengyuan Liu, Wei Shi, Yanguang Liu, Fei Sun, Na Zou, and Mengnan Du

entry.summary: RASFT is a policy-aware supervised fine-tuning framework that calibrates expert supervision based on problem-level solvability estimated from verified on-policy rollouts. It strengthens guidance when the policy struggles and incorporates correct self-generated trajectories otherwise.

entry.title: dots.tts Technical Report

author.name: Shi Lian, Changtao Li, Bohan Li, Hankun Wang, Da Zheng, Junfeng Tian, Yufeng Ma, Colin Zhang, Kai Yu

entry.summary: dots.tts is a 2B-parameter continuous autoregressive text-to-speech foundation model that models speech in a continuous latent space with a semantically structured AudioVAE, full-history conditioning, and reward-free self-corrective post-training. It achieves best average performance on Seed-TTS-Eval.

entry.title: Beyond Linear and Overcomplete Regimes: A Mean-Field Analysis of Bottleneck Autoencoders

author.name: Santanu Das, Ramyak Bilas, Pascal Esser, Satyaki Mukherjee

entry.summary: This paper provides a mean-field analysis of nonlinear bottleneck autoencoders, deriving explicit learning dynamics for both encoder and decoder beyond linear or overcomplete regimes. It shows finite-width risk tracks the mean-field trajectory with high probability and converges at optimality.

entry.title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention

author.name: Justin Y. Chen, Ying Feng, Piotr Indyk, Michael Kapralov, Ekaterina Kochetkova, Boris Prokhorov

entry.summary: This theory paper advances tight upper and lower bounds for the streaming attention approximation problem (KV cache compression), building on recent COLT and NeurIPS formalizations using discrepancy theory and information-theoretic limits. It closes open gaps in space-bounded transformer implementation. The work grounds practical KV-cache heuristics in rigorous theory.

entry.title: Spline Policy: A Structured Representation for Robot Policies

author.name: Mengze Tian, Yiming Li, Sichao Liu, Auke Ijspeert and Sylvain Calinon

entry.summary: Spline Policy replaces fixed-resolution action chunks in imitation-learning robot policies with spline parameters, yielding compact, continuous, resolution-flexible, and editable trajectories that can also be converted to state-dependent vector fields. Offers a structured action representation without changing the policy backbone.

entry.title: Generative Modeling of Discrete Latent Structures via Dynamic Policy Gradients

author.name: Stefan Ivanovic, Ge Liu, Mohammed El-Kebir

entry.summary: GReinSS is a policy-learning framework using dynamically rescaled rewards to infer mechanistic discrete latent states that maximize observed-data likelihood, outperforming VAEs and other baselines and reconstructing RNA isoforms from real sequencing data. Bridges generative modeling and combinatorial latent inference for science.

entry.title: M$^3$Exam: Benchmarking Multimodal Memory for Realistic User-Agent Interactions

author.name: Zhengjun Huang, Wenxuan Liu, Zhoujin Tian, Wei Chen, Junle Chen, Yuqian Wu, Fangyuan Zhang, Qintian Guo, Xiaofang Zhou

entry.summary: M3Exam is a query-centric multimodal conversational memory benchmark grounded in realistic user-agent file interactions, evaluating cross-modal grounding and implicit information inference, alongside a memory method (M3Proctor). Reveals persistent gaps in cross-modal grounding and cross-session reasoning for MLLM memory systems.

entry.title: TEVI: Text-Conditioned Editing of Visual Representations via Sparse Autoencoders for Improved Vision-Language Alignment

author.name: Sweta Mahajan, Sukrut Rao, Jiahao Xie, Alexander Koller, Bernt Schiele

entry.summary: TEVI uses sparse autoencoders to disentangle CLIP image embeddings and trains a masking module to selectively reconstruct only caption-described attributes, addressing the image-text information imbalance that harms vision-language alignment. Shows it preserves described attributes while discarding others.

entry.title: Act As a Real Researcher: A Suite of Benchmarks Evaluating Frontier LLMs and Agentic Harnesses in Research Lifecycle

author.name: Jiayu Wang, Weijiang Lv, Bowen Fu, Jing Fu, Jiayi Song, Lingyu Zhang, Lanxuan Xue, Luodi Chen, Zepeng Xin, Kaiyu Li, Xiangyong Cao

entry.summary: AARR (Act As a Real Researcher) is a benchmark series evaluating whether frontier LLMs and agentic harnesses can emulate the professionalism, field sensitivity, research ethics, and nuanced judgment of human researchers across the research lifecycle, not just execution. Highlights gaps preventing agents from replacing human researchers.

entry.title: Second-Order Path Kernel Interpolation Formulas in Machine Learning

author.name: Jin Guo, Roy Y. He, Jean-Michel Morel

entry.summary: Develops second-order extensions of Domingos's path-kernel interpolation formulas, showing the leading path-kernel term is supplemented by a curvature-weighted interpolation term and, for SGD, an additional sampling-induced coupling component. Deepens theoretical understanding of how training data shape network predictions.

entry.title: UniSHARP: Universal Sharp Monocular View Synthesis

author.name: Meixi Song, Dizhe Zhang, Hao Ren, Ruiyang Zhang, Bo Du, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Lu Qi

entry.summary: UniSHARP extends photorealistic Gaussian-splatting view synthesis to universal monocular rendering across perspective, wide-FOV, fisheye, and panoramic cameras by aligning images in a unified omnidirectional latent space with ray-based Gaussian primitives and jointly decoded 2D/3D features. Generalizes view synthesis beyond pinhole assumptions.

entry.title: Can activation verbalizers surface an internal chain of thought?

author.name: oakhu

entry.summary: Introduces an evaluation for activation verbalizers—interpretability tools mapping residual-stream activations to natural language—testing whether they can surface a model's single-forward-pass reasoning while solving math problems, finding it possible but unreliable for open-weight natural-language autoencoders. Probes monitoring of opaque internal reasoning.

entry.title: Learn to Match: Two-Sided Matching with Temporally Extended Feedback

author.name: Haijing Zong, Yancheng Liang, Boyang Zhou, Natasha Jaques

entry.summary: This paper introduces a framework for two-sided matching with temporally extended feedback, formulating it as a partially observable Markov game with costly pre-match screening, noisy observations, and evolving latent profiles. Learn2Match is a multi-agent RL benchmark for dynamic matching markets.

entry.title: From Sampled Outcomes to Capability Distributions: Rethinking Supervision for LLM Routing

author.name: Guannan Lai, Haoran Hu, Long Chen, Zhenguo Li, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: DARS rethinks LLM routing supervision by constructing capability labels from a distributional view of stochastic model behavior rather than single noisy responses. It captures both input-side and output-side uncertainty to improve routing reliability.

entry.title: SlimSearcher: Training Efficiency-Aware Web Agents via Adaptive Reward Gating

author.name: Zequn Xie, Junjie Wang, Dan Yang, Jie Feng, Yue Shen, Jian Wang and Jinjie Gu

entry.summary: SlimSearcher is a framework that pushes the accuracy-cost Pareto frontier for deep research web agents across SFT and RL, using Pareto-efficient filtration and adaptive reward gating to reduce redundant tool calls and token consumption. It addresses the efficiency trap of brute-force agent strategies.

entry.title: The Masked Advantage: Uncovering Local-Language Access to Cultural Knowledge in LLMs

author.name: Yang Zhang, Xiao Fei, Amr Mohamed, Sarah Almeida Carneiro, Mersin Konomi, Mingmeng Geng, Ahmed Asaad, Guokan Shang, Michalis Vazirgiannis

entry.summary: Using a controlled framework with item-response-theory ability estimation, the paper studies whether LLMs access local cultural knowledge better in English or the local language, separating language proficiency from language-conditioned knowledge access. Finds nuanced advantages for local-language querying of culture-specific knowledge.

entry.title: What an Autonomous Agent Discovers About Molecular Transformer Design: Does It Transfer?

author.name: Edward Wijaya

entry.summary: An autonomous agent runs over 3,000 architecture-search experiments across molecular (SMILES), protein, and English text sequences to test whether transformers designed for language transfer to molecular data. It finds architecture search is counterproductive for SMILES (tuning learning rates matters more) yet drives most gains for natural language, while discovered innovations transfer across all domains.

entry.title: Human Adults and LLMs as Scientists: Who Benefits from Active Exploration?

author.name: Mandana Samiei, Eunice Yiu, Anthony GX-Chen, Dongyan Lin, Jocelyn Shen, Blake A. Richards, Alison Gopnik, Doina Precup

entry.summary: Compares human adults and LLMs as active scientists in a blicket-detector causal learning task, finding active exploration improves adults' conjunctive causal reasoning that passive observation typically hinders. Investigates who benefits from agency in causal discovery.

entry.title: UnpredictaBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Distributional Randomness in LLMs

author.name: Amirhossein Abaskohi, Amirhossein Dabiriaghdam, Liang Luo, Ellie Dingqiao Wen, Lele Wang, Giuseppe Carenini, Peter West

entry.summary: Introduces UnpredictaBench, a benchmark testing whether LLMs can sample outcomes calibrated to true target distributions rather than collapsing to single plausible answers, covering statistical distributions, stochastic programs, and natural distributions. Motivated by LLMs being used as substitutes for humans in simulations.

entry.title: AEGIS: A Backup Reflex for Physical AI

author.name: Josef Chen

entry.summary: AEGIS uses a lightweight probe on a weak policy's frozen activations to detect high-risk steps in robot manipulation and selectively escalate control to a stronger policy only when needed. On LIBERO-Spatial it recovers more than double the failed trajectories of budget-matched baselines.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Imputation with Graph-Informed Flow Matching

author.name: Zepeng Zhang, Aref Einizade, Jhony H. Giraldo, Olga Fink

entry.summary: GiFlow is a graph-informed flow matching framework for spatiotemporal imputation that replaces the Gaussian prior with a prior built via spatiotemporal filtering of observable signals. This improves efficiency and accuracy over diffusion-based methods for applications like air quality and traffic monitoring.

entry.title: RECAP: Regression Evaluation for Continual Adaptation of Prompts

author.name: Harsh Deshpande, Kushal Chawla, Sangwoo Cho, William Campbell

entry.summary: RECAP is a benchmark measuring continual-learning phenomena (forgetting, regression, forward transfer) for prompt optimization in agentic systems under a strictly proactive adapt-then-test protocol. It targets production scenarios where agents must comply with evolving constraints from the next interaction.

entry.title: PromptPrint: Behavioral Biometrics Through Natural Language Prompting in LLMs

author.name: Shaiv Patel, Kartik Narayan, Vishal Patel

entry.summary: PromptPrint studies whether brief task-driven LLM prompts contain stable author-identifiable signals, using 20,680 real prompts from 1,034 users. It finds lexical representations outperform semantic encoders, supporting a lexical stability hypothesis for prompt-based behavioral biometrics.

entry.title: A Four-Condition Diagnostic Protocol for Evidence Utilization in Long-Context and Retrieval-Augmented Language Models

author.name: Haizhou Xia

entry.summary: This paper proposes a matched four-condition protocol (no evidence, full context, retrieved evidence, oracle reference) to diagnose whether long-context and RAG models actually use provided evidence rather than parametric memory. It introduces ONCU as a protocol-bound estimator of recovered oracle-reference evidence advantage.

entry.title: VideoSEG-O3: A Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reasoning Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Ming Dai, Sen Yang, Boqiang Duan, Boyuan Tong, Jiedong Zhuang, Wankou Yang, and Jingdong Wang

entry.summary: VideoSEG-O3 is a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework for reasoning video object segmentation that emulates coarse-to-fine cognition via temporal-spatial chain-of-thought. It actively acquires visual evidence to resolve complex references in long videos.

entry.title: The Dark Regulome: Disentangling Predictability from Regulation in Genomic Foundation Models

author.name: Chahat Baranwal, Aadtya Baranwal and Lakshya Nitin Tandon

entry.summary: This work introduces a residualization-and-permutation diagnostic to disentangle sequence predictability from genuine regulatory signal in genomic foundation models for glioma research. It tests three architectures across thousands of dark genome elements.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Learning for Long-Horizon Task Planning Under Complex Logical Constraints

author.name: Qiwei Du, Zitong Zhan, Shaoshu Su, Bowen Li, Yi Du, Zhipeng Zhao, Taimeng Fu, Sebastian Scherer, Jiaoyang Li, Chen Wang

entry.summary: This paper formulates object-importance learning for long-horizon robot task planning as an imperative bilevel optimization to address exposure bias from fixed offline supervision. It improves neuro-symbolic planning efficiency under complex logical constraints.

entry.title: ARAPDiffusion: ARAP Regularization for Diffusion-Based Deformable Shape Space Learning

author.name: Haibo Liu, Jinghan Ke, Haitao Yang, Xiangru Huang, Georgios Pavlakos, Qixing Huang

entry.summary: ARAPDiffusion injects as-rigid-as-possible deformation regularization into latent diffusion to learn continuous deformable shape spaces with limited 3D training data. It improves both the encoder/decoder and the diffusion model alternately.

entry.title: DRIFT: From Robustness Gaps to Invariance Manifolds for AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Abhishek Ameta, Sayan Banerjee, Shreyas Pandith, Harshit, Ankita Chatterjee, Akshay Janardan Bankar, Amit Satish Unde

entry.summary: DRIFT formulates AI-generated image detection as learning a structured invariance manifold of real images under one-class supervision, with projection heads decomposing representations into robust and fragile subspaces. It improves over training-free robustness-gap approaches for unseen generators.

entry.title: The Fine-Tuning Trap: Evaluating Negative Transfer and the Role of PEFT in Sub-1B Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Rahul Nair, Chun Tao

entry.summary: This study benchmarks five sub-1B models on math reasoning and finds that full fine-tuning actively harms models under 300M parameters (negative transfer), dropping below zero-shot baselines, making PEFT a stability requirement. LoRA and DoRA perform comparably with task-dependent strengths.

entry.title: Exploring Agentic Tool-Calling Decisions via Uncertainty-Aligned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yijin Zhou, Linqian Zeng, Xiaoya Lu, Wenyuan Xie, Dongrui Liu, Junchi Yan, Jing Shao

entry.summary: TRUST incorporates uncertainty quantification into reward design for LLM agents to improve tool-calling decisions, treating uncertainty as a repulsive force to maintain separation between correct and incorrect actions. It addresses overconfident mistakes in agentic tool use.

entry.title: DaX: Learning General Pathology Representations Across Scales

author.name: Bokai Zhao, Yiyang Zhang, Long Bai, Tai Ma, Hanqing Chao, Minfeng Xu

entry.summary: DaX is a pathology vision foundation model adapting DINOv3-style self-supervised learning to whole-slide histopathology, with continuous magnification training and acquisition-robust augmentations. It aims to produce representations robust across magnification, staining, and scanner variation.

entry.title: DataEvolver: Automatic Data Preparation for Large Language Models through Multi-Level Self-Evolving

author.name: Chao Deng, Shaolei Zhang, Ju Fan, Xiaoyong Du

entry.summary: DataEvolver is a self-evolving data preparation system that automatically constructs pipelines to transform raw data into high-quality training data for LLMs, using a multi-level mechanism for operator selection and pipeline construction. It reduces reliance on costly manual curation.

entry.title: ForensicConcept: Transferable Forensic Concepts for AIGI Detection

author.name: Menyanshu Zhou, Ziyin Zhou, Ke Sun, Yunpeng Luo, Jiayi Ji, Xiaoshuai Sun, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: ForensicConcept extracts explicit, transferable forensic concepts from AI-generated image detectors via attribution and concept codebooks, enabling auditable evidence readouts and cross-backbone transfer. It addresses the black-box nature and poor cross-generator generalization of detectors.

entry.title: Beyond Rubrics: Exploration-Guided Evaluation Skills for Reward Modeling

author.name: Xing Yue, Linjuan Wu, Daoxin Zhang, Yongliang Shen, Weiming Lu

entry.summary: Eval-Skill synthesizes reusable domain-level evaluation skills for reward modeling through workflow and principle generation, reframing reward guidance as context evolution rather than per-query rubric generation. It uses only 100 cases per domain to reduce inference overhead.

entry.title: LARA: Latent Action Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Mengya Liu, Baoxiong Jia, Jiangyong Huang, Jingze Zhang, Siyuan Huang

entry.summary: LARA is a plug-and-play framework that jointly optimizes latent action models and vision-language-action models via representation alignment, addressing the disconnect when they are trained separately. It enables grounding latent actions during VLA training while leveraging unlabeled human videos.

entry.title: OffQ: Taming Structured Outliers in LLM Quantization by Offsetting

author.name: Haoqi Wang, Lorenz K. Mueller, Jiawei Zhuang, Mathieu Salzmann, Lukas Cavigelli

entry.summary: OffQ mitigates activation outliers in low-bit LLM quantization through an offsetting mechanism that identifies a low-dimensional outlier subspace via top-1 PCA, concentrates outliers into one channel via rotation, and absorbs it as a shared offset. This reduces activation standard deviation for better quantization.

entry.title: Learning Explicit Behavioral Models with Adaptive Questions and World-Model Probes

author.name: Hikaru Shindo, Yu Deng, Teng Cao, Quentin Delfosse, Christopher Tauchmann, Jannis Bl\"uml, Gopika Sudhakaran, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Explicit Symbolic Behavioral Model, a trainable model coupling task performance with evidence-grounded question answering and executable mechanism prediction using typed predicates, weighted rules, and mechanism memory. It addresses brittle agents that score well without representing why actions succeed.

entry.title: Explicit Evidence Grounding via Structured Inline Citation Generation

author.name: Anar Yeginbergen, Amelie W\"uhrl, Anna Rogers, Rodrigo Agerri

entry.summary: FullCite generates structured inline citations linking each claim to both its source document and supporting evidence span, using prompt-based generation, constrained decoding over a citation grammar, and posthoc span alignment. It is evaluated on ASQA, BioASQ, and ExpertQA for citation quality and faithfulness.

entry.title: From Correctness to Utility: Gain-Based Prefix Evaluation for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yuhang Zhou, Yixin Cao, Guangnan Ye

entry.summary: This work introduces the Prefix Utility Model (PUM), which evaluates LLM reasoning prefixes by their causal solve-rate improvement (prefix gain) rather than local step correctness, trained with pairwise ranking. PUM improves Best-of-N, beam search, and RL on mathematical reasoning. The outcome-grounded utility framing is a meaningful shift for process reward models.

entry.title: The Proxy Benders Decomposition

author.name: Changkun Guan, El Mehdi Er Raqabi, Mathieu Tanneau, Pascal Van Hentenryck

entry.summary: Proxy-BD replaces repeated exact Benders subproblem solves with certified optimization proxies via a self-supervised predict-project-and-complete mechanism producing dual-feasible solutions. Aims to accelerate large-scale mixed-integer optimization by exploiting subproblem repetitiveness.

entry.title: DisPOSE: Projected Polystochastic Diffusion for Self-Supervised Multi-View 3D Human Pose Estimation

author.name: Tony Danjun Wang, Tolga Birdal, Nassir Navab

entry.summary: DisPOSE casts the discrete multi-view person-assignment problem in multi-person 3D pose estimation as a generative diffusion over polystochastic tensors with differentiable Sinkhorn projections, regressing skeletons via hypergraph convolution from 2D priors. Self-supervised approach reducing reliance on synthetic 3D pose catalogues.

entry.title: Skill-3D: Evolving Scene-Aware Skills for Agentic 3D Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Haoyuan Li, Zhengdong Hu, Jun Wang, Hehe Fan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Skill-3D enables MLLM agents to perform 3D spatial reasoning via self-evolving scene-aware skills stored in a Scene Memory, where successful tool-use trajectories from similar scenes are distilled into reusable skills, addressing biased and uniform tool use. Improves agentic 3D reasoning over non-agentic baselines.

entry.title: Network Recovery from Cascade Data: A Debiased Jacobian-Based Machine Learning Approach

author.name: Lei Huang

entry.summary: CascadeNet recovers hidden influence networks from cascade data without assuming a diffusion model, characterizing the influence structure via the Jacobian of the one-step transition function and applying Neyman-orthogonal debiasing via the Riesz representer. Robust network recovery across diffusion mechanisms.

entry.title: How reliable are LLMs when it comes to playing dice?

author.name: Luca Avena, Gianmarco Bet, Bernardo Busoni

entry.summary: Benchmarks probabilistic reasoning in 8 LLMs on standard versus counterintuitive discrete probability problems, finding 0.96 accuracy on standard but only 0.59 on counterintuitive ones, with over 20% drops from disguised formulations (token bias) and up to 34% drops when misleading hints are embedded. Reveals fragility and heuristic susceptibility in LLM probabilistic reasoning.

entry.title: Theory of learning of high-dimensional controlled non-linear dynamical systems (I): models and methods

author.name: Pierfrancesco Urbani

entry.summary: Part one of a theory of learning for high-dimensional controlled nonlinear dynamical systems via neural ODEs, presenting models and methods that exploit the dual inference and training dynamics to study training and generalization. Offers a unifying theoretical framework spanning many learning settings.

entry.title: FAIR-Calib: Frontier-Aware Instability-Reweighted Calibration for Post-Training Quantization of Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Haoyu Huang, Linlin Yang, Sheng Xu, Boyu Liu, Guodong Guo, Zhongqian Fu, Hang Zhou, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes FAIR-Calib, a two-stage post-training quantization framework for diffusion LLMs that protects fragile early token decisions at the write frontier by estimating a position prior and performing instability-reweighted layer-wise calibration. Addresses how quantization error flips and permanently locks in borderline decisions in dLLMs.

entry.title: HKJudge: A Legal Discourse-Annotated Corpus for Interpreting What Courts Find, How They Reason, and What They Rule

author.name: Xi Xuan, Wenxin Zhang, Yufei Zhou, King-kui Sin, Chunyu Kit

entry.summary: HKJudge is the first sentence-level expert-annotated legal discourse corpus for Hong Kong criminal judgments, with ~290k sentences labeled across 26 rhetorical roles and sentencing element spans. It supports interpreting what courts find, how they reason, and what they rule.

entry.title: Towards Serverless Semi-Decentralized Federated Learning with Heterogeneous Optimizers

author.name: Su Wang, Mung Chiang, H. Vincent Poor

entry.summary: SSD-FL proposes serverless semi-decentralized federated learning with heterogeneous optimizers, addressing cluster formation in fully decentralized settings without persistent server infrastructure. It uses a one-time device-to-device initialization phase coupling network structure, data heterogeneity, and optimizer diversity.

entry.title: STRIPS-WM: Learning Grounded Propositional STRIPS-style World Models from Images

author.name: Abhiroop Ajith and Constantinos Chamzas

entry.summary: STRIPS-WM learns grounded propositional STRIPS-style symbolic world models from raw image transitions for long-horizon robot manipulation planning. It bridges classical symbolic planning with learning from visual experience.

entry.title: Translate-R1: Cost-Aware Translation Tool Use via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Pratik Jayarao, Chaitanya Dwivedi, Himanshu Gupta, Neeraj Varshney, Adithya M Devraj, Meet Vadera, Priyanka Nigam, Bing Yin

entry.summary: Translate-R1 learns a single RL policy that decides when to invoke translation to the model's dominant language, balancing cost against the multilingual performance gap. It avoids manual heuristics and routers by learning from reward alone.

entry.title: SpectCount: Spectrotemporal Counting via Synthetic Signals Improves Large Audio Language Models

author.name: Seonuk Kim, Yonghyeon Jun, Ju Yeon Kang, Jimin Hong, Yoonhyeong Lee, Nam Soo Kim

entry.summary: SpectCount improves large audio language models via data-efficient fine-tuning on fully synthetic on-the-fly audio signals targeting spectrotemporal perceptual weaknesses. It improves performance across sound, music, and speech benchmarks unseen during fine-tuning.

entry.title: T-GMP: Terrain-conditioned Generative Motion Priors for Versatile and Natural Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Junhong Guo, Hao Hu, Chen Chen, Haoxuan Han, Linao Gong, Xin Yang, Zhicheng He, Yao Su, Fenghua He

entry.summary: T-GMP learns terrain-conditioned generative motion priors via a conditional VAE from few expert state-terrain demonstrations for humanoid locomotion. Integrated into an adversarial RL pipeline with a Foothold Penalty, it enables natural and robust terrain-adaptive locomotion.

entry.title: Auditing Training Data in Domain-adapted LLMs: LoRA-MINT

author.name: Gonzalo Mancera, Daniel DeAlcala, Aythami Morales, Julian Fierrez, Ruben Tolosana, Francisco Jurado

entry.summary: LoRA-MINT is a membership inference test for LLMs fine-tuned with LoRA, using model perplexity to determine whether individual samples were in the adaptation training data. It achieves precision of 0.77 to 0.92 across four models and three datasets, providing a data-auditing tool.

entry.title: Don't Pause: Streaming Video-Language Synchrony for Online Video Understanding

author.name: Zhenyu Yang, Kairui Zhang, Shengsheng Qian, Weiming Dong, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: LyraV introduces Streaming Video-Language Synchrony for online video understanding, with a frame-driven transition controller that avoids pausing video perception while generating responses. It addresses real-time stutters in streaming video-LLM interaction.

entry.title: StainFlow: Entity-Stain Tracking and Evidence Linking for Process Rewards in GUI Agents

author.name: Haojie Hao, Longkun Hao, Yihang Lou, Yan Bai, Zhenyang Li, Zhichao Yang, Dongshuo Huang, Hongyu Lin, Lanqing Hong, Jiakai Wang, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: StainFlow introduces entity-stain tracking and evidence linking to provide process rewards for GUI agents, addressing sparse trajectory-level feedback in long-horizon RL. It aims to improve credit assignment by accommodating multiple valid execution paths and capturing long-range evidence.

entry.title: STREAM: Stochastic Riemannian Flow Matching with Anisotropic Decoder for Digital Histopathology Image Generation

author.name: Won June Cho, Daeky Jeong, Hyeongyeol Lim, Hongjun Yoon

entry.summary: STREAM is a stochastic Riemannian flow matching framework with an anisotropic decoder for histopathology image generation that uses pretrained pathology foundation models as the latent space itself to avoid conditioning collapse. It targets high-quality, diverse synthetic pathology images.

entry.title: Predictive Style Matching: Natural and Robust Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Simeon Nedelchev, Ekaterina Chaikovskaia, Egor Davydenko, Eduard Zaliaev, and Roman Gorbachev

entry.summary: Predictive Style Matching improves humanoid locomotion naturalness by using an offline predictor that maps lower-body state history and velocity commands to interpretable upper-body and gait targets that shape RL rewards. State-conditioned targets avoid the disturbance sensitivity of time-indexed motion imitation.

entry.title: Dreaming when Necessary: Advancing World Action Models with Adaptive Multi-Modal Reasoning

author.name: Yinzhou Tang, Jingbo Xu, Yu Shang, Zihao Song, Chen Gao, Wei Wu, Yong Li

entry.summary: AdaWAM is a world action model with adaptive multimodal reasoning that uses a lightweight dynamic router to trigger textual reasoning during task transitions and visual reasoning during fine-grained manipulation. It addresses the limitations of video-prediction-only action priors on long-horizon embodied tasks.

entry.title: Native3D: End-to-End 3D Scene Generation via Unified Mesh-Texture Modeling and Semantic Alignment

author.name: Yibo Liu, Ziwei Zhang, Haozhou Pang, Menghao Li, Lanshan He, Gan Qi

entry.summary: Native3D is an end-to-end 3D scene generation framework that bypasses 2D intermediate representations using a unified mesh-texture joint representation with a transformer scene encoder and a 3D Representation Alignment Loss. It avoids domain adaptation issues like geometric distortion and texture degradation.

entry.title: QuadVerse: An Integrated Framework Aligning Visual-Physical Reality for Quadruped Simulation

author.name: Yuxiang Chen, Yuanhao Wang, Ziheng Zhang, Meng Zhang, Yu Liu, Yufei Jia, Tiancai Wang, Erjin Zhou, and Jin Xie

entry.summary: QuadVerse is an integrated quadruped simulation framework that uses reconstructed 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes as a calibration substrate to jointly align visual perception, physical interaction, and actuator dynamics. It addresses how visual and dynamic sim-to-real gaps accumulate together.

entry.title: Closed-Form Spectral Regularization for Multi-Task Model Merging

author.name: Yongxian Wei, Runxi Cheng, Xingxuan Zhang, Li Shen, Chun Yuan, Peng Cui, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: This paper explains why iterative gradient descent outperforms the exact closed-form pseudoinverse solution in multi-task model merging, showing the iterative solver acts as an implicit spectral regularizer for an ill-posed normal equation rather than as an optimizer. It then proposes a closed-form spectral regularization that captures this benefit. The mechanistic explanation plus efficient closed-form solution is a strong combination.

entry.title: SWE-Explore: Benchmarking How Coding Agents Explore Repositories

author.name: Shaoqiu Zhang, Yuhang Wang, Jialiang Liang, Yuling Shi, Wenhao Zeng, Maoquan Wang, Shilin He, Ningyuan Xu, Siyu Ye, Kai Cai, Xiaodong Gu

entry.summary: SWE-Explore is a benchmark isolating the repository-exploration capability of coding agents, asking explorers to return ranked relevant code regions under a fixed line budget across 848 issues, 10 languages, and 203 repositories with line-level ground truth. It complements holistic resolved/unresolved benchmarks like SWE-bench by evaluating fine-grained subskills. The decomposed evaluation is valuable for diagnosing agent capabilities.

entry.title: Mind the Gap: Disentangling Performance Bottlenecks in Video Instance Segmentation

author.name: Danial Hamdi, Fardin Ayar, Mahdi Javanmardi

entry.summary: Introduces an ILP-based oracle diagnostic framework that disentangles classification, segmentation, and tracking error sources in video instance segmentation, applied across seven methods and multiple datasets. Reveals tracking instability as the dominant bottleneck for online methods under occlusion.

entry.title: Drifting Models for Surrogate Flow Modeling

author.name: Chris R. Jung, Markus D\"orr, Natalie J\"ungling, Jennifer Niessner, Adam T. M\"uller, Nicolaj C. Stache

entry.summary: Adapts a generative drifting framework to fluid mechanics, performing conditional drifting in a learned VAE latent space with label-aware masking to align outputs with boundary conditions, matching iterative diffusion accuracy at roughly 100x faster single-pass CFD surrogate generation. Enables rapid indoor-flow design exploration.

entry.title: Sparse Subspace-to-Expert Sharing for Task-Agnostic Continual Learning

author.name: Fatema Siddika, Md Anwar Hossen, Tanwi Mallick, Ali Jannesari

entry.summary: SETA addresses the plasticity-stability dilemma in continual learning for LLMs via adaptive sparse subspace decomposition into task-specific and shared experts, isolating task knowledge to prevent catastrophic forgetting while sharing common capabilities. Targets task-agnostic continual learning.

entry.title: P-Cast Precision in FP8 Attention: Sink-Induced Collapse and the Optimality of S=2^8

author.name: Reed Lau

entry.summary: Analyzes FP8 precision challenges in attention computation, showing forward KV iteration causes P-collapse where probability values underflow under the attention sink phenomenon, while reverse iteration plus an optimal scaling factor of 256 eliminates it.
