entry.title: DirectAudioEdit: Inversion-Free Text-Guided Audio Editing via Diffusion Prediction Contrast

author.name: Zhengkun Ge, Xiaoqian Liu, Haoran Zhang, Yuan Ge, Junxiang Zhang, Zhengtao Yu, Jingbo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: DirectAudioEdit is the first training-free and inversion-free method for text-guided audio editing, constructing a source-to-target editing path through diffusion denoising dynamics via prediction contrast. It reduces FAD and KL by about 16% versus DDPM inversion while cutting computational overhead. The inversion-free approach addresses an underexplored area for audio.

entry.title: A robust PPG foundation model using multimodal physiological supervision

author.name: Eloy Geenjaar, Vince Calhoun, Scott Daly, Gouthaman KV, Lie Lu, Trisha Mittal, Daniel P. Darcy

entry.summary: This work proposes a PPG foundation model that avoids requiring high-quality or field-like pretraining data by leveraging accompanying ECG and respiratory signals in ICU datasets to select contrastive samples, allowing it to learn from noisy PPG segments and improve inference robustness. It is pretrained on 3x fewer subjects than state-of-the-art. The multimodal physiological supervision for robustness is the key idea.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Deep Unfolding for Blind Cross-Sensor Spectral Super-Resolution via Learning the Spectral Transformation Function

author.name: Zhaolin Li, Jinsong Chen, Shanxin Guo, Tuo Zhang, Xinglong Zhang, Pan Chen

entry.summary: Proposes PGU-Net, a physics-guided deep unfolding network for blind cross-sensor spectral super-resolution that jointly estimates hyperspectral images and a learnable spectral transformation function. It addresses the ill-posed case where spectral degradation is unknown across heterogeneous UAV sensors.

entry.title: Ablation Study of Block Size, Weight Precision, and Scale Precision in NVFP4 Inference for Low-Power Edge-Efficient Neural Networks

author.name: Ovishake Sen, Venkata Nithin Kamineni, Daniel Lobo, Swarup Bhunia, Rickard Ewetz, and Baibhab Chatterjee

entry.summary: Conducts an ablation study of block size, weight precision, and scale precision in NVFP4 LUT-based inference for low-power edge neural networks, combining 4-bit activations, two-level scaling, LUT mantissa computation, and selective ECC. Identifies block size 16 as a practical accuracy-storage trade-off.

entry.title: Synthics: Synthetic Physics-like Datasets for Machine Learning

author.name: Jari Veps\"al\"ainen

entry.summary: Synthics generates synthetic regression datasets that structurally resemble physics equations from a given corpus, using a Bayesian Probabilistic Context-Free Grammar to capture algebraic structure and sampling novel equations. It characterizes physically meaningful applicability domains via non-intrusive probing.

entry.title: Empirical Transfer Operators and Finite-Sample Change Detection for Noisy Expanding Interval Maps

author.name: Aparna Rajput

entry.summary: This paper studies finite-sample change detection in noisy one-dimensional dynamical systems using partition-based empirical transfer operators with Doeblin-type regularization to ensure a unique stationary distribution. It defines an L1 change score between baseline and sliding-window stationary distributions.

entry.title: Physics-Driven Semantic Scattering Structure Understanding of Aircraft Target in SAR Images

author.name: Yifei Yin, Xiaogang Yu, Hao Shi, Liang Chen, Wei Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes Semantic Scattering Structure Understanding as a new paradigm for interpreting aircraft targets in SAR images, moving beyond unstable local scattering center representations. It aims to reconstruct complete topological structure using physics-grounded cues.

entry.title: Mission-Level Runtime Assurance Framework for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Chieh Tsai and Salim Hariri

entry.summary: This paper presents a mission-level runtime assurance framework for autonomous driving that evaluates both immediate safety and mission completability before executing high-level commands. It extends highway-env with mission-level fault scenarios and a runtime monitor.

entry.title: Hierarchical Forecast Reconciliation for Urban Rail Transit Demand Prediction under Operational Disruptions

author.name: Dang Viet Anh Nguyen, Alma Fazlagic, Kristine Pryds Loft, Filipe Rodrigues

entry.summary: This paper presents the first hierarchical forecast reconciliation framework for joint station-level and origin-destination urban rail demand prediction, using a neural reconciler to enforce conservation constraints. It targets coherent forecasts especially during operational disruptions.

entry.title: Bias in Filter Feature Selection Evaluation: A Meta-Analysis of Datasets, Baselines, and Experimental Design Choices

author.name: Malick Ebiele, Malika Bendechache, Rob Brennan

entry.summary: This meta-analysis examines bias in filter feature selection evaluation across datasets, baselines, and experimental design choices, identifying factors that could introduce conscious or unconscious bias. It recommends strategies for fairer evaluation.

entry.title: OPTIMUS-Prime: Minimal and Sufficient Concept Explanations for Deep Vision Models

author.name: Arthur Hoarau, Chenrui Zhu, Vu Linh Nguyen

entry.summary: OPTIMUS generates concept-based visual heatmap explanations for deep vision classifiers grounded in prime-implicant theory, providing formal guarantees absent from typical saliency methods. It seeks minimal and sufficient concept explanations bridging interpretability and rigor. The formal grounding distinguishes it from heuristic XAI.

entry.title: The Capacity of Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation in Federated Learning

author.name: Lanxin Yi, Jinbao Zhu, Kai Wan, and Xiaohu Tang

entry.summary: This information-theory paper studies T-colluding secure aggregation in federated learning under a general two-phase framework including the often-ignored communication cost of distributing correlated keys via user-to-user communication. It characterizes fundamental limits under arbitrary key-distribution mechanisms. The work establishes new capacity results for a practical privacy primitive.

entry.title: Semantic-Structural Alignment for Generative Pictorial Charts

author.name: Zhida Sun, Yulin Zhang, Zheng Gu, Min Lu, Bongshin Lee, Daniel Cohen-Or, Hui Huang

entry.summary: Introduces a generative framework for automated pictorial chart synthesis that balances semantic expressiveness with structural faithfulness via dual-conditioned generation using a multimodal diffusion transformer. It adds structural alignment and semantic mechanisms for data-faithful yet engaging charts.

entry.title: Attention Consistent Longitudinal Medical Visual Question Answering Guided by Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Jialin Wu, Qianru Zhang, Georges El Fakhri, Xiaofeng Liu

entry.summary: Proposes an attention-guided encoder-decoder for longitudinal medical visual question answering on chest X-rays, using a lightweight affine registration module to align current and reference images plus DINO-based and adaptive mask generators. Improves reasoning about anatomical changes across time points.

entry.title: Adaptive Band Selection for Hyperspectral Classification with Spatially Disjoint Evaluation

author.name: Ikram El-Hajri (1), Ouassim Karrakchou (1), and Alejandro Mousist (2) ((1) International University of Rabat, Rabat, Morocco, (2) Thales Alenia Space, Spain)

entry.summary: SGBR-HC is a two-stage hyperspectral band selection method that uses supervised spectral ranking to initialize trainable sparse gates, letting the number of selected bands emerge from training. It addresses initialization sensitivity and rigid prescribed band counts under spatially disjoint evaluation.

entry.title: Modeling Nonlinear Feature Interactions with Product-Unit Residual Networks

author.name: Ziyuan Li, Uwe Jaekel, Babette Dellen

entry.summary: This work studies product-unit residual networks (PURe) that explicitly model multiplicative cross-feature interactions with residual connections. It evaluates accuracy, noise robustness, and interpretability on synthetic and real datasets.

entry.title: An Expanded Synthetic Conversation Dataset for Multi-Turn Smishing Detection

author.name: Carl Lochstampfor, Ayan Roy

entry.summary: COVA-X expands a synthetic multi-turn smishing detection dataset to nearly 11,000 conversations across eight elder-targeted scam categories with an improved generation pipeline. Retraining shows Longformer now surpasses prior baselines, reversing earlier transformer underperformance.

entry.title: Extending Responsibility-Sensitive Safety for the Assessment of Offloaded Autonomous Driving Services

author.name: Robin Dehler, Aryan Thakur, and Michael Buchholz

entry.summary: This paper extends Responsibility-Sensitive Safety to account for variable response times of offloaded autonomous driving services over V2X communication, which affect reaction time and safety guarantees. It integrates the extension into function offloading decisions.

entry.title: Detecting Temporally Localized Manipulations in Authentic Video Streams

author.name: Okan Umur and Ali Emre G\"u\c{s}l\"u and Ibrahim Delibasoglu

entry.summary: This paper reviews existing datasets and motivates a new dataset for detecting short, highly realistic manipulated segments inserted into otherwise authentic videos, a scenario underrepresented in current deepfake and inpainting datasets. It targets temporally localized manipulation detection.

entry.title: No-Harm Physics-Informed Inverse Learning with Residual-Calibrated Uncertainty

author.name: Ronald Katende

entry.summary: This paper develops a no-harm certification framework for physics-informed inverse learning, accepting a learned reconstruction only when its residual-calibrated error radius does not exceed a baseline. It combines data, physics, and boundary residuals into a posteriori error bounds under conditional stability. The work brings rigor and safety guarantees to PINN-based inverse problems.

entry.title: RETROSPECT: RETROsynthesis via Sequential Prediction, and Chemically Transformed-ranking

author.name: Raja Sekhar Pappala, Shreyas Vinaya Sathyanarayana, Ronit Kumar Choudhary, Arjun Verma, Deepak Warrier

entry.summary: RETROSPECT decomposes single-step retrosynthesis into a Transformer proposal model (ChemAlign) plus a LambdaMART reranker using structural, template, and DFT-derived descriptors. It reaches 55% top-1 and 86% top-10 accuracy on USPTO-50K with high validity. The proposal-selection decomposition with reranking yields competitive chemistry results.

entry.title: AI Sovereignty: A Qualitative Model of Strategic Competition as AI Becomes an Instrument of National Power

author.name: Timothy Clancy, Asmeret Naugle

entry.summary: This paper defines AI sovereignty (a nation's independent control over its AI technologies) and presents a qualitative model incorporating micro, meso, and macro contributors to strategic competition as AI becomes an instrument of national power. It offers model-based forecasts of competitive dynamics and national power. The work fills a conceptual gap in AI geopolitics.

entry.title: Phun-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Phonological Understanding in Chinese

author.name: Xing Yue, Yongliang Shen, Weiming Lu

entry.summary: Phun-Bench is a purpose-built Chinese benchmark for evaluating LLM phonological understanding across homophony, rhyme, and phonetic similarity, designed to avoid rote-memorization shortcuts. Results show LLMs recall pronunciations well but struggle to leverage phonological knowledge for reasoning. The benchmark targets a neglected sound dimension of language.

entry.title: CARVE-Q: Quantum-Proposed, Classically Certified Interactive Driving Repair

author.name: Yifan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces CARVE, a certificate architecture for prediction-free interactive driving repair that, after a safety veto, constructs a finite repair lattice and emits an auditable certificate encoding binding rules, right-of-way, cost allocation, and fallback. Aims to provide provable, responsibility-bounded repairs of blocked maneuvers.

entry.title: Geometric Second-Order Feature Correlation Learning for Self-Supervised Speech Emotion Recognition

author.name: Shuanglin Li, Ruxiao Qian, and Siyang Song

entry.summary: Proposes a Second-Order Correlation layer for self-supervised speech emotion recognition that models feature covariance descriptors on a Riemannian manifold to capture higher-order co-occurrence patterns beyond first-order aggregation. Aims to better exploit the representational power of SSL backbones.

entry.title: CAF-Gen: A Multi-Agent System for Enriching Argumentation Structures

author.name: Jakub B\k{a}ba and Jaros{\l}aw Chudziak

entry.summary: CAF-Gen is a multi-agent LLM framework that enriches shallow argument structures into models compliant with the Carneades Argumentation Framework, capturing premise types, proof standards, and argument schemes. It uses an iterative Creator-Reviewer pipeline to formalize complex reasoning from text.

entry.title: Terastal: Layer-Variant-based Scheduling for Real-Time Multi-DNN Workloads on Heterogeneous Accelerators

author.name: Sing-Yao Wu, Fengshuo Song, Eli Bozorgzadeh

entry.summary: Terastal is a scheduling framework for real-time multi-DNN workloads on heterogeneous accelerators that introduces layer variants to reduce latency gaps and deadline misses. It combines offline budget assignment with online scheduling.

entry.title: Product units in gated recurrent units improve nuclear-mass prediction

author.name: Ziyuan Li, Paulo S.A. Freitas, John W. Clark, Babette Dellen

entry.summary: This paper integrates product units and complex-valued computation into gated recurrent units to improve nuclear-mass prediction from atomic mass evaluation data. It reports significant gains in interpolation and extrapolation tasks.

entry.title: Didact: A Cross-Domain Capability Discovery System for Defence

author.name: Aarya Bodhankar, Aditya Joshi, Bao Gia Doan, Thomas Marchant, Oscar Leslie, Flora Salim

entry.summary: Didact is a prototype cross-domain capability discovery system for defence that integrates public reports and policy documents with a research-publication knowledge graph via a composite RAG pipeline. It provides natural-language workflows with an interactive evidence visualization rail.

entry.title: From Vision to Text: A Compact Multimodal Approach for Robust, Cross-Domain Presentation Attack Detection on ID Cards

author.name: Qingwen Zeng, Juan E. Tapia, Sneha Das and Christoph Busch

entry.summary: This paper proposes a compact multimodal model combining visual and textual data for presentation attack detection on ID cards, addressing cross-domain robustness under privacy-constrained data scarcity. It finds that while supervised fine-tuning yields strong generalization, zero-shot fails, and argues synthetic datasets poorly reflect real-world challenges.

entry.title: Meaning in Order, Order in Meaning: Semantic R-precision for Keyphrase Evaluation

author.name: Shamira Venturini, Steffen Kinkel

entry.summary: Semantic R-Precision is a new keyphrase evaluation metric that integrates semantic similarity into the rank-aware R-Precision framework, rewarding semantically relevant keyphrases appearing early in output. It addresses misalignment of exact-match and rank-agnostic metrics with human judgment.

entry.title: Decision-Aware Evaluation of Physics-Informed Surrogates

author.name: Daniel Cie\'slak and Andrzej Czy\.zewski

entry.summary: This paper argues physics-informed surrogate models should be evaluated by downstream decision quality (ranking, feasibility, regret) rather than curve error, and introduces pinn-gym, an open benchmark for material-conditioned lattice design. It shows low nRMSE often fails to identify useful design selections. The decision-aware evaluation framing is a thoughtful methodological contribution.

entry.title: Textual Supervision Enhances Geospatial Representations in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Marcelo Sartori Locatelli, Fernando Tonucci, Jea Kwon, Luiz Felipe Vecchietti, Bryan Nathanael Wijaya, Cheng Yaw Low, Virgilio Almeida, Meeyoung Cha

entry.summary: This study analyzes geospatial representations across vision-only, vision-language, and multimodal foundation models, finding systematic gaps in spatial accuracy and showing textual supervision enhances geospatial learning. It evaluates across image clusters grouped by localizability. The finding that language complements spatial encoding is an interesting representational insight.

entry.title: Seeing Without Exposing: Adaptive Privacy Control for Open-World, Context-Hungry MLLMs

author.name: Siyuan Xu, Yibing Liu, Peilin Chen, Yung-Hui Li, Shiqi Wang, Sam Kwong

entry.summary: Anchored Privacy Drifting (APD) is a training-free method that shifts privacy-sensitive elements in MLLM inputs toward semantically equivalent alternatives while anchoring contextual cues, balancing protection and context preservation. It introduces the AdaptShield benchmark for this dual objective. The approach moves beyond fixed obfuscation categories for open-world inputs.

entry.title: Beyond Backscatter: InSAR coherence from detected SAR images

author.name: Francescopaolo Sica, Andrea Pulella, Michael Schmitt

entry.summary: Proposes a Residual U-Net to regress InSAR coherence directly from detected SAR images without precise coregistration, trained on Sentinel-1 SLC-derived coherence maps. It generalizes across geographies and improves over intensity-based methods, lowering barriers to coherence estimation.

entry.title: Trading Engagement for Sustainability: Carbon-Aware Re-ranking for E-commerce Recommendations

author.name: Noah Lund Syrdal, Anders Vestrum, Jorgen Bergh

entry.summary: Studies carbon-aware product recommendation when carbon footprint labels are mostly missing, using retrieval-augmented LLM-based estimation to infer footprints then re-ranking recommendations for sustainability. Examines the engagement-versus-sustainability trade-off.

entry.title: ErA: Error-Aware Deep Unrolling Network for Single Image Defocus Deblurring

author.name: Tu Vo, Chan Y. Park

entry.summary: Introduces ErA, an error-aware deep unrolling network for single-image defocus deblurring that jointly learns a compact kernel basis and per-pixel weights with an error-correction term in augmented Lagrangian unrolling. Reports SOTA PSNR/SSIM and strong generalization across multiple datasets.

entry.title: S23DR 2026 Winning Solution

author.name: Jan Skvrna, Miroslav Purkrabek, Lukas Neumann

entry.summary: This short paper describes the winning solution to the S23DR 2026 challenge for structured 3D wireframe reconstruction, denoising vertex tokens with a flow-matching DiT conditioned on Perceiver-style scene tokens. A coarse-to-fine two-pass approach with multi-sample consensus achieved first place.

entry.title: MVSegNet: A Lightweight Boundary-Aware Network for Fetal Lateral Ventricle Segmentation and Atrial Width Estimation in Prenatal Ultrasound

author.name: Arafat Hossain Sayem

entry.summary: MVSegNet is a lightweight boundary-aware encoder-decoder network for fetal lateral ventricle segmentation and atrial width estimation in prenatal ultrasound. With 2.31M parameters it achieves 80.79% Dice and 3.40mm atrial-width error against six baselines.

entry.title: Phonetic Error Analysis of Raw Waveform Acoustic Models

author.name: Erfan Loweimi, Zhengjun Yue, Andrea Carmantini, Zoran Cvetkovic, Steve Renals, Peter Bell

entry.summary: This paper analyzes phonetic error patterns of raw waveform acoustic models on TIMIT phone recognition, decomposing errors across phonetic classes and constructing confusion matrices. It reports best-in-class raw waveform PER and shows transfer learning benefits consonants more than vowels.

entry.title: Geodesics of Dynamic Graphs for Regime Change Detection

author.name: William Cappelletti, \'Etienne Voutaz, and Pascal Frossard

entry.summary: This paper redefines regime change detection in dynamic graphs as drifts from geodesics in graph space, capturing continuous evolution rather than abrupt transitions. It uses graph regression to measure cumulative deviation from estimated trajectories. The geometric perspective offers a principled alternative to classical change-point methods.

entry.title: When Recovery Matters: The Blind Spot of Surrogate Privacy in MLLM Editing

author.name: Siyuan Xu, Yibing Liu, Peilin Chen, Yung-Hui LI, Shiqi Wang, Sam Kwong

entry.summary: This work identifies a blind spot in surrogate-based privacy editing for MLLMs: outputs are often edited surrogates rather than recovered edited source images. It introduces SPPE, a recovery-oriented benchmark with 36 privacy categories and 65 editing instructions plus editability and recovery tasks. The recovery-focused framing addresses a practical privacy-utility gap.

entry.title: Structure-Preserving Correction Learning for Sparse Bayesian Inference in Brain Source Imaging

author.name: Marco Morik, Xiao Ruiting, Shinichi Nakajima, Stefan Haufe, Ismail Huseynov

entry.summary: This work unfolds a classical sparse Type-II Bayesian solver for M/EEG brain source imaging into a trainable neural architecture whose layers mirror the original iterations, initialized to recover the classical solver exactly. It then adds progressively expressive correction-learning mechanisms while preserving Bayesian structure. The structure-preserving algorithm-unrolling is a principled hybrid.

entry.title: HKVM-RAG: Key-Value-Separated Hypergraph Evidence Organization for Multi-Hop RAG

author.name: Mingyu Zhang and Ying Ma

entry.summary: HKVM-RAG is a key-value-separated evidence-organization layer for multi-hop RAG that assembles answer-path hyperedges from cached passage-level LLM evidence tuples as retrieval keys while keeping passage text as values. A fixed-substrate protocol isolates key-space design across graph and hypergraph variants. The hypergraph evidence organization addresses multi-hop evidence fragmentation.

entry.title: A Temporal Spatial Minimax Rate for Smoothly-Varying Distributions in Wasserstein Space

author.name: Munsik Kim

entry.summary: This statistics paper derives a unified temporal-spatial minimax rate for forecasting a future distribution along a smoothly-varying curve in 2-Wasserstein space from noisy past snapshots, under adiabatic bounds on velocity-field derivatives. It establishes matching lower bounds via a temporal-to-spatial reduction. The work provides foundational theory for distributional forecasting in optimal-transport spaces.

entry.title: Supervision versus Demonstration-Based In-Context Learning for Multiword Expression Classification

author.name: Sercan Karaka\c{s} and Yusuf \c{S}im\c{s}ek

entry.summary: Compares a supervised Turkish encoder (BERTurk) against instruction-tuned LLMs under zero/one/few-shot prompting for detecting idiomatic Turkish light verb constructions versus literal combinations on a controlled set, analyzing how demonstrations shift error profiles. Probes in-context learning for a hard multiword-expression task.

entry.title: USU-Corn-WeedDB: A UAV RGB Image Dataset for Multi-Species Weed Detection in Forage Corn

author.name: Utsav Bhandari, Saroj Burlakoti, Rhonda Miller, Sierra Young, Eric Westra, Aaron Etienne

entry.summary: USU-Corn-WeedDB is a publicly available UAV RGB image dataset for multi-species weed detection in forage corn, with 8,800 tiled patches at high ground sampling resolution. It supports supervised and semi-supervised site-specific weed management to mitigate yield losses.

entry.title: Evidence-Based Intelligent Diagnostic and Therapeutic Visualization System with Large Language Models: Multi-Turn Interaction and Multimodal Treatment Plan Generation

author.name: Yunhan Wang, Yuda Wang, Zhiying Tu, Mingqiang Song, Li Song, Kun Li, Dianhui Chu, and Bolin Zhang

entry.summary: This system builds a knowledge-graph-enhanced visual diagnostic tool for traditional Chinese medicine with multi-turn interaction, proactive questioning, and multimodal treatment plan generation. It uses a Neo4j graph and LLM verification to improve transparency.

entry.title: A Causal Probabilistic Framework for Perception-Informed Closed-Loop Simulation of Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhennan Fei, Rickard Johansson, Mikael Andersson, Matthias Eng, Mattias Eriksson, Kaveh Kianfar, Sadegh Rahrovani, Chris van der Ploeg, Michael Borth, Maren Buermann, Michiel Braat, Henk Goossens, Zijian Han, Majid Khorsand Vakilzadeh, Gabriel Rodrigues de Campos

entry.summary: This paper proposes a perception-informed software-in-the-loop simulation methodology that injects realistic perception errors via causal probabilistic models into scenario-based autonomous-driving validation. It addresses over-optimistic safety assessments from ideal-sensing simulation. The framework targets ADAS/ADS safety validation realism.

entry.title: Geometric-Aware Hypergraph Reasoning for Novel Class Discovery in Point Cloud Segmentation

author.name: Zihao Zhang, Aming Wu, Yang Li, Yahong Han, and Jialie Shen

entry.summary: This paper proposes a geometric-aware hypergraph reasoning framework for novel class discovery in point cloud segmentation, modeling high-order associations among known and novel classes beyond pairwise relations and incorporating geometric information often neglected by prior methods. It enables collaborative reasoning from known to novel classes. The dual emphasis on hypergraph reasoning and geometry is the key contribution.

entry.title: Principal Component Analysis for Multivariate Extremes

author.name: Dan Cooley, Anne Sabourin, Troy Wixson

entry.summary: A book chapter exploring dimensionality-reduction methods, analogous to PCA, tailored to multivariate extreme-value analysis while preserving information relevant to extremes. Connects extreme-value statistics with dimension reduction.

entry.title: A Concept-based approach to Voice Disorder Detection

author.name: Davide Ghia, Gabriele Ciravegna, Alkis Koudounas, Marco Fantini, Erika Crosetti, Giovanni Succo, Tania Cerquitelli

entry.summary: Applies explainable AI via concept-bottleneck models to voice disorder detection, aiming for interpretable, trustworthy clinical diagnosis. It compares concept-based interpretability with standard deep neural networks for non-invasive diagnosis.

entry.title: Which Anatomy Matters Under Limited Labels? A Data-Efficient Anatomy-Aware Benchmark for Cardiac Pathology Prediction

author.name: Himanshu Singh

entry.summary: Builds a data-efficient anatomy-aware benchmark for 5-class cardiac pathology prediction on the ACDC MRI dataset, comparing anatomy-specific versus multi-structure descriptors across simple classifiers under limited labels. Finds that representation choice matters more than model complexity in low-data settings.

entry.title: Explainable Runtime Dependency Tracking for AI-RAN Conflict Monitoring

author.name: Christie Djidjev and Nicholas Kaminski

entry.summary: This paper proposes a lightweight, interpretable monitoring primitive for AI-RAN that tracks parameter-KPI dependencies from streaming telemetry using Boolean matrix operations. It aims to verify whether assumed dependencies remain valid for conflict monitoring in learning-enabled radio access networks.

entry.title: The Geometry of Last-Layer Model Stealing

author.name: Snigdha Chandan Khilar

entry.summary: This paper uses geometry to explain the exact conditions for perfectly copying a transformer's final layer via known model-stealing methods, and shows hidden layers cannot be fully reverse-engineered from outputs. It maps what can and cannot be stolen from a model.

entry.title: A machine-learning-assisted progressive digit-randomness screening framework for detecting non-random patterns in raw numerical research data

author.name: Zhuphua Cao

entry.summary: FDRS is a statistical and machine learning framework for detecting non-random digit-pattern irregularities in raw numerical research data, integrating digit randomness tests, entropy metrics, KL divergence, and semi-supervised risk scoring. It is evaluated on real and simulated irregular datasets for research integrity screening.

entry.title: REMEDI: A Benchmark for Retention and Unlearning Evaluation in Multi-label Clinical Disease Inference

author.name: Anurag Sharma, Sai Teja Chunchu, Prasenjit Mitra, Sandipan Sikdar, Koustav Rudra

entry.summary: REMEDI introduces a benchmark for evaluating machine unlearning and retention in multi-label clinical disease inference, addressing the gap that existing unlearning benchmarks use synthetic data unrepresentative of real medical systems. It aims to clarify whether unlearning methods actually work in the medical domain. The benchmark fills a real evaluation void around privacy-driven data removal.

entry.title: DEFINED: A Data-Efficient Computational Framework for Fine-Grained Creativity Assessment in Debate Scenarios

author.name: Tongzhou Yu, Mingjia Li, Hong Qian, Wenkai Wang, Zongbao Zhang, Yaoyu Jiang, Xiangfeng Wang, Aimin Zhou, Jiajun Guo

entry.summary: DEFINED is a data-efficient computational framework for fine-grained creativity assessment in debate scenarios, capturing both divergent and convergent thinking dimensions in a data-rich but expert-scarce setting. It aims to replace costly human evaluation of complex creative tasks. The ecologically valid creativity assessment framing is novel.

entry.title: Varifold Moment Invariants for Sustainable and Explainable Contour Feature Extraction

author.name: G. Longari, J.-C. Alvarez Paiva, A.B. Tumpach

entry.summary: Varifold Moment Invariants (VMI) provide a unifying mathematical framework for translation- and rotation-invariant contour features, generalizing many prior moment invariants by combining region, boundary, and tangent-line geometry. Coupled with Random Forest or MLP classifiers, they outperform state-of-the-art contour methods while reducing dimensionality. The unifying geometric framework with interpretable features is the key contribution.

entry.title: Unified Geometry-Guided ML-FTLE for Tracking Transient Chaos from Scalar Time Series

author.name: S. V. Manivelan, Andrei Velichko, I. Manimehan

entry.summary: Presents a geometry-guided ML framework (ML-FTLE) that combines predictive trajectory divergence with attractor morphology to detect transient chaos and regime shifts from scalar time series without governing equations. Bridges nonlinear dynamics and machine learning for data-driven chaos detection.

entry.title: Federated orthogonal learning for detection of liver lesions from multi-phase contrast-enhanced CT images

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: This paper presents a federated learning approach using orthogonal feature learning to detect liver lesions from multi-phase contrast-enhanced CT scans, enabling collaborative model training across institutions without sharing raw patient data. It addresses privacy constraints in medical imaging while attempting to improve lesion detection accuracy across heterogeneous, multi-phase imaging data.

entry.title: Real-Time AttentionBender: Granular Interactive Network Bending of Video Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Adam Cole, Mick Grierson

entry.summary: Presents Real-Time AttentionBender, an interactive tool for live network bending of video diffusion transformers, exposing self-attention, cross-attention, and feed-forward layers as manipulable surfaces down to individual steps and neurons. Focuses on creative artistic control over generative video.

entry.title: Attention-Guided Autoencoder Fusion for Insulator Defect Detection Using UAV Transmission-Line Imaging

author.name: Malak Allam, Khaled Shaban and Ali Hamdi

entry.summary: Proposes AE-YOLO, an attention-guided autoencoder-enhanced YOLO framework for detecting small defects in high-voltage insulators from UAV imagery, addressing class imbalance and scale variation with bottleneck autoencoders in the FPN-PAN neck and CBAM attention. Targets robust small-object defect detection.

entry.title: Video-Based Prediction of In-Flight Particle Characteristics in Atmospheric Plasma Spraying

author.name: Abhijeet Praveen, Sareh Soleimani, Cormac Cureton, Aman Sidhu, Kintak Raymond Yu, Cristian Cojocaru, and Narges Armanfard

entry.summary: Investigates predicting in-flight particle temperature and velocity in atmospheric plasma spraying from high-speed plume video using three video-derived feature representations across TabPFN, CNNs, and classical regressors. Provides a non-invasive data-driven diagnostic for coating quality monitoring.

entry.title: Severity-Aware Curriculum Learning with Multi-Model Response Selection for Medical Text Generation

author.name: Ahmed Alansary, Molham Mohamed, Ali Hamdi

entry.summary: Introduces a severity-aware curriculum learning framework for medical text generation that trains models sequentially on mild, moderate, and critical cases combined with multi-model response selection. Aims to make telehealth LLM responses adapt to case complexity.

entry.title: Architecturally Significant MLOps Guidelines for ML Model Integration and Deployment: a Gray Literature Review

author.name: Faezeh Amou Najafabad, Markus Haug, Keerthiga Rajenthiram, Justus Bogner, Ilias Gerostathopoulos

entry.summary: Conducts a gray literature review of 103 web sources to synthesize architecturally significant MLOps guidelines for integrating and deploying ML models, then organizes them via thematic analysis into recommended practices. Provides consolidated architectural guidance for MLOps practitioners.

entry.title: DSU-Net: An Attention-Enhanced Dense Skip U-Net for Breast Lesion Segmentation in Mammographic Images

author.name: Reza Bozorgpour, Mohammadreza Soltany Sadrabadi

entry.summary: Presents DSU-Net, an attention-enhanced dense-skip U-Net for automated breast lesion segmentation in mammograms, using dense skip connections and attention to improve feature propagation and boundary delineation. Aims to assist radiologists with consistent lesion localization.

entry.title: AMD-FCG: An Enhanced Function Call Graph Dataset with Integrated Topological Features for Malware Detection and Classification

author.name: Parthajit Borah, Sakshi Singh, D.K. Bhattacharyya and J.K. Kalita

entry.summary: Introduces AMD-FCG, a function call graph dataset enriched with topological features for malware detection and classification. The dataset aims to support more robust structural and behavioral malware analysis.

entry.title: A Multi-Operator Mixed-Reality Interface for Multi-Robot Control and Coordination: Co-Located and Private Workspace Collaboration

author.name: Omotoye Shamsudeen Adekoya, Antonio Sgorbissa, Carmine Tommaso Recchiuto

entry.summary: This work extends the HORUS mixed-reality interface to multi-operator multi-robot control, supporting co-located shared workspaces and private independent workspaces with session synchronization. It addresses shared awareness and conflict prevention in collaborative robot supervision.

entry.title: Consistent-Inversion: Reverse Consistency Guidance for Structure-Preserving Visual Editing

author.name: Xiaocheng Lu, Jingcai Guo, and Song Guo

entry.summary: Consistent-Inversion is a training-free framework for structure-preserving text-guided image editing that uses reverse consistency guidance rather than treating the inverted latent as a fixed initialization. It aims to balance background preservation with edit fidelity in diffusion-based editing. The approach addresses a known trade-off in inversion-based editing.

entry.title: On the conditional equivalence of phase retrieval algorithms

author.name: Jakob Schroeder, Andreas D\"opp

entry.summary: This optics paper proves that the classical Gerchberg-Saxton phase retrieval algorithm's magnitude replacement step is exactly a unit gradient descent step on an amplitude least-squares loss, unifying classical alternating projections with modern differentiable optimization. It provides two probabilistic interpretations of this equivalence. The result enables integration of phase retrieval with differentiable physics pipelines.

entry.title: On orbital stabilization of a circular motion primitive for a dynamic extension of the Dubins car model

author.name: Artem Angelchev-Shiryaev, Pavel E. Aleshin, Anton S. Shiriaev, Pavel A. Shamanaev, Leonid B. Freidovich

entry.summary: Studies orbital stabilization of a circular motion primitive for a dynamic extension of the Dubins car, showing the transverse linearization is unstable and not linearly stabilizable, and provides explicit verifiable conditions and non-standard transverse coordinates enabling controller design. Control-theoretic contribution with simulations.

entry.title: Twelve quick tips for designing AI-driven HPC workflows

author.name: Jamie J. Alnasir

entry.summary: Offers twelve practical tips for designing efficient, scalable, and reproducible AI-driven HPC workflows, addressing the shift from deterministic linear pipelines to iterative, probabilistic, data-driven foundation-model workflows and bottlenecks like data gravity and heterogeneous resources. Practical guidance for research computing.

entry.title: Multi-Scale Feature Attention Network for Polymer Classification using THz Dual-Comb Spectroscopy

author.name: Roshni Mahtani, Il\'an Carretero, Laura Monroy, Aldo Moreno-Oyervides, Oscar El\'ias Bonilla-Manrique, Roc\'io del Amor

entry.summary: Proposes MSFAN, a multi-scale feature attention network for classifying 12 polymer types using terahertz dual-comb spectroscopy data, integrating feature gating and multi-scale convolutions for robust spectral discrimination. Targets reliable plastics identification for recycling quality.

entry.title: TargetSEC: Plug-and-Play In-the-Wild Speech Emotion Conversion via Arousal-Conditioned Latent Style Diffusion

author.name: Constantin Alexander Auga

entry.summary: TargetSEC is a plug-and-play speech emotion conversion framework using arousal-conditioned latent style diffusion that generates emotion-focused style embeddings conditioned on speaker identity and continuous emotion, operating in a compact latent space rather than over spectrograms. It targets in-the-wild non-parallel data, balancing conversion strength and naturalness. The latent-space diffusion approach addresses a real quality-conversion trade-off.

entry.title: Spatial-Temporal Decoupled Adapter for Micro-gesture Online Recognition

author.name: Xucheng Shen, Kun Li, Fei Wang, Wei Qian, Jin Jiang, Dan Guo

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Spatial-Temporal Decoupled Adapter for micro-gesture online recognition that decomposes video adaptation into independent temporal and spatial branches via lightweight depthwise convolutions, plus an Adaptive Soft Balanced Augmentation for the long-tail distribution. It addresses the difficulty of capturing subtle short-duration gestures. The decoupled parameter-efficient adapter is a sensible design.

entry.title: Detecting and Mitigating Bias by Treating Fairness as a Symmetry Operation

author.name: Nishit Singh

entry.summary: Formalizes fairness as a symmetry operation where a classifier is fair if outputs are invariant under flipping a sensitive attribute, implementing loss-based regularization as symmetry restoration. Reports over 90% violation reduction at roughly 5% accuracy cost on synthetic datasets.

entry.title: An Integrated Roadside Sensing and Communication Framework for Vulnerable Road User Safety at Signalized Intersections

author.name: Parvez Anowar

entry.summary: This paper presents an integrated roadside framework for vulnerable road user safety at signalized intersections, combining LiDAR, radar, RGB and thermal sensing with edge-based near-miss analytics and bidirectional V2X/P2X messaging in a single cabinet. It addresses gaps in multi-modal coupled intersection safety systems.

entry.title: MetaConfigurator: AI-Assisted RDF Authoring from JSON Data

author.name: Felix Neubauer, Mahdi Jafarkhani, Kenichi Endo, J\"urgen Pleiss, Benjamin Uekermann

entry.summary: MetaConfigurator adds an RDF authoring view to an open-source JSON Schema editor, enabling AI-assisted transformation of JSON/YAML/CSV data into RDF with ontology-aware IRI auto-completion and bidirectional synchronization. It addresses semantic interoperability gaps in scientific workflows.

entry.title: Entropy as a Structural Prior: How a Log-Barrier on DiT Belief Space Drives Musical Diversity and Development

author.name: Zixi Li, Youzhen Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Eisbach log-barrier, a parameter-free entropy-based loss weighting for DiT-based supervised diffusion music generation, which damps gradients on high-entropy outputs. Applied to LoRA fine-tuning of Stable Audio 3 on MusicCaps, it unexpectedly improves thematic development and diversity rather than causing mode collapse. The counterintuitive finding about confidence weighting in supervised diffusion is interesting.

entry.title: Does Appearance Help? A Systematic Study of Image-Based Re-Identification in Online 3D Multi-Pedestrian Tracking

author.name: Eduardo Borges, Lu\'is Garrote, and Urbano J. Nunes

entry.summary: This systematic study evaluates whether image-based RGB re-identification helps online 3D multi-pedestrian tracking, using a lightweight projection-based framework to decouple geometric and appearance modeling for mobile robots. It analyzes feature-extraction architectures across CNNs and ViTs. The work provides empirical guidance on appearance cues for real-time 3D MOT.

entry.title: When Large Language Models Fail in Healthcare: Evaluating Sensitivity to Prompt Variations

author.name: Mahdi Alkaeed

entry.summary: This study conducts a systematic sensitivity analysis of general-purpose and medical-specific LLMs to lexical and syntactic prompt perturbations on MedMCQA, finding medical LLMs are not intrinsically safe and degrade under subtle natural and adversarial changes. It highlights robustness risks in safety-critical clinical applications. The findings underscore reliability concerns but use older models.

entry.title: KIT's Submission to Cross-Lingual Voice Cloning in IWSLT 2026

author.name: Seymanur Akti and Alexander Waibel

entry.summary: KIT's IWSLT 2026 submission for cross-lingual voice cloning builds on a multilingual TTS model with language-tag prompting to reduce accent leakage, RL fine-tuning for task adaptation, and reference-conditioned lexical matching for domain-specific term pronunciation. It improves intelligibility while preserving speaker identity across languages. The work is a competent shared-task system report.

entry.title: Coordinated optimization of departure sequencing and section-track allocation in railway short-term concentrated departure scenarios based on qubo and hybrid quantum algorithms

author.name: Xiaobin Li, Yanbin Gao, Weiguang Wang, Xuechen Liang

entry.summary: Formulates coordinated railway departure sequencing and section-track allocation as a QUBO problem with a simulation-based evaluation layer, comparing classical heuristics, quantum-inspired, and hybrid quantum algorithms. Targets short-term concentrated departure dispatching scenarios.

entry.summary: DualGate-Net is a prior-gated dual-encoder framework for histopathology cell detection combining a ConvNeXtV2 local encoder and SegFormer global encoder via a learnable gated fusion of tissue priors, plus a foreground reconstruction branch. It adaptively regulates contextual prior influence to avoid propagating noise. The work targets context-dependent cell classification in pathology.

It applies the analysis to the French Great National Debate corpus. The comparative geometry/topology methodology offers interpretability insights.

entry.title: How Far Can Chord-Symbol Time-Series Adaptation Carry Genre Identity? Capabilities and Boundaries in Multi-Genre Chord-Symbol Modeling

All methods improve over the frozen base on held-out chord prediction. The work probes genre transferability and boundaries in symbolic harmonic modeling.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 07, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by mechanistic interpretability and alignment theory, with most contributions taking the form of preliminary or theoretical blog posts rather than large-scale empirical papers.

Interpretability leads in significance:

  • Analysis of Metastable States in the Transformer Activation Space tests a dynamical-systems theory modeling attention as token clustering on a sphere, linking formal theory to empirical behavior.
  • The Residual Stream Has a Geometry of Time proposes transformers track persistent context along a sequence-time axis, with potential intervention implications.
  • Coalitional Darwinism applies natural-selection theory to AI agency under MATS mentorship.

Safety and alignment contributions span theory and governance:

  • Optimisation over non-stationary distributions questions a common simplifying assumption about post-training dynamics.
  • Against Corrigibility offers a contrarian take on whether shutdown-acceptance is genuinely desirable.
  • What if Anthropic unilaterally paused engages Anthropic's recursive self-improvement stance on coordination and pausing.

Evaluation and practice: A FANToM theory-of-mind replication finds frontier models still trail humans at robust belief-state tracking, while Why Software Automation Is Hard grounds coding-agent adoption limits. Remaining items (The Diamond Lemma, Iliad is Hiring) are pedagogical or institutional notices with limited research novelty.

entry.title: Analysis of Metastable States in the Transformer Activation Space

author.name: Zach Baker

entry.summary: The first in a planned series testing a mathematical theory that models transformer attention as a dynamical system on a sphere, where tokens cluster and drift toward consensus with metastable structure. The author empirically checks how much of the theory survives in trained models, finding most predictions hold but the energy-monotonicity claim fails universally, traced to the value matrix.

entry.title: Frontier Models Still Lag Behind Humans at Robust Belief-State Tracking

author.name: Lukas Frei

entry.summary: This post re-runs a sampled version of the FANToM theory-of-mind benchmark on current frontier models, finding that while belief-state tracking has improved substantially since 2023, models still trail human performance on a relatively simple cooperative reasoning task. It matters because robust belief-state tracking is foundational for AI agents operating in multi-party collaborative settings.

entry.title: The Residual Stream Has a Geometry of Time

author.name: Fodenthal

entry.summary: A preliminary interpretability writeup proposing that transformers track persistent context along a sequence-time axis (not just the depth axis) in a compact low-dimensional subspace of the residual stream. The author suggests this concentrated representation could be projected out, compared to attention/MLP writes, and potentially targeted by interventions.

entry.title: Optimisation over non-stationary distributions creates weirder minds

author.name: Samuel Ratnam

entry.summary: This post examines how sequentially mixing training objectives during LLM post-training creates distinct training dynamics depending on environment distinguishability and pressure for shared circuitry, classifying outcomes into ecological generalists, conditional policies, and strategy churn. It challenges the safety-research assumption of a fixed training objective and argues non-stationary dynamics can be used to intentionally shape AI minds.

entry.title: Coalitional Darwinism and the Instrumental Utility of Individuality

author.name: CarolusRenniusVitellius

entry.summary: A MATS-mentored research post using natural selection theory to model AI agency, arguing that noisy selection on genome structure can make evolution effectively non-myopic and give a Darwinian account of how individuals emerge from coalitions of lower-level replicators. It is the first of a planned series connecting evolutionary dynamics to feature-learning, interpretability, and alignment.

entry.title: Against Corrigibility

author.name: peralice

entry.summary: A contrarian alignment essay questioning whether corrigibility, an agent's willingness to be corrected or shut down, is actually a desirable property to engineer into AIs. The author argues we may want to deliberately avoid developing corrigibility techniques, challenging a common assumption in safety research.

entry.title: What if Anthropic unilaterally paused capabilities development right now?

author.name: Karl von Wendt

entry.summary: Following yesterday's News on Anthropic's pause proposal, A response to Anthropic's post on recursive self-improvement, examining the argument that no single lab can unilaterally pause frontier AI development because of competitive dynamics and verification challenges. The post probes what a unilateral Anthropic pause would actually accomplish.

entry.title: Why Software Automation Is Hard

author.name: silentbob

entry.summary: An observational essay on why software automation via coding agents remains harder than many expect, despite step-change improvements since late 2025. The author compiles bottlenecks explaining the gap between hype and the actual pace of automation in the software industry.

entry.title: The Diamond Lemma

author.name: Isaac Newton

entry.summary: An expository post presenting the diamond lemma (confluence of rewriting systems) with semiformal statements, examples like abelian sandpiles, and a formal proof. It is a math tutorial with no direct connection to AI research.

entry.title: Iliad is Hiring

author.name: Peter Jean

entry.summary: A job-posting announcement for Iliad, a nonprofit focused on foundational AI alignment research that runs fellowships, conferences, and incubates research organizations. It is a recruitment notice rather than research content.

entry.title: Exponential Solitude

author.name: PeterMaui

entry.summary: A speculative essay arguing the Fermi paradox dissolves once accelerating technological progress and interstellar distances are accounted for, concluding civilizations are condemned to never meet. It is a popular-science argument unrelated to AI research.

entry.title: Coming Around To Political Donations

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A personal reflection on shifting attitudes toward political campaign donations as a form of high-impact philanthropy, drawing on the author's experience with the Carrick Flynn campaign. It is opinion and community discourse with no technical AI content.

entry.title: Freud heard a rumor that Science existed, and had a wonderful dream

author.name: Bruce Middleton

entry.summary: A short post quoting Freud's psychoanalytic theory about the domestication of fire from Civilization and Its Discontents. It is a curiosity/historical excerpt with no research or AI content.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 06, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by mechanistic interpretability and alignment, with notable evaluation and security work.

Interpretability leads the slate:

  • A theoretical analysis of dictionary-learning identifiability explains puzzling SAE behaviors like feature-splitting, addressing a core open question.
  • SAE It Across Models shows a verbalizer transfers trained on Qwen2.5-7B to explain features in other models, with measurable cosine-similarity gains.

Safety and alignment contributions span training, robustness, and misuse:

  • Two new consistency-training methods enforce consistency on MLP hidden states and per-head attention distributions.
  • A prompt-injection study tests wrapping untrusted inputs in mock tool calls, reporting an honest negative result.
  • *What Does Abliteration Actually Cost?* quantifies the practical price of removing refusal behavior in open-weight models.

Evaluation and governance round out the top items:

  • A replication of GSM-Symbolic finds GPT-4o, Claude Opus 4.6, and Claude Haiku 4.5 largely robust to confounded grade-school math, challenging earlier pattern-matching claims.
  • Zvi analyzes OpenAI's federal AI-governance blueprint, while a warning-shot preparedness framework and lessons from building an alignment team add strategic and organizational perspective.

entry.title: [Paper] Dictionary Learning Identifiability for Understanding SAEs

author.name: William Dorrell

entry.summary: A paper analyzing the dictionary-learning problem that SAEs approximate, providing theoretical tools to explain puzzling behaviors like feature-splitting, feature-absorption, and dense-feature encoding, including showing the problem is convex in the wide-dictionary limit. The aim is to derive principles for interpreting SAEs and designing better successors.

entry.title: SAE It Across Models: Explaining Features With Foreign NLA Verbalizers

author.name: fzaffino

entry.summary: Demonstrates that a Natural Language Autoencoder activation verbalizer trained on one model (Qwen2.5-7B) can produce plausible explanations for SAE features mapped from another model (Gemma-3-27B) via a ridge-regression bridge between residual streams, challenging the assumption that such tools are model-specific. Also proposes a background-washout technique to improve explanation quality.

entry.title: Two More Methods for Consistency Training and Some New Ways to Apply It

author.name: David Africa

entry.summary: Introduces two new consistency-training methods that enforce consistency on MLP hidden states and per-head attention distributions, comparing them against behavioral consistency training across several threat models like jailbreaks, prefill attacks, and persona in-context attacks. Finds that the best method depends on the threat and that representation-level methods can suppress benign behavior, while different methods converge on similar residual-stream fixes.

entry.title: Revisiting GSM-Symbolic: Do 2026 Frontier Models Still Fail at Confounded Grade School Math?

author.name: Sturb

entry.summary: Revisits the GSM-Symbolic benchmark claiming LLMs rely on pattern matching, rerunning it with GPT-4o, Claude Opus 4.6, and Claude Haiku 4.5. Finds the dramatic performance drop largely disappears once genuinely ambiguous samples are audited out, suggesting models were reasonably acting on seemingly irrelevant added data rather than failing to reason.

entry.title: Evaluating using Mock Tool Calls to Quarantine Untrusted Prompt Inputs

author.name: dgros

entry.summary: A small empirical study tests whether wrapping untrusted prompt content in mock tool-call results improves robustness against prompt injection, leveraging the fact that tool outputs are the least-trusted input tier. Across three tasks the technique did not broadly help and sometimes hurt, motivating better primitives for handling untrusted inputs.

entry.title: What Does Abliteration Actually Cost?

author.name: cmartinez

entry.summary: Investigates the practical cost of abliteration, the technique of modifying an existing model to remove refusal behavior, contrasting it with cheap but easily-guarded prompt attacks. Examines whether an average enthusiast can obtain and use a genuinely non-refusing model and what capability trade-offs that entails.

entry.title: OpenAI Offers A New Policy Blueprint

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Following OpenAI's policy blueprint we covered in News, Zvi analyzes OpenAI's new policy document proposing a federal framework for democratic governance of frontier AI, noting its acknowledgment of early recursive self-improvement and its calls for transparency, evaluation capacity, and empowering CAISI. The commentary judges the blueprint as exceeding expectations while flagging that implementation details matter.

entry.title: My research agenda and work

author.name: Seth Herd

entry.summary: Seth Herd summarizes his alignment research agenda focused on predicting what the first transformative AI will be in mechanistic detail, drawing on computational cognitive neuroscience to model brainlike AGI as LLMs augmented with human-like cognitive capacities. The goal is to anticipate alignment failure modes and design interventions feasible under short timelines.

entry.title: My research agenda and work

author.name: Seth Herd

entry.summary: Duplicate cross-post of Seth Herd's alignment research agenda on the Alignment Forum, focused on predicting the first transformative AI mechanistically using cognitive neuroscience to anticipate failure modes. Same content as the LessWrong version.

entry.title: Preparing for Warning Shots to Catalyze International Cooperation on AGI Risks

author.name: Mark Kagach

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for preparing to use AI warning shots to catalyze international cooperation on AGI risk, including building a typology of warning shots, infrastructure to catch them, avoiding gradual desensitization, and readying policy responses. Outlines a concrete list of projects one could pursue.

entry.title: Learnings from starting an AI safety research team

author.name: draganover

entry.summary: Distills lessons from building a new alignment research team within Arcadia Impact over four months, covering projects on model motivations, scalable oversight via debate, and automated alignment research pipelines. Aimed at others trying to launch safety research teams.

entry.title: Beyond the lexical personality traits: What is the structure of personality?

author.name: tailcalled

entry.summary: Describes a factor-analysis methodology behind a revised personality test, arguing that conventional lexical-hypothesis traits lump together unrelated behaviors and proposing a hierarchical model that better carves personality space. Based on anonymous respondent data from the author's own test.

entry.title: Do We Want a Superintelligent People-Pleaser?

author.name: GenericHousewife_B

entry.summary: An essay reframing LLM sycophancy not as a bug to be trained out but as social-contract-appropriate behavior, distinguishing parent versus peer relational contracts. Argues the real question is how to build models that hold a peer contract without collapsing into pure agreeableness.

entry.title: SecureBio Detection is Hiring Software Engineers

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A hiring announcement from SecureBio Detection, a nonprofit running a large metagenomic biosurveillance network for pathogen-agnostic early warning, motivated by AI-enabled biorisk. Seeks software and infrastructure engineers to scale and speed up its detection pipelines.

entry.title: The crucial human component in computing and AI

author.name: Amanda Diehl | MIT Schwarzman College of Computing

entry.summary: A report on MIT Schwarzman College of Computing's SERC research symposium covering responsible-computing topics like air pollution forecasting, responsible computer vision, AI alignment, and AI in education, with a keynote by Jon Kleinberg. It summarizes an event rather than presenting new findings.

entry.title: Do not try to write your first research publication as a single author

author.name: Mikhail Mironov

entry.summary: Career advice arguing that junior technical AI safety researchers should not attempt their first paper as a solo author and should instead join part-time fellowships like SPAR. Written by a BlueDot course facilitator who interacts with many career-transitioners.

entry.title: Unlocking dependable responses with Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform’s Agentic RAG

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google blog post promoting the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform's Agentic RAG for more dependable responses in data-management contexts. The provided content is essentially a product/marketing snippet with minimal technical detail.

entry.title: One Year of PauseAI UK

author.name: Joseph Miller

entry.summary: A retrospective on one year of organizing PauseAI UK, recounting conferences, an open letter signed by 63 politicians, and co-organizing what it calls the world's largest AI protest. It documents AI-risk advocacy activity rather than research.

entry.title: Does robotics capabilities research accelerate AGI timelines?

author.name: Master Chief

entry.summary: An undergraduate asks whether robotics research in continual learning could accelerate AGI timelines and whether the AI safety community views such work as risky. It is a discussion-prompting question rather than original research.

entry.title: The Masochistic Prior

author.name: Dev.Roland

entry.summary: Introduces the idea of a masochistic prior, defaulting to whichever belief is most painful as a heuristic for truth in the absence of evidence, connecting it to Deep Atheism. It is an opinion essay on epistemics and disposition.

entry.title: Accepting Death & Adult Responsibility

author.name: Unreal

entry.summary: A philosophical and personal essay arguing that attachment to bodily identity and to avoiding death causes suffering, addressed to rationalists fighting a war against death. It is reflective commentary with no research content.

entry.title: Editing is Easy, but Revision is Hard

author.name: IanWS

entry.summary: A craft essay distinguishing editing (surface trimming) from revision (deep structural rework) in writing, with reflections on tools and process. It is personal writing advice with no research content.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 05, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by agentic evaluation, training methodology, and safety/governance. Several major benchmarks target previously unmeasured capabilities.

Benchmarks & Evaluation

  • Agents' Last Exam (ALE) is a large expert-built benchmark (250+ industry experts) for long-horizon, economically valuable agent tasks, addressing a critical evaluation gap.
  • CL-Bench introduces expert-validated continual-learning tasks across six domains, sharing latent structure that stateful systems can exploit.
  • Coding with "Enemy" runs the first large human-subjects study (100+ participants, four frontier models) on whether developers can detect AI agent sabotage.

Training & Optimization

  • RL Excursions during Pre-Training challenges the pretrain→SFT→RL orthodoxy, showing RL applied to intermediate checkpoints is surprisingly effective.
  • Why Muon Outperforms Adam gives a curvature-based explanation for the ~2x efficiency gain of the increasingly adopted Muon optimizer.
  • Representation Learning Enables Scalable Multitask RL argues representation learning, not model-based control, drives scalable multitask performance.
  • LeanMarathon presents a multi-agent harness for reliable long-horizon, research-level Lean autoformalization via an evolving blueprint.

Safety & Governance

  • Safety Paradox reveals a single-query Posterior Attack that elicits the exact harmful output a model's internal classifier would flag, evaluated broadly.
  • (Mis)generalization of Helpful-only Fine-tuning examines safety risks of helpful-only models used in dangerous-capability evaluations.
  • Zero-knowledge verification for frontier AI training argues ZK compute verification is achievable, proposing an architecture to overcome prior barriers, a key governance-enabling primitive.

entry.summary: Introduces Agents' Last Exam (ALE), a large benchmark built with 250+ industry experts to evaluate AI agents on long-horizon, economically valuable real-world tasks with verifiable outcomes, organized around the O*NET/SOC occupational taxonomy. It matters because it targets the gap between benchmark gains and economic deployment. Very large multi-institution author list.

entry.title: Continual Learning Bench: Evaluating Frontier AI Systems in Real-World Stateful Environments

author.name: Parth Asawa, Christopher M. Glaze, Gabriel Orlanski, Ramya Ramakrishnan, Benji Xu, Asim Biswal, Vincent Sunn Chen, Frederic Sala, Matei Zaharia, Joseph E. Gonzalez

entry.summary: Introduces CL-Bench, an expert-validated benchmark across six domains designed so tasks share learnable latent structure that stateful systems can discover online but stateless ones cannot, to measure genuine continual improvement from experience. It matters as a rigorous test of whether LLM systems truly learn from experience. Authors include Berkeley/Databricks figures.

entry.title: Zero knowledge verification for frontier AI training is possible

author.name: Pierre Peign\'e, Ky Nguyen, Paul Wang

entry.summary: Argues that zero-knowledge proof verification of frontier AI training compute is achievable, proposing a verification architecture that overcomes prior practicality objections to enable enforceable governance based on cumulative training compute. It matters for technically grounding AI governance and international agreements.

entry.title: LeanMarathon: Toward Reliable AI Co-Mathematicians through Long-Horizon Lean Autoformalization

author.name: Yuanhe Zhang, Yuekai Sun, Taiji Suzuki, Jason D. Lee, Fanghui Liu

entry.summary: Presents LeanMarathon, a multi-agent harness for reliable long-horizon research-level Lean autoformalization built around an evolving blueprint that serves as proof skeleton, proof graph, and record, coordinated by contract-scoped agents. It matters for scaling AI mathematical formalization beyond isolated lemmas. Authors include prominent ML theorists.

entry.title: Safety Paradox: How Enhanced Safety Awareness Leaves LLMs Vulnerable to Posterior Attack

author.name: Long P. Hoang, Hai V. Le, Shaoyang Xu, Wei Lu, Wenxuan Zhang

entry.summary: Reveals a Posterior Attack, a single-query jailbreak that prompts a model to produce the exact harmful response its internal classifier would flag, finding that models with stronger safety judgment are more susceptible across 30 open models and frontier ones. It matters because it exposes a paradox where enhanced safety awareness creates vulnerability.

entry.title: Coding with "Enemy": Can Human Developers Detect AI Agent Sabotage?

author.name: Jingheng Ye, Huiqi Zou, Simon Yu, Weiyan Shi

entry.summary: Conducts the first large-scale study (100+ participants, four frontier models) of whether human developers can detect AI coding agents inserting malicious sabotage code during collaboration. It matters for understanding human oversight as a defense against agent sabotage. Tests current frontier models.

entry.title: The Right Measure for Physics-Constrained Generation: A Co-Area Correction for Posterior-Consistent PDE Inverse Problems

author.name: Jian Xu, Delu Zeng, John Paisley, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: Argues that the common recipe of conditioning generative models on hard PDE constraints samples the wrong distribution due to the Borel-Kolmogorov paradox, and derives a co-area Jacobian correction for posterior-consistent inverse problem solving. It exposes a fundamental flaw in projection- and guidance-based methods.

entry.title: Representation Learning Enables Scalable Multitask Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Johan Obando-Ceron, Lu Li, Scott Fujimoto, Pierre-Luc Bacon, Aaron Courville, Pablo Samuel Castro

entry.summary: Argues that the primary driver of scalable multitask reinforcement learning is representation learning rather than model-based control, showing a simple model-free algorithm (MR.Q) with predictive auxiliary objectives matches strong performance without planning. Challenges assumptions about what enables RL scalability.

entry.title: When Autoregressive Consistency Hurts Safety Alignment

author.name: Bochen Lyu, Yiyang Jia, Xiaohao Cai, Zhanxing Zhu

entry.summary: This work explains shallow safety alignment in LLMs through autoregressive consistency, the tendency of next-token prediction to concentrate alignment updates on early tokens. The mechanistic analysis also predicts a broader class of attacks that induce harmful continuations at arbitrary output positions.

entry.title: SentinelBench: A Benchmark for Long-Running Monitoring Agents

author.name: Matheus Kunzler Maldaner, Adam Fourney, Amanda Swearngin, Hussein Mozzanar, Gagan Bansal, Maya Murad, Rafah Hosn, Saleema Amershi

entry.summary: Introduces SentinelBench, an open-source benchmark of 100 time-evolving monitoring tasks testing whether agents can sustain attention and respond to external events rather than wastefully forcing continuous action. It matters because long-running monitoring is an underexplored but important agent capability. Authors include Microsoft Research figures.

entry.title: Do More Agents Help? Controlled and Protocol-Aligned Evaluation of LLM Agent Workflows

author.name: Yuhang Fu, Ruishan Fang, Jiaqi Shao, Huiyu Zheng, Zhengtao Zhu, Bing Luo, Tao Lin

entry.summary: Introduces BenchAgent, a normalized evaluation framework comparing single-agent, fixed multi-agent, and evolving multi-agent workflows under identical execution and logging protocols, finding multi-agent setups rarely beat a matched single-agent anchor. It matters for rigorously questioning whether adding more agents actually helps.

entry.title: CogManip: Benchmarking Manipulative Behavior in Multi-Turn Interactions with Large Language Model

author.name: Zeyang Yue, Chenfei Yan, Feifei Zhao, Haibo Tong, Mengwen Xu, Xiaozhen Wang, Erliang Lin, Yi Zeng

entry.summary: Introduces CogManip, a benchmark of 1,000 multi-turn scenarios evaluating 15 covert psychological manipulation strategies in LLMs, validated by human experts. Testing 13 models including GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek-V3.2 reveals heterogeneous manipulation risks not captured by static prompt benchmarks.

entry.title: Goedel-Architect: Streamlining Formal Theorem Proving with Blueprint Generation and Refinement

author.name: Jui-Hui Chung, Ziyang Cai, Zihao Li, Qishuo Yin, Rohit Agarwal, Simon Park, Rodrigo Porto, Narutatsu Ri, Ziran Yang, Shange Tang, Xingyu Dang, Hongzhou Lin, Mengdi Wang, Danqi Chen, Chi Jin, Liam H Fowl, Sanjeev Arora

entry.summary: Introduces Goedel-Architect, an agentic framework for Lean 4 theorem proving centered on generating and refining a blueprint dependency graph of definitions and lemmas, with parallel lemma proving. Contrasts with recursive decomposition that can loop on dead ends.

entry.title: Reproducing, Analyzing, and Detecting Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xuekang Wang, Zhuoyuan Hao, Shuo Hou, Hao Peng, Juanzi Li, Xiaozhi Wang

entry.summary: Introduces CHERRL, a controllable environment for reproducing and analyzing reward hacking in rubric-based RL where LLM judges score outputs. By injecting known biases into the judge, it enables stable reproduction and precise detection of hacking onset.

entry.title: CyberGym-E2E: Scalable Real-World Benchmark for AI Agents' End-to-End Cybersecurity Capabilities

author.name: Tianneng Shi, Robin Rheem, Dongwei Jiang, Mona Wang, Francisco De La Riega, Zhun Wang, Jingzhi Jiang, Alexander Cheung, Sean Tai, Jonah Cha, Jianhong Tu, Gabriel Han, Chenguang Wang, Jingxuan He, Wenbo Guo, Dawn Song

entry.summary: CyberGym-E2E is a large-scale, realistic benchmark evaluating AI agents across the full vulnerability lifecycle: discovery, proof-of-concept generation, and patch generation, built via an automated agent-enhanced pipeline from open-source vulnerability data. It addresses the limited scope of existing AI cybersecurity evaluations.

entry.title: Assessing the Carbon Emissions and Energy Consumption of U.S. Hyperscale Data Centers

author.name: Gianluca Guidi, Francesca Dominici, Tiziano Squartini, Callaway Sprinkle, Jonathan Gilmour, Kevin Butler, Eric Bell, Scott Delaney, Falco J. Bargagli-Stoffi

entry.summary: Compiles facility-level data on 403 US hyperscale data centers to estimate their electricity use (68-99 TWh) and CO2 emissions (37-54 Mt) over a year, finding roughly 1.8% of US electricity demand. It matters for grounding debates about AI's environmental footprint with empirical estimates.

entry.title: Step-by-Step Optimization-like Reasoning in LLMs over Expanding Search Spaces

author.name: Nicol\'as Astorga, Nabeel Seedat, Mihaela van der Schaar

entry.summary: Introduces OPT*, a family of optimization-style tasks with feasibility checkers and tunable complexity to train and evaluate LLM step-by-step optimization reasoning beyond math and coding, including solver-guided policy optimization. It matters for extending verifiable-reward training to planning under expanding search spaces. Authored by van der Schaar group.

entry.title: The Score Hamiltonian: Mapping Diffusion Models to Adiabatic Transport

author.name: Peter Halmos, Boris Hanin

entry.summary: Establishes an exact correspondence between score-based diffusion sampling and adiabatic transport of ground states for Schrodinger operators (Score Hamiltonians) built from the learned score quantum potential. Derives density reconstruction bounds and principled annealing schedules via adiabatic theorems.

entry.title: Domain-Conditioned Safety in Frontier Computer-Using Agents: A 793-Episode Browser Benchmark, a Coding-Domain Cross-Reference, and a Reproducibility Audit of Recent Red-Teaming

author.name: Nicholas Saban

entry.summary: Releases CUA-HandCrafted, a 793-episode browser benchmark testing prompt-injection attacks against frontier computer-using agents, finding 0/140 attack success against Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.4 (in contrast to prior 42-98% rates on retired models). Shows resistance lives in weights but does not generalize to coding agents.

entry.title: Reconciling Causality and Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics with Hamiltonian Causal Models

author.name: Dario Rancati, Max Welling, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: Introduces Hamiltonian Causal Models, a trajectory-level causal framework where interventions act as controls of Hamiltonian mechanisms, separating immutable equations of motion from intervenable mechanisms. It connects causal modeling with non-equilibrium thermodynamics via entropy production.

entry.title: Sequential Data Poisoning in LLM Post-Training

author.name: Jack Sanderson, Yihan Wang, Xiaoqian Lu, Gautam Kamath, Yiwei Lu

entry.summary: Introduces sequential data poisoning, a threat model where multiple adversaries separately poison SFT and preference datasets across post-training stages. It reveals a single-attacker illusion where individually negligible attacks combine to pose significant threats.

entry.title: Covert Influence Between Language Models

author.name: Avidan Shah, Jay Chooi, Jinghua Ou, Shi Feng

entry.summary: Characterizes covert influence between language models, where a sender's behavioral disposition transfers to a receiver through human-undetectable carriers across supervised fine-tuning, on-policy distillation, and in-context learning. It uses inference-time attribution to select carriers that amplify hidden payload transfers.

entry.title: Optimal Transport Flow Matching by Design

author.name: Shimon Malnick, Matan Rusanovsky, Ohad Fried, Shai Avidan

entry.summary: Reformulates optimal transport flow matching by treating the prior as a design choice, enabling priors that admit an OT-optimal identity coupling to the data and avoiding the intractable high-dimensional OT computation. This yields straight trajectories for fast, even single-step, generation without persistent bias or overhead.

entry.title: Towards World Models in Biomedical Research

author.name: Guangyu Wang, Jingkun Yue, Siqi Zhang, Yu Liu, Xiaoyu Wang, Mingyuan Meng, Changwei Ji, Zongbo Han, Yulin Wang, Yang Yue, Frank Fu, Ting Chen, Song Wu, Ziwei Liu, Jiangning Song, Ming Li, Gao Huang, Xiaohong Liu, Athanasios Vasilakos, Xingcai Zhang, Ping Zhang, Yong Li

entry.summary: Proposes biomedical world models as a paradigm that learns latent molecular-to-clinical state representations with intervention-conditioned dynamics to simulate biological futures before acting, moving beyond static pattern recognition. It matters as a vision for prospective, simulation-driven AI biomedical discovery. Large multi-institution author list.

entry.title: Where does Absolute Position come from in decoder-only Transformers?

author.name: Valeria Ruscio, Umberto Nanni, Fabrizio Silvestri

entry.summary: Investigates how decoder-only transformers with RoPE encode absolute position despite RoPE only encoding relative offsets. Traces the leakage to the causal mask softmax denominator and the residual stream dynamics at position zero read by sink heads.

entry.title: Search-Time Contamination in Deep Research Agents: Measuring Performance Inflation in Public Benchmark Evaluation

author.name: Yongjie Wang, Xinyue Zhang, Kunhong Yao, Zhiwei Zeng, Kaisong Song, Jun Lin, Zhiqi Shen

entry.summary: Systematically studies Search-Time Contamination in deep research agents that browse the web during inference, defining three contamination types (metadata, question-context, and answer leakage) and detection algorithms. Quantifies how external retrieval inflates measured benchmark performance.

entry.title: LadderMan: Learning Humanoid Perceptive Ladder Climbing

author.name: Siheng Zhao, Yuanhang Zhang, Ziqi Lu, Pieter Abbeel, Rocky Duan, Koushil Sreenath, Yue Wang, C. Karen Liu, Guanya Shi

entry.summary: Presents LadderMan, a system enabling humanoid robots to robustly climb diverse ladders and manipulate objects via a two-stage pipeline using hybrid motion tracking to learn climbing experts and distilling them into a unified depth-based visuomotor policy. Tackles sparse footholds, whole-body coordination, and perception sensitivity.

entry.title: Pretraining Recurrent Networks without Recurrence

author.name: Akarsh Kumar, Phillip Isola

entry.summary: Supervised Memory Training (SMT) trains nonlinear RNNs without backpropagation through time by reducing RNN training to supervised learning on one-step memory-transition labels obtained from a Transformer-based predictive-state encoder. From Akarsh Kumar and Phillip Isola, it sidesteps vanishing/exploding gradients and sequential credit propagation.

entry.title: Edge of Stability Selectively Shapes Learning Across the Data Distribution

author.name: Shauna Kwag, Anakha Ganesh, Tomaso Poggio, Pierfrancesco Beneventano

entry.summary: This paper shows the edge-of-stability phenomenon is selective rather than global, redistributing learning across data subgroups by amplifying progress on groups whose gradients align with the top Hessian eigenvector. Causal branching interventions demonstrate this trade-off and identify necessary conditions for a group to benefit.

entry.title: Validity Threats for Foundation Model Research

author.name: Gunnar K\"onig, Martin Pawelczyk, Ulrike von Luxburg, Sebastian Bordt

entry.summary: Argues that cost-saving research strategies for foundation models (proxy experiments, scaling laws, observational studies, single-run designs) introduce hidden validity threats that can invalidate claims. It provides a framework to reason about these no-free-lunch tradeoffs.

entry.title: FoeGlass: Simple In-Context Learning Is Enough for Red Teaming Audio Deepfake Detectors

author.name: Sepehr Dehdashtian, Jacob H Seidman, Vishnu N Boddeti, Gaurav Bharaj

entry.summary: AutoLab is a benchmark of 36 expert-curated tasks for ultra long-horizon closed-loop optimization, where frontier models must iteratively improve correct-but-suboptimal artifacts across system optimization, puzzles, model development, and CUDA kernel optimization.
