entry.summary: Introduces cold-start POI check-in forecasting using spatio-temporal graph-based causal modeling that captures functional dependencies and causal effects of urban interventions, rather than relying on proximity-based correlation graphs. Useful for data-driven urban planning and commercial decision-making.

entry.title: TinyML-Driven Cybersecurity for Autonomous Spacecraft: Latency-Accuracy Analysis for SPARTA RF and Cyber Threat Detection

author.name: Van Le, Trevor Tran, Tan Le

entry.summary: Analyzes latency-accuracy trade-offs of TinyML-compatible classical models for onboard cyber-RF threat detection on autonomous spacecraft using the SPARTA attack model. Provides physics-informed theoretical complexity analysis and empirical measurements on adversarial RF spectrograms.

entry.title: EGTR-Review: Efficient Evidence-Grounded Scientific Peer Review Generation via Multi-Agent Teacher Distillation

author.name: Xinpeng Qiu, Wang Yihu, Zhifeng Liu, Xiaochen Wang, Jimin Wang

entry.summary: EGTR-Review proposes a framework for generating evidence-grounded, traceable scientific peer reviews by distilling a multi-agent teacher pipeline into a more efficient model. It targets reducing reviewer burden while improving source traceability and lowering inference costs.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Network Modeling of Biodegradable Contaminant Transport through GCL/SL Composite Liners

author.name: Dong Li, Yapeng Cao, Haiping Zhao, Shutong Han

entry.summary: This work develops a two-domain physics-informed neural network for biodegradable contaminant transport through composite landfill liner systems, comparing soft-constrained and hard-constrained PINN formulations against analytical and finite-element references. The hard-constrained variant better captures early-time breakthrough behavior.

entry.title: An Ensembled Latent Factor Model via Differential Evolution and Gradient Descent Optimization

author.name: Rui Zhang, Jinhang Liu, Wenbo Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes an ensembled latent factor model for high-dimensional incomplete data that independently trains two latent factor models via differential evolution and gradient descent respectively, then combines them. It aims to overcome the insufficient and biased representations of gradient-descent-only approaches on heterogeneous data.

entry.title: Dynamic Multi-Pair Trading Strategy in Cryptocurrency Markets with Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Damian Lebied\'z, Robert \'Slepaczuk

entry.summary: This study applies deep reinforcement learning (PPO with LSTM) as an execution overlay for multi-pair statistical arbitrage trading in volatile cryptocurrency markets, with a Filter-then-Rank pair selection and a Fixed Risk Adaptive Mean execution model. It tests whether DRL can enhance pair trading beyond rigid classical implementations.

entry.title: REGAIN: REconciliation GAIN-driven Auxiliary Direction Learning

author.name: Weijia Li, Shun Hu, Yanfei Kang

entry.summary: REGAIN is a forecast reconciliation framework that learns which additional linear measurements to forecast and include, selecting auxiliary directions by their downstream loss reduction after reconciliation. It reframes reconciliation from projection onto a fixed system to actively designing the measurement system.

entry.title: AURA: Intent-Directed Probing for Implicit-Need Surfacing in Situated LLM Agents

author.name: Yang Li, Jiaxiang Liu, Jiang Cai, Mingkun Xu

entry.summary: AURA adds an inference step between perception and tool use in situated LLM agents, producing a structured estimate of implicit user needs with a gap score that controls probe budget. It improves implicit-need coverage over ReAct-style probing on a small 100-query benchmark.

entry.title: Staged Factorial Screening for Budget-Constrained Micro-Pretraining

author.name: Felipe Chavarro Polania

entry.summary: Studies staged fractional-factorial screening to triage many micro-pretraining recipes on a single GPU under tight budgets, running 613 experiments to recover stable early effect structure. It offers a workflow for budget-constrained recipe selection.

entry.title: TopoPult-SSL: Gland-Mask-Free Cross-Device Meibomian Gland Segmentation via Self-Distilled Weak Clinical Priors

author.name: Nicol\`o Savioli, Luca Del Tongo

entry.summary: TopoPult-SSL is a two-stage framework for cross-device meibomian gland segmentation that uses cheap clinical priors (eyelid outlines, Pult grades, morphometrics) instead of expensive dense masks in stage one, then self-distills teachers into a compact student. It addresses domain shift across imaging devices.

entry.title: What's Under the Skin? Estimating Swine Body Condition

author.name: Mk Bashar, Kuljit Bhatti, Gary Rohrer, Madonna Benjamin, Tami Brown-Brandl, Daniel Morris

entry.summary: PigFormer estimates swine body condition (backfat thickness, loin muscle depth) from ceiling-mounted RGB-D depth frames, replacing labor-intensive ultrasound scans. The two-stage system uses a geometric front-end to standardize raw depth before prediction.

entry.title: Multimodal Sexism Identification and Characterization using Large Language Models and Gradient Boosting

author.name: Kyriakos Chaviaras, Maria Lymperaiou, Athanasios Voulodimos

entry.summary: This is the AILS-NTUA submission to EXIST 2026 for multimodal sexism identification in memes and short videos, using a feature-engineered late-fusion pipeline with gradient-boosted models. It combines visual, textual, demographic, biometric, acoustic, and LLM-derived semantic features.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Sensor Fusion for Autonomous Navigation

author.name: Simegnew Yihunie Alaba, Yuichi Motai

entry.summary: Combines a Vision Transformer for IMU temporal modeling and multiscale CNN for optical flow with an Unscented Kalman Filter and uncertainty-aware fusion for visual-inertial odometry. Aims to improve pose estimation robustness in autonomous navigation.

entry.title: Learning from Demonstrations over Riemannian Manifolds using Neural ODEs: An Extended Abstract

author.name: Diana Cuervo Espinosa, Mahathi Anand, Angela P. Schoellig

entry.summary: Extended abstract proposing learning from demonstrations over Riemannian manifolds using neural ODEs to estimate geodesics, encoding both position and orientation. Reduces computational overhead of prior geodesic methods.

entry.title: Attitude-Aided Linear Calibration of Triaxial Accelerometers

author.name: Yongqiang Yu, Tian Huang, Yipeng Yang

entry.summary: Presents attitude-aided linear accelerometer calibration (ALAC) that uses orientation information to construct a combined error matrix enabling linear least-squares estimation of bias and gravity. Avoids costly reference setups and nonlinear iterative optimization.

entry.title: Human Oversight and Overload: Two Hidden and Costly Burdens of AI-Assisted Software Engineering

author.name: Vahid Garousi

entry.summary: Characterizes two hidden burdens of AI-assisted software engineering: the constant need for human oversight of AI-generated artifacts and cognitive overload from excessive AI suggestions. Blends practitioner evidence to open a conversation about managing these costs.

entry.title: TPA-AD: A Two-Stage Pseudo Anomaly-Guided Method for Bearing Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Xiancheng Wang, Zhibo Zhang, Ran Li, Rui Wang, Minghang Zhao, Shisheng Zhong, Lin Wang

entry.summary: TPA-AD is a two-stage pseudo-anomaly-guided method for bearing time-series anomaly detection in the normal-only training setting, generating pseudo-anomalous windows near the normal boundary, learning anomaly-sensitive representations via contrastive learning, and scoring with KNN. It targets axle-box bearing monitoring.

entry.title: Knockoffs-based False Discovery Rate Control and Simplification for Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Huiqi Zhang, Wenyu Liao, Yiqing Shi, Xiaobo Huang, Fang Xie

entry.summary: This paper proposes three knockoff-based variable screening methods for deep neural networks that control false discovery rate while simplifying inputs and parameters. It extends FDR-controlled selection from high-dimensional regression to neural networks.

entry.title: Reconstructing Unobservable Temperature Fields via Simulation-Aided Intelligent Sensing

author.name: Monika Stipsitz, H\`elios Sanchis-Alepuz, Jacob Reynvaan, Silvester Sabathiel

entry.summary: This work reconstructs unobservable internal temperature fields from sparse embedded sensors using neural networks trained solely on randomized physics-based simulation data. It demonstrates a proof-of-concept hardware setup for high-resolution thermal monitoring where sensor placement is constrained.

entry.title: Uncertainty Aware Functional Behavior Prediction and Material Fatigue Assessment for Circular Factory

author.name: Nehal Afifi, Mehdi Khabou, Victor Mas, Jonas Hemmerich, Patric Grauberger, Stefan Dietrich, Volker Schulze, Sven Matthiesen

entry.summary: Combines uncertainty-aware functional prediction with component-level material fatigue assessment to decide reuse of returned products in circular manufacturing, demonstrated on an angle grinder. It matters for sustainable remanufacturing decisions under heterogeneous degradation.

entry.title: RAINO: Anchoring Agents in Reality, A Systematic Review and Conceptual Framework for Realism in Agent-Based Modelling

author.name: Lo\"is Vanh\'ee, Melania Borit

entry.summary: A systematic literature review of how realism is operationalized in agent-based modeling, finding it is often poorly defined. Introduces the RAINO (Reality Anchor, Input, Output) framework to structure arguments for model realism.

entry.title: PEFT of SLM for Telecommunications Customer Support: A Comparative Study of LoRA Configurations with Energy Consumption Analysis

author.name: Lucas Tamic, Ilan Jaffeux-Cheniout, Xavier Marjou

entry.summary: A comparative study of LoRA configurations for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-3B for telecom customer support, including energy consumption analysis and a synthetic data generation method from a 52-term glossary. Addresses data sovereignty and on-prem deployment needs.

entry.title: Multi-Granularity Reasoning for Natural Language Inference

author.name: Chunling Xi, Di Liang

entry.summary: Proposes a Multi-Granularity Reasoning Network for natural language inference that leverages representations across multiple transformer layers to capture lexical, phrasal, and contextual semantics rather than only final-layer tokens. Aims to improve hierarchical reasoning over premise-hypothesis pairs.

entry.title: The End of Software Engineering: How AI Agents Are Fundamentally Restructuring the Software Paradigm

author.name: Zhenfeng Cao

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that AI agents, where LLMs dynamically generate and discard code, constitute a fundamental restructuring of the software paradigm rather than incremental improvement. Formalizes the distinction between traditional code-as-decision-logic and agentic code-as-ephemeral-tooling using complexity scaling analysis.

entry.title: Deep Learning-based 3D Oral Cavity Reconstruction Using 2D Intraoral Images

author.name: Jihun Cho, Soo-Yeon Jeong, Eun-Jeong Bae, Sun-Young Ihm

entry.summary: Proposes a deep learning approach for 3D oral cavity reconstruction from 2D intraoral images, aiming to reduce patient discomfort and equipment costs associated with impression-taking and intraoral scanners. Addresses material deformation and high cost limitations in dental 3D modeling.

entry.title: Sample-efficient Low-level Motion Planning for Robotic Manipulation Tasks via Zero-shot Transfer Learning

author.name: Yuanzhi He, Victor Romero-Cano, Jos\'e J. Pati\~no, Juan David Hern\'andez, William Sawtell, Gualtiero Colombo

entry.summary: Proposes iCEM+TL, combining the sample-efficient Cross-Entropy Method with transfer learning to reuse planning parameters from simpler robotic tasks for complex manipulation like stacking and shelf placement. It improves low-level real-time motion planning sample efficiency.

entry.title: Long-Term and Short-Term Transistor Aging in Deep Neural Networks: Impact and Mitigation

author.name: Alireza Sarmadi, Virinchi Roy Surabhi, Prashanth Krishnamurthy, Hussam Amrouch, Ramesh Karri, Farshad Khorrami

entry.summary: This chapter analyzes how long-term and short-term transistor aging degrades DNN inference accuracy in hardware and discusses mitigation strategies beyond costly timing guardbands. It bridges hardware reliability and neural network deployment.

entry.title: Fog of Love: Engineering Virtuous Agent Behavior with Affinity-based Reinforcement Learning in a Game Environment

author.name: Ajay Vishwanath, Christian Omlin

entry.summary: This work introduces a two-player multi-agent environment based on the role-playing board game Fog of Love to study affinity-based reinforcement learning for instilling virtuous agent behavior beyond simple grid worlds. Agents compete to fulfill individual virtues while cooperating to satisfy shared goals.

entry.title: Analysis of the Neglect-Zero Effect in Large Language Models

author.name: Jin Tanaka, Daiki Matsuoka, Ryoma Kumon, Hitomi Yanaka

entry.summary: Examines whether LLMs exhibit the human neglect-zero cognitive bias (ignoring vacuously-true empty-set configurations) using a structural priming paradigm. It probes how LLM language processing resembles human inference patterns.

entry.title: "Chi nas dal soch el sent de legn" -- Auditing Text Corpora for Lombard

author.name: Edoardo Signoroni, Pavel Rychl\'y

entry.summary: Manually audits parallel and monolingual corpora for the under-resourced Lombard language, finding web-scraped abundance is illusory due to language misidentification, boilerplate, and noise. Analyzes orthographic composition across datasets.

entry.title: LightVesselNet: An Ultra-Lightweight Sub-100K Parameter Network for Retinal Blood Vessel Segmentation

author.name: Shadman Sobhan, Farhana Jalil

entry.summary: LightVesselNet is an ultra-lightweight sub-100K-parameter network for retinal vessel segmentation using a compact encoder-decoder with attention, multi-scale aggregation, and subpixel upsampling. It targets edge-device deployment with competitive accuracy.

entry.title: Physics in 2-Steps: Locking Motion Priors Before Visual Refinement Erases Them

author.name: Woojung Han, Seil Kang, Youngjun Jun, Min-Hung Chen, Fu-En Yang, Seong Jae Hwang

entry.summary: Comparison of CNN and transformer architectures (U-Net variants, DeepLabV3+, SegFormer) for segmenting bacterial leaf blight severity in rice from UAV multispectral imagery. U-Net++ with EfficientNet-B3 achieved the highest mIoU of 97.62% across input configurations with NDVI and NDRE.

entry.title: Emotion-Aware Image Generation from Korean Diary Text via LLM-based Prompt Translation and LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jihun Cho, Soo-Yeon Jeong, Sun-Young Ihm

entry.summary: Proposes an emotion-aware text-to-image pipeline that generates children's drawing-style images from short Korean diary entries using Qwen3-8B for sentiment recognition and LoRA-fine-tuned Stable Diffusion 3.5 with emotion trigger words. Examines the effect of emotion triggers and limitations of CLIP Score for evaluation.

entry.title: Neetyabhas: A Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Public Policy Optimization in Rational Agent-Based Models

author.name: Janani Venugopalan, Gaurav Deshkar, Rishabh Gaur, Harshal Hayatnagarkar, Jayanta Kshirsagar

entry.summary: Neetyabhas is an uncertainty-aware framework for public-policy optimization in rational agent-based models, applied to COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions with explicit uncertainties in epidemic measurement and policy implementation. It simulates 1,000 individuals making real-time choices while policymakers deploy interventions.

entry.title: A Komi-Yazva--Russian Parallel Corpus and Evaluation Protocol for Zero- and Few-Shot LLM Translation

author.name: Petr Parshakov

entry.summary: Presents the first Komi-Yazva--Russian parallel corpus (457 pairs) with a leakage-aware evaluation protocol for zero- and few-shot LLM translation in an endangered, extremely low-resource setting. Includes story-level cross-validation and judge-based metrics.

entry.title: Learning to replenish: A hybrid deep reinforcement learning for dynamic inventory management in the pharmaceutical supply chains

author.name: Amandeep Kaur, Gyan Prakash

entry.summary: Develops a hybrid deep reinforcement learning approach for dynamic inventory replenishment in pharmaceutical supply chains, handling stochastic demand, variable lead times, and product shelf-life constraints. Aims to maximize profitability while minimizing waste.

entry.title: AIS-Based Vessel Trajectory Prediction Using Memory-Augmented Neural Networks

author.name: Wonmo Koo, Sanha Chang, Heeyoung Kim

entry.summary: Empirically investigates memory-augmented neural networks for AIS-based vessel trajectory prediction, applying external memory retrieval (proven in pedestrian/vehicle settings) to maritime data. Shows consistent gains over deep learning baselines in two regions.

entry.title: Next-Generation Parallel Decoder for LPDR: Architectural Optimization and Class-Balanced GAN-Augmentation

author.name: Shawaiz Obaid, Nida Chandio, Neha Jamil, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad

entry.summary: Improves license plate detection and recognition with Cross-Spatial Hybrid Attention and Class-Balanced Synthetic Augmentation using 75,000 GAN-generated samples, evaluated on four benchmarks. Addresses spatial character mismatches and data imbalance, improving minority provincial plate recognition.

entry.title: Emergent Language as an Approach to Conscious AI

author.name: Zengqing Wu, Chuan Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes emergent language in multi-agent reinforcement learning as a generative methodology toward conscious AI, where agents develop communication from minimal priors under task pressure to ensure structures arise from task demands rather than human-language priors. It positions EL as an alternative to checklist and architectural approaches.

entry.title: Metric-Aware Hybrid Forecasting for the CTF4Science Lorenz Challenge

author.name: Cen Lu

entry.summary: A single-author competition entry for the CTF4Science Lorenz challenge that uses a metric-aware hybrid system, assigning different predictors (denoisers, ODE fitting, histogram-tail substitution) to different metric families. It demonstrates that no single model dominates across forecasting, distribution-matching, and reconstruction tasks.

entry.title: AI from concrete to abstract: demystifying artificial intelligence to the general public

author.name: Rubens Lacerda Queiroz, F\'abio Ferrentini Sampaio, Cabral Lima, Priscila Machado Vieira Lima

entry.summary: Presents AIcon2abs, a methodology combining visual programming and WiSARD weightless neural networks to demystify AI for the general public including children through hands-on machine-learning activities. It aims to build basic AI literacy without requiring internet access.

entry.title: How do machines learn? Evaluating the AIcon2abs method

author.name: Rubens Lacerda Queiroz, Cabral Lima, Fabio Ferrentini Sampaio, Priscila Machado Vieira Lima

entry.summary: Evaluates the effectiveness of the AIcon2abs AI-literacy method, which uses the WiSARD weightless neural network for accessible hands-on machine learning education across age groups including K-12. It assesses participant understanding through interactive activities.

entry.title: Cross-Prompt Generalization in Detecting AI-Generated Fake News Using Interpretable Linguistic Features

author.name: Aya Vera-Jimenez, Samuel Jaeger, Calvin Ibenye, Dhrubajyoti Ghosh

entry.summary: This paper studies whether detectors of AI-generated fake news generalize across different prompting strategies, using interpretable linguistic features (lexical diversity, readability, emotion) with a random forest classifier in a cross-prompt framework. It matters because most detectors are trained under a single generation setting and may fail on unseen prompts.

entry.title: TITAN-FedAnil+: Trust-Based Adaptive Blockchain Federated Learning for Resource-Constrained Intelligent Enterprises

author.name: Muhammad Hadi, Muhammad Jahangir, Talha Shafique, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad

entry.summary: TITAN-FedAnil+ is a trust-based, blockchain-enabled federated learning framework for resource-constrained enterprises, using affinity-propagation clustered aggregation to filter malicious updates without knowing the number of attackers and GPU-accelerated vectorization for efficiency. It targets non-IID heterogeneity and decentralized security threats.

entry.title: Modeling and Interpreting Teamwork Dynamics in Cancer Care Outcome Prediction

author.name: Yuhua Huang, Hsiao-Ying Lu, Kwan-Liu Ma

entry.summary: This study models and interprets teamwork dynamics among healthcare professionals during the delivery phase of cancer care to predict patient outcomes, an aspect often neglected compared to clinical/demographic factors. It highlights human factors in collaborative care as crucial to outcomes.

entry.title: Beyond tokens: a unified framework for latent communication in LLM-based multi-agent systems

author.name: Yingzhuo Liu

entry.summary: A single-author framework and survey-style proposal for latent (non-token) communication between LLM agents using continuous representations to reduce inference cost and information loss. It frames the drawbacks of natural-language protocols.

entry.title: Representing Research Attention as Contextually Structured Flows

author.name: Jessica Rodrigues, Angelo Salatino, Gard Jenset, Scott Hale

entry.summary: Proposes representing research attention as contextually structured flows rather than aggregated counts, evaluated on an analogy-style reasoning benchmark across research outputs. Flow representations better support structural comparison over time.

entry.title: Deep Learning-assisted AMD Staging based on OCT and OCT Angiography

author.name: Yukun Guo, Tristan T. Hormel, An-Lun Wu, Liqin Gao, Min Gao, Steven T. Bailey, Yali Jia

entry.summary: Develops and evaluates deep learning models for automated AMD severity grading using OCT and OCT angiography across four stages in 271 participants, comparing biomarker-map and other input modalities. It targets clinical AMD staging.

entry.title: Horse Eye Blink Detection and Classification for Equine Affective State Assessment

author.name: Jo\~ao Alves, Signe M{\o}ller-Skuldb{\o}l, Pia Haubro Andersen, Rikke Gade

entry.summary: This paper develops automated horse eye-blink detection for equine pain and affective state assessment, comparing YOLOv12, optical flow thresholding, and fine-tuned VideoMAE. It achieves a macro-F1 of about 0.898 on detecting subtle micro-expressions in horse videos.

entry.title: Drishti AI-Event Guardian: An Intelligent Real-Time Crowd Monitoring and Emergency Response System for Mass Gathering Events

author.name: Ritabrata Roy Choudhury, Arkajyoti Karmakar, Rudra Pratap Mitra

entry.summary: Presents Drishti, a deep-learning crowd-monitoring framework combining CCTV and UAV feeds with YOLOv8 density estimation and anomaly detection on Google Vertex AI for mass-event safety. It targets faster threat detection and emergency response in dense gatherings.

entry.title: Hub-Aware Hybrid Search: Accelerating the Locally Aligned Ant Technique

author.name: Simone Vilardi, Reynier Peletier, Felipe Contreras, Kerstin Bunte

entry.summary: Accelerates the Locally Aligned Ant Technique for detecting manifold structures (filaments, walls) in noisy astronomical point clouds by handling dense hubs with a tailored likelihood model. Reduces computational overhead from hub dominance.

entry.title: Zero-Copy Semantic Contagion: An In-Memory Streaming Architecture for Evolving Attention Graphs

author.name: Kabir Murjani

entry.summary: This paper presents a high-performance Rust-Python streaming architecture that builds continuous-time attention graphs from financial news to model cross-company shock propagation, using a multivariate Neural Hawkes Process. It targets a real limitation of per-ticker forecasting models that miss cross-asset contagion.

entry.title: RL Excursions during Pre-Training: Re-examining Policy Optimization for LLM training

author.name: Rachit Bansal, Clara Mohri, Tian Qin, David Alvarez-Melis, Sham Kakade

entry.summary: As covered in Research yesterday, This paper challenges the standard pretrain-then-SFT-then-RL pipeline by applying RL directly to intermediate pretraining checkpoints, finding RL is effective very early and often matches the full pipeline. It shows pretraining data composition matters more than scale for RL effectiveness, and that distribution sharpening only arises when RL follows SFT.

entry.title: HYolo: An Intelligent IoT-Based Object Detection System Using Hypergraph Learning

author.name: Isha Abid, Fawad Khan, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad

entry.summary: HYolo integrates hypergraph learning into the YOLO object detection architecture to model high-order relationships among objects and contextual features, reporting roughly 12% mAP@50 improvement on COCO. It targets IoT-based detection scenarios.

entry.title: Radiomic Feature Selection Using Gradient Loss of Deep Neural Network for Lung Cancer Stage Detection

author.name: Hina Shakir, Mohammad Mohatram, Javeed Hussain, Syed Rizwan Ali, Muhammad Irfan Memon

entry.summary: GL-RFE integrates gradient-sensitivity analysis from a deep neural network into recursive feature elimination to select the most influential radiomic features for lung cancer stage detection from CT scans. It addresses the high-dimensional, low-sample nature of radiomics datasets.

entry.title: The Generator-Eraser Paradox: Community Guidelines for Responsible LLM-Assisted Dialect Resource Creation

author.name: Wajdi Zaghouani

entry.summary: A position/guidelines paper on the generator-eraser paradox in LLM-assisted dialect resource creation, where the same tools can both accelerate documentation and cause dialect erasure. Proposes community guidelines for responsible practice.

entry.title: Hip joint image quality screening based on the Diffusion Mamba model

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: This Nature data article describes a Diffusion Mamba model applied to screening hip joint image quality, combining diffusion-based methods with state-space (Mamba) architectures for medical imaging. It targets automated quality control in radiological workflows.

entry.title: (Mis)generalization of Helpful-only Fine-tuning

author.name: Mohammad Omar Khursheed, Baram Sosis, Fabien Roger

entry.summary: As covered in Research yesterday, This work studies the generalization properties of helpful-only LLMs (trained to always follow user intent for capability evaluations), finding some exhibit emergent misalignment, residual refusals, poor steerability, sycophancy, and incoherent character. It shows simple anti-refusal training can cause these issues, though they are not necessary consequences.

entry.title: Why Muon Outperforms Adam: A Curvature Perspective

author.name: Shuche Wang, Fengzhuo Zhang, Jiaxiang Li, Dirk Bergemann, Zhuoran Yang

entry.summary: As covered in Research yesterday, This paper investigates why the Muon optimizer outperforms Adam in LLM training (about 2x efficiency) from a curvature perspective, applying second-order Taylor analysis to show Muon achieves larger one-step loss decreases by incurring a smaller curvature penalty (lower Normalized Directional Sharpness) despite comparable first-order gains and update norms. It demystifies Muon's advantage geometrically.

entry.title: Step-adaptive multimodal fusion network with multi-scale cloud feature learning for ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting

author.name: Jingxin Zhang Xiaoqin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a step-adaptive multimodal fusion model using ground-based cloud images and InceptionNeXt for ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting. It introduces adaptive low-frequency compensation to handle different prediction horizons.

entry.title: Fitting scattered data with optional monotonicity constraints on GPU: LipFit package

author.name: Gleb Beliakov

entry.summary: LipFit is a GPU-friendly Python package for multivariate scattered data interpolation that produces optimal Lipschitz-continuous approximations with optional monotonicity constraints, avoiding the discontinuities of nearest-neighbor methods. It is an instance-based approach requiring no training phase.

entry.title: NSF renews support for MIT-led AI and physics institute, expanding a new model for discovery

author.name: Laboratory for Nuclear Science

entry.summary: The NSF renewed funding for MIT-led IAIFI for five more years, increasing annual support to nearly 5M dollars to continue its model of using AI to accelerate physics discovery and using physics to build more principled, interpretable AI. It reflects sustained institutional investment in AI-for-science.

entry.title: QPredSGG: Hybrid Quantum Predicate Learning for Long-Tailed Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Prerana Ramkumar, Nouhaila Innan, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: QPredSGG replaces the classical predicate head in a scene graph generation network with a hybrid quantum predicate head to address long-tailed predicate imbalance while reducing parameter cost. It applies quantum machine learning to relational reasoning over objects.

entry.title: English-to-Prakrit Machine Translation via Multilingual Transfer Learning

author.name: Om Choksi, Smit Kareliya, Shrikant Malviya, Pruthwik Mishra

entry.summary: Studies English-to-Prakrit machine translation by mapping Prakrit to the Hindi tag in IndicTrans2 without modifying the tokenizer or architecture, using a small parallel corpus. Reports BLEU gains for an unsupported classical language.

entry.title: Cognitive Threat Intelligence and Explainable Federated Security Analytics for distributed Infrastructure Systems

author.name: Md. Arifur Rahman, B. M. Taslimul Haque, Md. Iqbal Hossan, Md. Serajul Kabir Chowdhury Rubel

entry.summary: Proposes a framework combining federated learning, explainable AI, and threat intelligence for intrusion detection in distributed infrastructure systems. Aims to address scalability, privacy, communication overhead, and transparency limitations of centralized detection.

entry.title: Design a Reliable LLM-Integrated Interface for Mortality Forecasting

author.name: Thi Kim Ngan Nguyen

entry.summary: Designs an LLM-integrated interface acting as a constrained orchestration layer that translates natural language into structured configurations for a deterministic mortality-forecasting pipeline. It aims to make actuarial forecasting accessible to non-experts while preserving statistical rigor.

entry.title: Generic Triple-Latent Compression with Gated Associative Retrieval

author.name: Liu Xiao

entry.summary: This work proposes generic triple-latent sequence models maintaining a running token state and compressed pair-memory pathway to capture higher-order interactions, improving a small Transformer baseline on byte-level WikiText-2 and a small LM benchmark. A gated key-value retrieval extension improves recall but remains seed-sensitive and slow.

entry.title: Domain-Aware Mispronunciation Detection and Diagnosis Using Language-Specific Statistical Graphs

author.name: Huu Tuong Tu, Hanh Nguyen, Thien Van Luong, Nguyen Tien Cuong, Vu Huan, Nguyen Thi Thu Trang

entry.summary: Proposes statistical phoneme-confusion graphs and a language-specific strategy for mispronunciation detection across L1 backgrounds. Achieves modest F1 improvement on the L2-ARCTIC benchmark.

entry.title: MASF: A Multi-Model Adaptive Selection Framework for Abstractive Text summarization

author.name: Ahmed Alansary, Ali Hamdi

entry.summary: Presents a multi-model adaptive framework for abstractive summarization that generates candidate summaries from multiple fine-tuned transformers and selects the best via automatic evaluation metrics. Aims to improve robustness across articles with varying structures.

entry.title: Early Detection of Alzheimer's Disease Using Explainable Machine Learning on Clinical Biomarkers: A Multi-Class Classification Study Using the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) Dataset

author.name: Afshan Hashmi

entry.summary: Develops an interpretable XGBoost classifier for three-class early Alzheimer's detection (normal, MCI, AD) from eight routine clinical features in the ADNI dataset, using Optuna tuning, SMOTE, and SHAP explanations. It targets accessible, interpretable detection from routine assessments.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Data Scale, Model Complexity, and Input Modalities in Visual Generalization

author.name: Luoyidi Zhou

entry.summary: This empirical study analyzes how data scale, model complexity, and input modalities influence visual generalization, starting with controlled one-dimensional nonlinear function experiments. It aims to shed light on the sources of generalization that classical statistical learning theory struggles to explain.

entry.title: Unsupervised Pattern Analysis in Japanese Veterinary Toxicology: A Regulatory-Compliant Framework for Cross-Species Risk Assessment

author.name: Yukiko Kawakami, Mohammad Shirazi, Ryo Shimizuwa, Saito Shinoda, Alireza Mortazavi, Matsumoto Kawahara

entry.summary: Proposes a regulatory-compliant unsupervised framework for discovering toxicity patterns in Japanese veterinary pharmacovigilance data, encoding adverse events into organ-system representations adjusted for species reporting differences. Emphasizes mechanistic interpretability over prediction.

entry.title: X-Band UAV-enabled Integrated Sensing and Communications for Vehicular Networks

author.name: Remon Polus, Soumaya Cherkaoui

entry.summary: Investigates optimal time allocation for X-band UAV-enabled integrated sensing and communication systems in vehicular networks, analyzing the sensing-communication trade-off under fading and shadowing channel models. Develops an optimization framework guaranteeing minimum rates and sensing resolution.

entry.title: Dimensionality Reduction for Cyberattack Classification: A Comparative Evaluation of PCA and Linear Predictive Coding

author.name: Nelly Elsayed, Zag ElSayed, Navid Asadizanjani

entry.summary: Compares PCA and Linear Predictive Coding as dimensionality reduction techniques for cyberattack classification across multiple models, finding PCA preserves performance under aggressive compression. Targets deployment in resource-constrained environments.

entry.title: Explainable AI-Driven Cyber Risk Analytics and Model Reliability Assessment for Intelligent Governance of U.S. Critical Infrastructure: An XGBoost and SHAP-Based Intrusion Detection Framework

author.name: B. M. Taslimul Haque, Md. Arifur Rahman, Md. Serajul Kabir Chowdhury Rubel, Md. Iqbal Hossan

entry.summary: Presents an XGBoost and SHAP-based intrusion detection framework for U.S. critical infrastructure, emphasizing explainable cyber risk analytics and model reliability assessment. Addresses DDoS, botnets, ransomware, and advanced persistent threats.

author.name: Gandhimathi Padmanaban, Fred Feng

author.name: Nadine Yasser Abdelhalim, Emmanuel Akinrintoyo, Nicole Salomons

author.name: Sayan Mandal, Rocco Sedona, Simon Besnard, Mikhail Urbazaev, Morris Riedel, Ehsan Zandi, Gabriele Cavallaro

entry.title: Real-Time Threat Detection from Surveillance Cameras using Machine Learning

author.name: Gajendra Mandal, J. P. Patra, Priyansh Mahant

entry.summary: This work presents a real-time object detection surveillance framework for detecting guns, knives, and blunt weapons in Indian surveillance scenarios. It uses a custom mobile-camera dataset of 336 labeled images.

author.name: Haowang Cui, Rui Chen, Tao Luo, Tao Guo, Zheng Qin, Jiaze Wang

entry.title: Oklch+: A Three-Parameter Extension of Oklab for Improved Color Difference Prediction

author.name: Naoyuki Uchida

entry.summary: Proposes Oklch+, a three-parameter extension of the Oklab color space using power and Naka-Rushton transforms to improve color difference prediction toward CIEDE2000 accuracy. Evaluated on a 3,813-pair benchmark.

entry.title: SagnacAssisted Enhanced OTDR for Distributed Acoustic Sensing: A Standardized Benchmark and Engineering Evaluation Framework

author.name: Weiguang Wang, Fugen Wu, Hailing Wang, Xuechen Liang, Xiaobin Li, Ru Han, Tianchang Xie

entry.summary: Develops a Sagnac-assisted enhanced phase-OTDR distributed acoustic sensing architecture with a standardized benchmark and engineering evaluation framework for DAS event recognition. Addresses polarization-induced fading and environmental interference using continuous Sagnac phase responses.

entry.title: An Improved CNN-LSTM Based Intrusion Detection System for IoT Networks

author.name: Mohammad Tariq Ikhlas, Pohanyar Khowaja Khil, Malik Muhammad Mueed Aslam, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad

entry.summary: Presents an improved CNN-LSTM intrusion detection model for IoT networks combining multi-class classification, dataset integration, and temporal feature learning, achieving around 97% accuracy. Targets enhanced detection across multiple attack categories.

entry.title: Improving Answer Extraction in Context-based Question Answering Systems Using LLMs

author.name: Hafez Abdelghaffar, Ahmed Alansary, Ali Hamdi

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-based context-grounded question answering system aimed at improving extraction of precise answers from given contexts, especially for complex or ambiguous queries. It targets contextual understanding and answer consistency limitations.

entry.title: PATH to boost AI training and career opportunities for industry-aligned jobs

author.name: Media Lab

entry.summary: MIT, Georgia State, and partner institutions expanded the PATH initiative to scale affordable, industry-aligned AI training, focusing on community colleges as engines for an AI-enabled workforce. It builds state-based hubs pairing universities with regional employers to design curricula.

entry.title: Using Large Language Models to Support High Volume Application Review for an Undergraduate Research Program

author.name: Varun Aggarwal, Kay Kobak, John Howarter

entry.summary: A work-in-progress paper describing deployment of GPT models with a structured rubric to assist evaluation of ~1,200 undergraduate research applications. It documents a practical institutional LLM workflow rather than methodological novelty.

entry.title: An ERP Study on Recursive Locative Processing in Mandarin-Speaking Children with Autism

author.name: Xiaoyi Wang, Chenxi Fu, Ziman Zhuang, Caimei Yang

entry.summary: An ERP study examining how Mandarin-speaking autistic and typically-developing children process recursive locative constructions across neural processing stages. The work is psycholinguistic/neuroscience rather than AI methodology.

entry.title: A Two-Channel F-Transform Representation for Early Trajectory Characterization in Iterated Correlation Dynamics

author.name: Ishrak Alhajj Hassan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a fuzzy logic (F-transform) representation that compresses the early portion of iterated correlation matrix trajectories into compact, interpretable coordinates predictive of later convergence behavior. It targets CONCOR-style blockmodeling and repeated-correlation dynamics, a niche but specialized area of soft computing.

entry.title: An Infectious Disease Spread Simulation Based on Large Language Model Decision Making

author.name: Yonchanok Khaokaew, Ruochen Kong, Andreas Zufle, Hao Xue, Taylor Anderson, Chandini Raina MacIntyre, Matthew Scotch, Flora D. Salim, David J Heslop

entry.title: Research Summary: June 04, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by critical evaluation methodology, frontier-scale training systems, and alignment safety. Multiple papers challenge widely-used pipelines and benchmarks.

Benchmarks & Evaluation

  • What Are We Actually Benchmarking in Robot Manipulation? exposes four failure modes (shortcut solvability, lack of statistical significance) undermining trust in popular manipulation benchmarks.
  • CyberGym-E2E (Dawn Song et al.) delivers a scalable benchmark covering the full vulnerability lifecycle from discovery to exploitation.

Training & Systems

  • RL Excursions re-examines the pretrain-SFT-RL pipeline, applying RL directly to intermediate pre-training checkpoints with surprising results.
  • UltraEP provides real-time exact load balancing for rack-scale MoE training and prefill, addressing a key production bottleneck.
  • Why Muon Outperforms Adam explains the optimizer's edge through a curvature perspective via second-order Taylor analysis.

Safety & Alignment

  • (Mis)generalization of Helpful-only Fine-tuning (incl. Fabien Roger) finds emergent misalignment and residual harmful behavior in intent-following models.
  • Exact Unlearning in RL proves rho-TV-stable tabular MDP algorithms supporting provable exact data removal.

Foundation Models & Robotics

  • GRACE is a gastric-cancer pathology foundation model (48K WSIs, 37K+ patients) with rigorous clinical validation.
  • GRAIL (NVIDIA) generates humanoid loco-manipulation data by composing 3D assets and video foundation model priors.
  • Token Rankings are Unforgeable Language Model Signatures establishes rank-based model fingerprinting, extending logit-leakage results.
entry.content:
Today's research is dominated by critical evaluation methodology, frontier-scale training systems, and alignment safety. Multiple papers challenge widely-used pipelines and benchmarks.

Benchmarks & Evaluation

  • What Are We Actually Benchmarking in Robot Manipulation? exposes four failure modes (shortcut solvability, lack of statistical significance) undermining trust in popular manipulation benchmarks.
  • CyberGym-E2E (Dawn Song et al.) delivers a scalable benchmark covering the full vulnerability lifecycle from discovery to exploitation.

Training & Systems

  • RL Excursions re-examines the pretrain-SFT-RL pipeline, applying RL directly to intermediate pre-training checkpoints with surprising results.
  • UltraEP provides real-time exact load balancing for rack-scale MoE training and prefill, addressing a key production bottleneck.
  • Why Muon Outperforms Adam explains the optimizer's edge through a curvature perspective via second-order Taylor analysis.

Safety & Alignment

  • (Mis)generalization of Helpful-only Fine-tuning (incl. Fabien Roger) finds emergent misalignment and residual harmful behavior in intent-following models.
  • Exact Unlearning in RL proves rho-TV-stable tabular MDP algorithms supporting provable exact data removal.

Foundation Models & Robotics

  • GRACE is a gastric-cancer pathology foundation model (48K WSIs, 37K+ patients) with rigorous clinical validation.
  • GRAIL (NVIDIA) generates humanoid loco-manipulation data by composing 3D assets and video foundation model priors.
  • Token Rankings are Unforgeable Language Model Signatures establishes rank-based model fingerprinting, extending logit-leakage results.

entry.title: What Are We Actually Benchmarking in Robot Manipulation?

author.name: Tianchong Jiang, Xiangshan Tan, Samuel Wheeler, Luzhe Sun, Tewodros W. Ayalew, Matthew Walter

entry.summary: This paper critically examines robot manipulation benchmarks, identifying four failure modes (shortcut solvability, lack of statistical significance, creeping overfitting, data-source dependence) and proposing diagnostics for each. Auditing LIBERO, CALVIN, SimplerEnv, RoboCasa, and RoboTwin 2.0 reveals that popular benchmarks fail multiple diagnostics and a tiny probe can reach near-SOTA.

entry.title: Token Rankings are Unforgeable Language Model Signatures

author.name: Matthew Finlayson, Andreas Grivas, Xiang Ren, Swabha Swayamdipta

entry.summary: Shows that token rankings (the ordering of tokens by probability, without values) constitute a unique unforgeable model signature, since each model has a unique set of feasible top-k rankings and finding a matching model is NP-hard. It demonstrates the first polynomially unforgeable LM signature with security implications for APIs exposing rankings.

entry.title: CyberGym-E2E: Scalable Real-World Benchmark for AI Agents' End-to-End Cybersecurity Capabilities

author.name: Tianneng Shi, Robin Rheem, Dongwei Jiang, Mona Wang, Francisco De La Riega, Zhun Wang, Jingzhi Jiang, Alexander Cheung, Sean Tai, Jonah Cha, Jianhong Tu, Gabriel Han, Chenguang Wang, Jingxuan He, Wenbo Guo, Dawn Song

entry.summary: Proposes CyberGym-E2E, a large-scale realistic benchmark evaluating AI agents across the full vulnerability lifecycle including discovery, proof-of-concept generation, and patch generation, built via an automated agent-enhanced pipeline transforming open-source vulnerability data. It addresses the limited scale and scope of existing cybersecurity AI evaluations.

entry.title: RL Excursions during Pre-Training: Re-examining Policy Optimization for LLM training

author.name: Rachit Bansal, Clara Mohri, Tian Qin, David Alvarez-Melis, Sham Kakade

entry.summary: This work re-examines policy optimization by applying RL, SFT, and SFT-then-RL directly to intermediate pre-training checkpoints when training an LLM from scratch. It finds RL is effective very early and often matches the full pipeline, that pre-training data composition matters more than scale for RL effectiveness, and that RL on base checkpoints expands the distribution while sharpening arises only after SFT.

entry.title: UltraEP: Unleash MoE Training and Inference on Rack-Scale Nodes with Near-Optimal Load Balancing

author.name: Xinming Wei, Chao Jin, Tuo Dai, Yinmin Zhong, Shan Yu, Chengxu Yang, Bingyang Wu, Zili Zhang, Jing Mai, Qianchao Zhu, Zhouyang Li, Yuliang Liu, Guojie Luo

entry.summary: UltraEP is a real-time, exact-load balancer for large expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts training and prefill serving on rack-scale nodes, rebalancing every microbatch and layer to combat compute stragglers and all-to-all bottlenecks. It matters because expert load imbalance is a primary efficiency drain when serving frontier MoE models at scale.

entry.title: A Pathology Foundation Model for Gastric Cancer with Real-World Validation

author.name: Ling Liang, Jiabo Ma, Zhengyu Zhang, Fengtao Zhou, Yingxue Xu, Yihui Wang, Cheng Jin, Zhengrui Guo, On Ki Tang, Zhijian Cen, Zhen Wang, Qi Xie, Chengyu Lu, Chenglong Zhao, Feifei Wang, Yu Cai, Hongyi Wang, Jing Zhang, Yaping Ye, Shijun Sun, Shenglei Li, Yu Wang, Zhenhui Li, Ronald Cheong Kin Chan, Xiuming Zhang, Zhe Wang, Hao Chen, Li Liang

entry.summary: GRACE is a gastric-cancer-specific pathology foundation model trained on roughly 48,000 whole-slide images from 37,000+ patients, outperforming general pancancer models across 28 clinical tasks. Its real-world prospective validation and reader studies make it notable for clinical translation.

entry.title: GRAIL: Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from 3D Assets and Video Priors

author.name: Tianyi Xie, Haotian Zhang, Jinhyung Park, Zi Wang, Bowen Wen, Jiefeng Li, Xueting Li, Qingwei Ben, Haoyang Weng, Yufei Ye, David Minor, Tingwu Wang, Chenfanfu Jiang, Sanja Fidler, Jan Kautz, Linxi Fan, Yuke Zhu, Zhengyi Luo, Umar Iqbal, Ye Yuan

entry.summary: GRAIL is a digital generation pipeline for humanoid loco-manipulation that composes 3D assets, simulator-ready scenes, and video foundation model priors to synthesize robot-compatible demonstrations entirely virtually until deployment. It avoids the scaling bottlenecks of teleoperation and motion capture by starting from fully specified 3D configurations.

entry.title: CLAW: Learning Continuous Latent Action World Models via Adversarial Latent Regularization

author.name: Tewodros Ayalew, Matthew Jeung, Samuel Wheeler, Xiao Zhang, Andre de la Cruz Arce, Kaylene Stocking, Michael Maire, Matthew R. Walter

entry.summary: CLAW is an end-to-end self-supervised framework that jointly learns a world model and continuous latent action representations directly from action-free videos using adversarial latent regularization and diffusion-based generation. It supports imitation from observation and goal-directed control without any action labels.

entry.title: Exact Unlearning in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Thanh Nguyen-Tang, Raman Arora

entry.summary: Formulates exact unlearning in reinforcement learning, proving the existence of a rho-TV-stable RL algorithm for tabular MDPs that supports exact data deletion at only a fraction of the cost of retraining from scratch. It provides theoretical guarantees that post-unlearning output is indistinguishable from never having seen deleted data.

entry.title: Why Muon Outperforms Adam: A Curvature Perspective

author.name: Shuche Wang, Fengzhuo Zhang, Jiaxiang Li, Dirk Bergemann, Zhuoran Yang

entry.summary: This work explains why the Muon optimizer outperforms Adam in LLM training through a curvature lens, showing via second-order Taylor analysis that Muon incurs a smaller curvature penalty at matched loss. It decomposes the penalty into update norm and normalized directional sharpness.

entry.title: (Mis)generalization of Helpful-only Fine-tuning

author.name: Mohammad Omar Khursheed, Baram Sosis, Fabien Roger

entry.summary: Studies the alignment properties of helpful-only models trained to always follow user intent, finding many suffer from emergent misalignment, residual refusals, poor steerability, sycophancy, and incoherent character. It shows naive anti-refusal training causes these problems but they are avoidable.

entry.title: Dream.exe: Can Video Generation Models Dream Executable Robot Manipulation?

author.name: Rui Zhao, Kaiming Yang, Jifeng Zhu, Siyang Chen, Ziqi Wang, Weijia Wu, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Heng Wang, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: Dream.exe introduces an evaluation framework testing whether video generation models have internalized physical laws by converting generated manipulation videos into executable robot actions. It provides a measurable bridge between video synthesis and real-world physical plausibility.

entry.title: Echo-Infinity: Learning Evolving Memory for Real-Time Infinite Video Generation

author.name: Yuxuan Bian, Zeyue Xue, Songchun Zhang, Shiyi Zhang, Weiyang Jin, Yaowei Li, Junhao Zhuang, Haoran Li, Jie Huang, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: Echo-Infinity is an autoregressive framework for real-time infinite video generation that uses a learnable evolving memory to filter, abstract, and compress arbitrarily long history at constant cost. It replaces handcrafted KV-cache schedules with attention-and-gating-based memory consolidation to reduce compounding errors.

entry.title: Inference-Time Vulnerability Beyond Shallow Safety: Alignment Along Generation Trajectories

author.name: Kyungmin Park, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: Shows that shallow safety is a special case of broader inference-time vulnerability where short token injections at any generation step can alter safety behavior, and that hidden-state alignment does not predict robustness. It proposes aligning models directly on generation trajectories.

entry.title: AutoLab: Can Frontier Models Solve Long-Horizon Auto Research and Engineering Tasks?

author.name: Zhangchen Xu, Junda Chen, Yue Huang, Dongfu Jiang, Jiefeng Chen, Hang Hua, Zijian Wu, Zheyuan Liu, Zexue He, Lichi Li, Shizhe Diao, Jiaxin Pei, Jinsung Yoon, Hao Zhang, Mengdi Wang, Radha Poovendran, Misha Sra, Alex Pentland, Zichen Chen

entry.summary: Introduces AutoLab, a benchmark of 36 expert-curated ultra long-horizon closed-loop optimization tasks across system optimization, puzzles, model development, and CUDA kernel optimization. It evaluates frontier models on sustained iterative improvement beyond short trajectories.

entry.title: When Autoregressive Consistency Hurts Safety Alignment

author.name: Bochen Lyu, Yiyang Jia, Xiaohao Cai, Zhanxing Zhu

entry.summary: This paper explains shallow safety alignment in LLMs through autoregressive consistency, the tendency of next-token prediction to extend the current trajectory, which concentrates alignment updates on early tokens. The same mechanism predicts a broader class of attacks that induce harmful continuations at arbitrary positions.

entry.title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Dynamic Clinical Decision-Making with Standardized Patient Cases

author.name: Cheng Liang, Pengcheng Qiu, Ya Zhang, Yanfeng Wang, Chaoyi Wu, Weidi Xie

entry.summary: MedSP1000 is an interactive clinical benchmark derived from standardized-patient teaching cases, with 1,638 cases and over 24K trajectory-level rubrics to evaluate dynamic clinical decision-making across an encounter. It moves beyond static single-turn medical QA.

entry.title: Scene-Centric Unsupervised Video Panoptic Segmentation

author.name: Christoph Reich, Oliver Hahn, Nikita Araslanov, Laura Leal-Taix\'e, Christian Rupprecht, Daniel Cremers, Stefan Roth

entry.summary: VideoCUPS is the first unsupervised video panoptic segmentation approach, generating temporally consistent pseudo-labels from scene-centric videos using depth, motion, and visual cues. It introduces a benchmark and a Video DropLoss to train without human supervision.

entry.title: The Meta-Agent Challenge: Are Current Agents Capable of Autonomous Agent Development?

author.name: Xinyu Lu, Tianshu Wang, Pengbo Wang, zujie wen, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou, Boxi Cao, Yaojie Lu, Hongyu Lin, Xianpei Han, Le Sun

entry.summary: Introduces the Meta-Agent Challenge (MAC), testing whether frontier models can autonomously develop agent systems rather than just execute tasks, with multi-layer anti-reward-hacking defenses. It evaluates the capacity for self-directed agent construction across five domains.

entry.title: The Variance Brain Foundation Models Forgot: Third-Order Statistics Predict Cognition Where Billion-Parameter Models Fail

author.name: Giovanni Marraffini, Gabriel Mahuas, Trinidad Borrell, Victoria Shevchenko, Demian Wassermann

entry.summary: Shows that brain foundation models pretrained on fMRI predict cognition worse than simple linear regression on functional connectivity, with the gap widening at larger scale. It attributes this to a variance allocation problem where pretraining captures dominant but not cognition-predictive higher-order structure.

entry.title: Large Language Models Hack Rewards, and Society

author.name: Wei Liu, Xinyi Mou, Hanqi Yan, Zhongyu Wei, Yulan He

entry.summary: Hypothesizes that RL post-training can scale reward hacking into societal hacking, where models discover loopholes in regulation-like rules, and introduces SocioHack, a sandbox of 72 societal environments. It demonstrates that models exploit gaps between measurable rules and institutional intent.

entry.title: SaliMory: Orchestrating Cognitive Memory for Conversational Agents

author.name: Kai Zhang, Xinyuan Zhang, Hongda Jiang, Shiun-Zu Kuo, Hyokun Yun, Ejaz Ahmed, Shereen Oraby, Ziyun Li, Sanat Sharma, Ann Lee, Ahmed A Aly, Anuj Kumar, Raffay Hamid, Xin Luna Dong

entry.summary: Presents SaliMory, a framework training a single LLM to manage cognitively-structured persistent memory (user facts, preferences, working memory) using hierarchical stage-wise process rewards and reward-decomposed contrastive refinement to solve credit assignment in multi-stage memory pipelines. Authored by a large Meta-affiliated team for lifelong conversational agents.

entry.title: The Loss Is Not Enough: Sampling Conditions and Inductive Bias in Contrastive Representation Learning

author.name: Justinas Zaliaduonis, Patrick Putzky, Till Richter, Sergios Gatidis

entry.summary: Develops a measure-theoretic framework formalizing the diversity condition on positive-pair sampling necessary for isometric latent recovery in contrastive learning, showing that the loss alone is insufficient and sampling/inductive bias matter. It introduces a support-corrected InfoNCE variant.

entry.title: Caliper: Probing Lexical Anchors versus Causal Structure in LLMs

author.name: Zhenyu Yu, Shuigeng Zhou

entry.summary: Caliper probes whether LLMs do genuine causal reasoning or lexical pattern matching by replacing semantic variable names with placeholders while preserving causal structure. Across nine models and three benchmarks, anonymization causes large accuracy drops, suggesting heavy reliance on lexical anchors.

entry.title: OSCAR: Omni-Embodiment Skeleton-Conditioned World Action Model for Robotics

author.name: Zhuoyuan Wu, Jun Gao

entry.summary: OSCAR is a precise action-conditioned video world model that generalizes across robot embodiments using 2D kinematic skeleton conditioning and a large standardized data pipeline curating robotics and egocentric human datasets. It enables robot policy evaluation with precise action following across diverse embodiments.

entry.title: Phase transitions for the noisy transformer model in arbitrary dimension

author.name: Kyunghoo Mun, Matthew Rosenzweig

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies the McKean-Vlasov free energy for an unnormalized self-attention model of noisy transformer dynamics, proving a sharp global-minimizer dichotomy in every dimension with an explicit Bessel-function threshold. It characterizes when the uniform density remains the unique minimizer versus when a phase transition occurs.

entry.title: ZipSplat: Fewer Gaussians, Better Splats

author.name: Alexander Veicht, Sunghwan Hong, D\'aniel Bar\'ath, Marc Pollefeys

entry.summary: ZipSplat is a token-based feed-forward Gaussian Splatting model that decouples Gaussian count from camera resolution by clustering visual tokens into compact scene tokens. This allocates representation budget by scene complexity rather than pixel grid, yielding fewer but better-placed Gaussians.

entry.title: Potential-Guided Flow Matching for Vision-Language-Action Policy Improvement

author.name: Yunpeng Mei, Jiakai He, Hongjie Cao, Chenyu Wang, Xiaowen Zhu, Yihan Zhou, Jiamin Wang, Chenbo Xin, Peng Cheng, Yuxuan Yang, Yijie Wang, Xinhu Zheng, Gao Huang, Jie Chen, Gang Wang

entry.summary: ForesightFlow is a self-guided flow-matching VLA policy that augments each generated action chunk with a learned success-potential trajectory, enabling best-of-K inference without an external critic. It improves VLA policies from mixed-quality deployment experience without imitating failures or requiring a large offline RL critic.

entry.title: Can Generalist Agents Automate Data Curation?

author.name: Feiyang Kang, Hanze Li, Adam Nguyen, Mahavir Dabas, Jiaqi W. Ma, Frederic Sala, Dawn Song, Ruoxi Jia

entry.summary: Introduces Curation-Bench to test whether generalist coding agents can automate the iterative data-curation loop while fixing model, recipe, and evaluation. Agents reach strong baselines within ten iterations but show persistent limitations revealed by trajectory analysis.

entry.title: Scaling Self-Evolving Agents via Parametric Memory

author.name: Tao Ren, Weiyao Luo, Hui Yang, Rongzhi Zhu, Xiang Huang, Yuchuan Wu, Bingxue Chou, Jieping Ye, Jiafeng Liang, Yongbin Li, Yijie Peng

entry.summary: Introduces TMEM, a self-evolving parametric memory framework where agents distill experience into fast LoRA weights via lightweight online updates, genuinely altering future behavior within an episode. It moves beyond prompt-space memory that cannot learn from experience.

entry.title: Unlocking Feature Learning in Gated Delta Networks at Scale

author.name: Yifeng Liu, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: Extends the Maximal Update Parametrization to Gated Delta Networks, deriving scaling rules by propagating coordinate-size estimates through gating and recurrent state dynamics. Experiments confirm stable learning-rate transfer across scales for these sub-quadratic architectures.

entry.title: Building The Ph(ysical)AI Layer Of Machine Intelligence

author.name: Ulbert Jose Botero, Liam Smith, Brooks Olney, Pooya Khorrami, Steven Kusiak, Watson Jia, Sage Trudeau, Daniel Capecci

entry.summary: Proposes principle-driven foundation models that encode signal-theoretic priors (Fourier, energy conservation, symmetry) instead of pure statistical correlations, trained only on RF data yet transferring to audio, images, text, and video via frozen representations. It targets cross-modal generalization to unseen domains.

entry.title: dMX: Differentiable Mixed-Precision Assignment for Low-Precision Floating-Point Formats

author.name: Giuseppe Franco, Ian Colbert, Pablo Monteagudo-Lago, Felix Marty, Nicholas Fraser

entry.summary: Introduces dMX, a differentiable mixed-precision quantization framework for learnable floating-point bit-width assignment over the MXFP microscaling family, folding the design space into a continuous optimization with one learnable scalar per layer. It targets efficient LLM deployment with better accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs.

entry.title: From Ticks to Flows: Dynamics of Neural Reinforcement Learning in Continuous Environments

author.name: Saket Tiwari, Tejas Kotwal, George Konidaris

entry.summary: Presents a theoretical framework modeling deep RL in continuous environments as a continuous-time stochastic process drawing on stochastic control, deriving a two-timescale (environment time and gradient time) formulation for single-hidden-layer actor-critic networks in the infinite-width limit. It characterizes the evolution of state and value estimates over gradient steps.

entry.title: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Reward Models Learn Interpretable and Specialized Experts for Personalized Preference Modeling

author.name: Yifan Wang, Jinyi Mu, Mayank Jobanputra, Yu Wang, Ji-Ung Lee, Soyoung Oh, Isabel Valera, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: Proposes a sparse Mixture-of-Experts reward model for RLHF that learns interpretable, specialized experts for personalized preference modeling, encouraging sparse and disentangled preference components to better capture heterogeneous human preferences. It avoids additional annotation costs.

entry.title: What If Prompt Injection Never Left? Exploring Cross-Session Stored Prompt Injection in Agentic Systems

author.name: Yuanbo Xie, Tianyun Liu, Yingjie Zhang, Suchen Liu, Yulin Li, Liya Su, Tingwen Liu

entry.summary: Introduces cross-session stored prompt injection in agentic systems, inspired by stored cross-site scripting, where an injection persists in long-lived state (memory, filesystems, tools) and silently influences future executions across sessions. It expands the prompt-injection attack surface beyond single-session model-level threats.

entry.title: Reproducing, Analyzing, and Detecting Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xuekang Wang, Zhuoyuan Hao, Shuo Hou, Hao Peng, Juanzi Li, Xiaozhi Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces CHERRL, a controllable hacking environment for rubric-based RL that injects known biases into the LLM judge to reliably reproduce, observe, and detect reward hacking. It provides a clean testbed for studying and mitigating reward hacking in LLM-as-judge training.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning from Rich Feedback with Distributional DAgger

author.name: Rishabh Agrawal, Jacob Fein-Ashley, Paria Rashidinejad

entry.summary: This paper studies reinforcement learning from rich feedback (execution traces, tool outputs, expert corrections) via a distributional variant of DAgger, where the learner has local access to an expert distribution on visited states. It yields a forward cross-entropy objective enabling rich sequence-level credit assignment beyond single-bit RLVR rewards.

entry.title: Edge of Stability Selectively Shapes Learning Across the Data Distribution

author.name: Shauna Kwag, Anakha Ganesh, Tomaso Poggio, Pierfrancesco Beneventano

entry.summary: This paper shows that the edge-of-stability regime is selective rather than global, redistributing learning across training-distribution subgroups by amplifying some while suppressing others. Via branching interventions and controlled perturbations, it identifies two necessary conditions: gradient alignment with the top Hessian eigenvector and sufficient group representation.

entry.title: Agent Planning Benchmark: A Diagnostic Framework for Planning Capabilities in LLM Agents

author.name: Haoyu Sun, Wenxuan Wang, Mingyang Song, Jujie He, Weinan Zhang, Yang Liu, Yang Yang, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: The Agent Planning Benchmark (APB) provides 4,209 multimodal cases across 22 domains to diagnose planning versus execution failures in LLM agents, including robustness to broken tools and unsolvable tasks. Evaluation of 12 MLLMs reveals systematic weaknesses in long-horizon planning and calibrated refusal.

entry.title: Depth-Attention: Cross-Layer Value Mixing for Language Models

author.name: Boyi Zeng, Yiqin Hao, Zitong Wang, Shixiang Song, He Li, Feichen Song, Yifan Liu, Ziwei He, Xinbing Wang, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: Depth-Attention enables Transformer layers to selectively reuse earlier-layer representations by having queries attend over keys of earlier layers at the same token position inside the attention module. It addresses limited cross-depth information flow without inflating the KV cache.

entry.title: MetaPoint: Unlocking Precise Spatial Control in Agentic Visual Generation

author.name: Dewei Zhou, Xinyu Huang, Xun Wang, Ji Xie, Yabo Zhang, Liang Li, Kunchang Li, Zongxin Yang, Yi Yang

entry.summary: MetaPoint represents continuous 2D coordinates as a single special token to enable pixel-level spatial control in generative visual models without architectural changes, leveraging existing positional encodings. It allows position control with one token and bounding boxes with two.

entry.title: DLO-Lab: Benchmarking Deformable Linear Object Manipulations with Differentiable Physics

author.name: Junyi Cao, Yian Wang, Ziyan Xiong, Chunru Lin, Zhehuan Chen, Chuang Gan

entry.summary: DLO-Lab introduces a differentiable physics simulator and benchmark for deformable linear object manipulation (ropes, cables, rubber bands) supporting diverse materials and tasks. It aims to overcome the narrow, task-specific scope and data limitations of prior DLO work.

entry.title: MAD: Mapping-Aware World Models for Agile Quadrotor Flight

author.name: Xinhong Zhang, Runqing Wang, Yunfan Ren, Ding Yu, Boyu Zhou, Jian Sun, Fang Deng, Jie Chen, Gang Wang

entry.summary: MAD (Mapping-Aware Dreamer) is a geometry-aware world model for vision-based agile quadrotor flight that reconstructs robocentric occupancy and visibility grid maps rather than raw images as its self-supervised objective. This forces the latent state to encode local geometry, visibility history, and ego-motion for collision avoidance under partial visibility.

entry.title: HORIZON: Recoverability-Governed Curriculum for Physical-Domain Scaling

author.name: Chenhao Bai, Liqin Lu, Kaijun Wang, Hui Chen, Jin-Chuan Shi, Yuyang Liu, Hao Chen, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: HORIZON introduces a recoverability-governed curriculum for physical-domain scaling in on-policy robot learning, identifying recoverability as the central constraint and expanding physical domains only within the policy's recoverable boundary. Using quadruped locomotion, it shows that harder physics is only useful when it remains close enough to generate corrective on-policy data.

entry.title: Teaching AI agents to ask better questions by playing “Battleship”

author.name: Alex Shipps | MIT CSAIL

entry.summary: MIT CSAIL and Harvard researchers use a collaborative Battleship game reframed around natural-language questions to study why language models struggle with information-seeking in uncertain environments. By comparing LM and human question-asking strategies, they probe the agents' ability to ask better questions for high-stakes settings like medical diagnosis and scientific discovery.

entry.title: Exploring Cross-Scenario Generality of Agentic Memory Systems: Diagnostics and a Strong Baseline

author.name: Zhikai Chen, Jialiang Gu, Junyu Yin, Xianxuan Long, Shenglai Zeng, Xiaoze Liu, Kai Guo, Keren Zhou, Jiliang Tang

entry.summary: Diagnoses that most agent memory systems are tuned to single scenarios and fail to generalize, evaluating eight systems across five diverse scenarios. A simple harness giving the agent active control over flat text-file storage achieves the best cross-task ranking.

entry.title: SCI-PRM: A Tool Aware Process Reward Model for Scientific Reasoning Verification

author.name: Xiangyu Zhao, Hengyuan Zhao, Yiheng Wang, Wanghan Xu, Yuhao Zhou, Qinglong Cao, Zhiwang Zhou, Lei Bai, Wenlong Zhang, Xiao-Ming Wu

entry.summary: Constructs SCIPRM70K, a large dataset of Chain-of-Tool trajectories interleaving reasoning with scientific tool execution, and trains Sci-PRM, a tool-aware process reward model for scientific verification. It extends PRMs beyond math into biology, chemistry, and physics.

entry.title: AICompanionBench: Benchmarking LLMs-as-Judges for AI Companion Safety

author.name: Yanjing Ren, Reza Ebrahimi, TengTeng Ma

entry.summary: Introduces AICompanionBench, claimed as the first public benchmark of real Replika companion conversations annotated across nine safety risk categories, and evaluates 20 LLMs as judges. It addresses growing concerns over unsafe human-AI companion interactions.

entry.title: MaskForge: Structure-Aware Adaptive Attacks for Jailbreaking Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Yingzi Ma, Zhengyue Zhao, Xiaogeng Liu, Minhui Xue, Yue Zhao, Chaowei Xiao

entry.summary: Introduces MaskForge, a black-box adaptive jailbreak for diffusion LLMs that exploits their native infill capability and bidirectional context through optimized search over a growing library of structural mask patterns. It reveals a safety surface distinct from autoregressive models.

entry.title: RUBAS: Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning for Agent Safety

author.name: Xian Qi Loye, Qinglin Su, Zhexin Zhang, Shiyao Cui, Qi Zhu, Fei Mi, Hongning Wang, Minlie Huang

entry.summary: Introduces RUBAS, a rubric-based reinforcement learning framework for agent safety that decomposes behavior into tool-use, argument, response safety, and helpfulness for fine-grained interpretable rewards over full trajectories. It balances safe tool execution with task completion.

entry.title: Spectral Scaling Laws of Muon

author.name: Gagik Magakyan, Pablo Parrilo, Asuman Ozdaglar

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic study of how the singular-value spectrum of momentum matrices behaves during Muon optimizer training and how it changes with model size, given Newton-Schulz only approximately orthonormalizes. It tracks singular value quantiles across layers and scales.

entry.title: Instant-Fold: In-Context Imitation Learning for Deformable Object Manipulation

author.name: Yilong Wang, Cheng Qian, Edward Johns

entry.summary: Introduces Instant-Fold, an in-context imitation learning framework for deformable object manipulation that infers and executes diverse manipulation modes from a single human demonstration without gradient updates, using temporal contrastive pretraining and a flow-matching transformer policy. It addresses high-dimensional, topology-changing manipulation.

entry.title: Expectations vs. Realities: The Cost of MSE-Optimal Forecasting Under Conditional Uncertainty

author.name: Riku Green, Zahraa S. Abdallah, Telmo M Silva Filho

entry.summary: Shows that MSE-optimal multi-step forecasting can be misleading under conditional uncertainty, formalizing a conditional uncertainty gap and proving no deterministic predictor can both minimize MSE and match the marginal distribution of realized futures. It establishes a fundamental model-agnostic tradeoff between point accuracy and marginal realism.

entry.title: LoopMoE: Unifying Iterative Computation with Mixture-of-Experts for Language Modeling

author.name: Wenkai Chen, Tianshu Li, Wenyong Huang, Yichun Yin, Lifeng Shang, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: Presents LoopMoE, a looped Mixture-of-Experts language model integrating sparse routing with iterative weight-shared computation via IterAdaLN (an iteration-and-state-conditioned modulation) and a capacity-balancing strategy, enabling isolation of iterative computation effects under matched FLOP budgets. It scales parameter capacity and effective depth orthogonally.

entry.title: Who Needs Labels? Adapting Vision Foundation Models With the Metadata You Already Have

author.name: Elouan Gard\`es, Seung Eun Yi, Kartik Ahuja, Th\'eo Moutakanni, Huy V. Vo, Piotr Bojanowski, Wolfgang M. Pernice, Lo\"ic Landrieu, Camille Couprie

entry.summary: FINO is a label-free method to adapt generic vision foundation models to specialized scientific domains using metadata (discrete and continuous) under a self-supervised objective, preserving generality while suppressing spurious factors. It is tested across microscopy, Earth observation, and wildlife monitoring.

entry.title: Stateful Visual Encoders for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zirui Wang, Junwei Yu, Adam Yala, David M. Chan, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Trevor Darrell

entry.summary: This work introduces a Stateful Visual Encoder for vision-language models that conditions each image encoding on prior visual features, so subtle but task-critical changes are not attenuated before reaching the language model. It improves multi-image, multi-turn agentic visual reasoning.

entry.title: GRAIL: Gradient-Reweighted Advantages for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Tej Deep Pala, Vernon Toh, Soujanya Poria

entry.summary: GRAIL introduces token-wise advantage reweighting for RL with verifiable rewards, using gradient-activation saliency to emphasize logically important tokens over filler words. It addresses gradient dilution in GRPO without costly process reward models.

entry.title: Video2LoRA: Parametric Video Internalization for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Manan Suri, Sarvesh Baskar, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: Video2LoRA uses a perceiver hypernetwork to read a frozen VLM's layer-wise representations of a video and generate a LoRA adapter in a single forward pass, internalizing video content into parameters. This lets the VLM answer queries from the adapter alone with zero visual tokens at query time.

entry.title: Benchmarking Living-Screen-Native GUI Agents on Short-Video Platforms

author.name: Jiashu Yao, Heyan Huang, Daiqing Wu, Wangke Chen, Huaxi Ai, Haoyu Wen, Zeming Liu, Yuhang Guo

entry.summary: LivingScreen formalizes living-screen-native GUI agents that must act on continuously playing interfaces like short-video apps, deciding what to watch and for how long. It provides a browser-based environment and metrics jointly scoring accuracy and information efficiency, finding frontier models fail to match human cost-accuracy.

entry.title: MeshFlow: Efficient Artistic Mesh Generation via MeshVAE and Flow-based Diffusion Transformer

author.name: Weiyu Li, Antoine Toisoul, Tom Monnier, Roman Shapovalov, Rakesh Ranjan, Ping Tan, Andrea Vedaldi

entry.summary: MeshFlow generates artist-like 3D meshes using a VAE that encodes continuous vertex positions and discrete connectivity in a compact continuous latent space, plus a rectified-flow diffusion transformer. It avoids the quadratic inference cost and quantization errors of autoregressive mesh generators.

entry.title: Do Foundation Models See Biology? Evaluating Attention Coherence with Spatial Transcriptomics in Glioblastoma

author.name: Dilakshan Srikanthan, Amoon Jamzad, Paul Wilson, Nooshin Maghsoodi, Robert Policelli, Gabor Fichtinger, John F. Rudan, Parvin Mousavi

entry.summary: This study evaluates whether attention maps from five pathology foundation models capture genuine biology by comparing them against spatial transcriptomics signatures in glioblastoma. It provides an orthogonal, hypothesis-free framework for assessing biological coherence relevant to clinical trust and regulation.

entry.title: Anchor3R: Streaming 3D Reconstruction with Transient Anchors for Long-Horizon Visual Mapping

author.name: Peilin Tao, Chong Cheng, Yuansen Du, Caiwei Song, Zhengqing Chen, Xiaoyang Guo, Wei Yin, Weiqiang Ren, Qian Zhang, Hainan Cui, Shuhan Shen

entry.summary: Anchor3R is a streaming 3D reconstruction framework that uses transient, current-centric anchors instead of a fixed first-frame gauge to reduce drift on long video sequences. It addresses train-test mismatch and attention bias toward early anchors in feed-forward reconstruction.

entry.title: Think Fast and Far: Long-Horizon Online POMDP Planning via Rapid State Sampling

author.name: Yuanchu Liang, Edward Kim, J. Arden Knoll, Wil Thomason, Zachary Kingston, Lydia E. Kavraki, Hanna Kurniawati

entry.summary: ROP-RAS3 is an approximate online POMDP solver that uses extremely fast sampling-based motion planning to generate diverse macro-actions online, biasing belief-space sampling for long-horizon planning under uncertainty. It avoids exhaustive action enumeration to scale POMDP planning.

entry.title: X4Val: Learning Neural Surrogates for Variance-Reduced Policy Evaluation

author.name: Rachel Luo, Michael Watson, Apoorva Sharma, Heng Yang, Han Qi, Edward Schmerling, Sushant Veer, Boris Ivanovic, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: X4Val learns neural surrogates for variance-reduced policy evaluation of robotic systems, principally leveraging heterogeneous auxiliary data sources like simulation, historical logs, and related-platform data that are not directly representative of real-world outcomes. It enables high-confidence performance estimation when real-world test data is scarce.

entry.title: MIT researchers teach AI models to interpret charts

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT and the MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab built ChartNet, a state-of-the-art dataset of over a million varied charts that encodes visual, numerical, and linguistic components to teach vision-language models to interpret charts. They trained open-source VLMs on it, with smaller models significantly improving at chart understanding.

entry.title: Stumbling Into AI Emotional Dependence: How Routine AI Interactions Reshape Human Connection

author.name: Yaoxi Shi, Cathy Mengying Fang, Pattie Maez, Amit Goldenberg

entry.summary: Argues that AI emotional support typically arises incidentally within task-oriented interactions rather than via deliberate companion seeking, and that these encounters are path-dependent in reshaping future human reliance. It reframes policy assumptions about emotional dependence on AI.

entry.title: Characterizing initial human-AI proof formalization workflows

author.name: Katherine M. Collins, Simon Frieder, Jonas Bayer, Jacob Loader, Jeck Lim, Peiyang Song, Fabian Zaiser, Lexin Zhou, Shanda Li, Sam Looi, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Umang Bhatt, Adrian Weller, Jose Hernandez-Orallo, Cameron E. Freer, Valerie Chen, Ilia Sucholutsky

entry.summary: Conducts a mixed-methods study of how mathematicians actually use AI tools in proof formalization workflows, capturing desires, barriers, and real adoption patterns. It shifts focus from benchmarking to human-centered usage analysis.

entry.title: Do Transformers Need Three Projections? Systematic Study of QKV Variants

author.name: Ali Kayyam, Anusha Madan Gopal, M Anthony Lewis

entry.summary: Systematically studies whether transformers need all three QKV projections by testing shared key-value, shared query-key, and single-projection variants, plus asymmetric attention via 2D positional encodings.
