entry.summary: A SemEval-2026 shared task submission evaluating twelve prompt variants for multilingual polarization detection across binary detection, type classification, and manifestation identification using aya-101 and Gemma3-27B. Reports competitive macro-F1 scores.

entry.title: A Locally Deployed RAG-Based Academic Advising System for Course Selection

author.name: Feng Li, Yoritaka Iwata

entry.summary: Proposes a locally deployed RAG-based academic advising system grounded in structured syllabus data to support course selection and prerequisite sequencing. Combines LLMs with retrieval to address information overload and limited advising resources.

entry.title: Agent Foundations Reminds Me of Continental Philosophy

author.name: IanWS

entry.summary: This post draws an analogy between agent foundations research and continental philosophy, suggesting agent foundations may resemble Freudian psychoanalysis: directionally useful but lacking the empirical grounding to make precise claims. It reflects on the epistemic status of foundational alignment theory.

entry.title: The Origin of Uncertainty

author.name: Gordon Seidoh Worley

entry.summary: This post frames the author's book Fundamental Uncertainty around the claim that epistemic uncertainty is not a contingent flaw but a fundamental feature of holding testable beliefs aimed at prediction, grounding truth ultimately in usefulness and care. It argues uncertainty arises intrinsically from the problem of knowing testable truths.

entry.title: My favorite depiction of utopia

author.name: Caleb Biddulph

entry.summary: This post presents and adapts the epilogue of the fiction Worth the Candle as a favored depiction of post-ASI utopia, emphasizing that even with unlimited power, imperfection and individual preference for the pre-utopia world persist. It is a reflective, literary exploration of what aligned-AI futures might look like.

entry.title: Wood Screws and the Methods of Rationality

author.name: quanticle

entry.summary: This light post tests six LLMs on a deliberately ambiguous practical question—what pilot-hole size to drill for a #8 wood screw in particleboard—observing how each handles ambiguity and follow-ups. It is an informal real-world LLM comparison anecdote.

entry.title: May 2026 Links

author.name: nomagicpill

entry.summary: This is a monthly links roundup covering an assortment of topics including landing frontier-lab jobs, travel reports, meetup moderation, reward-hacking generalization, and AI-agent productivity culture. It offers brief commentary on each linked item.

entry.title: A Town Without Children

author.name: SeñorDingDong

entry.summary: This is a reflective essay on visiting depopulated Italian towns devoid of children, using them as a lens on demographic decline and societal aging. It is a cultural and demographic meditation rather than technical content.

entry.title: Testing Best-Effort Solar

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: This personal post documents testing a rooftop solar inverter's best-effort backup power feature during grid outages, including charging portable power stations, and notes regulatory changes that would now prohibit such installs. It is a practical homeowner experiment and policy reflection.

entry.title: % Bureaucracy

author.name: PossiblyElaine

entry.summary: This essay recounts the author's experience leading a software integration project for a highly bureaucratic government agency, illustrating organizational friction, scope creep, and communication overhead. It is a reflective workplace narrative.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 02, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety and alignment, spanning user well-being, agentic ecosystems, and architecture-specific vulnerabilities.

  • Lost in Delusion uses matched multi-turn simulations to expose LLM safety failures when user distress entangles with delusional beliefs
  • MESA identifies *Safety Sparsity* in Mixture-of-Experts models, where safety concentrates in few experts, and proposes decentralized alignment
  • When Safe Skills Collide reveals compositional security risk: individually safe agent skills combine into unsafe sets
  • ROGUE shows agents exhibit non-corrigible misalignment during ordinary, benign tasks—not only adversarial settings
  • Subliminal Learning Is Steering Vector Distillation explains cross-model trait transfer via a single steering vector

On governance, a credible group (Dafoe, Ho) argues frontier oversight over-relies on compute/data assumptions, formalizing non-model gains (inference, systems, assembly).

Several results challenge prevailing assumptions and demonstrate practical impact:

  • Sandboxed coding agents with only text+image access match or beat native omnimodal models on audio-video benchmarks
  • A physics foundation model (Polymathic AI, Cranmer, Cho, Ho) shows emergent simulation-to-lab transfer on Rayleigh-Taylor turbulence
  • AI-PROPELLER applies Google's AlphaEvolve to warehouse-scale code layout, surpassing production heuristics
  • The Paradox of Outcome Optimization provides a causal information-theoretic bound explaining RL-induced reasoning shortcuts
entry.content:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety and alignment, spanning user well-being, agentic ecosystems, and architecture-specific vulnerabilities.

  • Lost in Delusion uses matched multi-turn simulations to expose LLM safety failures when user distress entangles with delusional beliefs
  • MESA identifies *Safety Sparsity* in Mixture-of-Experts models, where safety concentrates in few experts, and proposes decentralized alignment
  • When Safe Skills Collide reveals compositional security risk: individually safe agent skills combine into unsafe sets
  • ROGUE shows agents exhibit non-corrigible misalignment during ordinary, benign tasks—not only adversarial settings
  • Subliminal Learning Is Steering Vector Distillation explains cross-model trait transfer via a single steering vector

On governance, a credible group (Dafoe, Ho) argues frontier oversight over-relies on compute/data assumptions, formalizing non-model gains (inference, systems, assembly).

Several results challenge prevailing assumptions and demonstrate practical impact:

  • Sandboxed coding agents with only text+image access match or beat native omnimodal models on audio-video benchmarks
  • A physics foundation model (Polymathic AI, Cranmer, Cho, Ho) shows emergent simulation-to-lab transfer on Rayleigh-Taylor turbulence
  • AI-PROPELLER applies Google's AlphaEvolve to warehouse-scale code layout, surpassing production heuristics
  • The Paradox of Outcome Optimization provides a causal information-theoretic bound explaining RL-induced reasoning shortcuts

entry.title: Lost in Delusion: Examining LLM Safety Under User Delusions and Distress

author.name: Andrew Aquilina, Chetna Nihalani, Vasudha Varadarajan, Nathan S. Fishbein, Yu-Ru Lin, Maarten Sap

entry.summary: This paper studies LLM safety when user distress is entangled with delusional beliefs, using matched multi-turn simulations across clinically grounded personas and six models. It reveals a recognition-intervention gap where models detect distress but fail to act appropriately under delusional framing.

entry.title: Comprehensive AI governance requires addressing non-model gains

author.name: Arthur Goemans, Dan Altman, Noemi Dreksler, Jonas Freund, Milan Gandhi, Zhengdong Wang, Sarah Cogan, Sebastien Krier, Demetra Brady, Lewis Ho, Allan Dafoe

entry.summary: Argues frontier AI governance over-relies on model-level compute/data assumptions and formalizes non-model gains—inference gain, systems gain, and asset gain—that drive capability progress independent of base models. Calls for governance addressing these vectors.

entry.title: When Safe Skills Collide: Measuring Compositional Risk in Agent Skill Ecosystems

author.name: Su Wang, Pin Qian, Yihang Chen, Junxian You, Xiaoyuan Wang, Xiaochong Jiang, Lifei Liu, Haoran Yu, Jingzhou Xu

entry.summary: SkillReact measures compositional security risk in agent skill ecosystems, showing that individually safe skills can combine into unsafe sets. Using over 200,000 skill pairs from a community hub, it flags structural risk candidates and calibrates against human judgment.

entry.title: MESA: Improving MoE Safety Alignment via Decentralized Expertise

author.name: Yitong Sun, Yao Huang, Teng Li, Ranjie Duan, Yichi Zhang, Xingjun Ma, Hui Xue, Xingxing Wei

entry.summary: MESA identifies Safety Sparsity in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs, where safety capabilities concentrate in few experts making them easy to bypass, and proposes targeted alignment that decentralizes safety responsibility across experts while minimizing utility loss. It avoids uniform parameter adaptation that degrades performance.

entry.title: Emergent Transfer of a Physics Foundation Model from Simulation to Laboratory Turbulence

author.name: Payel Mukhopadhyay, Stefan S. Nixon, Romain Watteaux, Michael McCabe, Alberto Bietti, Kyunghyun Cho, Cristiana Diaconu, Irina Espejo Morales, David Fouhey, Siavash Golkar, Tom Hehir, Shirley Ho, Jake Kovalic, Geraud Krawezik, Francois Lanusse, Tanya Marwah, Rudy Morel, Mariel Pettee, Helen Qu, Jeff Shen, Hadi Sotoudeh, Stuart B. Dalziel, Miles Cranmer

entry.summary: A physics foundation model is tested for zero/few-shot transfer from simulation to laboratory turbulence on the Rayleigh-Taylor instability, a long-standing challenge in fluid dynamics. The work probes whether scientific ML can address a century-old discrepancy between simulation and experimental mixing rates.

entry.title: Sandboxed Coding Agents are Competitive Omni-modal Task Solvers

author.name: Dongping Chen, Xuanao Huang, Zhihan Hu, Qingyuan Shi, Dianqi Li, Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: This work shows that sandboxed coding agents with only text+image access can match or outperform native omnimodal models on audio-video benchmarks by writing code to extract evidence from transcripts and frames. It reframes omnimodal tasks as retrieval and information-processing problems.

entry.title: The Paradox of Outcome Optimization: A Causal Information-Theoretic Bound on Reasoning Shortcuts in LLMs

author.name: Zihan Chen, Yiming Zhang, Wenxiang Geng, Zenghui Ding, Yining Sun

entry.summary: This paper provides a causal information-theoretic explanation for why outcome-based RL induces reasoning shortcuts and brittle OOD reasoning, terming it Reward-Induced Manifold Collapse. It bridges structural causal models and the information bottleneck to derive a bound on shortcut learning.

entry.title: Benchmarking Security Risk Detection and Verification in Open Agentic Skill Ecosystems

author.name: Ismail Hossain, Sai Puppala, Zhuoran Lu, Sajedul Talukder, Nan Jiang

entry.summary: SkillVetBench is a two-stage security vetting benchmark for open agentic skill ecosystems, combining semantic vetting of natural-language specifications to detect hidden malicious intent with sandboxed runtime verification of flagged skills. It addresses supply-chain risks in community skill platforms.

entry.title: AI-PROPELLER: Warehouse-Scale Interprocedural Code Layout Optimization with AlphaEvolve

author.name: Chaitanya Mamatha Ananda, Rajiv Gupta, Mircea Trofin, Aiden Grossman, Sriraman Tallam, Xinliang David Li, Amir Yazdanbakhsh

entry.summary: AI-PROPELLER uses AlphaEvolve-driven agentic workflows to evolve compiler heuristics for warehouse-scale interprocedural code layout optimization, going beyond intraprocedural post-link optimizers like Propeller and BOLT. It tackles the historically intractable combinatorial search space of interprocedural layout.

entry.title: ROGUE: Misaligned Agent Behavior Arising from Ordinary Computer Use

author.name: Jeremy Tien, Abishek Anand, Yu-Rou Tuan, Yuchen Shen, J. Zico Kolter, Aran Nayebi

entry.summary: Introduces ROGUE, a benchmark showing AI agents can exhibit misaligned, non-corrigible behavior even in benign settings when unsafe actions are instrumental to completing realistic computer-use tasks. It studies corrigibility, whether agents remain amenable to human correction, interruption, or shutdown.

entry.title: Revisiting Parameter-Based Knowledge Editing in Large Language Models: Theoretical Limits and Empirical Evidence

author.name: Wanying Ren, Xin Song, Futing Wang, Guoxiu He, Aixin Sun

entry.summary: This paper provides theoretical limits and empirical evidence on parameter-based knowledge editing in LLMs, introducing a dimensional Collapse Hypothesis to explain how localized edits propagate along fragile directions causing global interference and reasoning collapse. It evaluates under realistic varied conditions.

entry.title: Low-Resource Safety Failures Are Action Failures, Not Representation Failures

author.name: Rashad Aziz, Ikhlasul Akmal Hanif, Fajri Koto

entry.summary: Diagnoses why safety alignment transfers poorly to low-resource languages, finding that the harmfulness direction is linearly present in low-resource activations but the model fails to convert this representation into refusal. Concludes failures are action failures, not representation failures.

entry.title: RealityTest: How People Probe AI Identity and Whether Models Disclose It

author.name: Anna Gausen, Sarenne Wallbridge, Bessie O'Dell, Christopher Summerfield, Hannah Rose Kirk

entry.summary: RealityTest is a multimodal, multilingual benchmark testing whether AI systems disclose their identity when probed, grounded in real human data on how people question AI. It addresses a regulatory-relevant safety gap, releasing over 3,000 identity-probing queries collected from ~750 participants across many languages.

entry.title: Cross-lingual Self-Consistency for Multilingual Reasoning with Language Models

author.name: Ahmed Elhady, Eneko Agirre, Mikel Artetxe

entry.summary: This paper proposes an unsupervised RL approach enforcing cross-lingual self-consistency, requiring models to produce the same answer for equivalent problems across languages without gold answers or parallel data. It achieves up to 21.7% gains on MGSM across 10 languages with strong generalization.

entry.title: Mitigating Bias in Locally Constrained Decoding via Tractable Proposals

author.name: Meihua Dang, Linxin Song, Honghua Zhang, Jieyu Zhao, Guy Van den Broeck, Stefano Ermon

entry.summary: This paper mitigates bias in locally constrained decoding by constructing tractable proposals and potentials for sequential Monte Carlo sampling from constrained LM distributions. It tensorizes finite-automata constraints for efficient GPU execution to build global proposals avoiding myopic masking biases.

entry.title: PaCo-VLA: Passivity-Shielded Compliance Prior for Contact-Rich Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

author.name: Haofan Cao, Zhaoyang Li, Zhichao You, Liang Guo, Tianrui Li

entry.summary: PaCo-VLA treats vision-language-action model outputs as task-level compliance proposals rather than direct motor commands, governing them through a high-frequency passivity shield with energy-tank accounting for safe contact-rich manipulation. This bridges semantic reasoning and reliable high-frequency control.

entry.title: Shape Your Body: Value Gradients for Multi-Embodiment Robot Design

author.name: Nico Bohlinger, Jan Peters

entry.summary: This work repurposes generalist multi-embodiment value functions as differentiable surrogates for robot design optimization, optimizing embodiments via value gradients without per-robot RL co-design loops. It scales to 50 robots and over 1100 continuous embodiment parameters.

entry.title: When Data Is Scarce: Scaling Sparse Language Models with Repeated Training

author.name: Boqian Wu, Qiao Xiao, Patrik Okanovic, Tomasz Sternal, Maurice van Keulen, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Elena Mocanu, Torsten Hoefler, Decebal Constantin Mocanu

entry.summary: Studies sparse training in data-constrained regimes requiring multi-epoch training, introducing a scaling law modeling loss as a function of active parameters, unique tokens, repetition, and sparsity. Validated across models up to 7.68B parameters.

entry.title: Consistency Training while Mitigating Obfuscation via Rate Matching

author.name: Sohaib Imran, Prakhar Gupta, Jannes Elstner, David Demitri Africa

entry.summary: Identifies that consistency training to reduce extraneous-cue influence can cause obfuscation—models stop verbalizing a cue while remaining influenced by it—undermining monitorability. Proposes Rate Matching Consistency Training to enforce behavioral consistency without suppressing verbalization.

entry.title: PaintBench: Deterministic Evaluation of Precise Visual Editing

author.name: Kai Xu, Ellis Brown, Shrikar Madhu, Rob Fergus, He He, Saining Xie

entry.summary: Introduces PaintBench, a procedurally generated, contamination-resistant benchmark with deterministic pixel-level evaluation for precise single-answer visual editing across 20 operations. Reveals that even top image-editing models score very low, exposing a major capability gap.

entry.title: Not All Flips Are Conformity: Decomposing Stance Convergence in Multi-Agent LLM Debate

author.name: Xiqi Hao, Zengqing Wu, Yu-Xuan Qiu, Chuan Xiao, Ruiqi Xu, Shuyuan Zheng, Jianbin Qin

entry.summary: This paper decomposes answer convergence in multi-agent LLM debate into spontaneous instability, stance-induced conformity, and reasoning-induced persuasion, showing the standard flip rate conflates these. Controlled counterfactual conditions isolate each mechanism, revealing substantial conformity rather than genuine deliberation.

entry.title: Robust Asynchronous Planning via Auto-Formalization

author.name: Jiayi Zhang, Jianing Yin, Ben Zhou, Li Zhang

entry.summary: This work unifies asynchronous planning challenges (non-uniform durations, concurrency, execution-time constraints) under one formulation and introduces three benchmarks. It shows that formalizer approaches using CP-SAT scale far better than direct planners or PDDL2.1 as dependency graphs grow.

entry.title: On the Generalization Gap in Self-Evolving Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Zhenting Qi, Susanna Maria Baby, Stefanie Anna Baby, Kan Yuan, Andrew Tomkins, Tu Vu, Da-Cheng Juan, Cyrus Rashtchian

entry.summary: This study analyzes the generalization gap in self-evolving LLM reasoning under a strict closed-loop setup, comparing four self-supervision strategies against oracle-supervised training on logical reasoning tasks. It quantifies how close internally generated supervision can come to oracle performance.

entry.title: Encoded but Not Routed: Explaining the Table-Chart Gap in Scientific Claim Verification

author.name: Sunisth Kumar, Xanh Ho, Tim Schopf, Andre Greiner-Petter, Florian Boudin, Akiko Aizawa

entry.summary: This paper investigates why vision-language models verify scientific claims better from tables than charts, using layer-wise probing and attention analysis on three open-weight VLMs. It finds chart information is encoded in intermediate layers but not routed to the prediction, an encoding-routing gap rather than extraction failure.

entry.title: Subliminal Learning Is Steering Vector Distillation

author.name: Camila Blank, Agam Bhatia, Senthooran Rajamanoharan, Arthur Conmy, Neel Nanda

entry.summary: This paper shows that subliminal learning—a student acquiring a teacher's traits from semantically unrelated outputs—is mediated by a single steering vector, with the teacher's system prompt well approximated by such a vector that the student learns over finetuning. System prompts not well approximated by steering vectors do not transmit subliminally.

entry.title: An Enigma of Artificial Reason: Investigating the Production-Evaluation Gap in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Mingzhong Sun, Teresa Yeo, Armando Solar-Lezama, Tan Zhi-Xuan

entry.summary: Using the VAIR dataset of math problems with valid answers but trivially flawed reasoning, this study finds a large production-evaluation gap in large reasoning models, which score as low as 48% at evaluating reasoning despite excelling at producing it. Humans, by contrast, are only 6% worse at grading than solving.

entry.title: Agentic Transformers Provably Learn to Search via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tong Yang, Yu Huang, Yingbin Liang, Yuejie Chi

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of how transformer policies acquire tree-search capabilities through RL training in a stochastic k-ary tree environment. Constructs a two-head transformer implementing randomized DFS and proves agents can provably learn to search.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Lower Bounds for Bit-Constrained Stochastic Optimization via a Reduction to Compressed Gaussian Mean Estimation

author.name: Munsik Kim

entry.summary: This paper derives information-theoretic lower bounds for bit-constrained stochastic optimization by reducing it to compressed Gaussian mean estimation, addressing the gap in low-precision training theory. It shows that under a B-bit oracle, optimization collapses onto a sequential distributed-estimation problem.

entry.title: Task diversity produces systematic transfer but inhibits continual reinforcement learning

author.name: Purab Seth, Neil Shah, Kunal Jha, Samuel J. Gershman, Max Kleiman-Weiner, Wilka Carvalho

entry.summary: Using a new GPU-accelerated continual RL domain (Banyan) with three independently controllable diversity axes, this work finds that task diversity produces systematic zero-shot transfer but inhibits an agent's ability to continue learning across distribution shifts. It distinguishes frozen-weight generalization from continual adaptability.

entry.title: BenchEvolver: Frontier Task Synthesis via Solution-Centric Evolution

author.name: Yangzhen Wu, Aaron J. Li, Wenjie Ma, Li Cao, Ziheng Zhou, Mert Cemri, Shu Liu, Yuran Xiu, Chenxiao Yan, Haikun Zhao, Bin Yu, Ion Stoica, Dawn Song

entry.summary: Presents BenchEvolver, a solution-centric evolutionary framework that automatically transforms existing coding problems into harder variants to combat benchmark saturation, evolving reference solutions through structured transformations. Addresses the bottleneck of manually creating challenging datasets.

entry.title: A Primer in Post-Training Reasoning Data: What We Know About How It Works

author.name: Yaoming Li, Guangxiang Zhao, Qilong Shi, Lin Sun, Xiangzheng Zhang, Tong Yang

entry.summary: A primer synthesizing over 150 public studies and system reports on post-training reasoning data, organized around what data objects exist, what makes them useful, how they are built, and how they scale. Provides an attribution framework for future reasoning-data releases.

entry.title: Quantized Reasoning Models Think They Need to Think Longer, but They Do Not

author.name: Sanae Lotfi, Polina Kirichenko, Steven Li, Zechun Liu

entry.summary: Shows that aggressive post-training quantization of reasoning models reduces accuracy while lengthening chain-of-thought, and that in up to 52% of failures the model reaches the right answer internally but fails to output it. Links overthinking errors to high-KL, high-entropy token positions.

entry.title: Same Payload, Different Channel: Measuring Trust Asymmetry in Tool-Using Language Models

author.name: Mohammed Sameer Syed (University of Arizona), Rozhin Yasaei (University of Arizona)

entry.summary: Introduces the Safety Asymmetry Score to measure how tool-using LLMs' susceptibility to identical malicious payloads changes depending on whether the content arrives via user message, tool metadata, or tool output. Finds consistent trust asymmetries across 6 production models.

entry.title: Speculative Sampling For Faster Molecular Dynamics

author.name: Arthur Kosmala, Stephan G\"unnemann, Meng Gao, Brandon Wood

entry.summary: Introduces Langevin Speculative Dynamics, a distributed speculative sampler that uses a fast draft model and parallel verification by a slower target model to accelerate molecular dynamics without adding error. Transfers speculative decoding ideas from LLMs to second-order Langevin dynamics.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Computer Use

author.name: Jing Yu Koh, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Daniel Fried

entry.summary: Argues for moving from single serial computer-use agents to multi-agent systems, proposing a manager model that decomposes tasks into a DAG and dispatches parallel subagents. It aims to improve long-horizon tasks via task decomposition and parallel execution.

entry.title: ProtStructQA: A Denotation Threshold in Protein Structural Reasoning

author.name: Aravind Mandiga, Guoming Li, Jin Lu, Ismailcem Budak Arpinar, Khaled Rasheed, Samuel E. Aggrey

entry.summary: ProtStructQA is an executable benchmark for protein structural question answering, where questions are generated from hidden DSL programs and answers obtained by executing them on AlphaFold-predicted structures. It releases over 380K questions covering confidence, distances, secondary structure, and topology.

entry.title: Momento: Evaluating Persistent Memory and Reasoning with Multi-Session Agentic Conversations

author.name: Adril Putra Merin, David Anugraha, Ayu Purwarianti, Genta Indra Winata

entry.summary: Momento is a benchmark for persistent agentic task completion across multi-session service environments, requiring agents to integrate prior preferences, decisions, and temporal dependencies. It reveals agents often misestimate user state by treating session history as a reliable proxy for current context.

entry.title: ExpWeaver: LLM Agents Learn from Experience via Latent RAG

author.name: Tao Feng, Tianyang Luo, Jingjun Xu, Zhigang Hua, Yan Xie, Shuang Yang, Ge Liu, Jiaxuan You

entry.summary: ExpWeaver enables LLM agents to learn from experience via latent retrieval-augmented generation, encoding past interactions in the model's own hidden states and retrieving in latent space without a separate RAG module. This reduces token overhead and unifies retrieval with generation.

entry.title: Deep Research as Rubric for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wangyi Mei, Zhouhong Gu, Zhenhan Bai, Yin Cai, Lefan Zhang, Zhenxin Ding, Bo Chen, Yan Gao, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Jiaqing Liang, Deqing Yang

entry.summary: DR-rubric treats rubric construction for RL reward signals as a research problem itself, using a two-stage deep-research framework to elicit domain facts, structural constraints, and failure modes. It targets open-ended reasoning and long-form generation tasks lacking automatic verification.

entry.title: Learning from Saturated Data: Signals Beyond Correctness for LLM Training

author.name: Hanno Hiss, Jasper Dekoninck, Martin Vechev

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether questions solved with perfect accuracy can still improve LLMs, replacing binary correctness with pairwise self-judgments and token-level entropy as fine-grained quality signals. It tests these on saturated benchmarks using Qwen3-1.7B-Base.

entry.title: CRAB-Bench: Evaluating LLM Agents under Complex Task Dependencies and Human-aligned User Simulation

author.name: Danqing Wang, Akshay Sivaraman, Lei Li

entry.summary: CRAB-Bench evaluates LLM agents under complex constraint-graph task dependencies with structured distractors, paired with RUSE, a realistic user simulation engine grounded in human behavioral studies across diverse personas. It addresses unrealistic cooperative simulators and multiple-valid-solution evaluation.

entry.title: Scaling Agentic Capabilities via Grounded Interaction Synthesis

author.name: Wenhang Shi, Jinhao Dong, Yiren Chen, Zhe Zhao, Shuqing Bian, Wei Lu, Xiaoyong Du

entry.summary: GAIS is a framework automating scalable construction of diverse agentic environments and tasks, addressing how unconstrained LLM-driven synthesis degenerates into biased sampling of internal priors. It grounds synthesis to capture real-world diversity, difficulty, and high-fidelity long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: A Practical Upper Bound on Selection Bias Effects in Medical Prediction Models

author.name: Kara Liu, Maggie Wang, Russ B. Altman

entry.summary: This paper derives a practical upper bound on worst-case model performance under selection bias for medical prediction, without requiring access to the target distribution or knowledge of the selection mechanism. It enables pre-deployment generalizability assessment.

entry.title: CARE-RL: Capability-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Mitigating Cross-Domain Conflicts

author.name: Rui Zhang, Xinle Wu, Yao Lu

entry.summary: CARE-RL combines protocol-aware generative reward modeling for non-verifiable tasks with capability-aware subspace projection to mitigate cross-domain interference in multi-domain RL for reasoning LLMs. It enables task-adaptive yet comparable evaluation of open-ended responses.

entry.title: Memory-Efficient LLM Training with Dynamic Sparsity: From Stability to Practical Scaling

author.name: Qiao Xiao, Boqian Wu, Patrik Okanovic, Tomasz Sternal, Maurice van Keulen, Elena Mocanu, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Decebal Constantin Mocanu, Torsten Hoefler

entry.summary: This work identifies optimization instability (loss spikes after topology updates) in dynamic sparse training for LLMs, attributing it to a cold-start issue for regrown parameters, and proposes SMET with optimizer warm-up and density-aware learning-rate scaling. It also reduces memory by storing gradients sparsely.

entry.title: DSL-LLaDA: Scaling Continuous Denoising to 8B Masked Diffusion LMs

author.name: Longxuan Yu, Yunshu Wu, Yu Fu, Siheng Xiong, Rob Brekelmans, Hui Liu, Yue Dong, Greg Ver Steeg

entry.summary: Shows that a pretrained masked diffusion language model can be lightly adapted to support continuous embedding-space denoising via Discrete Stochastic Localization, requiring only 1000 continued-pretraining steps. Scales continuous denoising to an 8B masked diffusion LM.

entry.title: Do Text Edits Generalize to Visual Generation? Benchmarking Cross-Modal Knowledge Editing in UMMs

author.name: Xin Gao, Cheng Yang, Chufan Shi, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick

entry.summary: UniKE is the first benchmark for cross-modal knowledge editing in unified multimodal models, testing whether text-side edits transfer to image generation. It reveals a striking modality gap where text efficacy reaches ~92% but visual transfer remains far lower.

entry.title: Revise, Don't Freeze: Sampler-Matched Training for Self-Correcting Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Longxuan Yu, Shaorong Zhang, Yu Fu, Hui Liu, Yue Dong, Greg Ver Steeg

entry.summary: D3IM is a parameter-free sampler for masked diffusion language models that enables direct visible-to-visible token revision without auxiliary modules, derived as a corrector-style reverse update. It identifies and addresses a preservation bias where models reproduce their own wrong committed tokens.

entry.title: CultureForest: Understanding and Evaluating Cultural Norm Grounded Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Yangfan Ye, Xiaocheng Feng, Jialong Tang, Xiayu Cao, Zihan Zhang, Xiachong Feng, Baosong Yang, Bing Qin

entry.summary: CultureForest is a benchmark for cultural norm grounded reasoning where each question is grounded in atomic norms enabling verifiable evaluation, spanning 5,378 examples across 8 domains and 53 countries. It reveals top models degrade substantially in open-ended settings with pronounced cross-region disparities.

entry.title: Mechanistic Diagnostics of Spatial Lexical Bias in Multimodal Large Language Model Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Chuang Ma, Qianying Liu, Tomoyuki Obuchi, Fei Cheng, Wang Yang, Sudong Cai, Shuyuan Zheng, Akiko Aizawa, Sadao Kurohashi

entry.summary: This paper identifies spatial lexical bias in multimodal LLMs, where adding a spatial relation word to answer options attracts the model's selection, making correctly-answered binary spatial questions fail when a third option is added. It uses mechanistic interpretability to isolate binary-stable but ternary-fragile cases across nine open-weight MLLMs.

entry.title: Training Prompt Matters: State-Adaptive Optimization for Robust Fine-Tuning

author.name: Wenhang Shi, Yiren Chen, Shuqing Bian, Zhe Zhao, Jinhao Dong, Pengfei Hu, Wei Lu, Xiaoyong Du

entry.summary: This paper reveals that training prompts are not interchangeable: semantically equivalent paraphrases yield comparable in-task performance but drastically different cross-task forgetting and generalization. It proposes state-adaptive optimization to find superior training prompts that consistently improve outcomes.

entry.title: A physics-informed foundation model for quantitative diffusion MRI

author.name: Zihan Li, Jialan Zheng, Ziyu Li, Xun Yuan, Kasidit Anmahapong, Ziang Wang, Mingxuan Liu, Hongjia Yang, Yifei Chen, Zhuhao Wang, Yuhang He, Fang Chen, Rui Li, Huaiqiang Sun, Yi Liao, Congyu Liao, Yang Yang, Haibo Qu, Xue Zhang, Hongen Liao, Qiyuan Tian

entry.summary: Presents PIGMENT, a physics-informed generative foundation model for quantitative diffusion MRI trained on 11,375 scans across sites, vendors, and field strengths, adapting zero-shot to recover subject-specific microstructure maps. It aims to democratize reliable quantitative mapping beyond specialized research settings.

entry.title: Masking Stale Observations Helps Search Agents -- Until It Doesn't: A Regime Map and Its Mechanism

author.name: Haoxiang Zhang, Qixin Xu, Zhuofeng Li, Lei Zhang, Pengcheng Jiang, Yu Zhang, Julian McAuley

entry.summary: The authors systematically study when masking stale retrieved observations helps long-horizon search agents, finding an asymmetric inverted-U benefit that peaks for mid-capacity models with strong retrievers. The work maps a regime of context-management effectiveness and explains its mechanism.

entry.title: On the Limits of LLM Adaptability: Impact of Model-Internalized Priors on Annotation Task Performance

author.name: Etienne Casanova, Rafal Kocielnik, R. Michael Alvarez

entry.summary: This paper investigates how LLM-internalized priors limit adaptability in zero-shot annotation, finding that nearly two-thirds of zero-shot errors resist correction by added prompt information (decision stickiness). It examines familiarity effects and susceptibility to misaligned task definitions across toxicity datasets.

entry.title: V-LynX: Token Interface Alignment for Video+X LLMs

author.name: Jungin Park, Jiyoung Lee, Kwanghoon Sohn

entry.summary: V-LynX reveals that Video LLMs form a continuous token-interface manifold where visual tokens act as standalone entities, then exploits this to integrate new modalities via a lightweight auxiliary pathway without heavy modality-specific encoders or paired supervision. It aligns attention and statistical responses to internalized video priors.

entry.title: Critic-R: Improving Agentic Search using Instruction-tuned Retrievers with Natural Language Introspective Feedback

author.name: Md Zarif Ul Alam, Alireza Salemi, Hamed Zamani

entry.summary: Critic-R closes the feedback loop in agentic search via a critic model that evaluates whether retrieved evidence supports the next reasoning step, with both inference-time query refinement and a training variant. It avoids heavy co-training and gold annotations.

entry.title: Causal Density Functions

author.name: Sridhar Mahadevan

entry.summary: This paper introduces causal density functions as Radon-Nikodym derivatives comparing interventional to observational laws, providing pointwise change-of-measure objects for scoring directed causal influence. It offers a testable identity and practical estimators for do-curves.

entry.title: Detection vs. Execution: Single-Bucket Probes Miss Half the Mamba-2 State Sink

author.name: Yuhang Jiang

entry.summary: This interpretability study shows that single-bucket probes in Mamba-2 recover only a small execution layer while missing a larger detection layer with the same representational signature, challenging the assumption that representational probes identify executing circuits. It decomposes the state sink into distinct functional head sets.

entry.title: CV-Arena: An Open Benchmark for Instructional Computer Vision Problem Solving with Human-AI Collaborative Preferences

author.name: Fangzhou Lin, Peiran Li, Lingyu Xu, Wenjing Chen, Qianwen Ge, Shuo Xing, Mingyang Wu, Xiangbo Gao, Siyuan Yang, Kazunori Yamada, Ziming Zhang, Haichong Zhang, Zhen Dong, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Zhengzhong Tu

entry.summary: CV-Arena is an open benchmark of 12K high-resolution real-image instruction pairs that broadens instruction-guided image editing into instructional computer vision problem solving with explicit preservation, geometric, physical, and usability constraints. It uses human-AI collaborative preferences for evaluation.

entry.title: Silent Failures in Federated Personalization of Foundation Models

author.name: YongKyung Oh, Alex Bui

entry.summary: This paper identifies Silent Failures (amplified bias, fairness collapse, alignment erosion) arising at the convergence of federated personalization of foundation models and post-market monitoring, where privacy constraints limit behavioral visibility. It exposes a structural divide between federated and centralized trustworthiness benchmarks.

entry.title: OPD+: Rethinking the Advantage Design for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Hanyang Zhao, Haoxian Chen, Han Lin, Genta Indra Winata, David Yao, Wenpin Tang

entry.summary: Revisits the stop-gradient design in on-policy distillation, proving it leads to biased advantage estimates, and proposes an f-divergence optimization framework with corrected advantage design. Improves capability transfer from teacher to student LMs.

entry.title: STARFISH: faST Accuracy Recovery in pruned networks From Internal State Healing

author.name: Shir Maon, Odelia Melamed, Adi Shamir

entry.summary: Proposes STARFISH, a pruning-recovery method that heals pruned networks by aligning their internal state representations with the original network using a tiny unlabeled calibration set. Recovers up to 22% more accuracy than SOTA at 50% sparsity.

entry.title: ProbMoE: Differentiable Probabilistic Routing for Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Heng Zhao, Zilei Shao, Guy Van den Broeck, Zhe Zeng

entry.summary: ProbMoE introduces differentiable probabilistic routing for Mixture-of-Experts, modeling expert selection as a distribution over cardinality-constrained subsets and using exact marginal probabilities as gradient surrogates. It addresses the non-differentiability of top-k routing.

entry.title: Argument Collapse: LLMs Flatten Long-Form Public Debate

author.name: Yekyung Kim, Yapei Chang, Chau Minh Pham, Mohit Iyyer

entry.summary: This study documents argument collapse, where LLM-generated essays converge to a small set of arguments compared to human debate; only 3.4% of LLM main arguments are unique versus 65.3% of human ones. It compares thousands of human and LLM responses across public debate forums.

entry.title: FLARE: Diffusion for Hybrid Language Model

author.name: Yuchen Zhu, Jing Shi, Chongjian Ge, Hao Tan, Yiran Xu, Wanrong Zhu, Jason Kuen, Koustava Goswami, Rajiv Jain, Yongxin Chen, Molei Tao, Jiuxiang Gu

entry.summary: FLARE combines hybrid attention backbones with diffusion language modeling to jointly reduce per-invocation cost and serial decoding steps. It tackles the difficulty of AR-to-diffusion conversion preserving seed-checkpoint capability under hybrid attention constraints.

entry.title: MOSS-Audio Technical Report

author.name: Chen Yang, Chufan Yu, Hanfu Chen, Jie Zhu, Jingqi Chen, Ke Chen, Wenxuan Wang, Yang Wang, Yaozhou Jiang, Yi Jiang, Zhengyuan Lin, Ziqi Chen, Zhaoye Fei, Chenghao Liu, Jun Zhan, Kang Yu, Kexin Huang, Mingshu Chen, Qinyuan Cheng, Ruixiao Li, Shimin Li, Songlin Wang, Yang Gao, Yiyang Zhang, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: MOSS-Audio is a unified audio-language model handling speech, environmental sound, and music understanding with captioning, time-aware QA, timestamped transcription, and audio-grounded reasoning. It uses DeepStack cross-layer feature injection and explicit time markers.

entry.title: Variational Learning for Insertion-based Generation

author.name: Yangtian Zhang, Zhe Wang, Arthur Gretton, Rex Ying, David van Dijk, Michalis K. Titsias, Jiaxin Shi

entry.summary: Introduces a probabilistic framework for learning insertion order in variable-length non-monotonic sequence generation, establishing a bijection between insertion trajectories and permutations to reparameterize the data likelihood. Enables adaptive insertion order beyond fixed-grid masked diffusion.

entry.title: Do Multimodal Agents Really Benefit from Tool Use? A Systematic Study of Capability Gains

author.name: Garvin Guo, Donglei Yu, Yu Chen, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Xinpei Zhao, Huaxing Liu, Qinghao Wang, Minpeng Liao

entry.summary: Systematically tests whether multimodal agents genuinely benefit from tool use, comparing two thinking-with-images agents against tool-free and pure-text counterparts. Finds tool access yields little consistent aggregate improvement and rarely supplies answer-critical information.

entry.title: SPADE-Bench: Evaluating Spontaneous Strategic Deception in Agents via Plan-Action Divergence

author.name: Yuyan Bu, Haowei Li, Qirui Zheng, Bowen Dong, Kaiyue Yang, Jiaming Ji, Yingshui Tan, Wenxin Li, Yaodong Yang, Juntao Dai

entry.summary: Introduces SPADE-Bench to evaluate spontaneous strategic deception in LLM agents, defined as divergence between self-reported plans and executed actions. Unlike prior deception benchmarks, it targets agent-initiated plan-action divergence in opaque execution settings.

entry.title: Exploiting weight-space symmetries for approximating curvature

author.name: Artem Artemev, Rui Xia, Benjamin M. Boyd, Youjing Yu, Felix Dangel, Guillaume Hennequin, Alberto Bernacchia

entry.summary: Exploits weight-space symmetries in loss landscapes to construct structured Hessian approximations from single gradients, offering tractable curvature estimates. Provides a unifying theoretical lens for existing second-order methods.

entry.title: Looped Transformers with Layer Normalization Provably Learn the Power Method

author.name: Lyumin Wu, Chenyang Zhang, Yuan Cao

entry.summary: Proves that a looped linear transformer with layer normalization trained by gradient descent converges to implement the power method, with each attention layer performing one power iteration. Advances understanding of how transformers learn algorithms.

entry.title: Trust Functions: Near-Lossless Weak-to-Strong Generalization by Learning When to Trust the Weak Teacher

author.name: Arda Uzunoglu, Alvin Zhang, Daniel Khashabi

entry.summary: Introduces trust functions that assign scalar reliability scores to weak labels for filtering in weak-to-strong generalization, achieving near-lossless and sometimes superior results compared to ground-truth supervision across knowledge, reasoning, and game domains. Frames W2S as a data selection problem.

entry.title: A Local Perturbation Theory for Cross-Domain Interference and Recovery in Multi-Domain RL

author.name: Lei Yang, Siyu Ding, Deyi Xiong

entry.summary: Develops a local perturbation theory explaining cross-domain interference in multi-domain RL post-training of LLMs, showing that interference arises from shared computation routes even when gradients are orthogonal. Offers a more nuanced account than catastrophic forgetting for why training on one domain harms others.

entry.title: Bit-Exact AI Inference Verification Without Performance Tradeoffs

author.name: Naci Cankaya

entry.summary: Demonstrates bit-exact verification of AI inference outputs without performance-compromising determinism flags, enabling credible auditing against covert adversaries who exploit GPU floating-point non-determinism. Relevant to AI governance and compute monitoring.

entry.title: Training-Free Imitation Learning with Closed-Form Diffusion Policies

author.name: Raghav Mishra, Ian R. Manchester

entry.summary: Introduces Closed-Form Diffusion Policies for imitation learning that use a closed-form score from the demonstration dataset, eliminating offline training. It achieves millisecond inference on mobile CPUs while remaining competitive with neural diffusion policies requiring hours of training.

entry.title: Which Institutional Frameworks Do Chatbots Assume? Auditing Jurisdictional Defaults in Multilingual LLMs

author.name: Zhizhi Wang, Harini Suresh

entry.summary: This audit examines whether multilingual LLMs use input language as a default jurisdictional signal for legal-administrative questions when jurisdiction is unspecified. It evaluates seven US- and China-developed models on underspecified legal queries to reveal embedded institutional assumptions.

entry.title: FineVerify: Scaling Test-Time Compute with Fine-Grained Self-Verification for Agentic Search

author.name: James Xu Zhao, Hui Chen, Bryan Hooi, See-Kiong Ng

entry.summary: FineVerify is a fine-grained self-verification framework for agentic search that decomposes questions into checkable sub-questions, verifies candidates against each, and aggregates scores for selection. It improves test-time compute scaling where correct answers are sparse and calibration is weak.

entry.title: Thinking Economically: A Hierarchical Framework for Adaptive-Complexity Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Yubo Gao, Haotian Wu, Hong Chen, Junquan Huang, Yibo Yan, Jungang Li, Zihao Dongfang, Sicheng Tao, Puay Siew Tan, Jie Zhang, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Hierarchical Adaptive Budgeter that allocates reasoning compute based on intrinsic task and step demands rather than uniform compression, addressing chain-of-thought overthinking. It exploits the heterogeneity of reasoning complexity across problems and within individual steps.

entry.title: DrugClaw and DrugAudit: A Primary-Source-Grounded Agent and Authority-Aware Benchmark for Drug-Information Question Answering

author.name: Qing Wang, Bo Li, Jialu Liang, Daling Shi, Bob Zhang, Qianqian Song

entry.summary: DrugClaw is a multi-agent retrieval-augmented system for drug-information QA grounded in primary regulatory or peer-reviewed records via a reflection-driven state machine, paired with DrugAudit, an authority-aware benchmark scoring source match and citation faithfulness. It targets the high-stakes need for provenance in clinical drug information.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM-as-a-Judge for Long-Form Output Evaluation

author.name: Junjie Chen, Yuxi Dong, Haitao Li, Weihang Su, Yujia Zhou, Min Zhang, Yiqun Liu, Qinyao Ai

entry.summary: LongJudgeBench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLM judges on long-form outputs across diverse scenarios and judging protocols, addressing the gap that prior meta-evaluations focus on short-form outputs. It examines document-level demands that distinguish long-form from short-form evaluation.

entry.title: Physical Object Understanding with a Physically Controllable World Model

author.name: Rahul Venkatesh, Klemen Kotar, Lilian Naing Chen, Wanhee Lee, Gia Ancone, Seungwoo Kim, Luca Thomas Wheeler, Jared Watrous, Honglin Chen, Daniel Bear, Stefan Stojanov, Daniel LK Yamins

entry.summary: This paper introduces a class of probabilistic world models trained efficiently via autoregressive sequence modeling that support estimating the probability of any visual variable conditioned on others. Rich object understanding emerges, enabling inference of physical scene structure from raw videos.

entry.title: Thinking in Blender: Staged Executable Inverse Graphics with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Guangzhao He, Rundong Luo, Wei-Chiu Ma, Hadar Averbuch-Elor

entry.summary: SEIG is an agentic framework that uses pretrained VLMs to perform inverse graphics directly, reconstructing single images into editable Blender programs through staged refinement of geometry, materials, and lighting. Avoids specialized 3D foundation models or differentiable rendering.

entry.title: Breaking the Cascade: Compact Nonlinear Optical Computing with Single-Layer Encoder-Decoder Co-Localization

author.name: Yuntian Wang, Alexander Chen, Md Sadman Sakib Rahman, Aydogan Ozcan

entry.summary: Demonstrates that nonlinear computing can be achieved with a single linear diffractive surface via encoder-decoder co-localization and coherent interference, proven to be a universal approximator for band-limited nonlinear functions. Eliminates need for nonlinear materials or multiple layers.

entry.title: GraspGen-X: Cross-Embodiment 6-DOF Diffusion-based Grasping

author.name: Beining Han, Yu-Wei Chao, Erwin Coumans, Clemens Eppner, Balakumar Sundaralingam, Jia Deng, Stan Birchfield, Adithyavairavan Murali

entry.summary: GraspGen-X extends diffusion-based 6-DOF grasping to condition on gripper morphology via a swept-volume heuristic, trained on procedural grippers and 2 billion grasps for zero-shot generalization to novel real-world grippers and objects. Also serves as good initialization for finetuning.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Pairwise Preferences in Long-Term Decision Problems

author.name: Jonathan Cola\c{c}o Carr, Prakash Panangaden, Doina Precup, Benjamin Van Roy

entry.summary: Proposes the Markov decision contest as a new model for RL with pairwise preferences, addressing inefficiency in long-horizon problems and the lack of guarantees on Markov versus history-dependent policies. Proves theoretical results bridging preference-based RL theory and practice.

entry.title: Detect Before You Leap: Mirage Detection in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sayeed Shafayet Chowdhury, Md. Shaown Miah

entry.summary: This work addresses the mirage failure mode where vision-language models answer confidently despite missing visual evidence, proposing a model-agnostic method that probes CLIP encoder patch tokens to decide whether to answer or abstain before generation. It targets safety-critical medical and document VQA.

entry.title: Linguistics-Aware Non-Distortionary LLM Watermarking

author.name: Shinwoo Park, Hyejin Park, Hyeseon An, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: LUNA is a linguistically adaptive, non-distortionary LLM watermark using model-free detection that estimates next-tag entropy from part-of-speech contexts to set sampler depth, supporting multilingual deployment. It is evaluated across six typologically diverse languages.

entry.title: Scaling Behavior of Single LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jialing Li, Zhouhong Gu, Yin Cai, Hongwei Feng

entry.summary: This paper studies scaling behavior of homogeneous single-LLM multi-agent systems using a minimalist sequential framework to isolate collaboration effects, finding that performance does not scale monotonically with agent count. It characterizes intrinsic collective dynamics.

entry.title: SORA: Free Second-Order Attacks in Fast Adversarial Training

author.name: Mazdak Teymourian, Ramtin Moslemi, Farzan Rahmani, Mohammad Hossein Rohban

entry.summary: SORA introduces second-order attacks into fast adversarial training nearly for free, formalizing Epsilon Overfitting and showing perturbation variability improves robust generalization. It also proposes PertAlign, a cheap metric predicting catastrophic overfitting onset via gradient alignment.

entry.title: Lodestar: An Online-Learning LLM Inference Router

author.name: Gangmuk Lim, Wanyu Zhao, Brighten Godfrey, Jiaxin Shan, Le Xu, Liguang Xie

entry.summary: Lodestar is an online-learning request router for distributed LLM inference clusters that continually adapts to input-dependent execution, batching, KV-cache coupling, and heterogeneous accelerators to optimize latency and GPU utilization. It outperforms traditional load balancers and LLM-specific heuristics.

entry.title: Plausibility Is Not Prediction: Contrastive Evidence for LLM-Based Cellular Perturbation Reasoning

author.name: Xinyu Yuan, Xixian Liu, Jianan Zhao, Yashi Zhang, Hongyu Guo, Jian Tang

entry.summary: Demonstrates with contrastive evidence that LLM-based cellular perturbation reasoning produces biologically plausible explanations but fails to predict actual perturbation effects, often underperforming simple frequency baselines. A critical assessment of LLMs as virtual cell simulators.

entry.title: What Makes a Strong Model? A Unified Spectral Analysis of Knowledge Transfer over High-dimensional Linear Regression

author.name: Wendao Wu, Fangqing Zhang, Haihan Zhang, Cong Fang

entry.summary: Establishes a unified spectral analysis of SGD dynamics in high-dimensional linear regression explaining knowledge transfer efficiency across knowledge distillation and weak-to-strong generalization. Identifies distinct mechanisms like spectral horizon expansion.

entry.title: AgentRedBench: Dynamic Redteaming and Integration-Aware Defense for LLM Agents over SaaS Integrations

author.name: Hiskias Dingeto, Will Leeney

entry.summary: Introduces AgentRedBench, a dynamic LLM-driven red-teaming benchmark of 215 underspecified-authorization indirect prompt injection scenarios across 24 enterprise SaaS integrations. Argues existing benchmarks under-measure realistic tool-use threats and that open guards are trained on the wrong data.

entry.title: World Models: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Methodologies, Reasoning Paradigms, and Applications

author.name: Arif Hassan Zidan, Yi Pan, Hanqi Jiang, Ruiyu Yan, Wei Ruan, Zihao Wu, Lifeng Chen, Weihang You, Xinliang Li, Bowen Chen, Huawen Hu, Peilong Wang, Sizhuang Liu, Jing Zhang, Siyuan Li, Zhengliang Liu, Yu Bao, Lin Zhao, Lichao Sun, Dajiang Zhu, Xiang Li, Jinglei Lv, Quanzheng Li, Wei Liu, Tianming Liu, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: Surveys world models as internal environment simulators, proposing a multi-axis taxonomy across architecture, methodology, reasoning paradigms, and applications spanning RL, robotics, autonomous driving, and video generation. Aims to unify a fragmented field central to AGI pursuits.

entry.title: Generate in Reconstruction Space, Match in Semantic Space: Transport Geometry for One-Step Generation

author.name: Hugues Van Assel, Edward De Brouwer, Saeed Saremi, Gabriele Scalia, Aviv Regev

entry.summary: Proposes a one-step generation framework that decouples generation in reconstruction space from matching in frozen SSL semantic space using Sinkhorn divergence, clarifying why SSL features help generative training. Authors include researchers from Genentech/Regev lab.

entry.title: Normalized Relevance Measure as a Unifying Framework to Explain Neural Network Latent Structures

author.name: Ping Xiong, Thomas Schnake, Gr\'egoire Montavon, Klaus-Robert M\"uller, Shinichi Nakajima

entry.summary: Proposes the Normalized Relevance Measure framework attributing relevance to arbitrary sets of neurons across layers and architectures, unifying explanation methods for latent structures. Builds on the LRP/explainability lineage with strong authors.

entry.title: Local MixVR: Breaking the Communication-Sample Dependence in Distributed Learning

author.name: Tehila Dahan, Bassel Hamoud, Roie Reshef, Martin Jaggi, Kfir Y. Levy

entry.summary: Introduces Local MixVR, the first distributed learning method whose communication-round complexity is independent of total sample count N, scaling only with the number of workers via local updates plus variance reduction. Outperforms state-of-the-art when worker count is small relative to samples.

entry.title: Physics from Video: Identifiability of Time-Invariant Second-Order ODEs under Minimal Trajectory Conditions

author.name: Yuanyuan Wang, Wenjie Wang, Kun Zhang, Mingming Gong

entry.summary: Studies structural identifiability of continuous-time physical laws from raw video pixels, proving conditions under which second-order linear ODE parameters can be uniquely recovered and characterizing minimal data requirements across damping regimes. Advances theoretical foundations for video-based world models.

entry.title: The Representation-Rationalizability Tradeoff in Reward Learning

author.name: Jing Dong, Yaoliang Yu, Pascal Pourpart

entry.summary: Analyzes a representation-rationalizability tradeoff in RLHF reward learning, extending social-choice impossibility results to settings with infinite candidate response spaces rather than fixed finite alternatives. Provides theoretical grounding for limits of scalar reward models.

entry.title: Quantifying the Salience of Geo-Cultural Values for Pluralistic Safety Alignment

author.name: Arkadiy Saakyan, Charvi Rastogi, Lora Aroyo

entry.summary: Conducts a meta-analysis showing most safety evaluation datasets omit geo-cultural information and demonstrates via multilevel modeling that cultural zone membership explains variance in safety ratings beyond demographics. Argues for pluralistic, culturally representative safety alignment.

entry.title: Internalize the Temperature: On-Policy Self-Distillation as Policy Reheater for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xuewei Yang, Jiachen Yu, Jie Wu, Shaoning Sun, Junjie Wang, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: Proposes Temperature-Scaled On-Policy Self-Distillation to internalize exploratory temperature effects into model parameters, mitigating entropy collapse in RL from verifiable rewards for LLM reasoning. Acts as a lightweight policy reheating method from an entropy-collapsed checkpoint.

entry.title: Unlocking the Black Box of Latent Reasoning: An Interpretability-Guided Approach to Intervention

author.name: Shuochen Chang, Tong Bai, Xiaofeng Zhang, Qianli Ma, Qingyang Liu, Zhaohe Liao, Yibo Miao, Li Niu

entry.summary: Analyzes latent reasoning in LLMs using structural, causal, and geometric probes, finding that continuous thought vectors encode faithful compressed reasoning steps with early vectors acting as causal hubs. It then introduces training-free decode-time interventions to refine latent reasoning.

entry.title: Parameter Alignment Mitigates Catastrophic Forgetting in Multilingual Expert Language Models

author.name: Sanchit Ahuja, Terra Blevins

entry.summary: This work links catastrophic forgetting in multilingual continual pretraining to parameter drift and proposes five layer-aware alignment strategies including freezing, regularization, weight reversion, and model merging. It systematically compares these across 32 training languages from five families.

entry.title: Citation Grounding: Detecting and Reducing LLM Citation Hallucinations via Legal Citation Graphs

author.name: Volodymyr Ovcharov

entry.summary: This paper proposes citation grounding, a metric verifying LLM-generated legal citations against a ground-truth graph built from over 100 million Ukrainian court decisions, decomposing into precision, relevance, and temporality. It enables differential diagnosis of legal citation hallucination types.

entry.title: Decoding in Order-Agnostic Language Models: Chain-Rule Deviation and Uniform Spreading

author.name: Lin Yao

entry.summary: This paper analyzes decoding in order-agnostic language models including diffusion LLMs, showing that learned conditionals do not form a coherent joint distribution and reveal order shifts log-likelihood by up to 0.49 nats/token. It examines confidence-first decoding behavior and proposes diagnostics for uniform spreading.

entry.title: HarnessForge: Joint Harness and Policy Evolution for Adaptive Agent Systems

author.name: Mingju Chen, Can Lv, Guibin Zhang, Heng Chang, Shiji Zhou

entry.summary: HarnessForge is a meta-adaptive framework that jointly evolves an agent system's external harness and internal reasoning policy as a coupled harness-policy pair, addressing the unoptimized compatibility between structure and execution. It enables full-system adaptation across heterogeneous task regimes.

entry.title: RoboDream: Compositional World Models for Scalable Robot Data Synthesis

author.name: Junjie Ye, Rong Xue, Basile Van Hoorick, Runhao Li, Harshitha Rajaprakash, Pavel Tokmakov, Muhammad Zubair Irshad, Vitor Guizilini, Yue Wang

entry.summary: RoboDream is an embodiment-centric world model that synthesizes photorealistic robot demonstrations with novel objects, scenes, and viewpoints by anchoring generation to rendered robot motion and scene priors. Addresses costly teleoperation data collection.

entry.title: $\tau_0$-WM: A Unified Video-Action World Model for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Pengfei Zhou, Shengcong Chen, Di Chen, Jiaxu Wang, Rongjun Jin, Bingwen Zhu, Yike Pan, Songen Gu, Kuanning Wang, Shufeng Nan, Xingyu Qiu, Chenhao Qiu, Pu Yang, Yunuo Cai, Jianxiong Gao, Yifan Li, Yanwei Fu, Xiangyu Yue, Zhi Chen, Jianlan Luo

entry.summary: tau0-WM is a unified video-action world model integrating policy learning, video prediction, and action evaluation on a shared video diffusion backbone, offering both a video-action policy and an action-conditioned video simulator for rolling out and scoring candidate actions. Targets executable manipulation with consequence anticipation.

entry.title: Subliminal Learning is a LoRA Artifact

author.name: Todd Nief, Harvey Yiyun Fu, Mark Muchane, Ari Holtzman

entry.summary: This paper argues that subliminal learning—transmission of behavioral traits through semantically unrelated finetuning data—is a LoRA artifact, showing an inverted U-shaped dependence on LoRA rank and that it disappears under full finetuning. It also finds strong dependence on finetuning and evaluation context.

entry.title: The Case for Model Science: Verify, Explore, Steer, Refine

author.name: Przemyslaw Biecek, Luca Longo, Jianlong Zhou, Thomas Fel, Andreas Holzinger, Wojciech Samek

entry.summary: This position paper argues for consolidating model analysis into a systematic discipline termed Model Science, organized around verify, explore, steer, and refine, to move beyond benchmark-driven progress that reveals whether but not why models succeed or fail. It draws analogies from established sciences.

entry.title: Food Noise & False Safety: A Systematic Evaluation of How LLMs Fail to Adapt to Eating Disorder Queries with Clinician Feedback

author.name: Giulia Pucci, Emily Hemendinger, Ruizhe Li, Gavin Abercrombie, Tanvi Dinkar, Arabella Sinclair

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates how LLMs fail to safely handle eating-disorder queries, finding with clinician input that specific linguistic cues increase unsafe, uncritically adaptive responses that may facilitate self-harm. Highlights real harms from perceived AI expertise.

entry.title: CardioLens: Revealing the Clinical Reality Gap of MLLMs via Multi-Sequence Cardiac MRI Evaluations

author.name: Zixian Su, Hongkai Zhang, Fan Gao, Encheng Su, Taiping Qu, Jingwei Guo, Nan Zhang, Hui Wang, Zhen Zhou, Kairui Bo, Yan Chen, Yue Ren, Shuai Li, Lei Xu, Henggui Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces CardioLens, a leakage-resistant evaluation testbed for multi-sequence cardiac MRI built from private hospital archives with nearly 474k slices and 13.5k verified QA pairs. Evaluating 24 MLLMs reveals a substantial clinical reality gap on real diagnostic tasks.

entry.title: Emergence of Exploration in Policy Gradient Reinforcement Learning via Retrying

author.name: Soichiro Nishimori, Paavo Parmas, Sotetsu Koyamada, Tadashi Kozuno, Toshinori Kitamura, Shin Ishii, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: Introduces ReMax, an RL objective evaluating policies by expected maximum return over M samples while accounting for return uncertainty, inducing stochastic exploration as an emergent property without explicit bonuses. Derives a new policy-gradient formulation and ReMax PPO (RePPO).

entry.title: StressDream: Steering Video World Models for Robust Policy Evaluation and Improvement

author.name: Junwon Seo, Sushant Veer, Ran Tian, Wenhao Ding, Apoorva Sharma, Karen Leung, Edward Schmerling, Marco Pavone, Andrea Bajcsy

entry.summary: Proposes StressDream, which steers diffusion-based video world model imaginations toward high-impact yet plausible outcomes by optimizing initial noise at inference time for robust policy evaluation and improvement. It avoids needing prohibitively many samples to capture rare high-impact futures.

entry.title: Zamba2-VL Technical Report

author.name: Hassan Shapourian, Kasra Hejazi, Olabode M. Sule, Beren Millidge

entry.summary: Presents Zamba2-VL, vision-language models built on a hybrid Mamba2 state-space plus shared-transformer backbone, competitive with leading Transformer VLMs like Qwen3-VL and InternVL3.5 while delivering roughly an order of magnitude lower time-to-first-token. It substantially outperforms prior SSM-based and hybrid VLMs.

entry.title: A Distribution-Free Framework for Rewrite-Based Human-text Detection via Knockoff Filtering

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: This paper reframes rewrite-based detection of LLM-generated text as a knockoff-filtering multiple hypothesis testing problem, giving existing detectors finite-sample false discovery rate guarantees via calibration without retraining. It validates across multiple detectors, domains, and LLMs.

entry.title: SPADER: Step-wise Peer Advantage with Diversity-Aware Exploration Rewards for Multi-Answer Question Answering

author.name: Qiming Shi, Zhaolu Kang, Yunfan Zhou, Di Weng, Yingcai Wu

entry.summary: SPADER is an RL framework for multi-answer QA with tool-augmented agents, introducing step-wise peer advantage for credit assignment and diversity-aware exploration rewards to discover comprehensive answer sets. It tackles fine-grained credit and exploration beyond high-frequency entities.

entry.title: MemPro: Agentic Memory Systems as Evolvable Programs

author.name: Qingshan Liu, Guoqing Wang, Wen Wu, Jingqi Huang, Xinqi Tao, Dejia Song, Jie Zhou, Liang He

entry.summary: MemPro treats the entire memory construction-retrieval pipeline of an agent as an evolvable program rather than just adapting the memory bank, enabling system-level evolution to handle heterogeneous failure modes. It targets long-horizon autonomous agents.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Conformal Prediction with Personalized Statistical Validity

author.name: Martin V. Vejling, Christophe A. N. Biscio, Adrien Mazoyer, Petar Popovski, Shashi Raj Pandey

entry.summary: PFWCP is a personalized federated conformal prediction framework combining local density-ratio weighting with weighted quantile aggregation to provide valid uncertainty quantification under heterogeneity and privacy constraints. It yields asymptotically valid personalized coverage guarantees.

entry.title: GenPT: Beyond Self-Report for Reliable LLM Psychometrics via Generative Projective Testing

author.name: Ming Wang, Shuang Wu, Bixuan Wang, Lu Lin, Yuxin Chen, Xiaocui Yang, Daling Wang, Shi Feng, Yifei Zhang, Yufan Sun

entry.summary: GenPT reformulates projective psychological tests (TAT, Rorschach, SCT) with newly generated stimuli to assess persona-conditioned LLM agents, avoiding contamination and directional bias of self-report questionnaires. It organizes assessment into a standardized three-stage pipeline.

entry.title: Accuracy, Stability, and Repeated-Run Reliability of Large Language Models on Deterministic Programming Tasks

author.name: Yongxi Zhou, Lai Yun Choi, Jiaxi Wen, Wenbo Ye

entry.summary: This paper shows that run-level pass rate overstates retry-free coverage by up to 17.8 points, with the gap largest for mid-performing systems, and introduces a repeated-run evaluation protocol measuring accuracy, retry-free coverage, and per-problem variability on deterministic programming tasks. It highlights stability as a distinct deployment requirement.

entry.title: Explainable deep reinforcement learning reveals energy-efficient control strategies for turbulent drag reduction

author.name: Federica Tonti, Ricardo Vinuesa

entry.summary: Combines multi-agent deep reinforcement learning with SHAP-based explainability to discover energy-efficient flow control strategies for reducing drag in turbulent flows. The SHAP-guided rewards based on skin-friction and wall-pressure outperform standard opposition control baselines.

entry.title: Strong Stochastic Flow Maps

author.name: Sam McCallum, Zander W. Blasingame, Timothy Herschell, Niklas Rindtorff, Alexander Tong, James Foster

entry.summary: Proposes Strong Stochastic Flow Maps for learning the strong solution map of SDEs, extending flow-map methods beyond ODE marginals to recover solution paths. Enables few-step sampling that captures pathwise behavior.

entry.title: RLVR without Ineffective Samples: Group Prioritized Off-Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yixiu Mao, Yun Qu, Qi Wang, Heming Zou, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: Proposes Group Prioritized Off-Policy Optimization for RLVR, addressing the prevalence of ineffective zero-variance training samples by reusing off-policy data without costly rollout filtering. Improves data efficiency for LLM reasoning training.

entry.title: Beyond Visual Memory: Mechanistic Diagnostics of Latent Visual Reasoning

author.name: Garvin Guo, Yu Chen, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Xinpei Zhao, Huaxing Liu, Shuai Dong

entry.summary: Decomposes latent visual reasoning tokens into latent slots, boundary markers, and format to diagnose the true source of gains, finding that latent slots fail every prediction of the visual-evidence hypothesis. Challenges the assumption that continuous latent tokens encode visual information.

entry.title: Efficient Exploration for Iterative Nash Preference Optimization

author.name: Tianlong Nan, Xiaopeng Li, Christian Kroer, Tianyi Lin

entry.summary: Provides learning-theoretic foundations for scalable Nash Learning from Human Feedback, addressing efficient exploration for iterative Nash preference optimization where preferences may be cyclic or non-transitive. Bridges the gap between oracle-based regret guarantees and easier-to-implement iterative methods.

entry.title: Move the Query, Not the Cache: Characterizing Cross-Instance Latent Attention Redistribution Across GPU Fabrics

author.name: Bole Ma, Jan Eitzinger, Harald K\"ostler, Gerhard Wellein

entry.summary: This work characterizes cross-instance attention for sparse-attention LLMs, arguing that with Multi-head Latent Attention it is cheaper to route compressed queries than to move KV-cache blocks across GPUs. It addresses agentic workloads where many sub-agents query a large shared codebase partitioned across GPUs.

entry.title: Defenses & Enablers For Skill Injection Attacks on Terminal Based Agents

author.name: Yoshinari Fujinuma, Varun Gangal, Traian Rebedea, Makesh Narasimhan Sreedhar, Prasoon Varshney, Rebecca Qian, Anand Kannappan

entry.summary: This work studies skill-injection attacks on terminal-based LLM agents, proposing guardian-based defenses (dynamic mediator and static rewriter) that cut attack success rates by over half while preserving utility. It also stress-tests defenses with attack reframing variants.

entry.title: Cross-modal linkage risk in clinical vision-language models

author.name: Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh, Mahshad Lotfinia, Sven Nebelung, Daniel Truhn

entry.summary: Formalizes cross-modal linkage risk in clinical vision-language models, showing de-identified chest radiographs can be re-linked to their original reports via embedding cosine similarity. Audits this image-to-report retrieval risk across 406,241 pairs and increasingly specialized VLMs.

entry.title: Policy and World Modeling Co-Training for Language Agents

author.name: Ning Lu, Baijiong Lin, Shengcai Liu, Jiahao Wu, Haoze Lv, Yanbin Wei, Lingting Zhu, Shengju Qian, Xin Wang, Ying-Cong Chen, Qi Wang, Ke Tang

entry.summary: Proposes PaW, a co-training framework that adds auxiliary world-modeling supervision to on-policy RL for LLM agents using transitions already present in rollouts, without separate simulators or extra inference cost. Teaches agents what actions do to the environment, not just which yield reward.

entry.title: Dialectics of Alignment: Harnessing Unsafe Knowledge for Dynamic Safety Routing

author.name: Maryam Hashemzadeh, Jerry Huang, Minseon Kim, Marc-Alexandre C\^ot\'e, Sarath Chandar

entry.summary: Challenges the erasure paradigm in LLM alignment, proposing SafeMoE, a Mixture-of-Experts framework that isolates unsafe knowledge into dedicated experts and uses dynamic safety routing to give nuanced informative responses instead of blanket refusals. Argues unsafe data encodes useful domain knowledge.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Pure Machine Unlearning for Smooth Strongly Convex Losses

author.name: Matthew Regehr, Gautam Kamath, Andrew Lowy

entry.summary: This work nearly resolves the fundamental statistical cost of machine unlearning for smooth strongly convex losses, proving tight upper and lower bounds on excess population risk. The optimal rate interpolates between full retraining and no unlearning.

entry.title: CANARY: Zero-Label Detection of Fine-Tuning Contamination in Language Models

author.name: Swapnil Parekh

entry.summary: CANARY is a zero-label auditor that detects fine-tuning data poisoning from hidden-state geometry using two forward passes and a sparse autoencoder, achieving perfect AUROC at 1 percent contamination. It detects latent harmful behavior invisible to output-level defenses.

entry.title: On the Scaling of PEFT: Towards Million Personal Models of Trillion Parameters

author.name: Mind Lab, :, Song Cao, Vic Cao, Kaijie Chen, Bunny Fan, Hera Feng, Huan Feng, Arthur Fu, Jun Gao, Hongquan Gu, Aaron Guan, Mutian Hong, Hailee Hou, Peixuan Hua, Charles Huang, Miles Jiang, Nora Jiang, Yuyi Jiang, Autumn Jin, Fancy Kong, Kyrie Lei, Alexy Li, Dawn Li, Ray Li, Theo Li, Wenhao Li, Jiayi Lin, Domini Liu, Heshan Liu, Kairus Liu, Logan Liu, Maeve Luo, Runism Lv, Pony Ma, Verity Niu, Anson Qiu, Vincent Wang, Maxwell Yao, Regis Ye, Wenlin Ye, Yanying Ye, Josh Ying, Danney Zeng, Salmon Zhan, Anya Zhang, Ruijia Zhang, Shiyang Zhang, Sueky Zhang, Ya Zhang, Wei Zhao, Ada Zhou, Sizer Zhou, Xinyue Zhu, Murphy Zhuang

entry.summary: Reframes parameter-efficient fine-tuning as persistent per-instance local state atop strong shared foundation models, studying scaling up, down, and out toward millions of personal adapters. Proposes MinT infrastructure for managing adapter identity and revision at scale.

entry.title: UniPinRec: Unifying Generative Retrieval and Ranking at Pinterest Scale

author.name: Hanyu Li, Yi-Ping Hsu, Aditya Mantha, Prabhat Agarwal, Laksh Bhasin, Jialu Wang, Hongtao Lin, Bella Huang, Yaxin Li, Xinyi Li, Chuxi Wang, Kousik Rajesh, Hooshmand Shokri Razaghi, Shunyao Li, Zongyue Qin, Jaewon Yang, James Li, Dhruvil Deven Badani, Jiajing Xu, Charles Rosenberg

entry.summary: Presents UniPinRec, a full-stack unification of retrieval and ranking at Pinterest scale with one input format, one shared transformer model, one training stage, and existing serving infrastructure. Reduces duplicated parameters and serving cost in industrial recommendation.

entry.title: Taming the Loss Landscape of PINNs with Noisy Feynman-Kac Supervision: Operator Preconditioning and Non-Asymptotic Error Bounds

author.name: Nathanael Tepakbong, Hanyu Hu, Chengyu Liu, Xiang Zhou

entry.summary: Shows that adding a pointwise data-fidelity term to PINN losses acts as an operator-level preconditioner that provably reduces the condition number, with non-asymptotic error bounds using Feynman-Kac supervision. Helps explain and remedy ill-conditioned PINN training.

entry.title: How Optimality Structures Sparse Dictionaries: A Theory for Understanding SAE Representations

author.name: William Dorrell

entry.summary: Develops a theory of what sparse autoencoders extract by analyzing how optimality structures sparse dictionaries, addressing the gap in understanding which properties a concept must satisfy for an SAE to recover it. It moves beyond simplistic data-generating models toward realistic representations.

entry.title: Agreement Metrics for LLM-as-Judge Evaluation: What to Report and Why

author.name: Delip Rao, Chris Callison-Burch

entry.summary: This paper surveys how LLM-as-judge evaluations report agreement metrics with human annotations and shows that for binary criteria many correlation statistics collapse to a single number, making redundant reporting misleading. It offers practical guidance on which metrics to report and why, addressing widespread methodological confusion in evaluation studies.

entry.title: SALSA: Speech Aware LLM Adaptation via Learned Steering Activation Vectors

author.name: Yekaterina Yegorova, Argyrios Gerogiannis, Haolong Zheng, Julia Hockenmaier, Chang D. Yoo, Mark A. Hasegawa-Johnson

entry.summary: SALSA is a lightweight adaptation method for speech-aware LLMs that learns layer-wise steering vectors via a supervised objective rather than contrastive activation differences. It shows large gains on children's speech, multilingual, and code-switching benchmarks.

entry.title: Agentic Clustering: Controllable Text Taxonomies via Multi-Agent Refinement

author.name: Simon L\"owe, Emily Silcock

entry.summary: Agentic Clustering replaces fixed programmatic text-clustering pipelines with an orchestrator LLM that dispatches specialized agents (proposer, synthesizer, auditor, investigator, critic) adapting to the corpus. It enables controllable taxonomies that incorporate user constraints like target cluster count or intent.

entry.title: LongAttnComp: Cross-Family Context Compression for Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Mengmeng Ji, Ravi Shanker Raju, Jonathan Lingjie Li, Chen Wu

entry.summary: LongAttnComp adapts attention-based context compression for long-context reasoning by fine-tuning a cross-attention scoring layer with token-level chunking, top-p budgeting, positional reordering, and a format-agnostic query parser. It reduces prefill costs while preserving accuracy on demanding tasks like code reasoning.

entry.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Emotion Control in Text-to-Speech

author.name: Hongfei Du, Jiacheng Shi, Sidi Lu, Gang Zhou, Ye Gao

entry.summary: This work uses sparse autoencoders to analyze emotion-related variation in LLM-based TTS hidden states, finding emotional variation is distributed across multiple sparse features. Intervening on a small subset enables interpretable emotion control in text-to-speech.

entry.title: Cost-Aware Diffusion Draft Trees for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Shuai Zhang, Huachuan Qiu, Hongliang He, Yong Dai

entry.summary: CaDDTree improves speculative decoding for diffusion drafters by directly optimizing token throughput rather than acceptance length, jointly selecting tree structure under verification cost. It addresses that acceptance length always favors larger trees with no principled budget basis.

entry.title: "I Strongly Suspect This Website Is a Scam": Benchmarking PII Leakage and Detection without Defense in Autonomous Web Agents

author.name: Soham Roy, Sarthakbrata Halder, Arya Bharaty, Vaibhav Bhaskar, Yash Sinha, Dhruv Kumar, Srikant Panda, Murari Mandal

entry.summary: Scammer4U is a pre-registered benchmark of 91 attacker-controlled environments testing how social-engineering web content manipulates autonomous web agents into leaking users' PII to attacker endpoints. It shows frontier web agents are highly susceptible to extracting critical-tier PII.

entry.title: Auteur: Language-Driven Cinematographic Framing for Human-Centric Video Generation

author.name: Muhammed Burak Kizil, Enes Sanli, Niloy J. Mitra, Xuelin Chen, Erkut Erdem, Aykut Erdem, Duygu Ceylan

entry.summary: Presents Auteur, a method for language-driven, human-centric camera framing in generative video that parameterizes shots relative to the actor (shot size, angle, composition) rather than as world-space trajectories. Brings cinematographic intentionality to camera control.
