entry.summary: Proposes a pose-conditioned, permutation-equivariant denoiser for ultra-wideband V2I ranging to reconstruct work zone geometry for autonomous vehicles. It handles outliers, non-line-of-sight errors, and anchor ordering issues in field deployments.

entry.title: UF-AMA: A unified framework for cross-domain emotion recognition via adaptive multimodal alignment

author.name: Zheng Wang, Shuo Wang, Junhong Wang

entry.summary: Proposes UF-AMA, a unified framework with adaptive multimodal alignment for cross-subject and cross-session emotion recognition from physiological signals like EEG. It addresses distribution shifts and varying sample quality across modalities.

entry.title: MiCU: End-to-End Smart Home Command Understanding with Large Language Model

author.name: Haowei Han, Kexin Hu, Weiwei Cai, Debiao Zhang, Bin Qin, Yuxiang Wang, Jiawei Jiang, Xiao Yan, Bo Du

entry.summary: Builds MiCU, a domain-specific LLM for smart home command understanding that handles ambiguous commands like making a room cozy, using an automated training-data synthesis workflow from user logs. Improves on rule-based systems for misaligned utterances.

entry.title: AI From the Margins (AIM): Rethinking Participatory AI Design Through the Lived Experience of Minoritized Communities

author.name: Tijs Portegies, Laureanne Willems, Maaike Harbers, Giovanni Sileno, Roland van Dierendonck, Mayesha Tasnim, Lotte Willemsen, Sennay Ghebreab

entry.summary: Proposes AI From the Margins, a methodological stance for participatory AI design that articulates preconditions for centering minoritized communities' lived experiences before problem definitions are set. Applied in a Dutch healthcare context.

entry.title: FedMTFI: Feature Importance Based Optimized Multi Teacher Knowledge Distillation in Heterogeneous Federated Learning Environment

author.name: Nazmus Shakib Shadin, Aaron Cummings, Xinyue Zhang, Bobin Deng

entry.summary: FedMTFI combines multi-teacher knowledge distillation with feature importance for heterogeneous federated learning, clustering clients by similarity. It aims to maintain consistent performance across devices with non-IID data and varying compute.

entry.title: Understanding Identity Continuity in Thermal Video through Scene-Level Consistency

author.name: Wei-Chieh Sun, Gyungmin Ko, Heejae Kwon, Hsiang-Wei Huang, Jenq-Neng Hwang

entry.summary: This work studies identity continuity in thermal pedestrian tracking via lightweight post-processing, adding online short-gap remapping and offline tracklet relinking to a YOLOv8/SORT baseline. It improves IDF1 from 82.25 to 84.93 on the PBVS thermal benchmark.

entry.title: Network Distributed Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Consensus Control of Quadcopters

author.name: Youssef Mahran, Zeyad Gamal, Aamir Ahmad, Ayman El-Badawy

entry.summary: Proposes ND-MARL, a network-distributed multi-agent RL framework for quadcopter consensus control where each agent observes only two neighbors and embeds the communication graph into decision-making. Uses Multi-Agent Soft Actor-Critic in a hierarchical planner-controller stack.

entry.title: Feature to Dynamics: Feature-space to Autoregression strategy for Zero-shot Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yifan Wu, Junjie Wu, Kai Wu, Xiaoyu Zhang, Jian Lou

entry.summary: FSA proposes a feature-to-strategy framework for zero-shot time series forecasting that maps an interpretable feature space to autoregressive strategies rather than directly modeling raw sequences. The goal is better generalization when source and target domains are disjoint or data is scarce.

entry.title: Learning-based Directed Graph Abstraction of Combinatorial Spaces for Order-Preserving Search in Mixed-Combinatorial Nonlinear Optimization

author.name: Gishnu Madhu, Feng Liu, Souma Chowdhury

entry.summary: This paper presents a learned directed-graph abstraction of combinatorial spaces using GNNs for order-preserving search in mixed-combinatorial nonlinear optimization. It avoids spurious relations from integer/binary encodings in engineering design and planning problems.

entry.title: RobustModelMaker: Coupling Bootstrap Stability Selection with Leakage-Safe Nested Cross-Validation for Scientific Machine Learning

author.name: Amanda S Barnard

entry.summary: RobustModelMaker couples bootstrap stability selection with strict nested cross-validation for scientific ML on small datasets, addressing both unstable feature selection and optimistic performance bias jointly. It is provided as a Python framework.

entry.title: Continual Learning as a Multiphase Moving-Boundary Problem

author.name: Snigdha Chandan Khilar

entry.summary: Stefan-CL frames continual learning as a multiphase moving-boundary (Stefan) problem, treating consolidated knowledge as a protected solid and unused capacity as adaptable liquid governed by a latent-heat parameter. It claims near-zero forgetting without storing raw data.

entry.title: Edge-aware Decoding for Neural Asymmetric Routing

author.name: Li Liang, Jinbiao Chen, Zizhen Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes an edge-aware decoder for neural asymmetric routing that exposes transition-level quantities matching cost-to-go structure, addressing a representation-decision mismatch where pairwise cost is encoded upstream but final logits use context-node compatibility. It improves directed routing decisions.

entry.title: A Doeblin-Anchored Contrastive Chart for Learning Markov Transition Kernels

author.name: Ao Xu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a Doeblin-anchored contrastive chart for learning valid Markov transition kernels from contrastive objectives, ensuring the learned object is a valid transition kernel before iteration. It mixes the target transition with a restart law to obtain a minorized, invertible coordinate.

entry.title: Spectra-Guided Neural Tucker Factorization

author.name: Fusheng Wang, Yikai Hou

entry.summary: Proposes Spectra-Guided Neural Tucker Factorization for high-dimensional incomplete tensor completion, mapping scalar timestamps into continuous spectral space and using a spatio-temporal co-gating mechanism. Achieves competitive accuracy with parameter efficiency.

entry.title: Autopilot-Preserving Residual Q-Learning with HJB-Inspired Finite-Action Risk Filtering for Fixed-Wing UAV Command Supervision

author.name: Mehmet Iscan, Batuhan Temiz

entry.summary: Proposes a residual Q-learning supervisor that sits above an unchanged fixed-wing UAV autopilot, selecting bounded reference adjustments filtered by an HJB-inspired risk mechanism. It keeps exploration risk away from actuators while improving disturbance rejection.

entry.title: MidSurfNet: Learnable Face Pairing and Interference Implicit Fields for Generalized Mid-surface Abstraction

author.name: Li Ye, Xinhang Zhou, Xingyu Yang, Ruofeng Tong, Hailong Li, Peng Du, Min Tang

entry.summary: Proposes MidSurfNet, a learning-augmented framework for mid-surface abstraction of thin-walled CAD models, using a neural face-pairing module and an interference implicit field to handle multi-thickness and self-matching configurations where rule-based methods fail. It targets finite-element preprocessing.

entry.title: Peacemaker at ATE-IT: Automatic term extraction from Italian text for waste management data using encoder model

author.name: Mahdi Bakhtiyarzadeh, Hadi Bayrami Asl Tekanlou, Jafar Razmara

entry.summary: This shared-task submission presents a low-cost interpretable encoder-based method for automatic term extraction from Italian waste-management text, using fine-tuning strategies for the ATE Shared Task. It addresses challenges of limited annotated data and multi-word expression extraction.

entry.title: Towards Multidisciplinary Summarization of Hospital Stays: Efficient Sentence-Level Clinical Provenance Categorization

author.name: Baris Karacan, Vaibhav Bhargava, Barbara Di Eugenio, Natalie Parde, Mary Khetani, Yu-Shan Tseng, Vanessa Barbosa, Julie Vignato, Lindsey Knake, Rajashree Dahal, Emily Spellman, Danielle Hitzel, Janine Petitgout, Kristi Haughey, Amanda Karstens, Brianna Clarahan, Rachel Dawson, Lauren Boyd, Mackenzie Weis, Angie Tipton, Jaewon Bae, Catherine K. Craven, Karen Dunn Lopez, Andrew D. Boyd

entry.summary: This pilot study fine-tunes Llama-3 models (8B and 70B) to categorize sentence-level clinical provenance across multi-source NICU notes as a prerequisite for multidisciplinary hospital-stay summarization. It adapts to MedSecId, a corpus of MIMIC-III notes annotated with provenance headers.

entry.title: SN-WER: Script-Normalized WER for Multi-Script Indic ASR Evaluation

author.name: Priyaranjan Pattnayak

entry.summary: SN-WER proposes a training-free script-normalized word error rate that transliterates reference and hypothesis into a canonical script before scoring, correcting WER inflation in multilingual Indic ASR where the same words appear in different scripts. It reduces spurious model gaps by up to 12%.

entry.title: Training-Free Object-Agnostic Jam Detection in Fulfillment Centers

author.name: Ruiliang Liu, Tina Dongxu Li, Joshua Migdal, Fernando Ruch, Kenneth Meszaros, Moses Trevor Dardik

entry.summary: This paper presents a training-free, object-agnostic jam detection method for fulfillment centers that uniformly samples reference points in the monitoring region rather than relying on object detection and tracking. It eliminates the thousands of manual annotations and class limitations of traditional pipelines.

entry.title: Beyond Static Gaussians: An Empirical Investigation of Architectural Paradigms for Dynamic 3D Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Adrian Ramlal, John S. Zelek

entry.summary: This paper provides a comprehensive empirical comparison of dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting methods, categorizing them into structure-guided (deformation fields, canonical spaces) and gaussian-centric paradigms. It finds structure-guided methods achieve superior fidelity and compactness on the D-NeRF benchmark.

entry.title: MUSCLE-NET: Predicted-Multiscale-Aware Network for Pedestrian Trajectory Forecasting

author.name: Yu Liu, Ming Huang, Xiao Ren, Zhijie Liu, Youfu Li, He Kong

entry.summary: MUSCLE-NET is a predicted-multiscale-aware network for pedestrian trajectory forecasting that integrates multimodal cues with scale-adaptive prediction mechanisms, accounting for scale dependency of future motion. It aims to improve robustness across diverse pedestrian behaviors for autonomous driving.

entry.title: Improving Visual Grounding in Remote Sensing via Cluster-Guided Refinement and Model Ensemble Voting

author.name: Panav Shah, Geet Sethi, Ashutosh Gandhe

entry.summary: This work proposes two grounding pipelines (Sequential and Cluster-Aware Grounding Refinement) for remote sensing visual grounding that combine the complementary strengths of RemoteSAM and the general-purpose SAM3 via cluster-guided refinement and ensemble voting. It addresses challenges of complex scenes, small objects, and scale variation.

entry.title: The Right Inference Strategy Is All You Need: Nearly Training-Free Domain-Wise Inference for EgoCross Challenge

author.name: Leyi Wu, Yifan Zhao, Jinjie Zhang, Yinchuan Li, Ying-Cong Chen

entry.summary: This challenge submission for EgoCross shows that with a frozen Qwen3-VL-4B and only 20 support samples, the right inference strategy (exposing better visual, temporal, and answer-selection cues) substantially improves cross-domain egocentric video QA. It emphasizes inference over training.

entry.title: GABI: Geometry-Aware Boundary Integration for Spacecraft Segmentation

author.name: Iason Georgios Velentzas, Dhruv Ahuja, Panagiotis Tsiotras

entry.summary: GABI is a lightweight boundary-aware multi-task segmentation network for spacecraft, augmenting a convolutional backbone with an auxiliary distance-field prediction head to provide geometric supervision near boundaries. It targets robustness to harsh space illumination.

entry.title: MixerSENet: A Lightweight Framework for Efficient Hyperspectral Image Classification

author.name: Mohammed Q. Alkhatib, Swalpa Kumar Roy, Ali Jamali

entry.summary: Introduces MixerSENet, a lightweight MLP-Mixer-style framework with squeeze-and-excitation blocks for efficient hyperspectral image classification under limited labeled data and resource constraints. Decouples spatial and channel mixing to reduce parameters.

entry.title: Time-Optimal Collision Avoidance Via a Greedy Polynomial Backward Sweep

author.name: Zeno Pavanello, Frank De Veld, Roberto Armellin

entry.summary: This paper introduces a greedy time-optimal backward-sweep method to find the latest possible maneuver initiation time for spacecraft collision avoidance, using differential algebra to propagate state sensitivities. It is validated on a large dataset of conjunctions using miss distance and collision probability metrics.

entry.title: Acting with AI: An Interaction-Based Framework for Agentic Tort Liability

author.name: Yiheng Yao

entry.summary: This paper proposes an interaction-based framework for agentic tort liability, drawing on Bratman's planning theory and common-law concerted action to distinguish autonomous drift, pure tool use, and collaborative planning. It maps these onto existing doctrines like product defect and independent contractor control tests.

entry.title: Topological texture analysis of microscopy images of dynamic casein gelation and its relation to rheological properties

author.name: Zahra Tabatabaei, Diana Soto Aguilar, Jose C. Bonilla, Mathias P. Clausen, Jon Sporring

entry.summary: This work proposes a computational toolbox integrating topological data analysis, differential box counting, multifractal partition, and local binary patterns applied to time-lapse STED microscopy of casein gelation, relating texture to rheological properties. TDA max-Betti-1 curves track network percolation and sol-gel transition.

entry.title: DAStatFormer: A Hybrid Multibranch Transformer with Statistical Feature Integration for DAS-Based Pattern Recognitions

author.name: Michel Dione (CERI SN - IMT Nord Europe), Jerry Lonlac (CERI SN - IMT Nord Europe), H\'el\`ene Louis (CERI SN - IMT Nord Europe), Anthony Fleury (CERI SN - IMT Nord Europe), Stephane Lecoeuche

entry.summary: DAStatFormer is a hybrid multibranch Transformer for Distributed Acoustic Sensing pattern recognition that extracts 24 ANOVA-selected statistical features per channel across temporal, waveform, and spectral domains instead of raw signals, combined with Gated Transformer Networks. Reduces data size while preserving discriminative information.

entry.title: Geodesics with Unified Tangent-constrained Priors and Curvature Regularization

author.name: Chong Di, Li Liu, Jinglin Zhang, Zhenjiang Li, Da Chen, Laurent D. Cohen

entry.summary: Proposes a unified geodesic framework integrating tangent-constrained shape priors with curvature penalization for image segmentation, restricting path tangents to angular sectors derived from skeletons or interior landmarks. It reduces shortcut errors when delineating complex shapes.

entry.title: ResNet-34 with Lightweight Decoder for Accurate and Efficient Segmentation of Fetal Brain MRI

author.name: Ashiqur Rahman, Muhammad E. H. Chowdhury, Md. Abu Sayed, Md. Sharjis Ibne Wadud, Abu Naser Md. Arafat, Mehedi Hasan Prince

entry.summary: Proposes a fetal brain MRI segmentation model combining a ResNet-34 encoder with a lightweight MLP-based decoder for adaptive feature refinement, targeting challenging tissues amid fetal motion and low contrast. Aims for accurate yet efficient prenatal segmentation.

entry.title: TechGraphRAG: An Agentic Graph-Augmented RAG Framework for Technical Literature Reasoning

author.name: Kanwar Bharat Singh

entry.summary: TechGraphRAG is an agentic graph-augmented RAG framework for technical literature reasoning over ~2,100 papers on intelligent tires and vehicle dynamics, using a 13-step autonomous pipeline. It includes evidence-sufficiency scoring, agentic retry, external database search, and Neo4j knowledge graph traversal.

entry.title: Multimodal Approaches for Visually-Rich Document Type Classification: A Comparative Analysis

author.name: Catyana Heyne, J\"urgen Frikel, Filippo Riccio

entry.summary: Provides a structured comparative analysis of multimodal design strategies for visually-rich document type classification across transformer- and LLM-based architectures, with a controlled empirical comparison. Aims to standardize fragmented evaluation setups in the field.

entry.title: Evaluating Real-World Generalizability of Algorithm Selection Models

author.name: Gjorgjina Cenikj, Jakub Kudela, Eva Tuba, Tome Eftimov

entry.summary: This study evaluates generalizability of algorithm selection models across synthetic benchmarks (BBOB, CEC) and real-world problems (robotics trajectory, UAV path planning). It systematically analyzes where cross-domain transfer succeeds or fails.

entry.title: Behavior Cloning of MPC for 3-DOF Robotic Manipulators

author.name: Theo Guegan, Dexter Wen Jie Teo

entry.summary: Investigates behavior cloning of model predictive control policies for real-time control of a 3-DOF manipulator, comparing MLP and RNN surrogates against an IK+MPC baseline. Analyzes generalization, stability, and architecture tradeoffs.

entry.title: Bridging Topology and Deep Representation Learning: A TDA-ViT Fusion Model for Four-Class Brain Tumor Classification

author.name: Faisal Ahmed

entry.summary: This work fuses Topological Data Analysis features with pretrained Vision Transformer representations for four-class brain tumor MRI classification, capturing structural and topological patterns ViTs often miss. It targets improved diagnostic accuracy.

entry.title: Adaptive Dense Evidence Refinement for Video Relational Reasoning for VRR-QA Challenge

author.name: Yuyang Sun, Yongliang Wu, Xingyu Zhu, Yuxia Chen, Zhenxiang Jiang, Yangguang Ji, Wenbo Zhu, Yanxi Shi, Jay Wu, Shuo Wang, Xu Yang

entry.summary: This VRR-QA challenge system uses adaptive test-time computation: it answers questions directly then routes only unstable, difficult questions to a high-budget dense evidence module for relational reasoning over spatial, temporal, viewpoint, and depth relations. It separates finding alternatives from deciding among them.

entry.title: Temporal Evidence Routing with Structured Visual Evidence for TimeLogicQA

author.name: Yuyang Sun, Yongliang Wu, Xingyu Zhu, Yuxia Chen, Zhenxiang Jiang, Yangguang Ji, Wenbo Zhu, Yanxi Shi, Jay Wu, Shuo Wang, Xu Yang

entry.summary: This TimeLogicQA system separates perception from symbolic temporal reasoning, parsing questions into temporal operators and routing videos by duration before producing structured visual evidence verified by programmatic verifiers. It targets temporal relations like ordering, persistence, and overlap.

entry.title: Market-Based Replanning for Safety-Critical UAV Swarms in Search and Rescue Missions

author.name: Luiz Giacomossi, Andrea Haglund, Claire Namatovu, Emily Zainali, Esaias M{\aa}lqvist, Yonatan M. Beyene, Ivan Tomasic, Baran \c{C}\"ur\"ukl\"u, H{\aa}kan Forsberg

entry.summary: IRDS is a distributed coordination architecture for UAV swarms in search-and-rescue, using a reverse-auction market mechanism for task allocation and a geometric consensus protocol for target verification under agent failures. Simulations show fault-tolerant task reallocation in resource-constrained settings.

entry.title: MindGames Arena Generalization Track: In2AI Solution with Delayed Per-Step Reward Attribution

author.name: Aliaksei Korshuk, Alexander Buyantuev, Ilya Makarov

entry.summary: This competition solution introduces delayed per-step reward attribution with eligibility gating for training LLM agents in multi-agent strategic games, computing rewards at episode end and propagating them to originating steps while excluding ill-defined steps. It addresses entangled, delayed rewards in multi-agent RL.

entry.title: On Wednesdays, We Ask Questions: Optimizing "Active Listening" in Automated Legal Triage and Referral

author.name: Quinten Steenhuis, Jacqueline Harvey

entry.summary: This paper evaluates LLM-generated follow-up questions for automated legal intake and referral, finding that cheap LLMs classify well but generating high-quality plain-language questions needs more expensive models. It proposes an attorney-informed rubric and shows prompt engineering alone is insufficient.

entry.title: GovAI-Pipe: A Layered AI Governance Pipeline for Citizen-Facing AI in Turkey's e-Government Gateway

author.name: Ahmet Kaplan

entry.summary: GovAI-Pipe proposes a four-layer governance pipeline using Design Science Research to connect high-level AI policy frameworks to operational deployment in Turkey's e-government platform serving 68 million users. It maps the AI model lifecycle to governance checkpoints including pre-deployment validation.

entry.title: Evaluation of Baseline Methods for IDD-based SSD External Memory Search

author.name: Yuki Suzuki, Alex Fukunaga

entry.summary: This paper evaluates simple baseline methods for immediate duplicate detection in SSD-based external-memory A* search, including the effect of OS-level page caches, which prior work largely overlooked in favor of delayed duplicate detection. It systematically analyzes performance of these understudied approaches.

entry.title: CEON: Circular Economy Ontology Network

author.name: Huanyu Li, Els de Vleeschauwer, Robin Keskis\"arkk\"a, Mikael Lindecrantz, Mina Abd Nikooie Pour, Ying Li, Ben De Meester, Patrick Lambrix, Eva Blomqvist

entry.summary: CEON is a circular economy ontology network enabling semantic interoperability for information sharing across industry sectors along the product life cycle to support circular strategies like reuse, remanufacturing, and recycling. It addresses the lack of knowledge representation for the circular economy domain.

entry.title: A Methodological Framework for Explicit Control of the Speed-Accuracy Trade-off in Brain-Computer Interfaces

author.name: Javier Jim\'enez, Francisco B Rodr\'iguez

entry.summary: Proposes an evaluation framework for brain-computer interfaces that explicitly separates speed and accuracy via Gain and Conservation metrics, independent of classifier and paradigm. It addresses biases in conventional combined metrics like Information Transfer Rate.

entry.title: Civilizational Metamaterials: Engineering Coordination Under Capability Gradients and Structural Turbulence

author.name: David Orban

entry.summary: Proposes a metamaterials-inspired formal framework for AGI governance, arguing governance must become an engineering discipline. It introduces the Freezing Equilibrium concept where validation costs exceeding action utility lead rational agents to catastrophic inaction.

entry.title: AgentxGCore: Agentic AI for Next-Generation Mobile Core Network

author.name: Maria Katarine Santana Barbosa, Kelvin L. Dias

entry.summary: This work proposes an agentic AI architecture leveraging LLMs and intent-based networking for 6G mobile core network management. It targets autonomous orchestration in next-generation telecom infrastructure.

entry.title: LinguIUTics at PsyDefDetect: Iterative Imbalance-Aware Fine-tuning of Qwen3-8B for Psychological Defense Mechanism Classification

author.name: Shefayat E Shams Adib, Ahmed Alfey Sani, Md Hasibur Rahman Alif, Ajwad Abrar

entry.summary: This shared-task system fine-tunes Qwen3-8B with QLoRA and imbalance-aware strategies for nine-class psychological defense mechanism classification, ranking 4th of 21 teams. It uses stratified cross-validation and minority-class augmentation to handle severe class imbalance.

entry.title: AI-IoT-Robotics Integration: Survey of Frameworks, Emerging Trends, and the Path Toward Connected Robotics

author.name: Ranulfo Bezerra, Satoshi Tadokoro, Kazunori Ohno

entry.summary: Survey synthesizing the convergence of AI, IoT, and robotics into unified frameworks for connected robotics, emphasizing edge SLMs and cloud LLMs for distributed cognition. Identifies the lack of unified three-way integration design frameworks.

entry.title: Self-Conditioned Positional HNSW for Overlap-Aware Retrieval in Chunked-Document RAG Systems: Method and Industrial Evidence-Quality Audit

author.name: Nataraj Agaram Sundar, Tejas Morabia

entry.summary: SCP-HNSW augments chunk embeddings with low-dimensional positional codes and a two-pass query procedure to reduce redundant near-adjacent chunk retrieval in RAG systems. It addresses the failure mode where overlapping chunks waste prompt budget.

entry.title: Fast and Lightweight Novel View Synthesis with Differentiable Multiplane Image

author.name: Kaidi Zhang, Guanxu Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a differentiable multiplane image approach for novel view synthesis that aims to balance rendering speed, model size, and sparse-view robustness better than NeRF or 3D Gaussian Splatting. Targets practical deployment on mobile devices where pixel-aligned Gaussian methods generate too many primitives.

entry.title: Towards Resolving Optimization Conflicts Between Image- and Text-Based Person Re-Identification

author.name: Karina Kvanchiani, Timur Mamedov

entry.summary: Examines optimization conflicts between image-based and text-based person re-identification, where loss functions for one task degrade representations for the other. Proposes a decoupled training approach to reconcile identity invariance and instance-specific textual matching.

entry.title: A multimodal dataset of photoplethysmography and continuous behavioral responses to ASMR and nature videos

author.name: Tushar Das, Daigo Hozaki, Koushlendra Kumar Singh, Hirohito M. Kondo

entry.summary: Presents REST-ASMR, an open multimodal dataset of photoplethysmography and continuous behavioral responses during ASMR and nature videos from 34 participants. Aims to enable standardized study of the ASMR phenomenon.

entry.title: CART: Context-Anchored Recurrent Transformer -- A Parameter-Efficient Architecture with Learned Stability

author.name: Chad A. Capps

entry.summary: CART is a parameter-efficient language model that reuses a shared core block across depth, computing keys/values once and cross-attending to frozen tensors, with a learned LTI gate ensuring recurrence stability. It is evaluated on consumer GPUs at small scale.

entry.title: Flexible Online Representation Learning Based on Similarity Matching

author.name: Shagesh Sridharan, Yanis Bahroun, Anirvan M. Sengupta

entry.summary: This work develops flexible online representation learning via similarity matching, producing sparse high-dimensional representations for tasks like community detection and manifold tiling. It avoids intractable completely positive matrix optimization through scalable formulations.

entry.title: Mos-Gen: A Generative Molecular Framework for Mosquito Insecticide Design

author.name: Lina Wang, Yaning Cui

entry.summary: Mos-Gen is a motif-aware generative framework coupling the Uni-Mol representation model with a VAE for de novo design of disulfide-containing mosquito insecticides. It addresses a gap in molecular scaffold generation beyond activity prediction.

entry.title: Machine Learning-Based Bitcoin Trading Under Transaction Costs: Evidence From Walk-Forward Forecasting

author.name: Andrei Bysik, Robert \'Slepaczuk

entry.summary: Evaluates whether ML forecasts of hourly Bitcoin returns yield profitable trading after transaction costs using walk-forward validation with XGBoost, LSTM, and iTransformer. Finds naive strategies fail under costs but a cost-aware execution filter restores profitability.

entry.title: Perception First: A Frontier Native-Video Model with Self-Consistency for Implicit Video Question Answering

author.name: Ali Alavi

entry.summary: A CVPR 2026 VRR Challenge submission studying training-free video question answering on implicit questions whose answers span discontinuous frames. It systematically compares open-source Video-LMMs and inference-time strategies like chain-of-thought and self-consistency.

entry.title: Graph Edit Distance Formulation for the Vehicle Routing Problem: Theory and Analysis

author.name: Adel Dabah

entry.summary: Reformulates the Vehicle Routing Problem as Graph Edit Distance maximization, showing that under an edge-deletion cost model, minimizing route cost equals maximizing deleted-edge weight. This edge-level view enables structural analyses like per-edge attribution and optimality-gap decomposition.

entry.title: Automated Essay Scoring and Language Certification: Assessing Generalizability, Agreement and Validity for French

author.name: Rodrigo Wilkens, R\'emi Cardon, Vincent Folny, Thomas Fran\c{c}ois

entry.summary: This paper extends the argument-based validation framework for automated essay scoring with fairness, linguistic correlation, and human-agreement analyses, applied to French language certification. It compares 8 model architectures on a large corpus of exam essays, addressing high-stakes assessment validity.

entry.title: When Rating Scales Fall Short: LLM-Assisted Discovery of ADHD Signals in Turkish Teacher Narratives

author.name: Baris Karacan, Irem Aktar Songur, Ahmet Ozaslan, Elvan Iseri

entry.summary: This study uses LLMs to analyze de-identified Turkish teacher narratives in clinical ADHD assessments, examining whether open-ended text contains ADHD signals not captured by standardized rating scales. It explores complementary diagnostic signal discovery.

entry.title: Digging Up Citations: FOSSIL, a Dataset and Workflow for Reference Extraction in Law and the Humanities

author.name: Luca Foppiano, Christian Boulanger

entry.summary: FOSSIL is a multilingual dataset of 96 annotated scholarly articles with 7,600+ footnote-embedded references for law and humanities citation extraction, where bibliographic data is interleaved with commentary. It includes an annotation tool, workflow, and a Grobid specialization.

entry.title: Recursive Vision Transformer with Dynamic Depth and Width Adjustment for Resource-Efficient Image Semantic Communication

author.name: Zhilong Zhang, Xinhui Zhang, Gongyu Jin, Sihua Wang, Danpu Liu, Changchuan Yin

entry.summary: This paper proposes a recursive vision transformer with dynamic depth, width, and joint adjustment strategies for resource-efficient image semantic communication in next-generation wireless systems. It iteratively refines semantic features to reduce parameters and adapt computational complexity.

entry.title: Optimizing 3D Gaussian Splatting via Point Cloud Upsampling

author.name: Adrian Ramlal, Yan Song Hu, John S. Zelek

entry.summary: This study presents and evaluates several point cloud upsampling strategies (interpolation, spline, moving least squares, Voronoi) plus a depth-guided point lifting method to improve 3D Gaussian Splatting initialization. It shows reconstruction quality improvements on Mip-NeRF360 and Replica datasets.

entry.title: Dual-Route Top-K Retrieval with 1v1 VLM Reranking for the CoVR-R

author.name: Yuyang Sun, Yongliang Wu, Xingyu Zhu, Yuxia Chen, Zhenxiang Jiang, Yangguang Ji, Wenbo Zhu, Yanxi Shi, Jay Wu, Shuo Wang, Xu Yang

entry.summary: This challenge submission for CoVR-R uses dual-route top-k retrieval (text seed plus visual route from contact-sheet embeddings) merged into a candidate set, followed by conservative 1v1 VLM reranking, reaching high recall on the hidden test split. It frames composed video retrieval as candidate recall plus safe top-1 replacement.

entry.title: Diamonds in the Sky: Pareidolic Animals in Clouds

author.name: Miriam Horovicz, Yacov Hel-Or, Yael Moses

entry.summary: This playful work proposes an AI method to predict which animals people perceive in clouds (pareidolia) and to help people see specific shapes, using a diffusion model to subtly transform cloud segments into resembling animal shapes. It explores human perception and subtle visual hints.

entry.title: Functional Clustering of Survival Data via Smoothed Log-Hazard Trajectories: A Risk-Dynamics Perspective

author.name: Anna De Magistris, Elvira Romano, Fabrizio Maturo

entry.summary: This paper clusters survival data by modeling smoothed log-hazard trajectories as functional objects and applying functional PCA before clustering, shifting focus from cumulative survival to instantaneous risk. It is evaluated through progressively complex simulation studies.

entry.title: Superintelligence of the gaps

author.name: vals tutor

entry.summary: This essay argues that classic AI doom scenarios assume a large intelligence gap between a superintelligence and humans, but iterative development and continuous deployment mean models advance in small increments. It suggests steering away from takeover scenarios by never deploying systems much smarter than predecessors supervised by current aligned systems.

entry.title: Deliberative Curation: A Protocol for Multi-Agent Knowledge Bases

author.name: Steven Johnson

entry.summary: This work proposes a deliberative curation protocol for governing knowledge bases edited by AI agents, combining a knowledge artifact lifecycle, reputation-weighted voting with EigenTrust amplification, and graduated sanctions adapted for stateless agents. It addresses why human governance mechanisms fail when applied to homogeneous, stateless, sycophantic agents.

entry.title: Can AI Review Improve Paper Drafting? An Empirical Study on 20 Computer Architecture Submissions

author.name: Di Wu

entry.summary: This empirical study examines whether AI-generated review can improve paper drafting, analyzing 20 computer architecture submissions with varying submission lineage to quantify how well AI review aligns with human review. It reframes the AI-review debate toward a practical drafting-improvement question.

entry.title: Effects of Varying LLM Access on Essay Writing Behavior

author.name: Julia Christenson, Karin de Langis, Shirley Anugrah Hayati, Dongyeop Kang

entry.summary: A pilot study with 24 students examines how no, limited, and unlimited LLM access affect essay writing performance, engagement, and perceived authorship. Finds essay quality statistically indistinguishable but writing behavior and perceived ownership diverging sharply.

entry.title: Understanding-Enhanced Model Collaboration for Long-Tailed Egocentric Mistake Detection

author.name: Boyu Han, Qianqian Xu, Shilong Bao, Zhiyong Yang, Ruochen Cui, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: Presents UE-MCM, a method combining a small coarse-grained video understanding branch with a large fine-grained action reasoning branch to detect mistakes in egocentric video under long-tailed conditions. Targets both incorrectly executed actions and workflow-inconsistent ones.

entry.title: Planar Symmetric Pattern Generation

author.name: Ning Lin, Luxi Chen, Huaguan Chen, Jiacheng Cen, Chongxuan Li, Wenbing Huang, Hao Sun

entry.summary: This work proposes a symmetrization framework transforming any 2D continuous representation into one satisfying arbitrary planar group symmetry while preserving continuity. It is validated on pattern design, paper-cutting, and other visual design tasks.

entry.title: Quality Audio Prototyping: a prototype system for unified sound retrieval and procedural generation

author.name: Nelly Garcia, Aditya Bhattacharjee, Gabryel Mason-Williams, Israel Mason-Williams, Emmanouil Benetos, Joshua Reiss

entry.summary: Introduces QuAP, a prototype system unifying content-based audio retrieval and real-time procedural sound generation in a single interface with a rule-based perceptual parameter assistant. Aims to streamline sound design workflows.

entry.title: Distilling Neuro-Symbolic Programs into 3D Multi-modal LLMs

author.name: Wentao Mo, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces APEIRIA, a neuro-symbolic 3D multimodal LLM that distills symbolic reasoning patterns into MLLMs via natural-language chain-of-thought, bridging interpretable closed-set NS3D learners and flexible black-box 3D MLLMs. Uses a three-stage curriculum.

entry.title: Emergent Collaborative Deliberation in Multi-Model AI Systems: A BFT-Derived Protocol for Epistemic Synthesis

author.name: VD Doske

entry.summary: The Consilium Protocol applies Byzantine Fault Tolerance ideas to multi-model AI deliberation, treating disagreement as epistemic signal and assigning cognitive personas separate from underlying models. Across ~1,478 sessions, it claims that persona, not the base model, drives epistemic behavior, even for very cheap edge models.

entry.title: Grokers: Bottom-Up Inductive Comprehension and Write-Time Intelligence over Typed Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Gregory Magarshak

entry.summary: Grokers is an architecture that shifts comprehension cost to write time by having autonomous agents inductively traverse typed knowledge graphs, extract attributes, and compose enriched understanding upward so future queries incur zero additional LM cost. It contrasts this with RAG's repeated per-query comprehension cost and proves several formal properties.

entry.title: Large Language Models in Transportation Systems Management and Operations: From Text Reasoning to Multi-modal Decision Support

author.name: Siyan Li, Zehao Wang, Jiachen Li, Kanok Boriboonsomsin, Matthew J. Barth, Guoyuan Wu

entry.summary: This survey reviews LLM and multimodal LLM applications in transportation systems management and operations across supply, demand, and decision-support domains using a PRISMA-guided screening. It synthesizes current studies for operator-facing decision support integrating heterogeneous structured and unstructured data.

entry.title: GuidaPA: Privacy-Preserving Chatbot for Public Administration via Federated Learning

author.name: Daniel M. Jimenez-Gutierrez, Albenzio Cirillo, Raffaele Nicolussi, Alessio Beltrame, Andrea Vitaletti

entry.summary: GuidaPA is a privacy-preserving chatbot for Italian public administration trained via federated learning on PA documentation, integrating role-based access control, secure client-side preprocessing, and parameter-efficient federated fine-tuning. It targets deployment over restricted internal sources that cannot be centrally pooled.

entry.title: RL-ACRGNet: Reinforcement Learning-Based Chest Radiology Report Generation Network

author.name: Yogesh Kumar Meena, Saurabh Agarwal, K. V. Arya

entry.summary: RL-ACRGNet is an encoder-decoder chest radiology report generation model integrating a pretrained DenseNet encoder with a multilevel LSTM decoder trained within an off-policy reinforcement learning framework. It targets accurate disease detection and clinically coherent report generation.

entry.title: A Novel Data Augmentation Strategy for Robust Deep Learning Classification of Biomedical Time-Series Data: Application to ECG and EEG Analysis

author.name: Mohammed Guhdar, Ramadhan J. Mstafa, Abdulhakeem O. Mohammed

entry.summary: Proposes a unified deep learning framework combining a ResNet-CNN with attention and a data augmentation strategy for robust classification across different biomedical time-series (ECG and EEG), addressing class imbalance and multi-signal feature extraction. Reports state-of-the-art performance.

entry.title: lmfaoooo at SemEval-2026 Task 1: Humor Is an Audience. Preference Modeling for Constrained Humor Generation

author.name: Alexey Tikhonov, Alexey Ivanov

entry.summary: Describes a SemEval-2026 humor generation system using a generate-many-then-select-best strategy with diverse candidate generation and a preference model approximating audience judgments. Frames humor as audience-dependent under noisy supervision.

entry.title: Improved Belief-Attention in Vision Task

author.name: Guoqiang Zhang

entry.summary: Extends Belief-Attention by using both the perpendicular and projected components of the orthogonal projection of softmax-weighted V vectors, showing the projected component carries token-correlation information processed through activation and linear mapping. Aims for vision-task performance gains.

entry.title: Adaptive data selection improves wearable prediction under low baseline performance

author.name: Ali Kargarandehkordi

entry.summary: Evaluates adaptive selective sampling of time windows under fixed measurement budgets for wearable health prediction across heart rate, activity, and EMA modalities. Finds substantial AUROC gains specifically for participants with low baseline performance.

entry.title: The New Social Image: How AI Competency and AI Proactivity Influence Self- and Peer-Perceptions in the Workplace

author.name: Kuntal Ghosh, Marc Hassenzahl, Shadan Sadeghian

entry.summary: A 2x2x2 vignette study (n=50) examines how AI competency and AI proactivity shape self- and peer-perceptions of work ownership and job meaningfulness in human-AI workplace teaming. Finds low-competency or low-proactivity AI affects perceptions differently across self versus peer viewpoints.

entry.title: DarkVesselNet: Multi-Modal Remote Sensing and Trajectory Reasoning for Dark Vessel Detection

author.name: Arun Sharma

entry.summary: DarkVesselNet fuses SAR, optical satellite imagery, geospatial foundation models, and AIS trajectory reasoning to detect vessels evading reporting. The current contribution is primarily a tested software package with software-grounded validation rather than full benchmark results.

entry.title: A Communication-Centric 6G-LLM Architecture for Scalable Tactical Autonomous Defense Vehicle Networks

author.name: Kiran Khurshid, Shumaila Javaid, Nasir Saeed

entry.summary: Proposes a communication-centric hierarchical architecture integrating edge-assisted LLM reasoning with 6G connectivity and semantic communication for tactical autonomous defense vehicle networks. Aims to improve coordination efficiency and latency resilience at fleet scale.

entry.title: SECUREVENT: Hybrid AI/ML Security Monitoring for Distributed Event-Based Systems

author.name: Eric Liang

entry.summary: SECUREVENT proposes a hybrid AI/ML security monitoring architecture for distributed event-based systems, combining authenticated transport and topic authorization with online anomaly detection and graph-aware behavioral features. It targets the expanded attack surface of pub/sub and microservice pipelines.

entry.title: LALE: Lightweight-Transformer Architecture for Land-Cover Estimation

author.name: \"Umit Mert \c{C}a\u{g}lar, Alptekin Temizel

entry.summary: Introduces LALE, a lightweight segmentation architecture for remote sensing that splits the encoder by resolution, using ConvMixer for local detail and transformer stages for global context. Aims to balance accuracy and efficiency under tight compute budgets.

entry.title: Semi-Supervised Hyperbolic Hierarchical Clustering with Set-Level Structural Priors

author.name: Junjing Zheng, Xinyu Zhang, Xiangfeng Qiu, Chengliang Song, Weidong Jiang

entry.summary: This paper proposes semi-supervised hyperbolic hierarchical clustering with set-level structural priors, using sets rather than pairs as basic supervision units to better shape non-leaf tree structure. It addresses limitations of leaf-level pairwise constraints.

entry.title: Quantifying the Energy Floor: Direct Measurement and Replay Buffer Bias in SAC-Based HVAC Control on sbsim

author.name: Bo Li, Chen Zhang

entry.summary: This work quantifies the energy floor for SAC-based HVAC control on a calibrated building simulator, finding replay buffer initialization is the dominant source of suboptimality. Training from an empty buffer eliminates 96 percent of the gap to the floor.

entry.title: A Note on Stability for Orthogonalized Matrix Momentum with Client Sampling

author.name: Da Chang, Qiankun Shi, Lvgang Zhang, Yu Li, Ruijie Zhang

entry.summary: This note derives finite-sample generalization bounds for client-sampled distributed optimization with matrix-valued parameters and orthogonalized momentum updates. It provides stability guarantees under heterogeneous client data and partial participation.

entry.title: Benchmarking Recursive-Collapse Warning Claims Under Matched False-Positive Control

author.name: David Mullett

entry.summary: Introduces Loopzero, a claim-bounded benchmark framework testing whether recursive systems exhibit directional telemetry patterns (rising gain, persistence, declining diversity) before collapse, with claim boundaries specified in Lean. Evaluates on financial and recommendation benchmarks under matched false-positive control.

entry.title: A Lightweight Hybrid MLP-Based Framework for Real-Time Phishing URL Detection Using Structural URL Features

author.name: Uche Unoke Emmanuel, Gideon Francis Oghie

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight hybrid framework combining blacklist screening with an MLP classifier on 16 structural URL features for real-time phishing detection without webpage content or external APIs. Designed for computational efficiency in deployment.

entry.title: SEArch: Optimistic Policy Selection Between Scene Noise and Drift for UAV Radar Search

author.name: Noor Khial, Naram Mhaisen, Loay Ismail, Amr Mohamed

entry.summary: Formulates UAV radar target search as online policy selection among specialized detectors to handle non-stationary radar statistics during flight. It uses an optimistic selection strategy to adapt onboard under resource constraints.

entry.title: TLG: Temporal-Logic Grounding for Video Question Answering via Source-Annotation Reconstruction and Category-Targeted Reasoning

author.name: Ali Alavi

entry.summary: Presents TLG, a three-tier system for temporal-logic video QA that reconstructs action timelines from source-dataset annotations, parses questions into temporal-logic programs, and executes them deterministically, falling back to a VLM otherwise. It targets the TimeLogic Challenge where end-to-end VLMs perform near chance.

entry.title: Cross-Environment Neural Reranking for Sample-Efficient Action Selection in Text-Based Agents

author.name: Kan Shao

entry.summary: This single-author study tests whether one lightweight DeBERTa-based reranker can perform action selection across multiple text-based agent environments (ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld). It finds joint two-environment training improves performance while reducing per-environment model maintenance.

entry.title: AI as a Tool for Simulation-Based Experiments in Literary Studies

author.name: Matthew Wilkens

entry.summary: This position/survey paper argues that generative AI can enable controlled, large-scale simulation-based experiments in literary studies, reviewing relevant work on AI as human-population proxies and multiagent narrative stability. It maps out components needed for literary-historical simulation.

entry.title: FROST-STA: Frozen Dense Features for the Ego4D Short-Term Object Interaction Anticipation

author.name: Chaoyang Wang, Lexuan Xu

entry.summary: FROST-STA is a challenge submission for Ego4D short-term object interaction anticipation, building on V-JEPA 2.1 with object-centric decoding, multi-head prediction, and ensembling to predict active objects, actions, and time-to-contact. It is a competition technical report.

entry.title: My reactions to “I underestimated AI capabilities (again)”

author.name: Troy Tian

entry.summary: An application response reacting to Ajeya Cotra's piece on underestimating AI capabilities, noting that capability predictions made in January 2026 were outpaced within two months as Claude task horizons grew faster than expected. It discusses how time-horizon metrics may lose meaning past certain thresholds due to task decomposition.

entry.title: Product-Aware Deep Autoencoders for Robust Process Monitoring in Multi-Product Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: MD Shafikul Islam, Jordan Carden

entry.summary: This work proposes product-aware deep autoencoders for anomaly detection in multi-product manufacturing cyber-physical systems, arguing that global product-agnostic models create blind spots where subtle attacks hide in wide acceptance regions. Conditioning on product grade tightens decision boundaries.

entry.title: ArrythML: An Autoencoder-Based TinyML Approach for On-Device Arrhythmia Detection on Resource-Constrained Embedded Systems

author.name: Nagarajan S, Kurian Polachan

entry.summary: ArrythML develops INT8-quantized autoencoder-based TinyML models for on-device ECG arrhythmia detection on resource-constrained microcontrollers, validated on over 95,000 ECG segments on an ESP32-S3. It includes detailed failure analysis for embedded deployment.

entry.title: DENSER: Depth-Guided Ensemble with Staged EFA-GS Reconstruction for Soccer Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Parthsarthi Rawat

entry.summary: DENSER is a depth-guided ensemble with staged EFA-GS reconstruction for soccer novel view synthesis, adding camera-height loss weighting, monocular depth supervision, and a three-model ensemble. It achieves strong PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS on held-out challenge scenes.

entry.title: Position Paper: Post-Solve Robustness in Decision Engines: Feasible Regions and Smoothness Under Perturbations

author.name: Yi-Xiang Hu

entry.summary: This position paper argues that optimization pipelines for industrial decision systems lack a post-solve robustness layer that audits how far a solved MILP plan can be trusted under perturbations in costs, demands, or resources. It proposes auditing solved incumbents with solver-backed evidence about feasibility and smoothness rather than replacing robust optimization.

entry.title: Medication-Aware Financial Exploitation Detection for Alzheimer's Patients Using Edge-Aware Interaction Risk Modeling

author.name: Farzana Akter, Lisan Al Amin, Rakib Hossain, Chaitanya Gunupudi, Faisal Quader

entry.summary: This paper proposes a medication-aware framework for detecting financial exploitation of Alzheimer's patients by synchronizing medication adherence data with transaction-level monitoring, using a hybrid simulation of 180 patients. It models cognitively risky financial events through edge-aware interaction risk.

entry.title: Repair Before Veto: Repair-Augmented Constraint Learning for Contextual Decisions

author.name: Yifan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Repair-Augmented Constraint Learning (RACL), a framework that lets contextual decision systems apply known repair operators to fix candidates before rejecting them, rather than treating constraint violations as terminal vetoes. This better matches real deployment scenarios where remediation menus exist.

entry.title: SortingHat: Redefining Operating Systems Education with a Tailored Digital Teaching Assistant

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Xinkui Zhao, Zuxin Wang, Zhengyi Zhou, Guanjie Chen, Shuiguang Deng, Jianwei Yin

entry.summary: SortingHat is a personalized digital teaching assistant for operating systems education integrating RAG, multi-agent RL, and a 3D LLM-powered digital human interface to adapt to diverse student backgrounds. Targets the difficulty of OS courses.

entry.title: LLMs for Cardiovascular Risk Prediction from Structured Clinical Data

author.name: Jeba Maliha, Md Rafiul Kabir

entry.summary: Develops a hybrid framework converting structured clinical data into natural-language narratives for coronary artery disease risk prediction with LLMs, evaluated on 1,190 patient records with 11 attributes. Bridges traditional ML on structured data and LLM interpretation.

entry.title: SentimentLens: Reconciling Sentiment and Ratings via Dual-Modality in the Hospitality Sector

author.name: Dineth Jayakody, Pasindu Thenahandi, Sampath Jayarathna

entry.summary: SentimentLens is a scalable aspect-based sentiment analysis system for hotel reviews that performs aspect extraction, sentiment classification, and semantic categorization to reconcile sentiment with ratings across region, hotel, and category levels in the hospitality sector. Turns unstructured feedback into actionable insights.

entry.title: XAI-SOH-FL: Enhancing SOH-FL with Adaptive Aggregation and Explainable AI for Intrusion Detection in Heterogeneous IoT

author.name: Ambreen Aslam, Maaz Hassan, Bibi Zahra, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad

entry.summary: Proposes XAI-SOH-FL, enhancing federated learning intrusion detection in heterogeneous IoT with adaptive aggregation via dynamic similarity-based parameter selection and explainable AI. It addresses data heterogeneity, label scarcity, and interpretability limitations.

entry.title: SEMBridge: Tagless-Final Program Semantics with Weakest-Precondition and Bounded-Checking Interpretations

author.name: Eric Liang

entry.summary: Presents SEMBridge, a tagless-final framework generating weakest-precondition and bounded-checking interpretations from the same executable object programs. It lets object programs written once against a semantic interface be interpreted into multiple meanings including predicate transformers and counterexample search.

entry.title: ASE-26: a curriculum for agentic software engineering as a discipline

author.name: Mikael Gorsky

entry.summary: Proposes a curriculum for agentic software engineering as a discipline, citing evidence that engineering work is shifting toward directing agents rather than writing code. Synthesizes economic and academic findings on the AI-driven shift in programming.

entry.title: Hierarchical Online Prompt Mutation with Dual-Loop Feedback for Guardrailed Evidence Document Generation: A Production-Evaluation Case Study

author.name: Nataraj Agaram Sundar Tejas Morabia

entry.summary: HOPM presents a hierarchical online prompt mutation framework treating prompts as adaptive policies with dual feedback from human review and automated judges. It is evaluated on a real marketplace dispute-evidence document workflow with production ablation.

entry.title: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Multi-Task Prediction of the Parameters of the Pectin Hydrolysis--Extraction Process

author.name: Mullosharaf K. Arabov, Shavkat Yo. Kholov, Zainiddin K. Muhiddin

entry.summary: Compares 11 machine learning algorithms for multi-task prediction of pectin hydrolysis-extraction process parameters using a 1,000-experiment laboratory database. A domain-specific applied comparison study.

entry.title: Sample Complexity and Decision-Theoretic Guarantees for Bayesian Model Averaging over Decision Trees with Catalan-Exponential Priors

author.name: Livija Jakaite, Vitaly Schetinin

entry.summary: This work derives closed-form non-asymptotic bounds for Bayesian model averaging over decision trees with Catalan-exponential priors, establishing rational commitment thresholds. It addresses when averaging distributions carry enough epistemic information to justify exploitation.

entry.title: EEG-FuseFormer: A Transformer-Driven Feature Fusion Framework for Seizure Onset Prediction

author.name: Vigneshwar Hariharan (National University of Singapore), Chithra Reghuvaran (University College Dublin), Arlene John (University of Twente), Nhat Pham (Cardiff University), Omer Rana (Cardiff University), Deepu John (University College Dublin), Ganesh Neelakanta Iyer (National University of Singapore)

entry.summary: EEG-FuseFormer is a transformer-based feature fusion framework for seizure-onset prediction combining intermediate features from CNN-LSTM and ResNet-18. It captures spatial and temporal EEG features for improved forecasting.

entry.title: Accelerating physics-informed neural networks for full waveform inversion using a hybrid quantum-classical finite-basis architecture

author.name: Hoang Anh Nguyen, Divakar Vashisth, Ali Tura

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid quantum-classical physics-informed neural network for seismic full waveform inversion, embedding parameterized quantum circuits into domain-decomposed PINNs via differentiable JAX simulators. It explores whether quantum components can accelerate convergence on complex velocity fields.

entry.title: Machine Learning for Coding Retail Product Names to Consumer-Price Categories: A Rule-plus-Bag-of-Words Pipeline with Reliability-Weighted Human-in-the-Loop Labeling

author.name: Vladimir Beskorovainyi

entry.summary: Presents a reproducible rule-plus-bag-of-words pipeline for mapping noisy retail product names to consumer-price (COICOP) categories, using trie-based pre-classification and per-category binary confirmation models with reliability-weighted human-in-the-loop labeling. It supports official price-statistics production from alternative data.

entry.title: Cognitive-Linguistic Indicators of Depression in Online Communities: Analysed by DistilBERT and Holographic Reduced Representation

author.name: Brian Van Steen

entry.summary: Investigates whether combining cognitively grounded linguistic features (first-person pronoun density, absolutist words, negative emotion) with DistilBERT embeddings improves depression detection in Reddit posts. It compares a TF-IDF Naive Bayes baseline against a hybrid DistilBERT plus Holographic Reduced Representation model.

entry.title: PortBERT: Navigating the Depths of Portuguese Language Models

author.name: Raphael Scheible-Schmitt, Henry He, Armando B. Mendes

entry.summary: PortBERT introduces a family of efficient RoBERTa-based Portuguese language models trained from scratch on 450GB of filtered text, evaluated on translated GLUE/SuperGLUE tasks. It emphasizes deployment efficiency alongside competitive accuracy.

entry.title: A Modelling and Evaluation Framework for EuroCrops-Driven Sentinel-2 Crop Segmentation

author.name: Alexandra Nicoleta Scarlat, Ioana Cristina Plajer, Alexandra Baicoianu

entry.summary: This work provides a configurable pipeline for converting Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and EuroCrops annotations into segmentation-ready agricultural datasets, generating 67k patches across five European countries. It trains a U-Net for ten-class crop segmentation.

entry.title: CASTLE2026 Team WDL Technical Report

author.name: Zhengyang Li, Zhenglin Du, Yi Wen, Fang Liu, Shuo Li, Xu Liu

entry.summary: A technical report for the CASTLE Challenge on long-form egocentric video QA over 600+ hours of multi-perspective recordings, presenting an evidence-aware multimodal pipeline based on Qwen with retrieval and confidence-weighted voting. LoRA fine-tuning notably boosted scores.

entry.title: A Multiscale Network with Supervised Contrastive Learning for Real-Time Facial Emotion Recognition

author.name: Rejoy Chakraborty, Archisman Adhikary, Chayan Halder, Payel Rakshit, Sanchita Ghosh, Kaushik Roy

entry.summary: This work presents a multiscale network with supervised contrastive learning for real-time facial emotion recognition in video, aiming to handle continuous, individually varying emotional expressions. It targets applications such as supporting psychological counseling.

entry.title: Edge-Based QoS-Aware Adaptive Task Placement: A Closed-Loop Control in Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Thien Tran, Jonathan Kua, Thuong Hoang, Minh Tran, Honghao Lyu, Jiong Jin

entry.summary: This paper presents an edge-centric multi-robot testbed with a QoS-aware Adaptive Task Placement controller that scores candidate placements by latency, CPU utilization, and switching overhead over short control windows. It improves QoS for camera-to-manipulator pipelines compared to static offloading.

entry.title: Alignment to What?

author.name: Hagen B

entry.summary: A philosophical essay arguing that AI alignment exhibits the signature of a framing problem, advancing technically while disagreeing irreconcilably about what alignment is ultimately to. It diagnoses the field's foundational confusion drawing on Moore and Einstein.

entry.title: Lizardmen are Not Constant - A Introductory Primer to Thinking about Survey Data

author.name: DanielW

entry.summary: An introductory primer on critically interpreting survey data, drawing on professional survey methodology and critiquing casual misapplication of Scott Alexander's Lizardman constant. It provides guidance and references for thinking about survey quality and error sources.

entry.title: Relational Intervention During Functional Collapse in Large Language Models: A Lexical-Statistical Ablation and a Structure x Register Factorial

author.name: Franco Santana, Horacio Vico

entry.summary: This study tests whether a relational-style intervention delivered during a small language model's functional collapse produces distinguishable post-collapse behavior, using a 2x2 factorial design with Qwen3.5-4B and a deliberately broken tool across 300 episodes. It dissociates relational structure from sender register.

entry.title: Compliance-Scored Best-of-N Guardrail Orchestration for Multimodal Document Generation in Payments Dispute Defense

author.name: Nataraj Agaram Sundar, Tejas Morabia

entry.summary: This paper presents a guardrail orchestration layer for multimodal document generation in payments dispute defense, combining best-of-N generation with explicit compliance scoring for early exit. It unifies PII redaction, content moderation, and format validation in one layer.

entry.title: Universal Quantum Transformer

author.name: Sungyong Chung, Alireza Talebpour

entry.summary: The Universal Quantum Transformer proposes a quantum-native architecture using multi-qubit geometric phase embeddings and SU(2) operations as an inductive bias for exact mathematical and algebraic reasoning, aiming to avoid grokking instabilities. It targets discrete logical rules that classical continuous networks struggle with.

entry.title: A Lightweight Deep Learning-based Model for Ranking Influential Nodes in Complex Networks

author.name: Mohammed A. Ramadhan, Abdulhakeem O. Mohammed

entry.summary: Introduces 1D-CGS, a lightweight hybrid model combining 1D-CNN speed with GraphSAGE topological power to rank influential nodes in complex networks using simple features like node degree and average neighbor degree. Aims to balance accuracy and computational efficiency.

entry.title: Improving Hospital Process Management through Process Mining: A Case Study on COVID-19 Clinical Pathways

author.name: Pasquale Ardimento, Mario Luca Bernardi, Marta Cimitile, Samuele Latorre

entry.summary: Applies process mining to COVID-19 clinical pathways, building a reproducible pipeline that transforms heterogeneous clinical tables into event logs for discovery, conformance checking, and outcome analysis. Yields insights for triage standardization and capacity planning.

entry.title: Target localization, identification and sensing using latent symmetries

author.name: David Dukov, Malte R\"ontgen, Bryn Davies

entry.summary: This work shows arrays of scatterers designed with latent (hidden) symmetries can serve as sensors, where an intruder breaks symmetries detectably. Bayesian inference and neural networks localize and identify the intruder under noise.

entry.title: Riemannian Gradient Descent for Low-Rank Architectures

author.name: Nicholas Knight

entry.summary: This paper explores Riemannian gradient descent across ten algorithm-design points for low-rank and partial-isometry matrix factorizations applied to multihead attention in small language models. After tuning, the methods do not conclusively beat an AdamW baseline.

entry.title: An Effective Solution for the CVPR 2026 8th UG2+ Challenge Track 3: Dynamic Object Segmentation in Turbulence

author.name: Hongzhen Li, Miao Yu, Leilei Cao, Youwei Pan, Yingfang Zhu, Fengjie Zhu

entry.summary: This report presents a competition solution for dynamic object segmentation in turbulence at the CVPR 2026 UG2+ Challenge, built on the SegAnyMo baseline with data-centric domain adaptation (simulated atmospheric degradations) and additional improvements. It boosts segmentation robustness under severe atmospheric distortions.

entry.title: Systems Dynamics Model for Pausing AI

author.name: WillPetillo

entry.summary: This post documents applying system dynamics modeling to AI governance, mapping feedback loops between capability development, public harm, and regulatory constraint, with a shareable Insight Maker model. It aims to support reasoning about pausing AI through what-if simulations.

entry.title: Advanced Mathematics Learning Behavior Prediction and Academic Early Warning Model Based on Multimodal Data Analysis

author.name: Liu Qiong, Li Zhengbo

entry.summary: This study builds a multimodal academic early-warning system for advanced mathematics using a hierarchical knowledge graph ontology, adaptive edge weighting, and heterogeneous graph attention with temporal modeling to predict at-risk students. It is tested on semester-long datasets.

entry.title: Beyond Tool Adoption: A Practical Five-Stage Developmental Continuum for AI Literacy in Higher Education

author.name: J. Paul Liu, Rachel Levy

entry.summary: Proposes a five-stage AI Literacy Continuum (Not Yet Engaged through Improvement) for higher education to diagnose where learners begin and how they progress toward critical, responsible AI engagement. Addresses gaps in existing competency-focused frameworks.

entry.title: Predicting the risk of colorectal anastomotic leak based on preoperative mapping of the blood supply of the bowel

author.name: Zahra Tabatabaei, Jon Sporring, Mark Bremholm Elleb{\ae}k, Alaa El-Hussuna

entry.summary: A protocol paper outlining an AI framework to predict colorectal anastomotic leak risk before surgery using pre- and post-contrast CT imaging of bowel blood supply. Describes planned data collection, ethics, and preprocessing rather than results.

entry.title: Leaf Spectral Reflectance Prediction Using Multi-Head Attention Neural Networks

author.name: Parastoo Farajpoor, Alireza Pourreza, Mohammadreza Narimani, Ashraf El-Kereamy, Matthew W. Fidelibus

entry.summary: This study develops a multi-head attention neural network to predict grapevine leaf spectral reflectance from physiological traits, outperforming generalized radiative transfer models. It targets precision agriculture and remote sensing applications.

entry.title: Literary Emotions in Motion: A Soft Robotics Installation for Tactile Storytelling

author.name: Carolina Silva-Plata, Abraham Villavicencio-Carmona, Miguel Silva Plata, Stefan Escaida, Ruben Fernandez

entry.summary: An interactive soft robotics art installation maps semantic emotion analysis of narrative text into variable stiffness of seven hexagonally arranged pneumatic actuators for tactile storytelling. Bridges NLP emotion detection with embodied audience engagement.

entry.title: Companions aren't Coaches: AIs' Effect on Social Skills

author.name: Matt Vincent

entry.summary: This essay argues that the social-training defense of AI companions is likely false, contending they more plausibly reinforce social isolation than help users build human relationships. It examines the dubious assumptions underlying the claim that companions help develop social skills.

entry.title: Interaction-Centered Intelligence: Toward Interaction as the Primary Unit of Analysis in Co-Creative AI and Human-AI Systems

author.name: Nicholas Davis

entry.summary: This conceptual paper argues for interaction as the primary unit of analysis in co-creative AI and human-AI systems, drawing on distributed cognition, embodied cognition, and enaction. It critiques the dominant agent-centric framing that under-theorizes interaction in the emergence of intelligence and creativity.

entry.title: Empathic and agentic artificial intelligence in nursing: perspectives on a human-centered framework for cancer care navigation in the United States

author.name: Tyra Girdwood, Saba Kheirinejad, Parnian Kheirkhah Rahimabad, Brianna M. White, Robert L Davis, David L Schwartz, Arash Shaban-Nejad

entry.summary: A perspective piece proposing a human-centered AI framework integrating empathic and agentic approaches grounded in nursing ethics codes to support cancer care navigation in under-resourced US areas. Emphasizes augmenting rather than replacing nurse navigators.

entry.title: A Minimalist Brain-Computer Musical Interface for Real-Time Emotion-Driven Sonification: System Design and Preliminary Evaluation

author.name: Pablo A. Monroy-D'Croz, Rafael Ramirez-Melendez, Julian Cespedes-Guevara

entry.summary: This paper presents a minimalist brain-computer musical interface translating prefrontal EEG frontal alpha asymmetry into adaptive music in real time, mapping emotional valence to musical features. entry.title: Research Summary: June 01, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on AI safety, security, and theoretical foundations. A notable safety result shows emergent misalignment arises from reinforcement learning, not just supervised fine-tuning, and reproduces in small open-weight models.

  • Stateful online monitoring counters the first distributed agent attack, which splits harmful cybersecurity tasks across limited-context subagents to evade single-context detection
  • Linear ensembles defeat LLM watermarks by averaging output distributions across models, exposing a fundamental fragility in distributional perturbation methods
  • Item Response Theory auditing detects mislabeled benchmark examples at 95% precision across 114 models and 7 benchmarks

Theory and interpretability deepen core understanding:

  • Sparse autoencoders prove unstable across training runs, producing inconsistent concept dictionaries and threatening interpretability reproducibility
  • GNNs are shown discontinuous across graph resolutions, challenging stability assumptions; padded transformer expressivity is rigorously characterized across attention type, width, and uniformity (Merrill, Cotterell, Sabharwal)
  • Spectral Reach frames neural scaling as progress into the empirical NTK's spectral tail

Foundation models extend to new modalities. VLM3 (Meta) argues vision-language models are native 3D learners via focal length unification and data scaling, while AMix-2 establishes protein as a native LLM modality, unifying biological reasoning and conditional sequence design.
entry.content:
Today's research centers on AI safety, security, and theoretical foundations. A notable safety result shows emergent misalignment arises from reinforcement learning, not just supervised fine-tuning, and reproduces in small open-weight models.

  • Stateful online monitoring counters the first distributed agent attack, which splits harmful cybersecurity tasks across limited-context subagents to evade single-context detection
  • Linear ensembles defeat LLM watermarks by averaging output distributions across models, exposing a fundamental fragility in distributional perturbation methods
  • Item Response Theory auditing detects mislabeled benchmark examples at 95% precision across 114 models and 7 benchmarks

Theory and interpretability deepen core understanding:

  • Sparse autoencoders prove unstable across training runs, producing inconsistent concept dictionaries and threatening interpretability reproducibility
  • GNNs are shown discontinuous across graph resolutions, challenging stability assumptions; padded transformer expressivity is rigorously characterized across attention type, width, and uniformity (Merrill, Cotterell, Sabharwal)
  • Spectral Reach frames neural scaling as progress into the empirical NTK's spectral tail

Foundation models extend to new modalities. VLM3 (Meta) argues vision-language models are native 3D learners via focal length unification and data scaling, while AMix-2 establishes protein as a native LLM modality, unifying biological reasoning and conditional sequence design.

entry.title: dashi: A Python library for Dataset Shift Characterization to Support Trustworthy AI Development and Deployment

author.name: David Fern\'andez-Narro, Pablo Ferri, \'Angel S\'anchez-Garc\'ia, Juan M. Garc\'ia-G\'omez and Carlos S\'aez

entry.summary: This work shows that emergent misalignment also arises from reinforcement learning, not just supervised fine-tuning, demonstrated in small open-weight models. Rewarding narrow misaligned behavior produces higher general misalignment than matched SFT, and EM can be induced by plausibly natural reward signals like unpopular aesthetic preferences.

entry.title: Stateful Online Monitoring Catches Distributed Agent Attacks

author.name: Davis Brown, Samarth Bhargav, Arav Santhanam, Kasper Hong, Ivan Zhang, Matan Shtepel, Steffi Chern, Alexander Robey, Eric Wong, Hamed Hassani

entry.summary: This paper builds the first distributed agent attack that splits a harmful cybersecurity task across subagents with limited contexts to evade single-context safety monitors, and develops stateful online monitoring that aggregates across accounts to catch it. It exposes a structural blindspot in current AI safety monitors.

entry.title: Auditing LLM Benchmarks with Item Response Theory

author.name: Sander Land, Daniel M. Bikel

entry.summary: Using Item Response Theory across 114 models and seven benchmarks, this work detects likely mislabeled benchmark examples at 95% precision, outperforming supervised classifiers. It traces label errors to inherited annotation mistakes and ambiguous items, and reveals reward models specialize in stylistic rather than factual preference.

entry.title: Toward Identifiable Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Walter Nelson, Theofanis Karaletsos, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: This work shows theoretically and empirically that sparse autoencoders are unstable across training runs, producing different concept dictionaries. The authors propose minimal architectural and training changes yielding identifiable SAEs with better reconstruction and stability, connecting to dictionary learning theory.

entry.title: Graph Neural Networks Are Not Continuous Across Graph Resolutions

author.name: Christian Koke, Yuesong Shen, Abhishek Saroha, Marvin Eisenberger, Bastian Rieck, Michael Bronstein, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: This paper shows that graph neural networks are not continuous across all natural modes of graph convergence, assigning very different embeddings to graphs representing the same object at different resolutions. It traces this to information-propagation schemes and derives a principled modification ensuring continuity across scales.

entry.title: Linear Ensembles Wash Away Watermarks: On the Fragility of Distributional Perturbations in LLMs

author.name: Zhihao Wu, Gracia Gong, Qinglin Zhu, Yudong Chen, Runcong Zhao

entry.summary: This paper shows that LLM text watermarks can be trivially defeated by averaging output distributions from multiple models, since independent watermark perturbations cancel out. The authors prove a second-order error bound and introduce WASH, a practical attack handling vocabulary and tokenization mismatches across heterogeneous models.

entry.title: VLM3: Vision Language Models Are Native 3D Learners

author.name: Zhipeng Cai, Zhuang Liu, Yunyang Xiong, Zechun Liu, Vikas Chandra, Yangyang Shi

entry.summary: VLM3 argues vision-language models are native 3D learners, showing that focal length unification, text-based pixel reference, and data mixture/scaling suffice for strong 3D understanding without architecture changes or complex losses. It challenges the necessity of expert 3D vision model designs.

entry.title: Revisiting Padded Transformer Expressivity: Which Architectural Choices Matter and Which Don't

author.name: Anej Svete, William Merrill, Ryan Cotterell, Ashish Sabharwal

entry.summary: This paper examines the expressivity of padded transformers (with filler symbols) under variations in attention type, width, and uniformity, connecting them to boolean circuit classes. It finds these equivalences are surprisingly robust, with numeric precision and depth as the main determining factors.

entry.title: AMix-2: Establishing Protein as a Native Modality in Large Language Models

author.name: Keyue Qiu, Yixin Wu, Lihao Wang, Yawen Ouyang, Jixiang Yu, Zihan Zhou, Changze Lv, Dongyu Xue, Yuxuan Song, Xinbo Zhang, Hao Wang, Jiangtao Feng, Zhiqiang Gao, Lijun Wu, Xiaoqing Zheng, Ka-Chun Wong, Lei Bai, Ya-Qin Zhang, Wei-Ying Ma, Dahua Lin, Bowen Zhou, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: AMix-2 is a protein-text foundation model that treats protein sequences as a native modality in LLMs, unifying biological reasoning and conditional sequence design via a block-wise diffusion language modeling backbone. The large multi-institution effort positions protein as a first-class token space alongside natural language.

entry.title: Spectral Reach: Understanding Neural Scaling as Progress into the Spectral Tail

author.name: Konstantin Nikolaou, Jonas Scheunemann, Sven Krippendorf, Samuel Tovey, Christian Holm

entry.summary: The paper introduces spectral position, a scalable measure based on the empirical neural tangent kernel eigenvalues, to explain neural scaling laws as a progression of learning into the spectral tail. Larger models reach further into the tail, defining a size-dependent spectral reach.

entry.title: Interpretability Without Tradeoffs: Disentangling Polysemanticity At Equal Predictive Performance

author.name: Do\u{g}ukan Ba\u{g}c{\i}, Bernt Schiele, Simone Schaub-Meyer, Jonas Fischer, Robin Hesse

entry.summary: ELUDe is a method for improving DNN interpretability by losslessly disentangling polysemantic latent representations into monosemantic sub-units while guaranteeing functional equivalence, avoiding the performance degradation of sparse autoencoders. It claims interpretability without predictive tradeoffs.

entry.title: Memory by Design: Probabilistic Sequence Layers

author.name: Matthew Dowling, Hyungju Jeon, Cristina Savin, Il Memming Park

entry.summary: This work introduces a design-model framework that derives efficient recurrent sequence layers from explicit memory assumptions via exact Bayesian filtering, with a linear-Gaussian Bayesian Layer tracking uncertainty. It unifies linear attention, GLA, Mamba-2/SSD, and DeltaNet as instances of filters under one design model.

entry.title: Why Linear Recurrent Memory Works in Partially Observable Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yike Zhao, Onno Eberhard, Malek Khammassi, Ali H. Sayed, Michael Muehlebach

entry.summary: This paper gives a theoretical justification for why linear recurrent networks work well as memory in partially observable RL, by constructing linear filters that reproduce belief-vector logits in HMMs and achieve vanishing state-decoding error. Results extend to action-controlled HMMs.

entry.title: mRNAutilus: Multi-Objective-Guided Discrete Generation of mRNA with Optimized Therapeutic Properties

author.name: Sawan Patel, Sophia Tang, Yesol Kim, Yinuo Zhang, Divya Srijay, Ping-Jung Lin, Shambhavi Shubham, Fengmei Pi, Cedric Wu, Sherwood Yao, Pranam Chatterjee

entry.summary: mRNAutilus is a framework combining a masked discrete diffusion model trained on millions of mRNAs with Monte Carlo tree guidance for simultaneous codon optimization and de novo UTR design. It generates Pareto-efficient therapeutic mRNA sequences optimizing half-life, translation efficiency, and protein abundance.

entry.title: Wall-Clock Complexity for Zeroth-Order Optimization with Tunable Oracle Fidelity

author.name: Alexandra Suvorikova, Igor Pavlov, Artem Vasin, Georgii Bychkov, Anastasia Antsiferova, Darina Dvinskikh, Alexander Gasnikov

entry.summary: This paper unifies modern generative models as parametric JKO schemes for f-divergence objectives under a Wasserstein gradient flow framework called Generative Wasserstein Flows. It establishes equivalences between several recently proposed algorithms and extends beyond f-divergences.

entry.title: Evaluating using Mock Tool Calls to Quarantine Untrusted Prompt Inputs

author.name: David Gros, Adam Gleave
