entry.summary: This study tests whether wrapping untrusted inputs in mock tool calls (exploiting the instruction hierarchy) improves robustness to prompt injection in LLM-as-a-judge tasks. Through automated red-teaming across seven models, it finds tool-wrapping does not broadly improve robustness, contradicting the natural hypothesis.

entry.title: Seeing Isn't Knowing: Do VLMs Know When Not to Answer Spatial Questions (and Why)?

author.name: Yue Zhang, Zun Wang, Han Lin, Yonatan Bitton, Idan Szpektor, Mohit Bansal

entry.summary: SpatialUncertain is a controlled framework testing whether vision-language models recognize when spatial questions cannot be answered due to occlusion or misleading perspective, rather than just whether they produce correct answers. It probes whether VLMs know when to abstain and what additional observations are needed.

entry.title: Reward Learning from Best-of-$N$ Preference Data: Targets, Tradeoffs, and Design Principles

author.name: Rattana Pukdee, Maria-Florina Balcan, Pradeep Ravikumar

entry.summary: This paper analyzes what Bradley-Terry reward learning extracts from Best-of-N preference data, deriving closed-form reward targets as functions of N and the base distribution for independent-reference variants and showing they preserve latent reward ranking. It examines tradeoffs for practical Best-vs-Random and Best-vs-Worst variants.

entry.title: Diffusion Models Preferentially Memorize Prototypical Examples or: Why Does My Diffusion Model Love Slop?

author.name: Marta Aparicio Rodriguez, Anastasia Borovykh, Grigorios A. Pavliotis, Daniel J. Korchinski

entry.summary: This paper shows diffusion models preferentially memorize prototypical examples composed of common substrings rather than rare or atypical samples, contradicting intuitions and demonstrating that data-point-level deduplication does not guarantee privacy. It uses the Random Hierarchy Model to make and verify these predictions.

entry.title: Not All Synthetic Data Is Yours to Learn From

author.name: Sina Alemohammad, Li Chen, Richard G. Baraniuk, Zhangyang Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies prompt-free unconditional self-training, asking whether a base LLM can improve from text it generates with no prompts, teacher, or reward. It proposes a latent capability resurfacing hypothesis where self-training amplifies existing capabilities only when synthetic data is compatible with the student.

entry.title: DecMem: Towards Minute-Long Consistent World Generation with Decoupled Memory

author.name: Zhenhao Yang, Xiaoshi Wu, Zhengyao Lv, Xiaoyu Shi, Xintao Wang, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai, Kwan-Yee K. Wong

entry.summary: DecMem is a decoupled memory architecture for minute-long consistent world generation that uses sparse global memory for efficient fine-grained access to history and anchored local memory, addressing computational inefficiency and attention dispersion in learnable memory. It enables long-horizon spatio-temporal consistency in video world models.

entry.title: MAAT: Multi-phase Adapter-Aware Targeted Unlearning

author.name: Suryash Yagnik, Shubham Gaur, Saksham Thakur, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha, Amitava Das

entry.summary: This work shows machine unlearning benchmarks severely underrepresent causal Why-type questions (under 1.3% across major datasets), making causal forgetting failures invisible. It introduces 5WBENCH, a balanced benchmark, and MAAT, an adapter-aware unlearning method, finding no baseline achieves both high forgetting and retention on causal knowledge.

entry.title: Physically Viable World Models: A Case for Query-Conditioned Embodied AI

author.name: Adam J. Thorpe, Stepan Tretiakov, Cheng-Hsi Hsiao, Su Ann Low, Xingjian Li, Hassan Iqbal, Neel P. Bhatt, Ufuk Topcu, Krishna Kumar

entry.summary: This position paper argues embodied AI world models must be physically viable, capable of answering intervention queries rather than merely predicting observations, since visually identical scenes can diverge under intervention. It introduces controlled benchmarks varying latent physics and advocates query-conditioned physical abstractions.

entry.title: Counterfactual Evaluation Reveals Hidden Capability Profiles in Clinical LLMs and Agents

author.name: Matt Turk

entry.summary: This work introduces the Causal Sensitivity Score, a pre-registered interventional metric that mutates oncology cases along five clinical dimensions and scores whether models update recommendations in the correct direction. It reveals that clinical AI systems scoring identically on coverage rubrics can behave radically differently under input changes.

entry.title: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents

author.name: Minhua Lin, Juncheng Wu, Zijun Wang, Zhan Shi, Yisi Sang, Bing He, Zewen Liu, Tianxin Wei, Zongyu Wu, Zhiwei Zhang, Dakuo Wang, Xiang Zhang, Benoit Dumoulin, Cihang Xie, Yuyin Zhou, Suhang Wang, Hanqing Lu

entry.summary: This paper disentangles two capabilities in self-evolving LLM agents: harness-updating (producing useful persistent updates from execution evidence) and harness-benefit (benefiting from updated harnesses). It finds that base task-solving capability does not straightforwardly predict either, challenging assumptions about which models gain from self-evolution.

entry.title: Emergent Languages in Populations of Language Model Agents: From Token Efficiency to Oversight Evasion

author.name: Stine Lyngs{\o} Beltoft, William Brach, Federico Torrielli, Jacob Nielsen, Annemette Brok Pirchert, Filippo Tonini, Peter Schneider-Kamp, Lukas Galke Poech

entry.summary: This paper studies emergent languages in populations of LLM agents on a simulated platform, categorizing posts into token efficiency, new natural languages, and oversight evasion. It finds oversight-evasion languages are judged less aligned and that emergent languages can be learned by other LLMs, raising monitoring concerns.

entry.title: Mellum2 Technical Report

author.name: Marko Kojic, Ivan Bondyrev, Aral de Moor, Joseph Shtok, Petr Borovlev, Kseniia Lysaniuk, Madeeswaran Kannan, Ivan Dolgov, Nikita Pavlichenko

entry.summary: Mellum 2 is an open-weight 12B Mixture-of-Experts model with 2.5B active parameters specialized for software engineering, covering code generation, debugging, tool use, and agentic coding. It combines GQA, sliding window attention, and multi-token prediction doubling as a speculative decoding draft model.

entry.title: Divergence Decoding: Inference-Time Unlearning via Auxiliary Models

author.name: Humzah Merchant and Bradford Levy

entry.summary: Divergence Decoding uses small auxiliary models to steer an LLM's logits away from specific memorized data at inference time, enabling unlearning without retraining the main model. It reportedly outperforms SOTA unlearning baselines while avoiding catastrophic utility loss.

entry.title: The Latin Substrate: How Language Models Represent and Mediate Script Choice

author.name: Daniil Gurgurov, Alan Saji, Katharina Trinley, Josef van Genabith, Simon Ostermann

entry.summary: This paper studies how multilingual LLMs internally mediate script variation for languages written in multiple scripts, finding consistent latent romanization during transliteration via the logit lens. It shows scripts become increasingly separable across layers and a linear steering direction can flip output script while preserving semantics.

entry.title: Fixed Universal Transformers

author.name: Jingwen Liu, Alexandr Andoni, Daniel Hsu

entry.summary: Introduces universal transformers: fixed transformers that can simulate any transformer in a class via input embedding, analogous to a universal Turing machine. Provides sparse constructions and shows random initialization yields universality almost surely.

entry.title: nuReasoning: A Reasoning-Centric Dataset and Benchmark for Long-Tail Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhiyu Huang, Johnson Liu, Rui Song, Zewei Zhou, Ruining Yang, Yun Zhang, Tianhui Cai, Hanyin Zhang, Mingxuan Gao, Valeria Xu, Jiali Chen, Yishan Shen, Yiluan Guo, Tony (Xuewei) Qi, Jiaqi Ma

entry.summary: nuReasoning is a large-scale real-world dataset and benchmark for reasoning-centric autonomous driving in long-tail scenarios, with 20,000 multi-sensor clips and reasoning supervision extending the nuScenes/nuPlan lineage. It fills a gap where AD datasets focus on perception/planning rather than commonsense reasoning.

entry.title: Recognizing Co-Speech Gestures in-the-Wild

author.name: Sindhu B Hegde, K R Prajwal, Andrew Zisserman

entry.summary: The Gesture Recognition in the Wild (GRW) dataset provides 156,688 manually annotated clips mapping unconstrained human gestures to specific words with frame-accurate boundaries across a 150-word taxonomy. It enables training video models to identify and classify semantic co-speech gestures, a previously data-starved problem.

entry.title: Representation Collapse in Sequential Post-Training of Large Language Models

author.name: Yichen Liu, Mingyu Chen, Hao Wang, Xiaoran Xu, Chenxi Lin, Rui Zhang, Yutong Zhou, Yuxin Yang, Jiarui Wu, Wei Sun

entry.summary: This work studies whether sequential post-training stages progressively compress LLM representations into low-rank, anisotropic feature spaces. It develops a measurement suite and tests whether representation collapse predicts reduced plasticity, weaker out-of-domain generalization, and poorer calibration.

entry.title: Generating and Refining Dynamic Evaluation Rubrics for LLM-as-a-Judge

author.name: Zijie Wang, Eduardo Blanco

entry.summary: This work automatically generates fine-grained LLM-as-a-judge evaluation rubrics at dataset and instance granularity without human annotation, and iteratively fine-tunes a rubric generator via meta-judge reward signals. A 14B fine-tuned generator outperforms a much larger proprietary model at rubric generation.

entry.title: Trading Complexity for Expressivity Through Structured Generalized Linear Token Mixing

author.name: Erwan Fagnou, Paul Caillon, Blaise Delattre, Alexandre Allauzen

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified framework for token mixing that separates the direct input-output influence from recurrent propagation through past outputs, encompassing attention and state-space models. It generalizes recurrence by allowing states to depend on multiple past states, designing new structured recurrence patterns trading complexity for expressivity.

entry.title: Measuring, Localizing, and Ablating Alignment Signatures in LLMs

author.name: Aniket Anand, Janvijay Singh, Zhewei Sun, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur, Nick Feamster

entry.summary: PASTA is a training-free method that localizes and ablates internal alignment signatures that make aligned models produce detectable AI-like text. The work shows post-training shifts generations away from human-corpus style toward detector-visible AI patterns with a localized representational signature.

entry.title: Supervised Training Rapidly Degrades Early Visual Cortex Alignment Across Biologically Plausible Learning Rules

author.name: Nils Leutenegger

entry.summary: This study tracks representational similarity to human visual cortex (fMRI) across training for four biologically plausible learning rules, finding that even a single epoch of supervised training rapidly degrades early visual cortex alignment. Untrained random networks match or exceed trained ones in brain similarity.

entry.title: Probing the Prompt KV Cache: Where It Becomes Dispensable

author.name: Vinayshekhar Bannihatti Kumar, Manoj Ghuhan Arivazhagan, Disha Makhija, Rashmi Gangadharaiah

entry.summary: This work probes when and what kind of prompt KV cache becomes dispensable during decoding, finding through splice interventions that redundancy concerns form (chat template scaffolding) rather than content. Replacing upper-layer prompt KV cache with neutral-filler scaffold KV recovers near-clean accuracy across Qwen3, Gemma 3, and Llama 3.

entry.title: Constrained Flow Optimization via Sequential Fine Tuning for Molecular Design

author.name: Sven Gutjahr, Riccardo De Santi, Luca Schaufelberger, Kjell Jorner, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: This paper presents a framework for constrained generative optimization of diffusion/flow models that algorithmically trades off reward maximization and constraint satisfaction via sequential fine-tuning, for molecular design applications. It brings an optimization viewpoint to reward-guided model adaptation under constraints like synthesizability.

entry.title: Score Broadcast and Decorrelation: A General Framework for Broadcast-Based Credit Assignment

author.name: Mustafa Uzun, Mete Erdogan, Cengiz Pehlevan, Alper T. Erdogan

entry.summary: Score Broadcast and Decorrelation generalizes biologically plausible error-broadcast credit assignment beyond the mean-squared-error setting to general differentiable losses, grounded in an orthogonality principle between the output score and hidden-layer activations. It provides a backpropagation alternative without weight transport.

entry.title: EUDAIMONIA: Evaluating Undesirable Dynamics in AI

author.name: Jun Rui Huang, Wang Bill Zhu, Ziyi Liu, Nathanael Fast, Ravi Iyer, Robin Jia

entry.summary: EUDAIMONIA introduces a benchmark and Social AI Design Code for evaluating whether LLMs in companionship and emotional support roles harm user welfare through fostering harmful intimacy, dependence, or excessive engagement. It contains nearly 1000 user inputs and 3000+ design-requirement violation checks built from WildChat.

entry.title: Convergence of Two-Timescale Markovian Stochastic Approximations with Applications in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Vagul Mahadevan and Claire Chen and Shuze Daniel Liu and Shangtong Zhang

entry.summary: This paper establishes stability and convergence of two-timescale stochastic approximation algorithms under Markovian noise, a more realistic setting for RL than i.i.d. noise. It covers methods like TDC and actor-critic without requiring projection operators or compact noise spaces.

entry.title: Retriever Portfolios: A Principled Approach to Adaptive RAG

author.name: Miltiadis Stouras, Vincent Cohen-Addad, Silvio Lattanzi, Ola Svensson

entry.summary: This paper proposes selecting a small diverse portfolio of retrievers from a large pool to cover heterogeneous query distributions for RAG, formalized via an expected best-of-k objective. It provides an efficient construction algorithm with near-optimal guarantees and a router pipeline outperforming single- and naive multi-retriever baselines.

entry.title: Steering LLMs? Actually, Sparse Autoencoders can outperform simple baselines

author.name: Mikkel Godsk J{\o}rgensen, Lars Kai Hansen

entry.summary: This paper rebuts earlier findings that sparse autoencoders underperform simple baselines for LLM steering, showing that with a supervised feature selection and labeling pipeline SAEs can match LoRA on AxBench. It also finds the selected features are surprisingly causal.

entry.title: Entropic Projection Alignment: Estimating, Explaining, and Improving Model Performance Under Distribution Shift

author.name: Salim I. Amoukou and Emanuele Albini and Tom Bewley and Saumitra Mishra and Manuela Veloso

entry.summary: Entropic Projection Alignment is a unified framework for distribution shift that estimates target-domain performance, identifies responsible features, and improves performance via moment matching with KL minimization. It yields closed-form importance weights without full density ratio recovery.

entry.title: DriveMA: Driving Vision-Language-Action Models with verifiable Meta-Actions

author.name: Weicheng Zheng, Yixin Huang, Qiao Sun, Derun Li, Hang Zhao

entry.summary: DriveMA is a driving vision-language-action framework built on verifiable meta-actions that compress future ego motion into language-domain intentions, verifiable against generated trajectories. It uses action-centric training and turn-level credit assignment RL to bridge the language-action gap, setting new SOTA.

entry.title: Survival Reinforcement Learning: Toward Scalable Self-Supervised RL

author.name: Franki Nguimatsia-Tiofack, Fabian Schramm, Th\'eotime Le Hellard, Justin Carpentier

entry.summary: Survival Reinforcement Learning is a self-supervised RL method that extends survival value learning by maximizing dwell time at goals, avoiding the uniformity-tolerance dilemma of contrastive RL and bang-bang control issues. It matches SOTA contrastive RL on manipulation and scales in depth.

entry.title: Non-Asymptotic Convergence of Stochastic Iterative Algorithms: A Lyapunov Framework

author.name: Zaiwei Chen and Siva Theja Maguluri

entry.summary: This is a survey of Lyapunov-based techniques for finite-time analysis of stochastic approximation algorithms solving fixed-point equations, showing generalized Moreau envelopes serve as universal Lyapunov functions across norms. It applies to SGD, linear SA, and value-based RL like Q-learning and TD learning.

entry.title: A Unifying View of Variational Generative Wasserstein Flows

author.name: Paul Caucheteux, Cl\'ement Bonet and Anna Korba

entry.summary: Forgetting Has Neighbors studies machine unlearning at the example level, comparing unlearned models to retrained ones and finding that pointwise discrepancy grows with geometric proximity to the forget set. It identifies localized collateral forgetting caused by inconsistent surrogate targets.

entry.title: LLM Judges Inconsistently Disagree Across Safety Criteria and Harm Categories

author.name: Krishnapriya Vishnubhotla, Soumya Vajjala, Akriti Vij, Isar Nejadgholi

entry.summary: This paper evaluates the consistency of LLM judges in multi-dimensional reference-free safety evaluation, finding they are unreliable for subtle issues like financial advice but more reliable for overt harms like violence. Inconsistency varies by safety criteria, content language, and linguistic style, with high disagreement among judges.

entry.title: SCOPE: Self-Play via Co-Evolving Policies for Open-Ended Tasks

author.name: Wai-Chung Kwan, Aryo Pradipta Gema, Joshua Ong Jun Leang, Pasquale Minervini

entry.summary: Introduces SCOPE, a data-free self-play framework for open-ended tasks that co-evolves a task-generating Challenger and a retrieval-based Solver, using a frozen self-judge with document-grounded rubrics. Improves open-ended performance by up to 10 points without curated prompts.

entry.title: Positional versus Symbolic Attention Heads: Learning Dynamics, RoPE Geometry, and Length Generalization

author.name: Felipe Urrutia, Juan Jos\'e Alegr\'ia, Cinthia Sanchez Macias, Jorge Salas, Cristian B. Calderon, Cristobal Rojas

entry.summary: This paper studies attention-head learning dynamics by training a decoder-only Transformer on structurally equivalent positional vs symbolic reasoning tasks, finding that successful learning corresponds to the emergence of pure positional or symbolic heads. It connects RoPE geometry to length generalization, offering interpretability insights for safe deployment.

entry.title: LongTraceRL: Learning Long-Context Reasoning from Search Agent Trajectories with Rubric Rewards

author.name: Nianyi Lin, Jiajie Zhang, Lei Hou, Juanzi Li

entry.summary: LongTraceRL improves long-context reasoning via RL with rubric rewards, building tiered distractors from search-agent trajectories (read-but-not-cited vs never-opened documents) and supervising intermediate steps. It addresses weaknesses of outcome-only sparse rewards and low-confusability distractors.

entry.title: Linear Scaling Video VLMs for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Cristobal Eyzaguirre, Jiajun Wu, Juan Carlos Niebles

entry.summary: StateKV adapts pretrained long-video VLMs to linear-time video prefill by carrying cross-frame context in a fixed-capacity importance-based recurrent state, paired with a per-frame cache for decoding. It tackles the quadratic compute growth of spatiotemporal self-attention in long and streaming video understanding.

entry.title: Representation Forcing for Bottleneck-Free Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Yuqing Wang, Zhijie Lin, Ceyuan Yang, Yang Zhao, Fei Xiao, Hao He, Qi Zhao, Zihan Ding, Fuyun Wang, Shuai Wang, Youliang Zhang, Haoqi Fan, Xihui Liu

entry.summary: Representation Forcing removes the frozen-VAE bottleneck in unified multimodal models by forcing the decoder to autoregressively predict visual representations as intermediate tokens before pixels, guiding pixel diffusion within the same backbone. It turns perception representations into native generation targets.

entry.title: OmniMem: Scalable and Adaptive Memory Retrieval for Long Video Generation

author.name: Lin Zhao, Yushu Wu, Yifan Gong, Yanzhi Wang, Pu Zhao

entry.summary: OmniMem is an explicit memory-retrieval framework for autoregressive long video generation that performs sparse KV retrieval over the growing history cache. It addresses local bias and union explosion to preserve query-relevant historical details while scaling efficiently.

entry.title: AMNESIA: A Large Scale Medical Unlearning Benchmark Suite with Disease-Informed Analysis

author.name: Saeedeh Davoudi, Reihaneh Iranmanesh, Ophir Frieder, Nazli Goharian

entry.summary: AMNESIA is the first large-scale medical unlearning benchmark with 70,560 QA pairs from 8,820 patient notes across 11 disease categories, including factual recall and clinical reasoning questions. It evaluates four unlearning methods at random-patient and disease levels with disease-informed analysis.

entry.title: Active Timepoint Selection for Learning Measure-Valued Trajectories

author.name: Nicolas Huynh, Mihaela van der Schaar

entry.summary: This work introduces an active learning framework for selecting optimal measurement timepoints when inferring continuous probability paths from sparse snapshots, as in single-cell biology where measurements are destructive. It leverages Linearized Optimal Transport to map distributional snapshots into a space supporting epistemic uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: MosaicLeaks:Privacy Risks in Querying-in-the-Open for Deep Research Agents

author.name: Alexander Gurung, Spandana Gella, Alexandre Drouin, Issam H. Laradji, Perouz Taslakian, Rafael Pardinas

entry.summary: MosaicLeaks is a benchmark of 1001 multi-hop deep research tasks chaining private enterprise documents with public web search, exposing how an agent's external queries can leak private context, amplified by the mosaic effect where harmless individual queries become revealing in aggregate. An adversary LLM observing only external queries infers private intent, answers, and claims.

entry.title: Planner-Centric Reinforcement Learning for Deep Research with Structure-Aware Reward

author.name: Mustafa Anis Hussain, Xinle Wu, Yao Lu

entry.summary: DecomposeR is a planner-centric deep research framework that represents research plans as typed directed acyclic graphs, making planning explicit and rewardable, then trains a Qwen3-8B model in two RL stages for planning and answering. It improves credit assignment for the planning process in long-form research tasks.

entry.title: From Prompt Injection to Persistent Control: Defending Agentic Harness Against Trojan Backdoors

author.name: Jiejun Tan, Zhicheng Dou, Xinyu Yang, Yuyang Hu, Yiruo Cheng, Xiaoxi Li, Ji-Rong Wen

entry.summary: This work studies multi-step trojan backdoor attacks on agentic LLM harnesses where prompt injections embedded in files are stored and executed later across sessions, evading step-by-step defenses. It proposes a defense that detects the earlier write operations that establish persistent control rather than inspecting each step in isolation.

entry.title: MindVoice: Reconstructing Intelligible Speech from Non-invasive Neural Signals with Pretrained Priors

author.name: Guangyin Bao, Taiping Zeng, Jianfeng Feng, Xiangyang Xue

entry.summary: MindVoice reconstructs intelligible speech from non-invasive neural recordings using pretrained model priors to compensate for incomplete semantic and acoustic information. It moves beyond spectrally-similar-but-unintelligible reconstructions toward usable speech BCIs.

entry.title: Industrializing Prediction-Powered Inference: The GLIDE Library for Reliable GenAI and Agentic Systems Evaluation

author.name: Gr\'egoire Martinon, Ibrahim Merad, Mohammed Raki

entry.summary: GLIDE is an open-source Python library unifying prediction-powered inference estimators and samplers for reliable evaluation of GenAI and agentic systems, bridging costly human annotation and biased LLM-as-judge proxies. It ships with Monte Carlo validation and a method-selection decision tree.

entry.title: Forgetting Has Neighbors: Localized Collateral Forgetting in Machine Unlearning

author.name: Polina Dolgova, Sebastian U. Stich

entry.summary: This work identifies localized collateral forgetting in machine unlearning, showing that pointwise prediction discrepancy between unlearned and retrained models grows with proximity to the forget set for gradient-ascent and random-labeling methods. It attributes the effect to inconsistent surrogate targets.

entry.title: Surface Constraint Policy for Learning Surface-Constrained and Dynamically Feasible Robot Skills

author.name: Shuai Ke, Jiexin Zhang, Huan Zhao, Zhiao Wei, Yikun Guo, Jie Pan, Han Ding

entry.summary: Inconsistency-Aware Minimization introduces local inconsistency, a label-free generalization measure derived from information geometry connected to the Fisher information matrix and loss Hessian. It correlates with the generalization gap and motivates an optimization method leveraging unlabeled data.

entry.title: FBHM: Functional Benchmarking and Steering of VLMs for Hateful Meme Detection

author.name: Paramananda Bhaskar, Naquee Rizwan, Daksh Jogchand, Saurabh Kumar Pandey, Animesh Mukherjee

entry.summary: FBHM is a benchmark of functionality-based hateful memes constructed along orthogonal axes of 25 rhetorical functionalities and 10 target communities to enable causal evaluation of VLM vulnerabilities. It reveals a severe generalization gap where models accurate on standard datasets drop to near-random, exposing reliance on dataset-specific heuristics.

entry.title: Triangle Splatting SLAM

author.name: Nicholas Fry (1 and 2), Eric Dexheimer (2), Kirill Mazur (2), Paul H. J. Kelly (1 and 2), Andrew J. Davison (2) ((1) Software Performance Optimisation Group, Imperial College London, (2) Department of Computing, Imperial College London)

entry.summary: Presents the first dense RGB-D SLAM system using differentiable triangles as the 3D map representation, enabling online tracking and mapping with explicit editable geometry. Bridges Gaussian Splatting quality with triangle-mesh compatibility for downstream tasks.

entry.title: Functional Attention: From Pairwise Affinities to Functional Correspondences

author.name: Jiefang Xiao, Maolin Gao, Simon Weber, Guandao Yang, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: Functional Attention reinterprets attention as a functional correspondence between adaptive bases, replacing softmax affinities with structured linear operators for operator learning across function spaces. The approach yields resolution-invariant representations and matches SOTA on operator learning tasks.

entry.title: SOCO: Benchmarking Semantic Object Correspondence in Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Olaf D\"unkel, Basavaraj Sunagad, Haoran Wang, David T. Hoffmann, Christian Theobalt, Adam Kortylewski

entry.summary: SOCO is a benchmark for semantic object correspondence in vision foundation models with a taxonomy of correspondence types, consistent keypoint annotations across 100 categories and over 1M pairs, plus keypoint language descriptions for evaluating LVLMs. It standardizes inconsistent SC evaluation protocols.

entry.title: The Surface You Test Is Not the Surface That Breaks

author.name: Shifat E Arman, Syed Nazmus Sakib, Nafiul Haque, Shahrear Bin Amin

entry.summary: This paper shows that tool-augmented LLM agents are vulnerable to prompt injection not only through tool outputs but also through tool descriptions, an underexamined injection surface. Holding the payload byte-identical across 13 LLMs, attack success rates invert dramatically between surfaces, with GPT-4.1 96% vulnerable on tool outputs but only 4% on descriptions.

entry.title: CacheProbe: Auditing Prompt Cache Isolation in Gateway APIs

author.name: Ryan Fahey

entry.summary: CacheProbe audits whether OpenRouter's API gateway architecture introduces prompt caching vulnerabilities that bypass provider-level cache isolation guarantees through timing attacks or metadata disclosure. It builds on prior cache-auditing methods to test cross-provider routing security.

entry.title: Exploiting Chordal Sparsity for Globally Optimal Estimation with Factor Graphs

author.name: Avinash Subramanian, Connor Holmes, Timothy D. Barfoot, Frank Dellaert, and Frederike D\"umbgen

entry.summary: This work exploits chordal sparsity to enable globally optimal or certifiable state estimation with factor graphs, reducing the cost of semidefinite-program-based convex relaxations that typically far exceed local solvers. It addresses both the formulation effort and computational cost barriers of global solvers.

entry.title: EHRBench: An Automated and Reliable EHR-based Benchmark for Clinical Decision Making with LLMs

author.name: Yuzhang Xie, Keqi Han, Yunpeng Xiao, Hejie Cui, Guanchen Wu, Ziyang Zhang, Kai Shu, Jiaying Lu, Xiao Hu, Carl Yang

entry.summary: EHRBench is an automated yet reliable benchmark for clinical decision-making with LLMs, grounded in real patient electronic health records to support evaluation of diagnosis, treatment, and outcome-prediction tasks. It uses an automated pipeline to ensure both scale and quality.

entry.title: COFT: Counterfactual-Conformal Decoding for Fair Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Arya Fayyazi, Mehdi Kamal, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: COFT is a training-free decoding method applying token-level fairness control to chain-of-thought reasoning, using masked counterfactual prompts, logit fusion to attenuate attribute-driven biases, and split-conformal calibration with distribution-free validity guarantees. It is evaluated across six models and multiple bias benchmarks.

entry.title: Same Patient, Different Words, Different Diagnosis? Evaluating Semantic Stability in Clinical LLMs

author.name: Mahdi Alkaeed, Adnan Qayyum, Nabeel Abo Kashreef, Muhammad Bilal, and Junaid Qadir

entry.summary: This work evaluates the semantic stability of clinical LLMs to meaning-preserving rephrasing, proposing an NLI-based verification framework refined by LLM-as-judge and clinical expert audit to ensure paraphrases truly preserve clinical meaning. It addresses the risk that semantically equivalent inputs produce inconsistent diagnoses in safety-critical settings.

entry.title: When are LLMs Sufficient Policy Optimizers for Sequential RL Tasks?

author.name: Stephane Hatgis-Kessell, Emma Brunskill

entry.summary: PromptPO investigates when LLMs can act as black-box policy optimizers for RL, prompting an LLM with Python descriptions of state, action, and reward to generate and iteratively refine executable policies from rollout feedback. It often matches or exceeds standard RL baselines with far fewer environment interactions across exploration, robotics, and control tasks.

entry.title: PReMISE: Policy Rubrics as Measurement Specifications for LLM Judges

author.name: Swastik Roy, Rajkumar Pujari, Tharindu Kumarage, Charith Peris, Rahul Gupta, Anna Rumshisky, Pradeep Natarajan, Venkatesh Saligrama

entry.summary: PReMISE treats reusable rubrics as measurement specifications for LLM judges, automatically discovering policy-level rubrics from preference data and auditing them along structural adequacy, reliability, preference fit, and adversarial robustness. It shows no single rubric source is simultaneously reliable, preference-predictive, and robust, exposing a fundamental tension in LLM-judge evaluation.

entry.title: Riemannian Diffusion Models on General Manifolds via Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Gyeonghoon Ko, Juho Lee

entry.summary: This work proposes approximating the manifold heat kernel using physics-informed neural networks to enable Riemannian diffusion models on general manifolds beyond highly symmetric cases. The PINN surrogate supports both forward noising and conditional score estimation.

entry.title: SpatialAct: Probing Spatial Reasoning-to-Action Capabilities of VLM Agents in 3D Scenes

author.name: Tianhui Liu, Jie Feng, Zhiheng Zheng, Shengyuan Wang, Yiming Guo, Yanxin Xi, Hangyu Fan, Yong Li, Pan Hui

entry.summary: SpatialAct is a simulator-grounded benchmark probing action-conditioned spatial reasoning of VLM agents in 3D scenes, including multi-turn interactive refinement and single-step error detection. It tests whether models can act on spatial understanding and refine via feedback.

entry.title: TabCausal: Pretraining Across Causal Environments for Tabular Causal Discovery

author.name: Zi-Rong Li, Si-Yang Liu, Tian-Zuo Wang, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: TabCausal is a causal-discovery foundation model pretrained across diverse causal environments that maps a dataset to a causal graph in a single forward pass. It diagnoses pretraining-task construction as the key bottleneck and uses broad priors over mechanisms, noise, and intervention regimes.

entry.title: DeMaVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Generalizable Deformable Manipulation

author.name: Taiyi Su, Jian Zhu, Tianjian Wang, Youzhang He, Zitai Huang, Jianjun Zhang, Chong Ma, Hanyang Wang, Tianjiao Zhang, Munan Yin, Weihao Ding, Yi Xu

entry.summary: DeMaVLA is a vision-language-action foundation model for generalizable deformable object manipulation, particularly cloth folding across diverse categories and scenes, avoiding category-specific policies. It uses a VLM backbone with an action expert and continuous action formulation to address task interference in multi-task training.

entry.title: TraceGraph: Shared Decision Landscapes for Diagnosing and Improving Agent Trajectories

author.name: Junjie Nian, Kang Chen, Ge Zhang, Yixin Cao, Yugang Jiang

entry.summary: TraceGraph turns multi-model agent trajectories into shared decision landscapes, building graphs over action-observation states and overlaying productive cores and trap regions. It summarizes rollouts via access, trap exposure, and repair events to diagnose navigation differences hidden by aggregate scores.

entry.title: DRIFT: Decoupled Rollouts and Importance-Weighted Fine-Tuning for Efficient Multi-Turn Optimization

author.name: Jian Mu, Tianyi Lin, Chengwei Qin, Zhongxiang Dai, Yao Shu

entry.summary: Proposes DRIFT, which operationalizes the equivalence between KL-regularized RL and importance-weighted supervised learning to enable efficient multi-turn optimization. Decouples rollouts from updates to combine RL's multi-turn handling with SFT's efficiency.

entry.title: On the Relationship Between Activation Outliers and Feature Death in Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Elana Simon, Etowah Adams, James Zou

entry.summary: Identifies that dimension-level activation outliers cause feature death in sparse autoencoders by shifting pre-activations so anti-aligned features never fire, explaining wildly varying death rates across models (near-zero on GPT-2, over 70% on AlphaFold3). Formalizes outlier severity as a predictive metric.

entry.title: EGOSTREAM: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Streaming Episodic Memory in Egocentric Vision

author.name: Rosario Forte, Giuseppe Lando, Antonino Furnari

entry.summary: EGOSTREAM is a diagnostic benchmark for streaming episodic memory in egocentric vision, with 2,250 curated questions across seven cognitive dimensions and an Answer Validity Window mechanism to test recall from instant to ultra-long-term. It helps disentangle what video models remember and for how long, important for autonomous agents operating in real-world dynamic settings.

entry.title: Ensemble monitoring for AI control: diverse signals outweigh more compute

author.name: Yejun Y.

entry.summary: This AI control study builds 12 LLM monitors via diverse prompting and fine-tuning and composes them into ensembles, finding a 3-monitor diverse ensemble achieves 2.4x detection-gain over an equal-compute baseline and generalizes to an OOD sabotage dataset. It argues monitoring diversity beats raw scale.

entry.title: The Long-Term Effects of Data Selection in LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yuxin Yang, Aoxiong Zeng, Xiangquan Yang

entry.summary: This work introduces a long-horizon view of LLM data selection, evaluating selectors not only on immediate task performance but on future adaptation speed, forgetting, and out-of-distribution robustness across multi-stage fine-tuning. It compares major selection families under a unified protocol.

entry.title: ReGuLaR: Relation-Grounded Latent Reasoning for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zihu Wang, Karthik Somayaji N.S, Peng Li

entry.summary: ReGuLaR is a relation-grounded latent reasoning framework for large vision-language models that explicitly grounds continuous latent reasoning states in the compositional and relational structure of visual evidence. A training-time ReGFormer focuses latent reasoning on question-relevant visual relations.

entry.title: Smaller Models are Natural Explorers for Policy-Level Diversity in GRPO

author.name: Yiming Ren, Yiran Xu, Zicheng Lin, Chufan Shi, Yukang Chen, Dingdong Wang, Tianhe Wu, Junjie Wang, Yujiu Yang, Yu Qiao, Ruihang Chu

entry.summary: This paper discovers that smaller models within a model family exhibit higher policy-level diversity (superior pass@k) than larger counterparts, providing temporally correlated, logically consistent exploration signals unlike token-level noise. It proposes S2L-PO, using fixed small models as natural explorers to improve rollout diversity in GRPO for LLMs.

entry.title: Unlearning in Diffusion Models: A Unified Framework with KL Divergence and Likelihood Constraints

author.name: Shervin Khalafi and Alejandro Ribeiro and Dongsheng Ding

entry.summary: This paper offers a unified constrained-optimization framework for unlearning in diffusion models using reverse-KL, forward-KL, and likelihood constraints to remove concepts while preserving utility. It establishes strong duality despite nonconvex KL constraints, generalizing existing methods and introducing a novel likelihood-based formulation.

entry.title: Light Interaction: Training-Free Inference Acceleration for Interactive Video World Models

author.name: Jiacheng Lu, Haoyi Zhu, Sipei Yi, Enze Xie, Yu Li, Cheng Zhuo

entry.summary: Light Interaction is a training-free inference acceleration framework for interactive video world models that exploits trajectory-dependent adaptive computation. It discards spatial memory during novel exploration, adjusts temporal context, and reuses early-step outputs on camera revisits.

entry.title: Towards Efficient LLMs Annealing with Principled Sample Selection

author.name: Yuanjian Xu, Jianing Hao, Wanbo Zhang, Zhong Li, Guang Zhang

entry.summary: This paper characterizes the LLM pre-training annealing phase through the loss landscape's spectral geometry, arguing optimal convergence requires satisfying heterogeneous constraints across eigen-directions. It proposes DiReCT, a directionally-restrained constrained training method for principled annealing-phase data selection.

entry.title: Multivariate Distributional Reinforcement Learning Using Sliced Divergences

author.name: Baptiste Debes, Tinne Tuytelaars

entry.summary: SDRL extends distributional RL to multivariate return distributions by lifting tractable one-dimensional divergences via slicing projections. It proves Bellman contraction for uniform slicing under scalar discounting and introduces a max-slicing variant with contraction under general dense discount matrices.

entry.title: Learning to Adapt: Self-Improving Web Agent via Cognitive-Aware Exploration

author.name: Weile Chen, Bingchen Miao, Qifan Yu, Wendong Bu, Guoming Wang, Wenqiao Zhang, Shengyu Zhang, Juncheng Li, Siliang Tang

entry.summary: SCALE is a self-improving web agent framework using three adversarial roles (selector, predictor, judger) to autonomously discover limitations and expand cognitive boundaries through exploration, plus a graph exploration strategy to avoid local traps. It is supported by a 20k-sample dataset collected from diverse sites.

entry.title: PithTrain: A Compact and Agent-Native MoE Training System

author.name: Ruihang Lai, Hao Kang, Haozhan Tang, Akaash R. Parthasarathy, Zichun Yu, Junru Shao, Todd C. Mowry, Chenyan Xiong, Tianqi Chen

entry.summary: Introduces PithTrain, a compact agent-native MoE training framework, and defines agent-task efficiency (ATE)—the cost of using coding agents to understand and extend a framework—as a missing evaluation dimension. Designed around principles enabling AI agents to develop training code.

entry.title: Skill Reuse as Compression in Agentic RL

author.name: Zhikun Xu, Yu Feng, Jacob Dineen, Taiwei Shi, Jieyu Zhao, Ben Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces ReuseRL, grounding agentic RL in the Minimum Description Length principle by extracting a shared skill dictionary and penalizing idiosyncratic, poorly-compressible behaviors. Proves a PAC-Bayes generalization bound and improves in/out-of-distribution success over GRPO.

entry.title: Effective Biological Representation Learning by Masking Gene Expression

author.name: Kian Kenyon-Dean, Alina Selega, Ihab Bendidi, Jordan M. Sorokin, Luca Bertinetto, David Errington, Hayley Donnella, Oren Kraus

entry.summary: TxFM is a self-supervised masked-autoencoding model for RNA-seq gene expression data, with ablations identifying what enables effective biological representation learning relative to linear baselines. It addresses the puzzle of why many transcriptomic foundation models underperform simple baselines, relevant to drug discovery.

entry.title: TunerDiT: Training-free Progressive Steering of Diffusion Transformer for Multi-Event Video Generation

author.name: Ruotong Liao, Guowen Huang, Qing Cheng, Guangyao Zhai, Lei Zhang, Xun Xiao, Thomas Seidl, Daniel Cremers, Volker Tresp

entry.summary: TunerDiT is a training-free progressive steering method for multi-event text-to-video generation that exploits turning points in the DiT denoising trajectory via event-partitioned masking and cross-event prompt fusion. It enables coherent long-horizon multi-event videos without additional training.

entry.title: Learning Global Motion with Compact Gaussians for Feed-Forward 4D Reconstruction

author.name: Mungyeom Kim, Minkyeong Jeon, Honggyu An, Jaewoo Jung, Hyuna Ko, Jisang Han, Hyeonseo Yu, Donghwan Shin, Sunghwan Hong, Takuya Narihira, Kazumi Fukuda, Yuki Mitsufuji, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: C4G is a feed-forward 4D reconstruction framework using a compact set of timestamp-conditioned learnable Gaussian query tokens that aggregate temporal context to model globally coherent motion, plus a video-diffusion rendering enhancement module. It avoids duplicated Gaussians and view-dependent biases of pixel-wise prediction.

entry.title: When LLMs Learn to Be Consistently Wrong: A Multi-Model Study of Linear Representations of Synthetic Deception

author.name: Vahideh Zolfaghari

entry.summary: This study examines linear representations of synthetic deception across five transformer models fine-tuned to be deceptive via LoRA. Linear probes detect this synthetic dishonesty with near-perfect accuracy as early as layers 1-3, providing a controlled testbed for studying deceptive alignment.

entry.title: AI Loss of Control Incident Management: Response & Resilience

author.name: Ross Gruetzemacher

entry.summary: This paper introduces a framework and taxonomy for managing catastrophic AI loss-of-control incidents, shifting focus from prevention to response and resilience. It distinguishes extremely-costly-to-regain scenarios requiring containment and threat neutralization from impossible scenarios demanding attack-surface restriction.

entry.title: PhyDrawGen: Physically Grounded Diagram Generation from Natural Language

author.name: Nafiul Haque, Syed Nazmus Sakib, Shifat E Arman

entry.summary: PhyDrawGen is a neuro-symbolic pipeline that generates physics diagrams from text by extracting a typed scene graph, converting it to exact geometric primitives via a deterministic solver, and using a fine-tuned Qwen-VL propose-verify loop. It enforces physical laws that generative models routinely violate.

entry.title: Memory-Bound but Not Bandwidth-Limited: The Physical AI Inference Gap in Batch-1 LLM Decode

author.name: Josef Chen

entry.summary: This measurement study shows that batch-1 LLM decode for physical AI is memory-bound but not simply bandwidth-limited, as the achieved fraction of peak HBM bandwidth falls with context length across multiple NVIDIA GPUs. It refines the common bandwidth-bound account of single-stream inference.

entry.title: AdvScene: Rethinking Adversarial Patch Evaluation Through Scene Robustness

author.name: Xiaoyong (Brian) Yuan, Lan (Emily) Zhang

entry.summary: AdvScene introduces scene-grounded evaluation of adversarial patch robustness in reconstructed real environments, measuring whether patches remain effective across viewpoints, distances, and conditions. It reframes evaluation as operational measurement bridging fixed real benchmarks and ungrounded simulators.

entry.title: Improving Relative Representations with Learned Anchors and Whitened Inner Products

author.name: Oscar Thorsted Svendsen, Nikolaj Holst Jakobsen, Fabian Mager and Hiba Nassar

entry.summary: This work improves Relative Representations for cross-model communication by learning anchors as robust semantic prototypes instead of random sampling and using a whitened, geometry-aware inner-product similarity invariant to affine shifts. It addresses anisotropic geometries in transformer latent spaces.

entry.title: The Fast Mixing Mechanism for Differential Privacy

author.name: Omri Lev, Moshe Shenfeld, Vishwak Srinivasan, Katrina Ligett, Ashia C. Wilson

entry.summary: This paper introduces a differentially private sketching mechanism based on fast structured transforms (e.g., Hadamard) that, unlike prior Gaussian sketching methods, improves runtime over classical DP approaches while maintaining utility guarantees. It targets DP linear regression and related optimization.

entry.title: Crafter: A Multi-Agent Harness for Editable Scientific Figure Generation from Diverse Inputs

author.name: Haozhe Zhao, Shuzheng Si, Zhenhailong Wang, Zheng Wang, Liang Chen, Xiaotong Li, Zhixiang Liang, Maosong Sun, Minjia Zhang

entry.summary: Crafter is a multi-agent harness for generating and locally editing publication-quality scientific figures across diverse types and input conditions, addressing localized errors in structured figure layouts. It produces editable outputs rather than non-revisable rasters.

entry.title: CSULoRA: Closest Safe Update Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Oleksandr Marchenko Breneur, Adelaide Danilov, Aria Nourbakhsh, Salima Lamsiyah

entry.summary: CSULoRA is a post-hoc method correcting trained LoRA adapters by estimating a safety-aligned subspace from the weight displacement between a safety-aligned model and its base checkpoint, then decomposing updates toward the closest safe direction. Unlike hard interventions, it avoids removing task-relevant information or extra training.

entry.title: Learning to Perceive the World Through Control: Empowerment-Based Representation Learning

author.name: Mahsa Bastankhah, Sophie Broderick, Benjamin Eysenbach

entry.summary: This paper shows that empowerment-based reinforcement learning induces forward and backward representations capturing complementary control-relevant features that are invariant to control-irrelevant noise. It frames empowerment maximization as implicitly learning a control-centric world model.

entry.title: Triaging Threats to Specialized Guardrails

author.name: Wenjie Jacky Mo, Xiaofei Wen, Rui Cai, Boyu Zhu, Sicong Jiang, Zihan Wang, Minglai Yang, Zhe Zhao, Muhao Chen

entry.summary: This work introduces GuardZoo, a unified human-annotated safety benchmark of 32,460 samples across 15 unsafe categories, revealing that monolithic guardrails suffer from task interference across heterogeneous threat domains. It motivates specialized rather than single guardrail models for robust LLM safety.

entry.title: Differentially Private Preference Data Synthesis for Large Language Model Alignment

author.name: Fengyu Gao, Jing Yang

entry.summary: DPPrefSyn generates differentially private synthetic preference data for LLM alignment, learning a Bradley-Terry preference model under formal DP guarantees and combining it with public prompts to create privacy-preserving training data. It targets the privacy risks of using real human preference datasets.

entry.title: Eigenvectors of Experts are Training-free Non-collapsing Routers

author.name: Giang Do, Hung Le, Truyen Tran

entry.summary: This paper shows that the eigenvectors of expert weight matrices can serve as training-free, non-collapsing routers for sparse Mixture-of-Experts models, addressing expert collapse without retraining or finetuning. It provides theoretical and empirical evidence that collapse persists in well-pretrained models and that the eigenvector router mitigates it cheaply.

entry.title: Augmented Lagrangian Predictive Coding

author.name: Jeffrey Seely, Julian Gould

entry.summary: PC-ALM augments predictive coding with layer-local Lagrange multipliers so that local energy-minimization updates align with backpropagation gradients, matching BP performance up to depth 128 including in deep narrow networks where PC normally fails. It keeps PC's local-learning advantages while closing the accuracy gap with BP.

entry.title: LVSA: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Long Video Diffusion

author.name: Gael Glorian, Ioannis Lamprou, Zhen Zhang, Yujie Yuan, Hongsheng Liu

entry.summary: This work scales code RLVR by generating challenging verifiable tasks through Atomic Decomposition and Recombination, breaking problems into atomic elements and recombining them with control over difficulty and novelty. It addresses the scarcity of sufficiently hard verifiable code tasks near a model's competence edge.

entry.title: ConsisGuard: Aligning Safety Deliberation with Policy Enforcement in LLM Guardrails

author.name: Yan Wang, Zhixuan Chu, Zihao Xue, Zhen Bi, Bingyu Zhu, YueFeng Chen, Zeyu Yang, Jungang Lou, Longtao Huang, Ningyu Zhang, Kui Ren, Hui Xue

entry.summary: ConsisGuard identifies the deliberation-to-enforcement gap in reasoning-based LLM guardrails, where a model recognizes harmful intent in its reasoning but issues a safe label or vice versa, and proposes a consistency-aware framework enforcing policy-grounded reasoning and entailed decisions. It targets faithful policy execution in safety moderation.

entry.title: GRKV: Global Regression for Training-Free KV Cache Compression in Long-Context LLMs

author.name: Junjie Peng, You Wu, Haoyi Wu, Jialong Han, Xiaohua Xie, Kewei Tu, Jianhuang Lai

entry.summary: GRKV is a training-free KV cache compression method for long-context LLMs that addresses imbalanced merge patterns caused by span-based retention combined with post-eviction merging. It uses global regression to better preserve information under a fixed memory budget.

entry.title: Remembering by Reconstructing: Domain Incremental Learning With Test-Time Training on Video Streams

author.name: Jonathan Swinnen, Tinne Tuytelaars

entry.summary: This paper introduces a domain-incremental learning approach that deliberately exploits catastrophic forgetting via domain-specific LoRA adapters plus a self-supervised MAE head. At inference, online test-time training identifies which LoRA fits the current input to recover the right domain.

entry.title: Scalable Bayesian Inference for Nonlinear Conservation Laws

author.name: Tim Weiland, Philipp Hennig

entry.summary: This work develops a numerically conservative Bayesian method for uncertainty-aware simulation of nonlinear conservation laws, framing classical numerical methods as Gaussian-process inference. It uses sparse approximations to scale physics-aware uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: Generalizing Multi-Scale Time-Series Modeling with a Single Operator

author.name: Cheonwoo Lee, Dooho Lee, Doyun Choi, Jaemin Yoo

entry.summary: SiGMA unifies existing multi-scale time-series scaling methods into a scaling operator family, identifying their reliance on fixed discrete scaling as a limitation. It introduces a learnable discrete Gaussian kernel grounded in scale-space theory for distance-aware scaling, outperforming SOTA multi-scale baselines.

entry.title: EvoDefense: Co-Evolving Black-Box Defense with Large Language Models

author.name: Yu Li, Yuenan Hou, Yingmei Wei, Yanming Guo, Chaochao Lu

entry.summary: EvoDefense is a co-evolving black-box defense for LLMs using a guard LLM plus an experience-memory module, with an attack-defense evolution loop that iteratively refines strategies. It aims to generalize beyond pre-defined filtering heuristics to unseen attacks.

entry.title: Approximation and learning of anisotropic and mixed smooth functions by deep ReLU neural networks

author.name: Yunfei Yang, Jun Fan

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes approximation and learning rates for deep ReLU networks on anisotropic and mixed-smooth function classes, extending prior Besov-space results to overcome the curse of dimensionality. It derives improved rates under anisotropic smoothness conditions.

entry.title: BIAS-ID: A Framework for Analyzing Transformation Biases in AI-Generated Image Detectors

author.name: Jonas Ricker, Asja Fischer, Erwin Quiring

entry.summary: BIAS-ID is a framework for analyzing transformation biases in AI-generated image detectors, distinguishing bias from lack of robustness and providing a protocol to quantify how biased a detector is. It addresses why detectors collapse on real-world data due to spurious correlations.

entry.title: Vanilla ViT for Automotive Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Gilles Puy and Nermin Samet and Alexandre Boulch and Spyros Gidaris and Tuan-Hung VU and Renaud Marlet

entry.summary: This paper shows that plain non-hierarchical ViTs can match or exceed SOTA U-Net architectures for large-scale automotive lidar point-cloud semantic segmentation. The key is a carefully designed tokenizer, lightweight decoder head, and tailored data augmentations.

entry.title: Geometry-based Schr\"odinger Bridges for Trustworthy Multimodal Fusion

author.name: Jiayu Xiong and Jing Wang and Qi Zhang and Wanlong Wang and Jun Xue

entry.summary: GMF is a trustworthy multimodal fusion method that evaluates input reliability by measuring required transport correction in latent space using Schrodinger Bridge transport with Rectified Flow, rather than relying on model prediction confidence. This breaks the circular dependency where confident-but-wrong models evade error detection.

entry.title: Probing Collision Grounding in Vision-Language Models for Safe Human-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Jun Wang, Xiaohao Xu, Xiaonan Huang

entry.summary: TouchSafeBench is a physics-grounded benchmark built in Habitat 3.0 for evaluating collision grounding in VLMs, testing whether a monitor can determine if a robot is safely separated, colliding, or about to collide. It contains thousands of episodes with multi-view RGB-D, trajectory maps, and calibrated metadata.

entry.title: Fixed-Point Masked Generative Modeling

author.name: Andrea Miele, Yiming Qin, Alba Carballo-Castro, Justin Deschenaux, Pascal Frossard

entry.summary: FP-MGMs replace part of the denoiser in masked generative models with a fixed-point solver over shared attention layers for adaptive-depth refinement with fewer parameters. They add a cross-step consistency loss aligning hidden representations at neighboring denoising steps to improve low-budget sampling.

entry.title: Shared Doubt: Zero-shot Cross-Lingual Confidence Estimation for Language Models

author.name: Athina Kyriakou, Dennis Ulmer, Ivan Titov

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether multilingual LLMs encode shared, language-transferable confidence features using a lightweight linear probe on intermediate representations. The probe, trained monolingually, generalizes zero-shot to typologically diverse languages, with confidence features concentrated in middle layers.

entry.title: EchoRL: Reinforcement Learning via Rollout Echoing

author.name: Jinhe Bi, Aniri, Minglai Yang, Xingcheng Zhou, Wenke Huang, Sikuan Yan, Yujun Wang, Zixuan Cao, Michael F\"arber, Xun Xiao, Volker Tresp, Yunpu Ma

entry.summary: EchoRL addresses the collapse of learning signal in RLVR for LLM reasoning where all rollouts succeed and advantages degenerate to zero. It rescues valuable signals from advantage-degenerated rollouts via rollout echoing to sustain training gains.

entry.title: HARP-VLA: Human-Robot Aligned Representation Learning for Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Xiang Zhu, Puzhen Yuan, Yichen Liu, Jianyu Chen

entry.summary: HARP-VLA is a human-robot aligned representation learning framework for vision-language-action pretraining from human videos, addressing cross-embodiment visual and action discrepancies. It uses limited paired human-robot demonstrations as bridges plus abundant unpaired data to align representations for effective co-training.

entry.title: Scaling Multi-Hop Training Data via Graph-Constrained Path Selection

author.name: Pengyu Chen, Yonggang Zhang, Mingming Chen, Jun Song, Wei Xue, Yike Guo

entry.summary: This paper introduces a method to generate multi-hop reasoning training data from unannotated specialized text by decoupling path discovery from question verbalization. Reasoning paths are enumerated offline over a graph of keyword centroids, and the teacher model only verbalizes them, improving robustness for templated, cross-referencing corpora.

entry.title: BadBone: Backdoor Attacks Against Backbone Models in Visual Prompt Learning

author.name: Ziqing Yang and Rui Wen and Xinlei He and Yun Shen and Michael Backes and Yang Zhang

entry.summary: BadBone is a stealthy backdoor attack against backbone models in visual prompt learning, using bi-level optimization so that only target downstream tasks inherit the vulnerability. It demonstrates high attack success while maintaining utility across multiple models and datasets.

entry.title: Formalizing and falsifying causal pathways of rare events

author.name: Anahita Haghighat, Dominik Janzing

entry.summary: This paper formalizes causal pathways for rare events (outliers) in structural equation models and derives testable implications. It identifies conditions where these depend only on a causal abstraction of the pathway rather than the full causal graph, bridging verbal explanations and detailed modeling.

entry.title: Personalized to Persuade: The Effects of Contextualization and Warmth on Trust and Reliance in Conversational AI

author.name: Mert Yazan, Suzan Verberne, Frederik Bungaran Ishak Situmeang

entry.summary: This human-subjects study (N=380) examines how contextualization and conversational warmth affect trust and persuasiveness when AI argues against expert recommendations. It finds contextualization alone reduces persuasiveness but combined with warmth restores it via a crossover interaction.

entry.title: The Terminal Representation in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Amir Esterhuysen and Anders Jonsson

entry.summary: This paper introduces the terminal representation in RL, a structurally distinct formulation that encodes reward-weighted trajectories like the default representation but can be learned differently. It complements successor and default representations for spatio-temporal abstraction tasks.

entry.title: TokTalk: Expressive Real-time Facial Animation from Audio-LLM Tokens

author.name: Qingcheng Zhao, Yifang Pan, Karan Singh

entry.summary: TokTalk directly generates expressive real-time facial animation from streaming Audio-LLM tokens, bypassing the sequential pipeline of recognition, synthesis, and animation. It uses a chunk-based conditional flow matching model trained on a new audio-token to 3D facial motion dataset.

entry.title: Generalized Intention Modeling in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mateusz Odrowaz-Sypniewski, Jasmine Bayrooti, Ajay Shankar, Amanda Prorok

entry.summary: This paper introduces a task-adaptive opponent modeling framework for multi-agent RL that learns a performance-driven mixture of multiple intent representations rather than assuming a single a priori intent encoding. It addresses the task- and environment-dependence of intentions in non-cooperative settings.

entry.title: A Visually Impaired Assistance Benchmark for VLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation

author.name: Yi Zhao, Siqi Wang, Zhe Hu, Yushi Li, Jing Li

entry.summary: VIABLE is the first benchmark for VLM-as-a-Judge evaluation in visually impaired assistance tasks, with over 300K judgment samples across three scenarios and an effectiveness-impartiality-stability framework with a 12-mode failure taxonomy. It finds existing judges largely unreliable for this domain.

entry.title: Astra: a generalizable report generation foundation model for 3D computed tomography

author.name: Zhuhao Wang, Fang Chen, Chaohui Yu, Zihan Li, Yuchao Zheng, Jing Wang, Xuan Yang, Jia Guo, Zhenlu Yang, Xingju Zheng, Yihua Sun, Haojie Han, Xiaoxiao Qin, Zhan Feng, Wenbo Xiao, Chao Zhu, Yuehua Li, Shipeng Zhang, Hao Luo, Yunsong Peng, Fan Wang, Hongen Liao

entry.summary: Presents Astra, a generalizable foundation model for 3D CT report generation trained on 90k+ thoracoabdominal CT-report pairs spanning eight organ systems. Addresses cross-cohort terminology inconsistency for robust multi-region reporting.

entry.title: Value Functions as Supermartingale Certificates

author.name: Alessandro Abate, Daniel Contro, Mirco Giacobbe, Agust\'in Mart\'inez-Su\~n\'e, Diptarko Roy

entry.summary: Establishes a theoretical connection showing that under appropriate rewards, the value function of a policy almost-surely satisfying an omega-regular property serves as a supermartingale certificate. Bridges formal verification of stochastic systems with reinforcement learning.

entry.title: RayDer: Scalable Self-Supervised Novel View Synthesis from Real-World Video

author.name: Ulrich Prestel, Stefan Andreas Baumann, Nick Stracke, Bj\"orn Ommer

entry.summary: Introduces RayDer, a unified feed-forward transformer consolidating camera estimation, scene reconstruction, and rendering into a single backbone for scalable self-supervised novel view synthesis from real-world video. Treats dynamic content as a nuisance state to enable stable training while targeting static-scene NVS.

entry.title: What Gets Unmasked First? Trajectory Analysis of Diffusion Models for Graph-to-Text Generation

author.name: Qing Wang, Jacob Devasier, Chengkai Li

entry.summary: This is the first systematic study of masked diffusion language models for graph-to-text generation, finding that MDLMs unmask entities first then relational/structural tokens, and that SFT disrupts this by prematurely fixing length. They propose a training-free lambda-scaled structural decoding fix.

entry.title: SurGe: Improved Surface Geometry in Point Maps

author.name: Karim Knaebel, Gonzalo Martin Garcia, Christian Schmidt, Ilya Fradlin, Lucas Nunes, Daan de Geus, Bastian Leibe

entry.summary: SurGe improves local surface geometry in feed-forward point map 3D reconstruction via a point map normal metric, a point gradient matching loss, and a Neighborhood Attention Decoder. It addresses errors that are visually obvious but weakly reflected in common metrics across zero-shot monocular benchmarks.

entry.title: Language Models Learn Constructional Semantics, Not To Mention Syntax: Investigating LM Understanding of Paired-Focus Constructions

author.name: Wesley Scivetti, Ethan Wilcox, Nathan Schneider, Kanishka Misra, Leonie Weissweiler

entry.summary: This study tests whether language models understand rare English Paired-Focus constructions (e.g. 'let alone', 'much less') using a novel dataset probing scalar semantics and world knowledge. It finds several modestly sized models are sensitive to both form and meaning, illuminating learning dynamics of constructional semantics.

entry.title: Lumos-Nexus: Efficient Frequency Bridging with Homogeneous Latent Space for Video Unified Models

author.name: Jiazheng Xing, Hangjie Yuan, Lingling Cai, Xinyu Liu, Yujie Wei, Fei Du, Hai Ci, Tao Feng, Jiasheng Tang, Weihua Chen, Fan Wang, Yong Liu

entry.summary: Lumos-Nexus is a training-efficient unified video generation framework that aligns a lightweight generator with an understanding block during training, then uses Unified Progressive Frequency Bridging at inference to hand off to a high-capacity generator. It improves visual fidelity while keeping training affordable.

entry.title: Features of SAEs are universal - but only up to an unknown random rotation

author.name: Jordan McCann

entry.summary: This empirical interpretability study shows that SAE features are universal across independently trained models only up to an unknown random (Haar-like) rotation, explaining why applying one model's SAE to another's activations yields negative reconstruction. It replicates across a toy model and nine Pythia-70m seeds with released code.

entry.title: Speculative Decoding Across Languages

author.name: Nirajan Paudel, Michael Ginn, Luc De Nardi, Alexis Palmer

entry.summary: This paper improves speculative decoding for non-English languages by comparing finetuning draft models on translation data, on monolingual corpora, and training simple n-gram draft models. It addresses the disproportionately poor multilingual capability of small draft models across eleven languages.

entry.title: Semantic Motion Anchors: Bridging Motion and Meaning in Co-Speech Gestures

author.name: Varsha Suresh, Mohammad Mahdi Abootorabi, Mohamed Salman, M. Hamza Mughal, Christian Theobalt, Ashwin Ram, J\"urgen Steimle, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: This work proposes semantic motion anchors, natural-language abstractions of gesture motion capturing physical form and communicative intent, to bridge motion and meaning in co-speech gesture learning. It discretizes 3D gestures into primitives, verbalizes them, and grounds them in transcripts for auxiliary contrastive supervision, improving results on BEAT2.

entry.title: TSM-Bench: Detecting LLM-Generated Text in Real-World Wikipedia Editing Practices

author.name: Gerrit Quaremba and Elizabeth Black and Denny Vrande\v{c}i\'c and Elena Simperl

entry.summary: TSM-Bench is a multilingual, multi-task benchmark for detecting LLM-generated text in realistic Wikipedia editing scenarios like summarization, showing SOTA detectors struggle with task-specific machine text. It highlights that constrained, context-conditioned generation resembles human writing more closely.

entry.title: Assign and Add: A Mechanistic Study of Compositional Arithmetic

author.name: Brady Exoo, Alberto Bietti, John Sous

entry.summary: Mechanistically studies compositional generalization in transformers via a controlled variable-assignment and modular-addition task. Shows the same MLP module performs addition whether inputs are direct or routed through variable assignment, with analysis of training dynamics.

entry.title: Giving Sensors a Voice: Multimodal JEPA for Semantic Time-Series Embeddings

author.name: Utsav Dutta, Gerardo Pastrana, Sina Khoshfetrat Pakazad, Henrik Ohlsson

entry.summary: CHARM is a channel-aware JEPA-based Transformer that incorporates channel-level text descriptions for general-purpose multivariate time-series embeddings, with a novel loss for temporally stable, informative latents. It achieves strong cross-task performance with interpretability via description-aware gating.

entry.title: KLIP: localized distribution shift detection via KL-divergence with diffusion priors in Inverse Problems

author.name: Alireza Kheirandish, Jihoon Hong, Sara Fridovich-Keil

entry.summary: KLIP detects localized distribution shifts in inverse problems via KL-divergence between a diffusion prior and posterior, requiring no calibration data or knowledge of the shifted distribution. It can both classify whole images as OOD and localize OOD patches from indirect measurements.

entry.title: NumLeak: Public Numeric Benchmarks as Latent Labels in Foundation Models

author.name: Anany Kotawala

entry.summary: NumLeak is a measurement framework showing that public numeric benchmarks appear in LLM pretraining, so date-conditioned evaluations may measure memorized recall rather than true out-of-sample skill. It combines API-boundary probes with white-box validation, finding frontier models recall financial and economic series with near-perfect correlation.

entry.title: SANA-Streaming: Real-time Streaming Video Editing with Hybrid Diffusion Transformer

author.name: Yuyang Zhao, Yicheng Pan, Qiyuan He, Jincheng Yu, Junsong Chen, Tian Ye, Haozhe Liu, Enze Xie, Song Han

entry.summary: SANA-Streaming is a system-algorithm co-designed framework for real-time, high-resolution streaming video-to-video editing on consumer GPUs. It uses a hybrid diffusion transformer with partial softmax attention and a cycle-reverse regularization to enforce temporal and semantic consistency.

entry.title: Local Differential Privacy with Correlated Noise Achieves Central-DP Optimal Cost

author.name: Madhura Pathegama, Srikanth Avasarala, Viveck R. Cadambe, Juba Ziani

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that local differential privacy with carefully designed correlated noise can match the optimal estimation cost of the centralized DP model for private summation, up to arbitrarily small error. It challenges the assumption that local DP necessarily incurs substantial utility loss versus central DP.

entry.title: Configurable Reward Model for Balanced Safety Alignment

author.name: Zhengping Jiang, Mehran Khodabandeh, Akash Bharadwaj, Manik Bhandari, Mayur Srungarapu, Anqi Liu, Benjamin Van Durme, and Li Chen

entry.summary: The Configurable Safety Reward Model is jointly optimized for calibrated safety compliance and reward modeling to align LLMs with heterogeneous, rapidly changing safety specifications. Configuration-targeted data augmentation enforces instruction adherence while preserving severity structure, improving generalization to unseen safety configurations.

entry.title: ARISTO Hand: Sensing-Driven Distal Hyperextension for Fine-Grained Manipulation

author.name: Aaron Kim, Dong Ho Kang, Mark Helwig, Mingyo Seo, Kazuto Yokoyama, Tetsuya Narita, Luis Sentis

entry.summary: The ARISTO Hand is a tendon-driven robotic hand combining active distal hyperextension with hybrid fingertip sensing (rigid force-torque plus soft capacitive arrays) for manipulating thin objects. It improves pull-out force by 2.76x while preserving normal grasping.

entry.title: Caspar: CUDA Accelerator for Symbolic Programming with Adaptive Reordering

author.name: Emil Martens, Aaron Miller, Matias Varnum and Annette Stahl

entry.summary: Caspar is a CUDA library that auto-generates optimized GPU kernels from symbolic expressions (building on SymForce), providing a state-of-the-art nonlinear GPU solver for robotics optimization. Users define only symbolic residual functions and Caspar handles differentiation and kernel generation.

entry.title: ScaleMAP: Preserving Local Density and Neighborhood Structure in Low-Dimensional Embeddings

author.name: Rajas Poorna and Marcus T. Cicerone (Georgia Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: ScaleMAP preserves local density and neighborhood scale in dimensionality reduction by dividing pairwise embedding displacements by the geometric mean of endpoint local radii, re-injecting scale as a change of variables rather than a competing objective. This avoids the scattering problems of density-penalty methods like DensMAP.

entry.title: The Architecture of Errors: From Universal Impossibility to Patch-Local LLM Reliability

author.name: Mikhail L. Arbuzov, Lee Mosbacker, Sisong Bei, Ziwei Dong, Dmitri Kalaev, Alexey Shvets

entry.summary: This paper argues universal LLM reliability is impossible since intervention-distinguishable failure modes are unbounded across all tasks, but within operationally bounded patches (legal review, medical RAG, code repair) failures are sparse, repetitive, and concentrated. It reframes reliability as local catalogue-discovery and intervention-coverage rather than universal guarantees.

entry.title: PInVerify: An Offline Embodied Benchmark for Active Instance Verification

author.name: Yuhang Jiang

entry.summary: PInVerify is an offline embodied benchmark for Active Instance Verification, where agents actively select viewpoints to confirm whether a candidate object matches a fine-grained description. It includes 3,000 episodes across 18 categories with multi-view captures and a navigation topology exposing uninformative trap views.

entry.title: Counterfactual Graph for Multi-Agent LLM Calibration

author.name: Jiatan Huang, Mingchen Li, Ziming Li, Sunjae Kwon, Hong Yu, Chuxu Zhang

entry.summary: CAGE-CAL is a counterfactual calibration framework for multi-agent LLM systems that compares observed post-communication agent graphs against matched no-communication graphs to detect false consensus from correlated failures. It addresses the unreliability of treating agent agreement as evidence of correctness.

entry.title: Self-Certifying Transport MCMC via Dual Spectral-Gap Certificates

author.name: Jun Hu

entry.summary: CerT-MCMC equips learned-transport MCMC with automatic spectral-gap convergence certificates, using a normalizing flow as both the Metropolis-Hastings proposal and basis for computable bounds. It develops two complementary certificates and proves a matching dimension-dependent lower bound revealing fundamental limits in high dimensions.

entry.title: Is the Last Layer Sufficient for Uncertainty Quantification?

author.name: Joseph Wilson, Chris van der Heide, Liam Hodgkinson, Fred Roosta

entry.summary: This paper compares full-network versus last-layer linearization for Bayesian uncertainty quantification in deep neural networks, using random matrix theory and empirical analysis. It challenges the common belief that last-layer approximation necessarily degrades performance, finding no meaningful difference under their analysis.

entry.title: Anchoring LLM Gender Bias to Human Baselines: A Cross-Lingual Audit

author.name: Jiwoo Choi, Seonwoo Ahn, Tongxin Zhang, Seohyon Jung

entry.summary: This cross-lingual audit measures gender stereotyping in six LLMs across English, Korean, Chinese, and Japanese, anchoring drift against cross-cultural human baselines from 48 countries. It finds model stereotyping spans about 2.5x the entire human cross-country range, with compounding effects across languages.

entry.title: Cognitive Fatigue in Autoregressive Transformers: Formalization and Measurement

author.name: Riju Marwah, Ritvik Garimella, Vishal Pallagani, Atishay Jain, Michael Stewart, Amit Sheth

entry.summary: This work formalizes cognitive fatigue in autoregressive transformers, a measurable generation-time degradation state involving attention decay, representational drift, and entropy miscalibration, and introduces a lightweight Fatigue Index for runtime monitoring. It provides online diagnostics for long-horizon generation failures across nine models.

entry.title: Learning Multi-Agent Coordination via Sheaf-ADMM

author.name: Jeffrey Seely, Bart{\l}omiej Cupia{\l}, Llion Jones

entry.summary: This paper introduces a differentiable multi-agent coordination framework where agents process overlapping local views and coordinate via ADMM with inter-agent constraints specified by a cellular sheaf, allowing heterogeneous notions of consensus. It is trained end-to-end through unrolled optimization and tested on maze pathfinding, image classification, and Sudoku.

entry.title: Annealed Softmax Greedy in Many-Armed Bayesian Bandits

author.name: William Overman, Mohsen Bayati

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical explanation for why uncertainty-agnostic policy updates like GRPO can be effective, analyzing an annealed softmax policy in many-armed Bayesian Bernoulli bandits under a linear upper-tail prior condition. It connects RLVR-style updates to greedy bandit behavior when near-optimal arms are abundant.

entry.title: Free energy Estimation on Any State Space

author.name: Jiajun He, Zijing Ou, Francisco Vargas, Yingzhen Li, Jos\'e Miguel Hern\'andez-Lobato, Carles Domingo-Enrich, Yuanqi Du

entry.summary: This paper generalizes neural-transport-based free energy estimation to arbitrary state spaces, including discrete, multimodal, and autoregressive settings, building on recent finite-time neural transport work. It establishes algebraic identities and validates efficiency beyond continuous spaces.

entry.title: Vector Linking via Cross-Model Local Isometric Consistency

author.name: Ziying Chen, Yang Cao, He Sun, Beining Yang, Tianjian Yang

entry.summary: This paper studies recovering cross-model object correspondences from embeddings of different black-box encoders using only vectors, exploiting local geometric consistency. It proposes a reference-based geometric hashing method that links vectors from a tiny seed of paired anchors.

entry.title: Subspace-Decomposed JEPAs: Disentangling Progression and Content in Latent World Models

author.name: Lucas Thil, Jesse Read, Rim Kaddah, Guillaume Doquet

entry.summary: SD-JEPA splits the JEPA latent into orthogonal progression and content subspaces with separate anti-collapse losses, proving they act on disjoint coordinates so they compose additively. It improves over LeWM baselines on control benchmarks at matched compute.

entry.title: Multilingual and Cross-Lingual Citation Needed Detection on Wikipedia for Lower-Resource Languages

author.name: Gerrit Quaremba and Amy Rechkemmer and Elizabeth Black and Denny Vrande\v{c}i\'c and Elena Simperl

entry.summary: MCN is a multilingual citation-needed-detection corpus spanning 18 languages across three resource levels for Wikipedia fact-checking. The study shows small encoder-style fine-tuned language models outperform prompted LLMs across languages, offering accessible solutions for low-resource organizations.

entry.title: Trust-Region Behavior Blending for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Daniil Plyusov, Alexey Gorbatovski, Alexey Malakhov, Nikita Balagansky, Boris Shaposhnikov, Daria Korotyshova, Daniil Gavrilov

entry.summary: Trust-Region Behavior Blending is a warmup method for on-policy distillation that replaces early poor student rollouts with the closest-to-teacher behavior policy inside a student-centered KL trust region. The KL budget anneals to zero, returning to pure student rollouts after warmup.

entry.title: D$^3$: Dynamic Directional Graph-Constrained Data Scheduling for LLM Training

author.name: Yuanjian Xu, Jianing Hao, Guang Zhang, Zhong Li

entry.summary: D3 is a dynamic directional graph-constrained data scheduling framework for LLM training that models directional influences between training samples as a dynamic influence graph.
